notes:
SCOPE IS FAR LARGER THAN THIS BEAD'S TITLE, and the discriminator is DEV vs RELEASE, not the feed. Established 2026-09-03 by pilot 1 of the rf2-t4jpz rehearsal - a BLINDED agent that had never seen this bead, reading only the 29 published pages - which lost roughly a third of its run to it before isolating it. Same pin, 6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba.

THE RULE. In a DEVELOPMENT build the demo backend's HTTP replies do not settle in Chrome. In a RELEASE build, same machine, same browser, same commit, they all do.

Development build, headless Chrome, four screens:
  the feed                  Hicasso (migrated)   "No articles are here... yet."
  article detail (deep link) Reagent, UNTOUCHED  "No article loaded."
  profile (deep link)        Reagent, UNTOUCHED  "No profile loaded."
  sign in                    Reagent, UNTOUCHED  stays `anonymous`

Release build, same browser, same driver:
  the feed        10 cards, "Hello, Conduit", pagination 1/2/3
  article detail  a real backend reply - "Couldn't load article: Article not found."
  sign in         `authed`
  the editor      renders, publishes, navigates

TWO UNTOUCHED REAGENT SCREENS FAIL IDENTICALLY TO THE MIGRATED ONE. So this is neither the view layer, nor the migration, nor the feed - it is application-wide and substrate-independent, and my own operator measurement (the description above) was taken on a `shadow-cljs watch` build, which is why it looked like a feed defect. The Popular Tags sidebar populating while articles did not is the one fact that still needs explaining against this rule, and it is the loose end worth pulling.

WHAT THE PILOT RULED OUT, each measured: headless timer throttling (`setTimeout(...,0)` at 0 ms, `requestAnimationFrame` at 0 ms, microtasks running); a stale bundle (reproduced on a clean watch restart); the reply delay (`reply-delay-ms` is 20); an SPA fallback artefact (reproduced before any fallback existed).

THE PILOT'S ONE UNTESTED LEAD, and it could not test it without reading source the fence bars: the demo backend defers every reply through `:dispatch-later`, and `:dispatch-later` is the common factor in everything that fails. That is where a fix dispatch should start.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE EXAMPLE. If deferred effects do not settle in development builds generally, every developer meets it on every async path, and the symptom is an empty screen with no error - the most expensive failure shape there is. The pilot graded its own entry `none` for defect class because it could not honestly attribute a cause; that is the right grading and it is not a judgement that the finding is small.

CROSS-REFERENCE: the pilot's own entry is P1-F21 in ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-realworld.friction-log.md (local-only), and the same log's outcome-6 row records the release build passing both halves against this bundle.

MECHANISM PINNED 2026-09-04 (worker/dispatchlater-a, PR #9134). NOT :dispatch-later,
and no request was ever issued. :dispatch-later, the demo backend, the canned-reply
path and managed HTTP are all healthy; the after-fix event stream shows both
:rf.http/deliver-canned-reply hops through :dispatch-later working exactly as designed.

THE MECHANISM. examples/real-apps/realworld_http/schema.cljs registers NINETEEN app-db
path schemas against :rf/default at ns-load, all of them non-nilable. app-db starts {},
and each slice is seeded by its OWN feature's :*/initialise, fanned out from
:app/initialise - separate events, therefore separate commits. The candidate validator
(re-frame.router/run-candidate-validation! -> re-frame.schemas.validate/validate-app-schema!)
walks EVERY registered path over the WHOLE candidate app-db at EVERY :db commit,
(get-in db path), with NO exemption for a path nothing has written yet - spec/010 line 73
states this outright ('a normal [:map ...] schema over the nil app-db slot ... detonates
every dev commit'). An unwritten path reads nil, which is not a [:map ...]. So the FIRST
seed was rejected by the eighteen siblings still absent; every later seed was rejected the
same way; app-db never left {}. Measured: app-db is {} on a live page while
[:rf.runtime/routing :current] is fully populated.

WHY IT LOOKED LIKE 'REPLIES DO NOT SETTLE'. A rejected candidate does NOT walk :fx
(spec/010 row 4). So :articles/load's [:rf.http/managed ...] never fired - no request, no
:dispatch-later armed. Measured two ways on the same dispatch: a :trace listener showed
:rf.event/dispatched, :run-start, :db-pending, 17 x :rf.error/schema-validation-failure
(:rollback? true, :where :app-db), :run-end - and NO :rf.fx/handled at all; and a patched
re-frame.interop/set-timeout! recorded zero timers armed.

WHY DEV ONLY. validate-app-schema!'s entire body sits inside
(if interop/debug-enabled? ... true) - goog.DEBUG. A release build returns true without
walking anything and every candidate installs. That is the whole dev/release split the
pilot found; it is not timers, not the view layer, not the migration.

THE POPULAR TAGS LOOSE END, EXPLAINED. The tags lifecycle lives ENTIRELY in the
:realworld/tags state machine. Its snapshot is runtime-db, validated by the machine-data
boundary against the machine's own [:schemas :data], whose :data the machine spec seeds
itself. :tags/load and :tags/loaded return ONLY :fx, never :db, so app-effect? is false and
the app-db validator never ran for them. The one panel on the page that never touches
app-db is the one that worked. The pilot's LinearLite control renders because it registers
no app-db schemas at all (grep: no reg-app-schema under examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite).

WHY THE BASELINE COULD NOT SEE IT. reg-app-schemas is FRAME-LOCAL and the example registers
against :rf/default. Every existing test drives the example in an anonymous frame
(make-anon-frame-record!), which carries no app-db schemas - so the registry that kills the
real app is inert in the harness. realworld_cljs_test.cljs even re-registers [:auth] against
its own frame by hand for one regression, which is the tell.

VERDICT: EXAMPLE DEFECT, not a framework defect. The semantics is documented (spec/010) and
the corpus already teaches the correct usage with a written rationale -
examples/patterns/boot/schema.cljs: 'Each slot below starts out nil - the boot machine fills
it in later - so every registration wears a :maybe to stay valid through the loading phases.'

FIX (PR #9134): every registration in realworld_http/schema.cljs now wears :maybe for the
boot window, with the rationale written out, and the registry becomes a named value
app-db-schemas so a harness can install the app's real registry on its own frame. Plus a new
substrate contract test, implementation/core/test/re_frame/example_realworld_boot_seed_cljs_test.cljs
(examples stay test-free), which drives the example's own boot fan-out under its own registry
AND pins the framework semantics underneath it.

WITNESS. dev build, headless Chrome, real shadow-cljs bundle over HTTP:
  before  #app 2350, 'No articles are here... yet.', app-db {}
  after   #app 13236, ten article cards + pagination, app-db seeded
  release after: #app 9130, ten cards - dev and release now agree.
Article detail, sign-in and post-login home all render in dev after the fix. Zero page errors
either side.
Same instrument both sides on the identical dispatch: before {:event [:articles/load]
:outcome :rolled-back}; after {:event [:articles/load] :outcome :ok} plus five more events
ending in :articles/loaded with ten articles.
Test witness: with the pre-fix registrations planted back (17 sites), the new ns is exit 1
with 15/17 assertions failing and app-db {}; with the fix, exit 0. The two assertions that
pass either way are the ones pinning framework semantics. Restore verified by blob hash.
Gates (exit codes captured to files): shadow-cljs compile node-test 0; node out/node-test.js
--test= the new ns + the five existing realworld nses 0, 'Ran 90 tests containing 899
assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.'; clj-kondo on both changed files 0; shadow-cljs release
:examples/realworld 0.

THREE THINGS FILED SEPARATELY RATHER THAN FIXED HERE (outside this fence):
  1. examples/real-apps/realworld_resources has the SAME defect - MEASURED, not inferred:
     dev build, app-db {}, zero cards, page renders a 1698-char shell. Four non-nilable
     schemas at ns-load ([:auth], [:auth :login-form], [:auth :register-form],
     [:settings-form]) and [:settings-form] is never seeded at boot at all, so that app's
     every :db commit is rejected permanently rather than only during boot.
  2. :rf.error/schema-validation-failure reaches ONLY the dev-only :trace stream
     (schemas/validate.cljc calls trace/emit-error!, not the both-axes emitter), never the
     always-on :errors stream. Measured with a control on the same frame: an :errors listener
     saw 0 records while :trace carried all 17, and the same listener DID receive
     :rf.error/no-such-handler for an unregistered event id. That silence is what turned a
     one-line schema mistake into an invisible app-wide rollback loop and cost the pilot a
     third of its run - worth a ruling even if the current behaviour is deliberate.
  3. A React duplicate-key warning on the article-card tag list, visible only once cards
     render (dev React only).
close_reason:
CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor (backlog-reread loop): the fix is on the trunk and all three carried findings are re-homed. Nothing remains on this bead.

THE FIX. PR #9134 merged as 627d6da0a1, 'fix(realworld): the example boots under its own app-db schemas'. examples/real-apps/realworld_http/schema.cljs now wraps each app-db path registration in :maybe for the boot window with the rationale written out, names the registry as a value so a harness can install it on its own frame, and is pinned by a differential contract test in the framework tree at implementation/core/test/re_frame/example_realworld_boot_seed_cljs_test.cljs (examples are test-free, rf2-8cevm).

THE MECHANISM, for the record, because it is nothing like this bead's title. Not :dispatch-later and not HTTP: nineteen NON-NILABLE app-db path schemas registered at ns-load, against a candidate validator that walks EVERY registered path over the WHOLE candidate app-db at EVERY :db commit with no exemption for a path nothing has written yet. app-db starts {}, :app/initialise fans out to separate dispatches, so each seed is its own commit and each is rejected by the siblings still absent — app-db never leaves {}. DEV ONLY, because validate-app-schema!'s whole body sits inside (if interop/debug-enabled? ... true), which is what makes it so disorienting: the app works in release and is dead in dev. And because a rejected candidate does not walk :fx either, no request is ever ISSUED — a patched set-timeout! recorded zero timers armed, which is why the :dispatch-later lead was a dead end.

THE THREE CARRIED FINDINGS, all re-homed and none lost:
1. The same defect in examples/real-apps/realworld_resources -> rf2-ghxt, CLOSED, PR #9143 merged.
2. :rf.error/schema-validation-failure reaching only the dev-only :trace stream and never the always-on :errors stream -> rf2-xpd8, OPEN and HELD FOR MIKE. It needs a product ruling on which stream carries a rollback, not a worker.
3. The duplicate React key warning on the article-card tag list -> rf2-sefb, OPEN and dispatched to worker/exfix-a.

The DOCUMENTATION half also landed: rf2-aaam put the whole-registry-per-commit rule, the nil-reads-as-a-value trap, both escapes and the dev/release direction into docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md.

WHY CLOSE RATHER THAN HOLD: keeping a P1 open whose every part is either merged or re-homed keeps it at the head of the ready list drawing dispatch attention it cannot use. That is the 'item already DONE in the tree' case this loop exists to catch.

title: bug(story-mcp): retire the transport-unreachable blocking recorder
description:
## Scope

Retire the unreachable blocking recorder workflow from the published headless Story-MCP catalogue. Limit the change to `tools/story-mcp/**` plus directly coupled current Story MCP-surface prose/fixtures. Preserve Story core's recorder primitives and the settled Pair-owned live-browser route.

## Correctness finding

`record-as-variant` advertises a successful non-empty capture while making the actor that must produce the events unreachable. The handler performs `start-recording!`, blocks the only stdio dispatch loop for `:duration-ms`, then calls `stop-recording!`. While it sleeps, the server cannot read or dispatch a second MCP request. A human canvas cannot supply events either: the shipped server is a headless JVM subprocess with no JVM-to-browser bridge. Therefore a normal MCP client has no transport-reachable way to drive an event during the recording window. The tool normally returns a successful empty snippet, not the recorded interaction its name and contract promise.

This violates the tool-boundary invariant: every advertised success path must be exercisable through the published transport, without an undisclosed in-process collaborator. A green zero-event response is especially misleading because it looks like a valid recording artefact.

## Evidence

- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc:297-333` owns one synchronous read -> dispatch -> write loop; it does not read the next frame until the current handler returns.
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/recorder.cljc:343-350` starts the recorder, calls blocking `sleep-ms`, and only then stops it. Lines 43-62 and 136-178 explicitly define the duration window as blocking the server loop.
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/recorder.cljc:418-457` advertises this as a first-class tool that starts, blocks, stops, and returns captured dispatches.
- `tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md:586-593` says the agent or human drives dispatches during that blocked window. `tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md:425-436` separately describes start, intervening MCP interactions, and stop, but Story-MCP exposes no independent start/stop request pair and the live browser is explicitly Pair-owned.
- `tools/story-mcp/README.md:15-20,54-95` and `tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md:37-72` establish that the shipped process sees only its own JVM registry and has no browser/nREPL bridge.
- The focused JVM tests do not exercise the transport path: `tools/story-mcp/test/re_frame/story_mcp/tools_test.clj:1854-1920` installs an `add-watch` on the recorder atom that injects events synchronously inside `start-recording!` on the handler's own thread. That is a hidden in-process collaborator unavailable to MCP clients.
- The official SDK witness explicitly accepts only the vacuous arm: `tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-story.cjs:633-653` calls the tool with zero duration and requires `recorded-event-count` to be 0. No stdio/SDK witness produces one captured event.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch Story-MCP through its documented consumer alias with one JVM-loadable variant registered.
2. Complete `initialize`, then call `record-as-variant` for that variant with `duration-ms: 5000`.
3. Before that call returns, write a second valid `tools/call` intended to execute the variant to the same server stdin.
4. Observe that no response to the second call arrives during the recording window; the synchronous run loop cannot read it until `record-as-variant` has stopped recording and returned.
5. Observe that the first call succeeds with `recorded-event-count: 0` and an empty generated script. Interacting with a browser Story canvas cannot change this JVM recorder because the server has no browser bridge.

## Failure scenario / invariant

The second MCP request remains unread until after the first call has already stopped recording. A browser interaction cannot reach the JVM recorder. The result is a green, empty artefact from a capture path whose advertised producer cannot overlap its window.

Required invariant: a catalogue tool must not report successful capture when every producer available through that catalogue is sequenced outside its capture window.

## Recommended minimal fix

Take the pre-alpha subtraction: remove `record-as-variant` from Story-MCP's live registry, generated descriptor manifest, tool-name fixture, current Story-MCP specs/README, and its adapter-only tests. Keep the recorder in `tools/story/` for its real in-process/browser consumers, and state once that interactive canvas recording is performed through Pair in the attached CLJS runtime.

Do not make the stdio loop concurrent, add background jobs/session tokens, add a second browser bridge, or preserve a deprecated alias. If a future concrete headless use case needs capture, require an executable SDK witness with a transport-reachable event producer before adding a turn-shaped start/finish surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A live official-SDK `tools/list` response no longer contains `record-as-variant`; the committed tool-name fixture, generated descriptor manifest, catalogue counts, README, and current normative Story-MCP API/spec tables agree with the reduced registry.
2. An SDK `tools/call` naming `record-as-variant` receives the server's existing method-not-found response, and a before/after read of the Story recorder state proves the rejected call did not start or alter a recording.
3. No reachable Story-MCP handler starts a recorder and sleeps for a duration window, and no current Story-MCP prose claims an agent or human can inject events while its only stdio loop is blocked. Browser-canvas recording is routed to the established Pair/live-CLJS door without adding another transport.
4. Non-vacuity: the end-to-end witness first proves the same launched server has a working catalogue and execution path (`register-variant` followed by `run-variant` returns the fixture verdict), then proves recorder absence. The absence assertion must not pass merely because initialization, registry loading, or all tool dispatch is broken.
5. Control: a focused inventory test compares the live `tools/list` surface with the committed fixture and explicitly rejects the retired name; temporarily reintroducing the descriptor (or the forbidden fixture name) makes that test red, restoring the edit makes it green.
6. Story core recorder tests remain green, demonstrating that only the impossible headless adapter is removed. Story-MCP JVM tests, descriptor generation/check, stdio roundtrip, and official SDK Story conformance pass with the reduced surface.

## Non-goals

- No changes to `re-frame.story` recorder semantics, event filtering, coeffect capture, snippet generation, or browser UI recording.
- No concurrent/multiplexed stdio dispatcher, worker queue, progress stream, polling protocol, session token, or background scheduler.
- No nREPL/JVM-to-browser bridge and no new Pair-MCP tool.
- No redesign of `register-variant`, `run-variant`, write gating, sensitive-read egress, dedup, or token caps.
- No compatibility warning, alias, deprecation period, or migration ceremony for the pre-alpha tool.

## Related / duplicate search

- `rf2-p1keh` (open) removes false cross-process Story-MCP calls from the Pair skill and keeps live Story work on Pair's attached browser. It explicitly does not change Story-MCP; this bug removes the impossible headless recorder tool itself, so the outcomes are complementary, not duplicates.
- `rf2-cfq8a` (closed) made JVM-loadable project stories reachable at Story-MCP launch; it preserves the headless/live-browser boundary and does not make an actor reachable during a blocked recorder call.
- `rf2-7dewo` (closed) converged Story variant vocabulary and touched recorder write-back spelling; it did not address capture reachability.
- All-status title, description, and notes searches for `record-as-variant`, recorder, `duration-ms`, blocking/recording window, `start-recording!`, `stop-recording!`, drives interactions, zero/empty capture, turn-shaped, browser bridge, same JVM, and existing MCP write surface found no bead owning this outcome.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Official-SDK `tools/list` excludes `record-as-variant`, and the manifest, fixture, catalogue counts, README, and normative API/spec tables agree.
2. Calling the retired name returns method-not-found and leaves recorder state byte-equal before/after.
3. No reachable Story-MCP path starts a recorder then blocks its sole dispatch loop; browser recording is routed to Pair without a new transport.
4. Non-vacuity: the same E2E process successfully registers and runs a fixture variant before asserting recorder absence.
5. Control: a planted reintroduction of the descriptor/name makes the focused inventory check red; restoration is green.
6. Story core recorder tests plus Story-MCP JVM, descriptor, stdio, and official SDK conformance gates pass.

The advertised capture path is transport-unreachable; the recommended retirement is a subtraction that fits the pre-alpha stance, and the non-goals correctly ban a concurrent dispatcher - NOT a reject-candidate. COLLISIONS: live pair-mcp-streams holds mcp-conformance fixtures + drift checker - end-to-end-story.cjs is a different file in the same package, so fence it and soft-sequence if that worker diff reaches story files; live interceptor-prose holds tools/story/spec/017 (different file, same dir - fine). GATES: clojure -M:test from tools/story-mcp (JVM); clojure -M:test from tools/story (JVM); npm run test:mcp-conformance --prefix implementation (moderate - launches JVM servers, not a shadow/browser lane). close_reason: Retired record-as-variant from the Story-MCP catalogue (PR #8830). The blocking recorder handler slept the server's only stdio dispatch loop for :duration-ms, so no MCP client could drive an event during the advertised capture window (headless JVM, no browser bridge) and the tool could only return a green EMPTY capture. Preserved: re-frame.story.recorder primitives untouched (suite 1876/6851 green) and the Pair-owned live-browser recording route, stated as the one interactive-canvas door. Acceptance pins landed: JVM inventory test explicitly rejects the name (planted reintroduction reds it naming fixture-only=#{record-as-variant}; restore blob-verified green); tools/call on the retired name is the existing -32601 method-not-found with recorder state byte-equal before/after; SDK witness proves absence on a server that first registers AND runs a fixture variant. Gates (final base after rebase onto ead1d8529c, captured exits all 0): story-mcp JVM 278/1457, story JVM 1876/6851, mcp-base 277/948, gen --check in sync 19, stdio-roundtrip, SDK end-to-end-story, flag-gates, watchdog 3/3, skill-mcp drift, doc slugs, readme links. Fence: check_skill_mcp_drift.py needed a story-scoped edit (leaves tuple named the deleted file); NOT edited and left for mayor sequencing behind rf2-ahjbc: mcp-conformance/NAMING.md record-as-<thing> example row and re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md ~675 comparative mention.

title: surface-review(skill-re-frame2): let the authoring agent run the gate it already discovers
description:
## Scope

Turn the published `skills/re-frame2/` authoring skill from an edit-then-handoff recipe emitter into a closed-loop author for an existing re-frame2 ClojureScript application. Let a tool-capable agent discover and run the project's own narrow, noninteractive compile/test/lint gate after it writes code. Keep live-runtime inspection and run-side Story MCP work with `re-frame2-pair`, and keep interactive or visual verification with the programmer when no drivable runtime exists.

The coherent change includes the published skill, its normative design/index wording, the Q14 enforcement arm in the drift guard, and one focused behavioural eval. It does not change any re-frame2 framework API.

## Findings

1. The contract defeats its own outcome. `skills/re-frame2/spec/design.md:9` says the output should compile, run, and pass the author's tests, but `SKILL.md:29-32` removes every Bash compile/test/lint tool and `SKILL.md:153` requires a gate handoff. `skills/README.md:201` goes further and describes the agent as emitting a recipe for a human to paste, even though the skill is allowed to Read/Edit/Write the application.
2. The handoff is pure programmer relay work. `references/cross-cutting/testing.md:355-364` already teaches the agent how to inspect `deps.edn`, `shadow-cljs.edn`, `package.json`, and the nearest README to select the exact narrow gate. It then spends its final instruction telling the programmer to execute that command and return the result. Running the already-discovered noninteractive command closes the loop in the same turn.
3. There is no matching trust rationale. The published-skill policy at `skills/README.md:261-281` explicitly trusts the invoker and accepts routine `npm`, `npx`, `clojure`, `shadow-cljs`, and `clj-kondo` wildcards while barring genuinely dangerous commands. The migration row names a hard trust boundary; the re-frame2 authoring row names only the old Q14 decision.
4. Static drift checks do not substitute for compiling authored code. `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/skills_check.clj` verifies that call-position `(rf/<var>` names exist plus three retired-keyword families; it cannot check arity, option maps, requires, macro expansion, or composition. `scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py:140-147` explicitly says its rules are retrospective token patterns and a green run is not evidence a leaf agrees with its source.
5. History shows this gap is active under pre-alpha API churn. Representative follow-ups include six wrong-arity `reg-*` examples (`7075f1d079`), a deleted `dispatch-to-system` recipe (`b73f3b5949`), the retired Managed HTTP reply contract (`d78fabd19d`), and a fail-open CSRF recipe (`887fd87d67`). These all needed later correction despite the structural gates.
6. The eval corpus does not validate the handoff posture. `evals/` contains eleven rich JSON scenarios but no runner output or `benchmark.json`; `spec/design.md:135` calls it not yet load-bearing and `evals/README.md:16,89-110` describes a future/tool-agnostic manual runner. No eval requires the agent to compile or test an authored change, while the Q14 drift guard rejects the capability by construction.
7. Routing and progressive disclosure are broadly sound and should be preserved: the central skill matrix distinguishes setup/migration/pairing, `SKILL.md` is a 166-line router, and depth is one leaf away. Token economy argues against adding a verification module: the router is already about 1,700 words and `testing.md` is 379 lines/about 3,700 words. The useful move is to delete handoff ceremony and add one short execution rule.

## Recommended Action

Explicitly unlock L3/Q14 for safe project-local verification. Remove the author-runs-the-gate wording from `spec/design.md`, `spec/authoring-prompt.md`, `SKILL.md`, `references/cross-cutting/testing.md`, and the verification-posture row in `skills/README.md`. Retire only the Q14/verification-posture classifier and self-test cases from `scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py`; retain its unrelated correctness guards.

Give the skill the smallest routine command surface needed to run gates already declared by the consumer project, aligned with the repository's existing published-skill baseline: focused `clojure` test aliases, declared `npm test` / `npm run test:*` scripts, `npx shadow-cljs` or `shadow-cljs` compile/test targets, and `clj-kondo --lint`. Do not grant a blanket Bash wildcard.

Replace the discover-then-handoff prose with one concise workflow: after an edit, discover the nearest declared noninteractive gate, run it, repair a relevant failure, and report the exact command and result. Hand off only when the gate is interactive/visual, requires a live runtime owned by Pair, is unavailable, or the user asked not to run it. Add one focused existing-project eval/fixture whose transcript proves the agent edits and invokes the declared gate; do not build a general eval platform as part of this task.

## Evidence

- Contradictory goal/posture: `skills/re-frame2/spec/design.md:9,13,30-32`; `skills/re-frame2/SKILL.md:29-32,153`; `skills/README.md:195-201`.
- Existing gate discovery that ends in a relay: `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing.md:3,355-374`.
- Trust-the-invoker command policy: `skills/README.md:261-281`.
- Limits of structural coverage: `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/skills_check.clj:4-16,41-80`; `scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py:140-147`.
- Non-load-bearing evals: `skills/re-frame2/spec/design.md:133-135`; `skills/re-frame2/evals/README.md:89-128`; the directory contains only `README.md` and `evals.json`.
- Token census at current main: `SKILL.md` 166 lines/1,713 words; `testing.md` 379 lines/3,704 words; many task leaves are already 1,800-3,500 words. A new verification leaf would tax every routed task without improving the binding.
- Decision history: commit `d96a6026d0` (`rf2-tnikip`, historical tracker id) removed an already-existing narrow Bash allow-list and "Verify what you changed" section solely to reconcile the skill to Q14, then added CI that makes reintroducing agent-run verification fail. This task consciously reverses that decision rather than layering an exception around it.
- Duplicate search: all-status bead title/description/notes searches for `Q14`, `verification posture`, `authoring-only`, `allowed-tools`, `run tests`, `eval runner`, `eval harness`, `recipe correctness`, and `re-frame2 skill` found no current owner for this outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A tool-capable `re-frame2` authoring session on an existing project may run narrowly scoped, project-declared, noninteractive compile/test/lint commands; no published or normative text tells it to delegate such a runnable gate to the programmer by default.
2. L3/Q14, `skills/README.md`'s verification table, frontmatter `allowed-tools`, the done checklist, the testing leaf, and `check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py` agree on the new posture. The drift script retains its non-Q14 rules and self-tests.
3. A focused checked-in eval/fixture gives the agent an existing project plus an authoring change. The captured tool transcript shows it discovers the gate from project files, invokes that exact gate, and reports the real exit/result. A controlled wrong API shape makes the fixture gate red, proving the signal is non-vacuous.
4. The routing evals for greenfield setup and v1 migration still hand off, and the Story authoring/run-boundary eval still forbids `run-variant` / `read-failures` here. Safe compile/test permission does not absorb `re-frame2-pair` or live-runtime work.
5. No `references/verify.md`, generic verification framework, policy essay, compatibility mode, or blanket `Bash(*)` is added. Across `SKILL.md` plus `references/cross-cutting/testing.md`, the new instruction is no longer than the handoff/discovery ceremony it replaces; target a net prose reduction.
6. The PR reports the focused eval result and the existing skill drift, eval-doc, packaging, link, and API-manifest projection checks relevant to its changed paths.

## Non-goals

- No framework, registrar, macro, test-support, Story MCP, or Pair MCP API change.
- No new live-runtime driver in the authoring skill and no access to Pair-owned run-side Story tools.
- No automatic dependency installation, daemon/watch-server launch, browser interaction, visual sign-off, network mutation, or destructive shell permission.
- No general runner for all eleven skill evals; one repeatable behavioural witness is enough for this outcome.

title: surface-review(story): make :setup/:script the one variant vocabulary end to end
description:
## Scope

Converge Story's variant/fragment data contract on the already-documented public vocabulary, `:setup` + `:script` (retaining `:plays` for named multi-play), across `tools/story/**` and the directly coupled Story-MCP read/write boundary. Migrate the remaining registry, plan, identity, canvas/workspace, runner, recorder/save-variant, test-mode/watch/CI, docs, testbeds, and MCP consumers that still depend on transitional body keys.

## Verified Findings

1. Story teaches one language but stores another. `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md` calls this a clean pre-alpha rename; `schemas.cljc` still accepts both pairs, and `registrar/reg-variant*` rewrites authored `:setup` -> `:events` and `:script` -> `:play-script` through `lower-public-vocabulary`.
2. The rewrite is publicly observable. `story/variant->edn` promises the side-table body verbatim, so canonical registration changes keys on read-back. Story-MCP's recorder explicitly documents that canonical `:script` write-back returns as `:play-script`. Humans and agents therefore need two vocabularies and cannot round-trip a body by inspection.
3. The runtime is ready for the cut: `runtime.cljc` executes compiled `[:world :setup]` and `[:world :scripts]`, while `plan.cljc` owns normalized semantics. Remaining direct legacy reads are concrete in `identity.cljc`, `play.cljc`, `play/ci_runner.cljc`, `play/runner_events.cljc`, `ui/state/tests.cljc`, `ui/test_mode/pure.cljc`, and `ui/sidebar_signals.cljc`.
4. Drift is broad: measured text hits include 165 `:play-script` references in `tools/story/src`, 277 in tests, 81 in specs, and 42 in `tools/story-mcp` (some are prose/test names, but the production readers above are direct). The template, current testbeds, tutorials, recorder snippets, and promotion output already author the target keys.
5. History shows unfinished convergence, not a new feature. Commit `a9e3f07523` (finish public `:script` rename) completed author-facing emission/docs but not storage/readers. The current spec says to remove lowering once remaining readers consume the plan.
6. No new API is needed: `re-frame.story` already has 88 `defn`/`defmacro` entries inventoried in `spec/api-manifest.edn`. This outcome should shrink a data contract.

## Recommended Action

- Store `:setup` and `:script` verbatim in registered variant/fragment bodies; keep `:plays` as named multi-play.
- Remove `:events`/`:play-script` from authoring schemas, xor/precedence branches, and `lower-public-vocabulary`.
- Route consumers through the compiled plan where they need resolved semantics; raw-author-data readers use canonical keys only.
- Make Story-MCP registration, record/write-back, discovery, and read-back accept and emit those same keys.
- Migrate Story-owned fixtures, tests, specs, API/tutorial prose in the same change. Use the pre-alpha posture: delete aliases outright, with no warnings, shim, or deprecation ceremony.
- Do not mechanically rename unrelated `:events` collections such as recorder capture state or trace channels.

## Evidence

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/registrar.cljc` `reg-variant*` validates canonical input, lowers it, then stores legacy keys.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/schemas.cljc` `Variant` and `lower-public-vocabulary` contain dual schemas and the rewrite.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc` `variant->edn` is a verbatim side-table read.
- `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md` names the clean rename, plan-routed runtime, remaining readers, and removal condition.
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/recorder.cljc` documents canonical write / legacy read-back.
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_shared/stories.cljs` and Story testbeds already use the target form.
- Commit `a9e3f07523` landed the author-facing half only.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `reg-variant` and `reg-fragment` accept `:setup`, `:script`, and `:plays`; authoring-body `:events` or `:play-script` fail shape validation. `:plays` remains mutually exclusive with single `:script`.
2. `handler-meta`, `variant->edn`, Story-MCP `get-variant`, `register-variant`, and `record-as-variant` preserve canonical key names through write/read round trips, apart from documented source/origin/provenance stamps.
3. A canonical-only fixture exercises frame setup, canvas/workspace rendering, auto-play, step debugger, watch/test discovery, snapshot identity, recorder write-back, save/promote, static build, and the browser CI runner.
4. Plan/hash/snapshot behavior remains deterministic for migrated fixtures, and named multi-play remains covered.
5. Public docs, API tables, examples, MCP descriptors/instructions, and production source no longer describe or inspect transitional variant `:play-script`/`:events` slots. Retained `events` wording denotes a real collection/channel.
6. Focused JVM, CLJS/browser Story, Story-MCP, feature-load/play-runner, descriptor-generation, and API-manifest gates pass. Tests include a red witness for each removed key and a canonical register -> read-back identity witness.
7. No facade symbol or manifest row is added unless proven unavoidable and explicitly classified.

## Non-goals

- No new DSL, convenience macro, migration mode, warning framework, compatibility alias, or versioned schema.
- Do not remove or redesign named `:plays`.
- Do not rename generic recorder `:events` state, trace channels, or historical command/job names merely because their English name contains play script.
- No shell/chrome redesign or new MCP capability.
- No retrospective pruning of the Story facade; that is separate API-freeze work.

## Related beads

- `rf2-1s53x` (closed): CI play-runner prose correction; no ownership of body-key convergence.
- `rf2-2hpxo` (deferred): retrospective facade classification; distinct because this task should add no export.

title: [LANE GRANTED - in flight] False finite-diff preservation: a capped before-side hides the counted after-tail
description:
Merged-PR audit #10102 (bbb665a34a6a6f8ab7835b2a6bb57692668a8aa2), source rf2-brmyq. The new counted? split can cap only one side; the claim that bounding both sides at the same ceiling preserves every finite diff is false for an ordinary lazy before-value and a counted vector after-value.

Reproduction using the merged sequential-diff-children with the REAL merged engine projection: before = (map identity (range 1050)); after = (assoc (vec (range 1050)) 1049 :changed-at-tail); projection = (engine/project before after); walk kind :vector. The pre-PR helper emits 1050 rows including [1049 :changed-at-tail 1049]. The merged helper emits only 1001 rows, ending [1000 1000 1000], while diff-pair-count's max bounded-count remains 1050 because after is counted. The changed after-tail silently disappears.

At views/edn_inspector.cljs:1500-1501, bounded-vec caps before to 1001 but retains all 1050 after values. survivor-bis:1521 is now shorter than survivor-ais, zipmap:1523 discards the unmatched after survivors, and before-order:1538 can only visit capped before indices. added-rows does not recover those ordinary/modified survivors. This is the projection-PRESENT path introduced by this PR, distinct from rf2-jh12f's existing children-of-pair fallback cap. Its new alignment test uses two vectors, so both are counted and neither exercises the changed bound.

Required correction: preserve accessible counted after-side data when the before side is bounded, representing any unknown/truncated before tail honestly rather than dropping after rows or inventing precise prior values. Keep lazy work bounded and preserve removal alignment. Add the mixed-representation tail-change regression alongside the two-vector removal and guarded-input controls. A small correction to this walk/boundary is sufficient; no new framework.

Evidence: exact merged helper plus exact .cljc engine/pinned editscript 0.6.5, source-isolated JVM probe ai/gate-inspector-boundary-audit-sep20-monitor-1.log and .exit, exit 0. Same run confirms the original guarded fallback now returns 1001 rows with 1001 realised elements, pre-PR fallback hits guard 1500, and 1050-element counted-vector removal alignment still passes. Correct worktree and SHA printed; no mounted browser claim. No exact OPEN Bead records this mixed-side projection regression.

GREEN after the fix: `COMPILE_EXIT=0 RUN_EXIT=0`, 12355 / 61933, 0 failures 0 errors. Re-run after

+8 / +27 being the trunk's own machine_after_rings landings arriving with the rebase. Delta over my
own baseline at the merge base (12352 / 61912) PREDICTED FROM THE DIFF before any log was opened as
+3 tests / +21 assertions; actual +3 / +21, EXACT. Under this tree's quiet reporter a namespace grep
of a green log cannot establish that the branch was compiled; the exact count delta can.

## THE MECHANISM

`bounded-vec` (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs:876` at trunk
`a924d3d9b0`) dispatches on `counted?`, so the two sides of `sequential-diff-children` have
INDEPENDENT ceilings. For a lazy before-value against a vector after-value, `a-vec` is realised
whole at 1050 and `b-vec` caps at 1001 (`:1519-1520`). `bi->ai` is a `zipmap` (`:1542`), which
truncates to the shorter side; `before-order` (`:1549`) walks `(range (count b-vec))` (`:1557`). So
after-indices past the before bound are visited by NO ARM of the walk, and `added-rows` (`:1560`)
does not recover them because they are modified survivors, not additions. `diff-pair-count`
(`:1564`) meanwhile reports 1050, because the after side is counted.

This is an ordinary shape rather than an exotic one: `map`, `filter`, `concat`, `for` and `rest` all
return something that is not `counted?`.

## THE FIX IS APPEND-ONLY, WHICH IS WHAT KEEPS rf2-vu42n INTACT

`zipmap` truncating to the shorter side means the pairs it DOES make are the unbounded ones, so the
zip is never widened, re-based or re-ordered. The surplus after-side survivors it could not reach
are appended in after-order carrying a new `::unrealised` before slot. Where neither side is capped,
`paired-ais` covers every survivor and the new tail run is exactly the `added-rows` it replaces —
element for element, in the same order.

## THE THIRD STATE, AND WHY `::missing` WOULD HAVE BEEN WORSE THAN THE DROP

`::missing` is the STRUCTURAL sentinel: `leaf-diff-op` reads it as a definitional addition and it
OVERRIDES the projection (rf2-8pfkk), so a surviving element would be painted green as newly added —
a confident lie in place of a silent loss. `::unrealised` (`unrealised-sentinel`, public beside
`missing-sentinel`) is deliberately NOT structural, so the op falls through to the projection, which
was computed over the FULL inputs and classifies the element correctly.

PINNED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is what makes it evidence: an `::unrealised` before slot renders
`data-rf-diff-op "modified"` and NO `"added"` node; `::missing` in the SAME slot, against the SAME
projection, renders `"added"` and suppresses `"modified"` entirely. Without that second half the
first could have been green merely because nothing renders an added marker on that path. The
`left-arrow was <prior>` chip renders the sentinel as an explicit unknown rather than leaking
`:day8...edn-inspector/unrealised` into the output — rf2-8pfkk's defect through a new door — and the
test asserts the leak is absent AND the unknown chip present.

1. `count-bound`'s docstring, "agree on every shape": **NARROWED**. A diff has TWO collections and
   the `counted?` dispatch gives them independent ceilings. Over the bound the header is a FLOOR
   rather than a promise — the body may EXCEED it by the removals struck inside the bound, which no
   count that refuses to realise the tail can know. Under the bound, and for any single collection,
   the two still agree exactly. It never falls SHORT, which is the direction that loses data.
2. `sequential-diff-children`'s docstring, "whose size is the same number diff-pair-count printed":
   **NARROWED** the same way, and it now names the `::unrealised` slot.
3. The reconstruction comment, "Bounding BOTH sides at the SAME ceiling": **MADE TRUE**. Its premise
   held while `bounded-vec` was an unconditional `(take count-bound ...)`; rf2-jh12f's `counted?`
   split falsified it silently, leaving a correct warning about a LIVE condition written as though
   it were impossible. It now states what actually keeps the zip exact, and why the repair is
   append-only.

## WHY THE EXISTING TESTS COULD NOT SEE THIS

rf2-brmyq's alignment test uses TWO VECTORS, so both sides are `counted?`, both ceilings coincide,
and the changed bound is never exercised. The new tests use the mixed representation. Two
properties, because either alone is green against a plausible wrong fix: P1 no silent loss (the tail
element present with its REAL value — a row count alone would accept 1050 placeholders); P2 still
bounded and still aligned (a REALISATION counter over a guarded ENDLESS before-side, and rf2-vu42n's
in-place strike over two vectors). Widening the before bound is green on P1 and red on P2's first
half; sliding `bi->ai` is green on P1 and red on its second.

## children-of-pair HAS THE SAME EXPOSURE AND THE OTHER FAILURE MODE — NAMED, NOT FIXED

Asked as a standing question and answered either way. `children-of-pair`'s sequential arm bounds
both sides through `bounded-vec` at `:1404-1405` (trunk) and has the SAME independent-ceiling
exposure. It does NOT drop rows: it walks `(range (max (count a-vec) (count b-vec)))`, so all 1050
are emitted. But for every index past the before bound it fills the before slot with `::missing`,
which is the OTHER failure mode — a survivor mislabelled `:added` rather than dropped. Read from
source, not executed. Deliberately NOT fixed here: different lines from the ones this item edits,
and rf2-bmed1 may own it.

## CENSUS — THREE PASSES, TWO TOKEN AXES, CONTROLS BOTH WAYS

Fixed strings throughout, never a word-boundary assertion: every target here ends in punctuation
(`counted?`, `bounded-vec`), where `\b` after a non-word character can never match. Occurrences and

title: clj-kondo --fail-level error exits 0 on an unresolved symbol: the lint is blind to exactly the fault a deletion produces
description:
Measured 2026-09-18 by rf2-y8doi.21's worker (PR #9953) while proving its gates read its own worktree, and
independently corroborated by a sibling the same hour.

## The defect

**`clj-kondo --fail-level error` EXITS 0 ON AN UNRESOLVED SYMBOL in this tree, because unresolved symbols
are classified as WARNINGS here rather than errors.** The planted fault left the runner at **exit 0**; the
only discrimination available was the finding LINE in the output and the warning COUNT moving **139 → 140**.

The sibling half of the measurement, which is what makes this a flag effect rather than a tool defect:
rf2-y8doi.20's worker ran clj-kondo WITHOUT that flag and reported *"control confirmed kondo exits 2 on a
planted unresolved symbol"*. **So the two readings are not in conflict — the default fail level takes
warnings and reddens; `--fail-level error` suppresses exactly the class that matters.**

## Why it is dangerous rather than merely surprising

**It fails OPEN, and it fails open on precisely the fault that DELETIONS produce.** A reference left behind
pointing at something that was removed IS an unresolved symbol. This project deletes constantly — rf2-jd0bp
deleted a lint, rf2-y8doi.29 is deleting roughly 420 lines across thirteen files as this is filed — and a
worker whose brief says "run clj-kondo" reaches for the strictest-sounding flag, gets exit 0, and reports a
green that could not have failed on the thing most likely to be wrong.

**And it is a GATE-NOMINATION defect, not just an instrument one**, which is why it belongs in the tree
rather than only in a memory: every dispatch brief that nominates clj-kondo for a deletion is nominating a
gate that cannot see the deletion's characteristic failure.

Related and already recorded: rf2-y8doi.30's worker found that **a raw `"` inside a docstring is likewise
not caught by clj-kondo** — the file still parses and it dies at macroexpansion minutes into a lane run.
Same shape, different fault class: the lint's green is narrower than its reputation.

## Required correction

Add it to CLAUDE.md's instrument-defect catalogue, § "Ways the INSTRUMENTS misreport", as a new lettered
item in the existing style: the observable, the measurement both ways, the direction it fails in, and the
guard. **It fails OPEN**, which is the property that earns it a place.

**The guard has two acceptable forms** and the entry should give both: run clj-kondo WITHOUT
`--fail-level error` so warnings redden, or read the warning COUNT and the finding lines rather than the
exit code — and in either case state in the report which was done and what the before/after counts were.
**A bare "clj-kondo exit 0" is not evidence that nothing dangles.**

Say also, because it is the reusable half: for a deletion the stronger instrument is a census of the deleted
names across the tree reading 0 **with the control taken FROM the target**, which is what rf2-jd0bp did
(deleted tokens 0, live sibling `orphaned-owner-lint` 4).

## Scope and sequencing

- Fence: `CLAUDE.md`, the instrument-defect bullet only. **No new gate, no script, no wrapper, and do NOT
  change any gate's flags** — this is a documentation correction about how to read a tool.
- **`CLAUDE.md` is heavily contended**: four beads edited it on 2026-09-17 (`rf2-d3l8g`, `rf2-oitjw`,
  `rf2-1hh87`, all merged) and **`rf2-48awk` is OPEN against item (s) in the same bullet — sequence against
  it; two workers must never hold one file.**
- `CLAUDE.md` is `i/lf w/crlf`: never `sed -i` (item (u)); build replacement text with the Write tool rather
  than a heredoc (item (o)); take the three line-ending numbers with Python on bytes.
- The gate for repo-root markdown is `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci`, **NOT** `check_doc_slugs.py`,
  whose roots exclude repo-root markdown and which two workers have separately DEMONSTRATED exits 0 on a
  planted broken link there.

**Re-measure both invocations yourself before writing it up** — with and without the flag, on a planted
unresolved symbol, quoting the exit code and the warning count each time. The catalogue's whole value is
that its entries are measured, and this project has already found one catalogued entry (item (s)) to be
intermittent when re-tested.
notes:
## THIRD INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION (mayor, 2026-09-18) — measured on a third file by a third worker

rf2-m0ve6's worker (PR #9957) reproduced the defect exactly, unprompted beyond the warning in its brief,
while proving its own gates read its worktree:

    planted unresolved symbol at resources_helpers.cljc:1916
      plain clj-kondo                  -> exit 2,  warnings 1
      SAME fault, --fail-level error   -> exit 0

**That is now three independent measurements on three different files** — rf2-y8doi.21 (its own fence,
warning count 139 → 140), rf2-y8doi.20 (which additionally used it to prove the tools/xray JVM artefact
does NOT cover a `.cljs` diff: the planted symbol left that JVM run at exit 0 with byte-identical counts
while clj-kondo went to exit 2), and now rf2-m0ve6.

**Independent reproduction is not a formality for this bullet specifically.** An existing entry in the very
same catalogue section — item (s) — turned out to be INTERMITTENT when re-tested, which is what rf2-48awk
is open to correct. So when you write this entry up, the three-file reproduction IS part of the evidence
and should be stated: it is what distinguishes this from a one-machine one-file oddity.

**Also worth writing into the entry, because it is the practical half:** rf2-y8doi.20 used the plain form's
exit 2 as a POSITIVE control to establish that a different gate was blind — the JVM artefact. So the plain
form is not merely "the one that works"; it is a usable discriminator for what a `.cljs` diff is and is not
graded by. That is a better reason to prefer it than "the flag is wrong".

Re-measure yourself before writing, as your bead already instructs. Three prior measurements make the
observable very likely; they do not excuse a fourth.

title: Narrow label on a broad exclusive: 'shadow-cljs / browser lane' reads as browser-only, but the NODE lane is the same resource
description:
Found 2026-09-17 by a dispatched worker (rf2-y8doi.18) that refused to act on a contradictory brief and
asked instead. Verified at source by the mayor before this bead was filed.

## The defect

CLAUDE.md § Workflow names the exclusive as **"The shadow-cljs / browser lane"**. That slash reads as an
apposition — *the shadow-cljs lane, i.e. the browser lane* — so the label names a NARROWER resource than
the one the rule actually governs. Every consequence follows from the label rather than from the rule's
body, which is itself correct.

**The exclusive covers ANY shadow-cljs build, and the NODE lane is one.** Measured:

  * `implementation/package.json:27` — `"test:cljs": "node scripts/compile-node-test.cjs node-test
    out/node-test.js && node out/node-test.js"`.
  * `implementation/scripts/compile-node-test.cjs` runs shadow-cljs's own `runner.js` under
    `process.execPath` from IMPL_DIR (comments at 143-144 say so), and other comments in the same file
    discuss reading the shadow-cljs cache directory before and after compiling.
  * Swept over the whole `scripts` block: **17 npm scripts are shadow-cljs builds** — `test:cljs`,
    `test:cljs-isolation`, `test:security`, `test:testbed-support`, `test:xray-manual-epoch`,
    `test:cljs-perf-emit-nightly`, `test:elision`, `test:perf-bundle`, `test:schemas-bundle`,
    `test:bundle-isolation`, `test:reagent-slim:bundle-isolation`, `test:tools-machines-viz`,
    `build:machines-viz-viewer`, `build:fresco-release`, `test:browser`,
    `test:browser-schemas-boundary-prod`, `test:browser-prod-elision`.

So "run the node lane" and "do not start a shadow-cljs build" are the SAME instruction pointing both
ways, and a brief containing both cannot be satisfied.

## The cost, observed rather than hypothesised

The mayor issued exactly that contradiction in a dispatch brief: `npm run test:cljs` nominated as the
worker's gate in one paragraph, "do not start any shadow-cljs build" in the next, because the lane had
been granted exclusively to a different worker the same tick. The worker measured the collision, did NOT
start the build, and asked for a queue position — correctly, since CLAUDE.md's own protocol says an
announcement is not an acquisition.

**The near-miss is the point.** Had that worker followed the nominated gate rather than the prohibition,
two shadow-cljs builds would have run concurrently, and the documented failure mode is SILENT: no error,
no exit file, no output, just two builds that never finish, presenting to each worker as a hang on its
own gate and to the coordinator as two unrelated infrastructure reports with nothing connecting them.

It is also not a one-off phrasing slip: the mayor repeated the "shadow-cljs / browser lane" framing
across several briefs this session, and told at least two workers that CI grades the node lane so the
lane "was never required" — true as far as it goes, and reached through a model in which node and
browser were separate resources.

## Required correction

Rename the resource in the bullet's opening so the label carries the scope: it is the **shadow-cljs
build lane**, and it covers every shadow-cljs invocation — node, browser, release, bundle-isolation and
the build:* scripts alike — not the browser lane alone. Keep the whole body of that bullet unchanged:
the wedge description, FIRST ACQUIRER HOLDS, never granting on a release message alone, granting
explicitly to ONE with a queue, the yielding worker killing rather than finishing a started run,
verifying by effect, and the closing generalisation that a rule phrased as "announce X" says what to SAY
and not what to CHECK. None of that is wrong; only the label is.

Worth adding, because it is what makes the scope checkable rather than memorable: say that the roster of
shadow-cljs entry points is `implementation/package.json`'s scripts block, and that a reader should ASK
it (grep the block for `shadow-cljs` and for `compile-node-test.cjs`) rather than trusting a list in
prose — a list here goes stale exactly the way this file's other enumerations do, and the indirection
through `compile-node-test.cjs` means a grep for `shadow-cljs` ALONE under-reports by six scripts.

Acceptance: a reader nominating a gate for a dispatch can tell, from this file, whether that gate takes
the exclusive. Verify by re-running the sweep above rather than against this bead's report of it.

## Scope and sequencing

- Fence: `CLAUDE.md`, the § Workflow shadow-cljs exclusive bullet only.
- SEQUENCE BEHIND rf2-oitjw, which is itself sequenced behind the now-merged rf2-d3l8g. Three beads
  edit `CLAUDE.md` and two workers must never hold one file.
- No new gate, no script, no CI lane. This is a wording fix.
- `CLAUDE.md` is `i/lf w/crlf`: never `sed -i` (item (u)), build replacement text with the Write tool
  rather than a heredoc (item (o)), take the three line-ending numbers with Python on bytes since a bare
  `grep -c $'\r'` reads 0 on this exact file (item (s)).
- The gate for repo-root markdown is `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci`, NOT `check_doc_slugs.py`.

## The shape it belongs to

This is the THIRD breadth defect found in `CLAUDE.md` in one day, after rf2-d3l8g (late-bind graded by
the node lane ALONE) and rf2-oitjw (`bd` rewrites the export in EVERY checkout). The first two state a
narrow truth as a universal; **this one runs the other way, labelling a broad resource with a narrow
name.** Both directions produce the same failure — a reader acts on the label instead of the body — so
the family is "the summary sentence and the evidence under it do not have the same scope", and it is
worth a sweep of this file's other opening sentences rather than three isolated repairs.

title: CLAUDE.md: report-changed-surfaces.sh takes paths, not revisions — handed revisions it reports every surface false
description:
`.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` TAKES PATHS, NOT REVISIONS, and handed revisions it reports
EVERY SURFACE FALSE at exit 0 -- indistinguishable from a genuinely unaffected change.

MEASURED 2026-09-17 by the rf2-s2ecl worker and re-verified at source by the mayor. The script's own usage
line is:

    .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh [--all] [path ...]

and its argument loop puts every non-`--all` argument into `explicit_paths`. So the natural invocation
`... origin/main HEAD` classifies the two LITERAL STRINGS "origin/main" and "HEAD" as file paths. Neither
matches any surface pattern, so every surface reports false, exit 0, nothing on stderr. The worker
measured it reading all-false even on a range that DOES touch story code; only a control caught it.
Invoked correctly with paths, `assertion_strip.cljs` arms six surfaces and a `tools/story/spec/*.md` path
arms none.

## WHY THIS WANTS A HOME IN CLAUDE.md

The CLASS is already recorded, so this is a CONCRETION and not a discovery.
`docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md` states it generically, in the "any instrument that can
say nothing here" block: *"a surface classifier handed revisions where it expects file paths reported
every surface as unaffected, which is exactly what a genuinely unaffected change looks like."* That page
is the reusable, OS-neutral method and correctly names NO script -- exactly the division of labour
CLAUDE.md items (b), (p) and (q) have with loops.md, where the method states the class and CLAUDE.md
names this repo's concrete instrument.

**The generic statement did not prevent it.** The worker was carrying that very paragraph in its dispatch
preamble and still invoked the script with revisions, because nothing connected the abstract "a surface
classifier" to the concrete script sitting in this tree. That is the evidence that the concretion is
worth its space rather than a restatement.

IT FAILS IN THE REASSURING DIRECTION for the only question the script is ever asked -- *which gates does
my diff arm?* -- and answers "none", which invites a worker to run nothing and report a clean spine.

## THE WORK

Add a lettered item to CLAUDE.md's "Ways the INSTRUMENTS misreport on this machine" list, in the house
style of the existing items: the observable, the mechanism, the measurement in both directions, and the
guard. **The guard is: hand it PATHS, and take a control** -- run it once against a path you know arms a
surface, so an all-false reading means "unaffected" rather than "misused".

Note the list's own opening warning: THE LETTERS ARE LABELS, NOT A CENSUS. Do not add a count anywhere,
and do not "fix" the opening sentence to name a new total.

**Do NOT edit `dispatch-prompt-template.md`** -- it is right as written and is deliberately script-free,
exactly as items (b), (p), (q) and (r) leave `loops.md` alone.

Consider also whether the script itself should REFUSE an argument that looks like a revision rather than
silently classifying it as a path -- but that is a second question, and CLAUDE.md § the stance says an
item may die with its reasoning recorded rather than growing. If the refusal is more than a few lines,
record the reasoning and leave it.

## SURFACE AND GATES

`CLAUDE.md` only, unless you take the optional script change, which is
`.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` -- **a HOT-ZONE file paired with its mirror
`implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs`**, one-toucher by construction. If you touch the
script you must move the mirror in the SAME commit; if that looks like more than a small change, don't.

`CLAUDE.md` is repo-root markdown, so **`check_doc_slugs.py` does NOT cover it** -- its roots exclude
repo-root markdown. The gate is `python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci`.

**CRLF, and CLAUDE.md is the file this project's own item (e) warns about:** after editing, take THREE
numbers with Python reading bytes -- total CR, total CRLF, and bare LF -- and require CR == CRLF AND
bare LF == 0. A bare `grep -c` reads 0 on this file and makes the check pass vacuously (item (s)).
Never `sed -i` (item (u)). At the time of filing the file reads cr=161 crlf=161 bare_lf=0.

description:

Same defect class, two more call sites: they call the PURE plan compiler without `:run-args`, so global-args and the parent story's `:args` are absent, while the run path (`runtime/prepare-context`, which passes `(rf.story.args/run-arg-layers variant-id opts)`) resolves them.

REPRO (JVM, reproduced on the rf2-noxox branch rebased onto trunk a34c318c8d; these two sites are untouched by that branch):

    (reg-story*   :story.sib {:args {:heading "Sign in"}})
    (reg-variant* :story.sib/uses-arg {:setup [[:dispatch [:sib/set [:arg :heading]]]]})
    (reg-variant* :story.sib/plain {})

- `(story/resolve-args :story.sib/uses-arg)` returns `{:heading "Sign in"}` — the run resolves the placeholder.
- SITE 1, View-State panel: `(re-frame.story.ui.view-state/compile-model :story.sib/uses-arg [])` returns `:error "re-frame2-story: [:arg :heading] references an arg that is not declared on the variant or its parents [:rf.error/story-missing-arg]"` — the panel shows an error for a variant that runs fine. Both of its compiles (`variant-plan` and `explain`) are bare.
- SITE 2, render prep: `(re-frame.story.render/prepare-render :story.sib/plain)` returns `:effective-args {}`, and for `:story.sib/uses-arg` it THROWS the same missing-arg error. `prepare-render` backs `story/render-variant` and computes the render `:plan-hash` from that plan; its `compile-opts` select-keys omit `:run-args`.

SITES: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/view_state.cljc `compile-model`; tools/story/src/re_frame/story/render.cljc `prepare-render`.

FIX SHAPE (the one rf2-noxox used): for a keyword target, pass `{:run-args (rf.story.args/run-arg-layers variant-id)}` at the CALL SITE; keep the pure compiler explicit; do not build a second resolver. - render: 017 §Args, controls, and render-variant says render-variant keeps its own post-compile path (control overrides layered on the plan-time effective args). Folding the ambient layers into the plan keeps that shape — the control layer still sits on top — but check the spec paragraph before editing.

title: Xray palette: recent-event selection must update the shared frame-qualified focus
description:
Route command-palette recent-event selection through the existing frame-qualified spine focus event. The current entry loses the dispatch identity and writes a stale app-db slot, so choosing an older event opens the Epoch tab while it continues displaying the currently focused event.

Ownership: tools/xray/**, slice tools_xray. Reviewed revision 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). Parent review rf2-gwye. This is an independent P2 correctness defect, distinct from the LIVE-pause defect already owned by rf2-fzbj.2.

Evidence and producer/consumer chain:
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/palette/sources.cljc:100-145 builds recent-event items from dispatched trace rows. At 129-142 it chooses the event vector as ev-id and emits [:palette/select-event ev-id]. The item retains a trace id, but the action carries neither :rf.trace/dispatch-id nor the owning frame. Two occurrences of the same event vector generate identical actions even though the rendered items are separate.
- palette/events.cljs:365-373 handles that action by writing :selected-tab :epoch and :selected-event-id. It does not alter :focus or dispatch a spine event.
- panels/epoch_panel.cljs:198-209 registers :rf.xray/epoch-pipeline with inputs :rf.xray/focus and :rf.xray/epoch-history; it resolves the record by focus :epoch-id. It does not read :selected-event-id. The display renderer consumes that composite.
- spine.cljs:1040-1047 composes the public focus from the actual focus slot, event bundles and epoch history. Its :rf.xray/focus-event handler at 1059-1073 already reseeds the selected frame's epoch history and resolves the dispatch into an epoch atomically.
- tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md:1117 explicitly includes palette jump among the callers of :rf.xray/focus-event. The separate selected-event slot contradicts the shared focus contract.
- palette/events_cljs_test.cljs:154-172 tests tab and stale-slot writes only; it never checks the selected Epoch record. Thus the test accepts the incorrect routing.

Reproducer:
1. Open Xray and dispatch the same event twice, for example [:counter/inc], yielding dispatch 1 / epoch 101 and dispatch 2 / epoch 102.
2. Leave focus on the latest event, then open Cmd/Ctrl+K and invoke the older recent-event result.
Expected: the spine and Epoch panel select dispatch 1 / epoch 101, using that event's frame.
Actual: the palette closes and selects the Epoch tab, but focus remains dispatch 2 / epoch 102. Repeated event values also cannot be distinguished by the action. Choosing an event belonging to another frame cannot select its frame through this path.

Validation performed:
Babashka loaded the unchanged source namespace palette.sources and read/evaluated the original :palette/select-event branch expression directly from palette/events.cljs, with synthetic bindings for its already-computed close-db/args/base-fx. It also loaded original spine defn forms and the actual common-helpers dependency. Two dispatched rows with identical event vectors and different trace/dispatch ids produced identical action tuples. Applying the older item's original branch retained the prior :focus, and the original compose-focus still resolved epoch 102. This is an exact source-expression witness, not a rewritten implementation, but it does not claim the full registered CLJS event or browser was executed. Probe exit 0 asserted the counterexample. Evidence: ai/surface-review-20260913/tools_xray/probe-tools-xray-1.{clj,log,exit}.

Suggested repair:
Carry the event's dispatch id and owning frame in the recent item's action. Resolve both from the real trace/event-bundle producer shape, not the event vector or the trace-record id. Lower selection into :rf.xray/focus-event with that identity, plus the existing Epoch tab selection. Reuse the spine's frame/history reseeding and head/RETRO behavior; remove the stale selected-event write and fix its misleading comment. Keep all Dynamic panels on the existing single focus axis. Respect the current view/filter scope while choosing the source representation; no second selection store is needed.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end event/sub regression selects the older of two identical event vectors and checks both focused dispatch and the actual epoch-pipeline record id.
- Two frames with overlapping dispatch ids select the intended frame and its Epoch record.
- Head selection retains existing head-aware semantics; an evicted item must not silently show an unrelated event as the selected result.
- Palette closes normally; tab selection and existing popup/keyboard behavior remain intact.
- Existing source-shape tests assert frame/dispatch identity, and invocation tests replace stale-slot assertions with actual focus/record assertions. A browser witness through the real Cmd/Ctrl+K invocation path is appropriate in the existing centralized harness.

Deduplication/dispositions: current tracker searches for palette titles/descriptions, selected-event-id, recent-event, palette/select-event and matching notes found no dedicated open issue for this defect. Historical rf2-qy0nu is cited by the tests but bd has no current record for that id; its comment is not a current disposition. rf2-elrh remains explicitly closed and B.9 copy restrictions are untouched. No source edits, builds, installs, servers, commits or pushes were performed by this worker.

title: surface-review(impl_build_support): preserve nested JVM test discovery directories
description:
Recommendation: repair the JVM quiet runner's discovery-path check so a valid nested `-d` directory retains Cognitect's normal behavior. This review confirms ONE P2 defect: the runner treats the discovery directory as the classpath root and rejects correctly named, loadable tests before execution. Keep this bead OPEN for remediation. No production changes were made.

SLICE, REVISION, AND OWNERSHIP
Slice: impl_build_support. Parent: rf2-fzbj.
Reviewed revision: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f (verified HEAD).
