survived to be filed. The `:done` snapshot and the `:before :idle` / `:after
:done` assertions PASSED in that same run, confirming the fold was already
correct and only the record was lossy. The parallel misattribution was measured
directly: the top-level (non-microstep) region set read `#{:right :left}` where
only `:left` handled `:go`.

RE-DERIVED LINE NUMBERS (all had drifted, as the brief warned):
- `transition.cljc` raise-dequeue arm: item said ~4060-4138, actually 4097-4144.
  Line 4144 was the defect: `recur ... cascade` unchanged.
- `transition.cljc` `:always` branch (the shape to follow): item said ~3988-4039,
  actually 3993-4051 (`:microstep` step built at 4031-4036).
- `parallel.cljc` `drain-parent-queue`: item said ~1320-1370; the fn spans
  1167-1357 and the raise-rebroadcast `:else` arm is 1310-1357. Line 1356 was
  the defect: `(into acc-casc (result/cascade step))` -- flattened, no boundary.
- `registration.cljc` `:cascade` emit: item said ~711-734, actually 711-734
  (this one had NOT drifted); the emit is at 723-734.

SHAPE SHIPPED. One `:kind :raised-transition` step per HANDLED dequeue, FIFO
ordered, in BOTH engines:

  {:kind :raised-transition :region <r-or-nil> :event [:settle]
   :from :working :to :done :steps [...nested...]}

It mirrors the existing `:microstep` step's shape, swapping the microstep index
for the triggering `:event` -- one nested boundary, not a second protocol.
Gated on the nested Result's `::handled?`, so an ignored/guard-blocked raise
fabricates nothing while a handled targetless raise still records its boundary.
The synthetic `[:rf.machine/done <path>]` signal is itself a `[:raise ...]` fx,
so it rides the same step with no done-state and no parallel-only dialect.
`:microsteps` untouched -- still the `:always`-iteration count.

DIVERGENCE FROM THE ITEM'S EXAMPLE SPELLING (deliberate, and the item licenses
it as "a recommendation, not a request for aliases"): `:source :raise` is
OMITTED. Spec 005 documents the cascade's `:source` key as history-only
(`:recorded` / `:default`), "present ONLY on an :entry step"; every step
reaching this arm comes off the same `:raise` queue, so the field would be
constant -- zero information bought at the price of contradicting an existing
contract. `:kind` plus `:event` already carry it.

STATE/EFFECT FOLD UNCHANGED -- established three ways:
1. Structurally: the only changed value flowing into either loop is the cascade
   accumulator. Every other `recur` argument (snapshot, machine, fx, pending
   queue, depth counters, `visited`) is byte-identical. The entire non-comment
   diff of both engine files is two `let` bindings plus two argument renames.
2. By census: all 24 `result/cascade` reader sites across `implementation/` and
   `tools/` either re-stamp via `with-cascade`, feed the trace emit in
   `registration.cljc`, or are tests. None flows into a snapshot or an fx
   vector. Trap avoided: `transition.cljc`'s `commit-snapshot ... cascade`
   reads the transition-GEOMETRY local, a different binding from
   `cascade-steps`.
3. Empirically: the pre-existing suites (which pin snapshot values, `:data`,

title: xray: two more focus consumers discard the pinned dispatch-id — the Issues ribbon reads the whole focus and throws it away, and Views is one discriminator short
description:
Two more focus-resolution consumers still discard the pinned `:dispatch-id`, in the same way `rf2-c4abp`
(PR #10001) just fixed for Trace and the Machine Inspector, and `PR #9954` before it for Epoch.

Handed back by the rf2-c4abp worker, which found them in an audit it was not asked for and **correctly did
not touch them** — both are outside the fence I set.

## VERIFIED AT SOURCE BY THE MAYOR at trunk bc741cb23a, not taken from the report

### Site 1 — `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/registry.cljs` :950-958 (the Issues ribbon)

**This is the same defect shape exactly**, and it is the more clear-cut of the two:

    (rf/reg-sub :rf.xray/issues-ribbon
      {:inputs [[:rf.xray/focus] [:rf.xray/epoch-history]]}
      (fn [[focus epoch-history] _query]
        (let [focus-epoch-id (:epoch-id focus)
              focus-status   (issues-helpers/resolve-focus-status focus-epoch-id epoch-history)
              record         (issues-helpers/find-epoch-record focus-epoch-id epoch-history)]
          (issues-helpers/project-feed record focus-status))))

It takes the **whole focus map as an input**, then destructures `:epoch-id` alone and passes that to both
`resolve-focus-status` and `find-epoch-record`. The pinned `:dispatch-id` is read and thrown away — which
is precisely what `rf2-c4abp` removed from `panels/trace.cljs`.

### Site 2 — `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reactive_panel_subs.cljs` :151-152 (Views)

    [epoch-history epoch-id]
    (focus/find-epoch-record epoch-id epoch-history)

**This one is NOT the same shape and must not be treated as such.** Its signature takes an `epoch-id`, not
a focus map, so the discriminator is discarded by whoever CALLS it rather than here. **Fixing it therefore
means changing its callers, which is a wider change than site 1** — establish the call sites before
deciding, and it is entirely defensible to close this half with a reasoned decline.

**Its own docstring is the reason it is worth looking at rather than a stylistic nit** — it already
describes deliberately NOT falling back to HEAD for an evicted bundle, "which lied about which epoch the
operator was inspecting". So the file already cares about this exact class of lie, one discriminator short.

The rf2-c4abp worker described this as "the other half of the pair `rf2-uo0rc.1` fixed for eviction" —
**that attribution came through a report and I have not verified it. Treat it as a lead, not a premise.**

## The reproduction, which is the item's acceptance

From `rf2-c4abp`'s bead and reproduced by that worker on the JVM before it touched anything: with history
containing epoch/dispatch 11 and focus `{:dispatch-id 999 :epoch-id nil}`, the three-arity resolves
`:no-epoch`/nil while a two-arity call returns **record 11**. So switching tabs after selecting a refused,
unsettled or ungrouped bundle presents an unrelated cascade or ribbon state as the selected event.

title: Understated privacy gate: 023 says the history read drops on the rollup alone, but it now drops on either signal
description:
## The claim

`tools/xray/spec/023-Trace-Panel.md`, in its three-gates section, says the history-read gate drops a
record on the framework rollup ALONE. Since `rf2-vaont` merged, it drops on **either** of two signals, and
the spec names only one.

## Measured at trunk 85a3fce891, verified by the mayor at source

**The spec, at 023:215-216:**

    - **At history read.** `epoch/redact-history` drops any epoch record whose framework-stamped
      `:rf.epoch/sensitive?` rollup is true, so a sensitive record never enters the history this panel
      focuses.

**The code, `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/epoch.cljs`, `redact-history`'s own docstring:**

    Otherwise a record is dropped WHOLE when EITHER signal fires — the framework's
    `:rf.epoch/sensitive?` rollup, or a `config/suppress-sensitive?` event in its own `:trace-events`.
    That is the same predicate `collect-trace!` and `snapshot-from-rings` gate on, so the three ingress
    paths share ONE policy rather than three.

So the sentence is not merely thin — **it is thin in the direction that matters for a privacy gate**. A
reader auditing whether a record without a rollup can carry sensitive data reads this chapter and
concludes it can. It cannot, and the reason it cannot is the second signal the chapter omits.

## Why this is worth an item rather than a word

The chapter's own framing is what makes the omission expensive: it presents **three gates** and describes
each one's grain deliberately, and the ingest bullet immediately above it **already explains the
record-grain reasoning in the general case** — that a bundle carrying any suppressed event is dropped
whole because scrubbing one row is unsafe when a non-sensitive sibling in the same cascade can carry the
value. The history-read bullet is the one place that reasoning is NOT carried through, and it now
describes a narrower gate than the one that ships.

**There is a second, smaller understatement in the same passage**: the merged docstring says the three
ingress paths share ONE policy. The chapter presents the three gates as three separate mechanisms, which
was right before and is now worth a clause.

## What to do

**Re-derive the cite at tip and report the delta including a zero.** This chapter is in an active review

title: Stale prose in the Xray trace helpers namespace: a comment names a key its map lacks, and what-happened's docstring names the wrong fold
description:
Two pieces of stale prose in `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace_helpers.cljc`, both describing
behaviour the code beside them does not have.

## The two findings

1. The comment above `operation->verb` claims `recalculated` is in a map that **does not contain it**.
2. `what-happened`'s docstring says it folds **slashes and dots**; the code folds **hyphens**.

## Provenance

Found 2026-09-18 by the worker on rf2-y8doi.50 (PR #9964) while truthing
`tools/xray/spec/023-Trace-Panel.md` against this namespace. Both sites are OUTSIDE that item's fence, so
it named them rather than editing them — which is the instructed behaviour and the reason this bead exists.
That worker read this file closely enough to re-derive nine code cites in it, so the observation is a
by-product of work already done rather than a fresh guess.

## Why this is worth an item rather than a shrug

A docstring is the first thing the next reader of this namespace trusts, and both of these are the kind of
wrong that does not announce itself: a reader checking whether `recalculated` is handled will read the
comment, believe the map covers it, and stop. The verb mapping is what the Trace panel shows a user, so a
wrong account of it misleads whoever next changes the taxonomy.

## What to do

**Re-derive both at tip before editing.** These were read at a base where several xray changes were in
flight, and this namespace has taken merges recently. Report the delta, including zero.

For each, decide deliberately whether the PROSE or the CODE is wrong, and say which you concluded and why.
The likeliest answer for both is that the prose is stale and the code is correct — but that is a claim to
test, not to assume, and the hyphen/slash one in particular could be a fold that was deliberately narrowed
and whose docstring was left behind, in which case the narrowing may itself deserve a look.

**Take a control both ways**: a probe that finds the term where it IS present, so a zero means absence
rather than a broken pattern.

## Fence

    tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace_helpers.cljc

Comment and docstring text only. **If either turns out to be a CODE defect rather than stale prose, STOP
and say so** rather than changing behaviour under a documentation item — that is a different decision and
wants its own item and its own red-then-green evidence.

## Gate note

A comment-and-docstring change cannot fail a test, so a green JVM or node lane says only that the file still
compiles. Say that plainly rather than reporting an exit code as though it graded the edit. clj-kondo will
not redden on an unresolved symbol here either (see rf2-9gs83) — read the findings and the warning count,
not the exit code.
notes:
---

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN GATE NOTE (mayor, 2026-09-18, method-reread loop).

The gate note above says clj-kondo "will not redden on an unresolved symbol here". **That is narrower than
what is now true, and narrower in the direction that under-warns.**

rf2-9gs83 merged at `eec66772a7` as CLAUDE.md item (w), and its worker widened the claim on evidence I did
not have when I wrote this bead. Four single-linter probes, each as (plain exit / `--fail-level error`
exit): clean 0/0, unresolved symbol 2/0, **unused binding 2/0**, invalid arity 3/3. The unused-binding row
is the discriminator — a different linter, an unrelated fault, the flag equally blind.

**So the mechanism is the FLAG, not the fault.** `--fail-level error` reddens only on findings graded AT
error, and which findings sit below error is a per-linter, per-config fact rather than a property of the
fault. It is also this repo's choice rather than the tool's: with `.clj-kondo/config.edn` present, an
unresolved symbol reads `warning` and the flag exits 0; with no config above it, `error` and exit 3.

**Why the narrow version is worse than useless here**: it invites you to think that a fault of some OTHER
kind would be caught, so a green under that flag reads as evidence. It is not. **Read the findings and the
warning count; the exit code under that flag is not the discrimination for anything graded below error.**

I am not restating how many files this has been reproduced on. I wrote such a count into the earlier note
and it was stale within the hour — the same failure this project has already paid for twice in reusable
text. It has been reproduced independently on several trees and files; read item (w) for the current

## The problem, carefully

**What the runtime emits for one `:rf.http/managed` request.** A multiline search for `emit!\s+:\w+\s+:rf\.http/…` over `implementation/http/src` reads 8 sites / 6 distinct literal ops, matching the reviewer's census — but the literal census is INCOMPLETE, and the correction matters:

| op | emitted at | when / from where | dispatch-id it carries |
|---|---|---|---|
| `:rf.fx/handled` (op-type `:rf.fx`, tags `:rf.fx/id :rf.fx/args :frame`) | `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:1273-1278` | inside the issuing drain, during the `:fx` walk | the issuing run's |
| `:rf.http/retry-attempt` | `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:1107` (called at :1486, :2065) | when the NEXT attempt starts, i.e. from the backoff/transport callback | none |
| `:rf.http/transport` / `timeout` / `decode-failure` / `http-4xx` / … (op-type `:error`) | `transport.cljc:919` — `(rf.trace/emit-error! (:kind failure) redacted)` | failure finalisation, from the transport callback | none |
| `:rf.http/aborted` (op-type `:error`) | `transport.cljc:775` | the abort-fn choke — from whichever drain or callback aborted it | the ABORTING run's, or none |
| `:rf.http/replied` (tags = the reply's `trace-summary`: `:status`, `:rf.reply/work-id`, `:rf.reply/work-kind`, `:rf.reply/work-status`, `:attempt`, `:rf.frame/id`, `:completed-at` verbatim; `:value`/`:error`/`:correlation`/`:meta` elided — `implementation/core/src/re_frame/reply.cljc:618-626`) | `transport.cljc:557` | completion, "from the transport callback, OUTSIDE any `with-frame` scope" (`transport.cljc:538-541`) | none |
| `:rf.http/stale-suppressed` | `transport.cljc:622`, `:705`; `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc:927` | supersede / frame-destroy / actor-destroy suppression | the superseding run's, or none |
| `:rf.http/aborted-on-actor-destroy` (tags `:request-id :actor-id :url`) | `registry.cljc:869` | inside the actor's DESTROY drain | the destroying run's |

The correction: the reviewer's ripgrep found "zero emit sites" for `:rf.http/transport` / `timeout` / `decode-failure` / `aborted` and called them phantoms. They are not — they are emitted with the failure `:kind` as the OPERATION, dynamically, at `transport.cljc:919` and `:775`; `emit-error!` builds an `:error`-typed event whose operation is its first argument (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:900-924`). The two genuine phantoms are `:rf.http/handled` and `:rf.http/managed-issued` (a repo-wide search for either as an emitted op returns nothing; control: `:rf.http/replied` at `transport.cljc:557`).

**Why the correction makes the finding stronger, not weaker.** Both `emit!` and `emit-error!` take the dispatch-id from the dynamic `*handler-scope*` (`trace.cljc:863-865`, `:906-907`); a transport-callback emit has no scope, so it carries no `:rf.trace/dispatch-id`, and the grouper files it under `[nil :ungrouped]` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/projection.cljc:142-159`, `:189-199`). The two ops that DO fire inside a drain fire inside a DIFFERENT run's drain (the abort / destroy event's). So **nothing the runtime emits after issuance can ever land in the issuing bundle's `:other` slot** — not the completion, not the retries, not the failures, not the aborts — whatever names the collector carries. The reply the handler receives is then a fresh dispatch with its own run id. The bundle the panel projects contains exactly one HTTP fact: the `:rf.fx/handled` issuance row (op-type `:rf.fx` → the bundle's `:effects` slot, `projection.cljc:100-104`, `:235`).

### A. Join the completion to the issuing record across the whole buffer by work identity (the 019 F-C2 feature)

## Recommendation

**B, with the floor, now; file A as a feature bead and do not dispatch it.**

From the stance: a tool that shows a wrong status is worse than one that shows less — today's record says `✓ OK · completed` on a request that failed, so the floor is not optional and neither is retiring `:ok` as the issuance status. ## Codex Recommendation

**Choose a corrected B: make this an honest HTTP effect-invocation record now, and defer the joined exchange view.** The underlying defect is real, but several premises used to make B sound complete are false. A smaller record is appropriate for the current evidence; it should not retain claims that the response handler ran or that an exchange is one gesture away.

**Research basis.** Independently inspected source, tests, the managed-HTTP testbed, normative specs, `bd show rf2-y8doi.18`, bead history, and relevant git history at `1dbef19ef9ecc3c30ca629b7cb478224b1dcebea`. **Confirmed.** The production subscription passes no changed-path data (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_subs.cljs:65`). The helper turns a handled effect into `:ok/:completed` (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_helpers.cljc:293-304,353-366`), while the renderer treats empty paths as evidence of programmer error (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_template.cljs:428-449`). A bounded Babashka probe loading the actual pure namespaces produced `{:status :ok :phase :completed :handler [:done] :dispatch-id 7 :paths-touched []}` from a source-shaped issuance row. Feeding that row and an asynchronous error reply through the actual grouper put the reply in `[nil :ungrouped]`. The waterfall probe also confirmed that `[[:issued 0] [:elapsed 12]]` loses its first row.

**Corrections that affect the decision:**

- **The proposed B still misreports handler execution.** `args-handler-event` merely picks configured arguments, preferring `:on-success`; it does not observe delivery and does not read `:reply-to` (`managed_fx_helpers.cljc:370-380`, under the same Xray panels directory). The focus button dispatches the *issuing* record's dispatch-id (`managed_fx_template.cljs:401-426`). This affects a real caller: `tools/xray/testbeds/managed_http/core.cljs:262-266` uses `:reply-to [::reply]`. Retain configuration as configuration, or omit this section; do not label it HANDLER DISPATCHED.

- **The claimed correlation-filter escape route does not match the producer.** `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/filters/typed_predicates.cljc:196-208` looks for a flat `:correlation-id` tag. The issue carries `:request-id` inside `:rf.fx/args`; the completion carries it inside `:correlation`. Executing the matcher against both producer-shaped rows returned false; a control with the invented flat tag returned true. Therefore “A buys convenience, not visibility” is not established. Correcting that matcher is outside this bead's seven-file fence; B should not depend on it.

- **“No HTTP event can ever appear in the issuing bundle” is too strong.** Request-body preparation can fail synchronously before transport starts (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:2072-2086`), reaching the real dynamic failure emit at line 919 within the invoking stack. The existing regression covers this no-socket path (`implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_body_prep_failure_test.clj:42-78`; inspected, not run). Moreover, `:rf.fx/handled` is emitted *after* the effect handler returns (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:1608-1657`). It proves successful invocation, not that bytes went onto the network. Same-bundle HTTP rows also cannot safely be attributed to every HTTP effect in that bundle.

- **A's proposed duration calculation mixes clocks.** Trace `:time` uses `now-ms` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:713`); browser `now-ms` uses `performance.now()`, while completion time uses epoch milliseconds (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs:170-189`; `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:354-377`). Subtracting them would produce a meaningless duration in the SPA. An origin dispatch-id alone also cannot distinguish two HTTP effects issued by one event; any future exact linkage must identify the invocation and frame.

**Options and tradeoffs.** Leaving the current display is unacceptable. Corrected B provides trustworthy invocation/configuration information with a small local change, but explicitly gives up the integrated exchange picture. A is a useful feature for SPA debugging, not gold plating by definition; however, the proposed request-id/time heuristic cannot reliably attribute overlapping requests, and a completion join alone still does not implement F.1's handler-and-app-db story (`tools/xray/spec/019-Cross-Cutting-Insight.md:546-590`). Remove the amber warning globally: even a measured unchanged app-db can be legitimate. Do not wire the issuing event's diff and call it the response handler's changes. title: http_managed_machine CLJS tests (2)/(2b) encode the spawn run-propagation bug: route them to a silent fx (blocks PR #9790)
description:
FILED 2026-09-13 by the spawnprop-a worker (rf2-gbzv9, PR #9790), measured at trunk 6f8cd459b2. BLOCKS the merge of PR #9790.

THE DEFECT. Two tests in `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_managed_machine_cljs_test.cljs` encode the run-propagation bug rf2-gbzv9 fixes, so they go red under the fix:
- `invoke-spawns-wrapper-and-injects-framework-keys` (6 assertions);
- `invoke-preserves-nested-request-content-type` (1 assertion).

Each installs `(rf.http.test-support/install-managed-request-stubs! {})` and dispatches `{:fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed :rf.http/managed-test-stub}}` into a parent that `:spawn`s the `:rf.http/managed` wrapper, then asserts a stable `:requesting` wrapper snapshot. Their comments say that stub "NEVER replies". It does not: with an empty route map, `stub-handler` in `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc` emits a canned `:rf.http/transport` failure ("no stub matched"). The tests only ever saw `:requesting` because, before rf2-gbzv9, the per-call override never reached the spawned wrapper, so the wrapper's real `:rf.http/managed` fx ran and never answered under node. With the override now reaching the wrapper, the wrapper fails, the parent's `:on {:failed :idle}` exits the spawn state, and the wrapper's snapshot and spawn slot read nil.

PROVEN CAUSAL on CLJS (`npm run test:cljs`, same tree and counts). With the rf2-gbzv9 fix: exit 1, 7 failures, all in those two tests. With the fix reverted at one line: those two tests pass, and the 10 failures move into the rf2-gbzv9 regression. Test (3) `parent-exit-destroys-wrapper-child` uses the same pattern, but it asserts only that the wrapper is gone after a cancel, so it holds either way.

THE REPAIR (two call sites plus two comments). Route those two dispatches to a genuinely silent fx rather than the route-map stub. For example, in the test ns register `(rf/reg-fx ::silent (fn [_ _] nil))` and dispatch with `{:fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed ::silent}}`; the `install-managed-request-stubs!` / `uninstall-managed-request-stubs!` pair then becomes unnecessary in those two tests. Correct the "NEVER replies" / "no-reply stub" comments. It lands in the same PR as rf2-gbzv9 or immediately before it; either way PR #9790 cannot go green without it.

WHY NOT IN PR #9790. `implementation/http/**` was read-only for the rf2-gbzv9 dispatch (held by PR #9780, which has since merged).

title: xray: testid-for composes one string for both a mount's container and its root render-node, so one mount answers it twice
description:
ONE MOUNT ANSWERS ITS OWN CONTAINER TESTID TWICE, so any DOM count keyed on it reads
double and any `querySelector` on it silently picks one of two nodes.

VERIFIED BY THE MAYOR AT TIP ba26dd1aa7 (fact):

`testid-for` in tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs:1580 is

    (defn- testid-for
      "Compose a stable data-testid for a node — `[panel-id mount-id path]`."
      [panel-id mount-id path]
      (str "rf-xray-edn-inspector-"
           (name (or panel-id :anon))
           "-" mount-id
           (when (seq path) (str "-" (str/join "/" (map pr-str path))))))

The path suffix is appended only `(when (seq path))`, so **an EMPTY path composes the
same string as no path at all**. Two call sites emit that bare form:

    2435:  [:div (merge {:data-testid (testid-for panel-id mount-id path) ...
    2633:  [:div {:data-testid      (testid-for panel-id mount-id path) ...

one being the widget's outer CONTAINER and the other its ROOT RENDER-NODE at path `[]`.
So a single mount puts that identical `data-testid` on two nodes.

HOW IT SURFACED, AND WHY IT HAD NOT BEFORE (rf2-d2aj, PR #9597): that PR's W5 row is the
first test in the tree to mount TWO panels at once. Its first draft counted panels by this
selector and read **4 for 2**. Every earlier row mounts a single widget, and
`container-node` never noticed because `querySelector` returns the FIRST match — so the
duplication has been invisible for as long as it has existed.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN DOCUMENTING: it fails in the DIRECTION THAT REASSURES.
`querySelector` always finds something, so a helper resolving a container gets a node and
proceeds; whether it got the container or the render-node depends on document order, and
the two are not interchangeable — one carries the widget chrome and the ResizeObserver
target, the other the rendered tree. A future test that asserts on geometry through this
selector can pass while measuring the wrong element.

THE SHAPE OF THE REPAIR IS AN OPEN QUESTION AND YOURS TO SETTLE. Two obvious candidates,
and there may be better:

  (a) give the container its own suffix (`"-container"`), matching the existing
      `-toggle` / `-body` convention already used at 1985, 2048, 2074, 2545, 2576, 2649;
  (b) make the root render-node's empty path compose a suffix of its own, so `[]` is not
      the same as absent.

**(a) LOOKS OBVIOUSLY RIGHT AND IS THE ONE TO CHECK HARDEST**, because the container
testid is the PUBLIC handle every existing test and every consumer reaches for: renaming
it moves a surface, and this is a tool whose testids are deliberately stable. Count the
call sites in the test trees before choosing, and say what you found. (b) touches nobody
but changes what `[]` means inside the composer. Argue the one you pick.

DO NOT widen this into a testid audit of the whole inspector. One duplicated string.

GATES: the Xray JVM suite, `test:cljs` (node), `test:browser`, plus clj-kondo and Splint
over what you touch. **GATE THE BROWSER STEP ON THE COMPILE'S CAPTURED EXIT** — a browser
lane chained behind a failed compile serves the PREVIOUS BUNDLE and returns a plausible
green with its own honest exit code (measured, 885 tests against stale code, rf2-fr7y).

SABOTAGE: this is a selector change, so the discriminating plant is a row that asserts the
container resolves to the container. Break the composition and watch it name what it got.

**BUT THE BEAD NAMED THE WRONG SECOND PARTY, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS MORE THAN THE FIX.** I filed it citing call sites 2435 and 2633. title: ssr: structural slots reach native tags as DOM attributes; the fix belongs in shared strip-prop?
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-10 by the rf2-3357 worker, which deliberately did NOT fold it in because it is NOT the cheap
one-liner the parent bead assumed. That judgement is the useful part of this bead and is recorded first.

THE DEFECT. The SSR emitters pass STRUCTURAL SLOTS through as DOM attributes on native tags. Confirmed live:

    [:div {:key "k"}]  =>  key="k"
    [:div {:ref "R"}]  =>  ref="R"

React's own serialiser emits neither. A function-valued `:ref` is already correctly dropped, and a string
`:ref` is illegal in React, so the reachable case is `:key` — and `:key` on a native tag is ordinary
application markup, which is what makes this worth fixing rather than a curiosity.

WHY IT IS NOT CHEAP, AND WHY AN `emit.cljc`-LOCAL FIX IS THE WRONG ONE. The correct site is `strip-prop?` in
`re-frame.ssr.html-helpers` — a DIFFERENT file, SHARED with the head emitter, and the roster that the
STREAMING walker also reads via `emit/attr-string`. One line there fixes both paths. A `dissoc` local to
`emit.cljc` would mint a SECOND stripping roster, which that file's own notes forbid in terms — "ONE roster…
a second copy is a drift surface" — and would leave the streaming path divergent from the non-streaming one,
which is precisely the class of split that produced this bead's sibling.

SO THE SHAPE IS: one edit in `strip-prop?`, and evidence covering BOTH the emitter and the streaming path,
because the whole argument for editing there rather than locally is that it reaches both. A change that fixes
`strip-prop?` and only proves the emitter has not demonstrated the thing that justified its own location.

WHAT TO BE CAREFUL OF: `strip-prop?` is shared, so widening it affects the head emitter too. Establish what
the head emitter currently does with `:key` and `:ref` before changing the roster, and say so — a fix that
silently changes head output while fixing body output is a second finding, not a bonus.

OUT OF SCOPE: the fragment props-map defect, which is rf2-3357 (landed) and its streaming sibling (filed
separately). This bead is about structural slots reaching NATIVE TAGS as attributes, which is a different
mechanism in a different place — do not merge the two.

title: Expose React 19.3 Fragment refs through Fresco fragment lowering
description: Follow-up to rf2-3y09. implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/codec.cljs fragment-element currently copies only :key into React.Fragment props and silently drops :ref. React 19.3 stabilizes Fragment refs (https://react.dev/reference/react/Fragment). Assess and implement direct identity-preserving :ref forwarding under the adopted React baseline, with the smallest specification and documentation change. Verify object/callback refs, cleanup, sibling DOM shape, focus/measurement, conditional children, Activity hide/reveal and SSR/hydration. Keep hooks inside raw React/UIx hosts; no universal ref/hook or per-boundary DOM registry. Check reagent-slim separately because its fragment props already take a different conversion route.

title: CLAUDE.md: the dispatch-ledger contract has no spelling for a NO-WORKTREE dispatch, so the writer improvises (1 of 8 mayor rows non-conforming); plus a fallback line for the note-writing guard
description:
Found by the method-reread loop (loops.md section 6), 2026-09-09, checking rules the mayor has been ENFORCING against what the tree does. Two small CLAUDE.md edits, one surface, one PR.

## ITEM 1 (the substantive one) — THE DISPATCH LEDGER CONTRACT HAS NO SPELLING FOR A DISPATCH WITH NO WORKTREE, SO THE WRITER IMPROVISES

CLAUDE.md's Workflow section defines `ai/worktree-agent-ids.tsv` as five tab-separated fields: worktree (THE ABSOLUTE PATH, never the bare directory name), agentId, dispatched, branch, beads. It then documents that the shape had no spelling for a MAYOR-OCCUPIED tree, that the writer therefore improvised, and that the improvisation shifted every field by one — "which is the positional failure this bullet exists to stop". It fixes that case by prescribing `(mayor)` in field 2 and `--` in field 5.

THE SAME DEFECT RECURS IN A NEW POSITION. A ZERO-EDIT dispatch — a research or verification bead that changes no tracked file and therefore needs no worktree — has no spelling either. rf2-d1nr.1 was exactly that shape (verify a product name is free, apply a pre-committed rule, no file edits at all, briefed read-only), and it was correctly dispatched without a worktree.

MEASURED, and the measurement is of the rule's own author: of the eight rows the mayor wrote this session, SEVEN carry a conforming absolute path in field 1 and ONE does not — the improvised `(no-worktree: zero-edit research bead)`. That is prose in the field the contract reserves for a path, written by someone who had read the contract in the same session, for the same reason the mayor-occupied row went wrong: the shape does not admit the case.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC: field 1 is what a hygiene sweep keys on to decide whether a worktree still exists and whether it may be reaped. A row whose field 1 is not a path is a row that no path-keyed sweep can evaluate — it is neither a live worktree nor a reapable one, and it will sit unadjudicated for ever. CLAUDE.md already records that reading this file positionally "is right about one row in eight and wrong with a well-formed answer on the rest"; this adds a row that is wrong in field 1 specifically.

PROPOSED FIX, one clause in the existing bullet, in the same shape as the mayor-occupied row: a dispatch with NO worktree writes `(none)` in field 1, the agentId in field 2, the timestamp in field 3, `(none)` in field 4, and the beads in field 5. Five fields, positionally intact, and a path-keyed sweep can skip it on an exact match rather than trying to parse prose. Alternatively rule that such dispatches are not recorded in this file at all — but say so explicitly, because the current silence reads as an oversight and produces improvisation. EITHER RULING IS FINE; the defect is the absence of one.

DO NOT normalise the existing rows. CLAUDE.md is explicit that the contract binds the NEXT line and that normalising history is not wanted. Fix the one improvised row only if that is free.

## ITEM 2 (subordinate, and DO NOT ASSERT A CAUSE) — THE PRESCRIBED NOTE-WRITING FORM FAILED TO PARSE TWICE, UNEXPLAINED

CLAUDE.md's Beads durability section prescribes, as the guard against backtick command substitution eating a note: "write the note with a quoted heredoc and pass it as `"$(cat <file>)"`". THE GUARD IS CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE WEAKENED — a quoted heredoc was tested this session against the exact shapes that had been suspected (a bare apostrophe; a backtick-quoted term followed by an apostrophe; an unbalanced double quote) and all three came back exit 0 with byte-correct content.

BUT THE FORM FAILED TO PARSE TWICE, in two independent sessions, both on long multi-line notes: once for a worker (reported as "exit 2, unmatched quote", recorded in rf2-dluk's close reason) and once for the mayor (`unexpected EOF while looking for matching quote`). NEITHER FAILURE WAS REPRODUCED, and the short-input tests above do not reproduce it either.

SO ASSERT NOTHING ABOUT THE MECHANISM. The honest statement is that the observation supports neither "quoted heredocs are unreliable here" nor any particular cause; the loop's own rule against a correction overshooting into the inverse of the claim it replaces applies directly, and the first draft of this finding DID overshoot before the test refuted it.

WHAT IS WORTH ADDING IS A FALLBACK SENTENCE RESTING ON ASYMMETRIC COST, not on a mechanism: if the heredoc form does not parse, write the file by any other means and still pass it as `"$(cat <file>)"` — the protection that matters is that the content reaches `bd` from a FILE rather than through a double-quoted shell string, and the heredoc is one way to build that file rather than the thing doing the protecting. That sentence costs a line, cannot be wrong, and gives a reader who hits the failure somewhere to go; at present the guard names exactly one form and a reader who cannot make it parse has nothing.

DELIBERATELY NOT PROPOSED: any change to the guard itself, any wrapper around `bd`, any script, any gate. Section 6 warns that where a reader-side rule has failed, more text is usually not the repair — item 2 is one sentence precisely because of that.

## SEQUENCING — READ THIS BEFORE DISPATCHING

SEQUENCE BEHIND rf2-d1nr.2 (the Hicasso-to-Fresco rename sweep), which was IN FLIGHT when this was filed. That sweep rewrites every occurrence of the old product name across 911 files, and CLAUDE.md is one of them. A concurrent CLAUDE.md edit conflicts with it, and the sweep is atomic and must not be made to rebase. Wait for its PR to merge, then dispatch this.

## GATES

CLAUDE.md is repo-root markdown, so it is OUTSIDE `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`'s roots and INSIDE `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci`'s surface — nominate by PATH, not by job name, and note that both run in `test.yml`'s `verify-readme-links` job. `mkdocs build --strict` does not cover repo-root markdown at all (`docs_dir` is `docs`), so do not nominate it. Nothing validates this file's PROSE; verify by hand and say so.

ONE TRAP SPECIFIC TO EDITING CLAUDE.md, recorded in the file itself: writing a literal carriage return into it reclassifies the file from `w/crlf` to `w/-text`, git stops normalising it, and a one-clause edit stages ~156 changed lines. After editing, check that the total CR count equals the CRLF count.

title: [implementation/hicasso] impl/overlay.cljs has no :advanced compilation coverage
description:
https://github.com/day8/re-frame2 — implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/overlay.cljs

Found and NAMED rather than fixed by worker hicasso-a while delivering rf2-kx9f (PR #9367), which is
the right call: it is PRE-EXISTING and was not introduced by that change.

THE GAP: nothing compiles `impl/overlay.cljs` under `:advanced`. Two things look like they would and
neither does — `check_modules_compile` is a plain warnings-fatal compile rather than an advanced one,
and `npm run build:hicasso-release` starts at the PUBLIC DOOR, which by design does not reach an
optional module. So the optional overlay module has no advanced-compilation coverage at all.

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS NOT URGENT: advanced compilation is where npm interop and externs
problems surface, and this file uses `react/useLayoutEffect` (added by rf2-kx9f) alongside the
`react/useContext` and `react/useRef` already there. The worker checked and reported that
`useLayoutEffect` takes the IDENTICAL npm-interop path as those two, so nothing new is exposed — the
risk is unchanged by rf2-kx9f, not raised. What is missing is a gate that would catch a FUTURE
interop mistake in this module.

CHECK BEFORE BUILDING: verify at source that the two gates behave as described (a `:advanced` sweep
may have been added since), and establish whether other optional modules share the gap — a fix that
covers only this one file would be the wrong shape if the hole is structural. The cheap test is to
plant a deliberate externs-sensitive construct and confirm no current gate reds.

Under the project stance this is a real gap but not a crisis: do not build an advanced-compile
framework for one file. Either extend an existing sweep's roster to reach optional modules, or record
that optional modules are deliberately uncovered and why.

title: api(pair-mcp): flow / frame leave the MCP kind enum, or map to a structured refusal
description:
Filed 2026-09-07 by the rf2-kuky.30 / rf2-kuky.80 worker (PR #9356), as the one acceptance item of rf2-kuky.30 that PR deliberately did NOT satisfy.

## What rf2-kuky.30 asked

Its acceptance reads: "the pair-mcp kind enum still lists flow / frame only if the tool maps them to a structured refusal (say which in the PR body)". PR #9356 says which: it does NOT map them to a structured refusal today.

## Measured state at PR #9356's tip

`(rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :flow})` and `:kind :frame` now throw the catalogued `:rf.error/registrar-kind-not-queryable`, whose message names the real door (`re-frame.flows/flows-snapshot` / `flow-meta-at`; `rf/frame-ids` / `frame-meta`). That is the rf2-kuky.30 deliverable and it landed.

But the pair-MCP still offers both as kinds and does not catch:

- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/handler_meta.cljs` — `registrar-kinds` (the `#{...}` set) carries `:frame` and `:flow`; `supported-kinds` is that set plus `:machine`; `parse-kind` accepts anything in it.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs:1711` and `:1777` — the MCP schema `:enum` lists "frame" and "flow".
- `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:597` `registrar-list` calls `(rf/registrations {:source :store :kind kind})` with no try/catch.

So `list-handlers {kind "flow"}` propagates the framework throw rather than returning the tool's structured error envelope.

This is still an IMPROVEMENT on the pre-rf2-kuky.30 behaviour, which is why it was not treated as a blocker: the old path returned an apparently authoritative EMPTY catalogue (the silent swallow rf2-kuky.30 was filed against). A loud catalogued throw is strictly better than a silent lie. It is simply not yet the structured refusal the acceptance criterion contemplates.

## Why it was split rather than done in PR #9356

Ten sites across `tools/` and `skills/` pin that kind enum's spelling, and the surface is graded by `mcp-conformance`, a CI-only gate the fast-PR spine does not run. PR #9356 was measured GREEN AT BAND (87 checks, 0 failures, 0 non-terminal) before this was reached, and a multi-site enum change on an ungated-locally surface is the wrong thing to bolt onto a green PR. rf2-kuky.80's own text sanctions exactly this split.

## Suggested shape (not a ruling)

Drop `:frame` and `:flow` from `registrar-kinds` in `handler_meta.cljs` and from both `:enum` lists in `descriptors_data.cljs`. `parse-kind` then returns nil for them and the EXISTING `kinds-hint` machinery produces the structured "unrecognised kind" envelope with a corrective hint — no new error path to write. Consider whether the hint should name the real door (`flows-snapshot` / `frame-ids`) the way the framework error now does, rather than only listing the accepted kinds; a user who asked for "flow" wants to be told where flows live, not merely that "flow" is not a kind.

Verify against `mcp-conformance` and the pair skill's tests, neither of which the fast-PR spine runs.

title: [examples/core/login] Canonical Story success fixture omits the required session token
description:
## Observed contract failure

The auxiliary login Story showcase's canonical `:story.login/success` variant supplies no HTTP response fixture satisfying the real login model. The normal live login app has the correct demo override; the separate Story variant frame does not inherit that frame configuration. Its generic canned success is missing the required token, so the documented development showcase cannot reach its advertised Welcome state.

Inspected snapshot `7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd`; relevant files remain unchanged on mayor HEAD `90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d`.

## Exact causal evidence

- `examples/core/login/README.md` documents `npm run dev:example -- examples/login-with-stories` and `#/stories` to see every reachable login state. `examples/core/login/stories.cljs:323-332` declares the canonical success variant with only the form-base composition and `[:login.story/submit good-creds]` setup; it has no `:network` or `:fx-overrides` response fixture. The parent story at lines 163-168 and fragment at lines 188-197 supply none either.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc:568-581` allocates a separate variant frame with `:preset :story`. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:2368-2369` expands that preset to redirect `:rf.http/managed` to `:rf.http/managed-canned-success`, not the live app's demo handler.
- The real model submit handler, `examples/core/login/model.cljc:581-626`, sends the request with `:on-success [:auth.login/succeeded]` and no canned `:value`.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc:158-175` therefore creates `{:status :ok :value {:stubbed true}}` and dispatches it to `[:auth.login/succeeded ...]` through the actual reply-address seam at lines 179-193.
- `examples/core/login/model.cljc:665-677` declares the successor schema `[:cat [:= :auth.login/succeeded] [:map [:value [:map [:token :string]]]]]`. It persists `(:token value)` and only then dispatches the credential-free machine success signal. The generic stub response does not satisfy that schema.
- Validation is present on the documented dev path: `login.model` requires `re-frame.schemas`; `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas.cljc:10-22` loads the default Malli validator. `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:1148-1189` validates event schemas in development, and `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:2527-2558,3074-3083` skips the handler when validation fails. The variant thus stays submitting instead of rendering Welcome. Disabling dev checks would only allow the malformed continuation to persist nil as the token; it would not make the fixture faithful.
- In contrast, the live app's `model/frame-config` at `model.cljc:765-767` redirects to `:auth.login.demo/managed-stub`, which explicitly supplies a fake token. That config is applied in `login.core/mount!` and in the live showcase frame, not to Story's independently allocated variants.
- The existing success-token regression at `implementation/core/test/re_frame/example_login_success_token_cljs_test.cljs:85-91,126` drives the successor with an explicitly token-bearing reply, so it does not cover the canonical Story variant's generic response.

## Reproduction / impact

Start the documented `examples/login-with-stories` dev build, open `#/stories`, and choose `:story.login/success` (also included in both login workspaces). Setup submits valid credentials and enters submitting; the canned response is exactly:

```clojure
[:auth.login/succeeded {:status :ok :value {:stubbed true}}]
```

The required `[:value :token]` is absent. The development event-schema refusal prevents the machine success dispatch, so the advertised canonical Welcome screenshot is a busy form instead. This is a P3 auxiliary example-fixture defect; the main live login app's correct canned success is not implicated.

## Smallest repair

Give this example's success variant an explicit canned/network response fixture with the fake token shape expected by its real model, using the existing Story fixture surface. Keep the generic Story preset generic and preserve the classified successor/token-owning auth model. No validation bypass, new boot protocol or production auth redesign.

## Focused acceptance

Drive the actual registered `:story.login/success` setup in a newly allocated Story variant frame with the default development validator enabled. It reaches the machine's authenticated state and Welcome view without an event-schema refusal, and the storage effect receives the intended fake token (stub storage so no browser persistence is needed). The test must fail with the present generic `{:stubbed true}` response. Keep the submitting variant unresolved and the invalid-credentials variant rejected by form validation. Place regression coverage in the existing framework/tool test tree, not under examples.

## Dedupe and limits

title: spec/006 §Cross-host: say that Hicasso's author-wins-a-collision guarantee is held at the canonical React slot, not at the key
description:
ONE SENTENCE, ONE SECTION. `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` §Cross-host, in the paragraph beginning "**One clause is deliberately NOT taken: Hicasso emits no one-shot warning for a non-DOM root.**" — the clause that currently ends "...so fragments, `[:> …]` crossings, `defhost` islands and boundary heads are all skipped, and the author's own value wins a collision."

That sentence is TRUE as it stands (PR #9200 made it true again), so this is a sharpening and not a correction: it does not say WHERE the win is held, and the audit of PR #9191 showed that the difference is the whole of the contract. Replace the trailing clause "and the author's own value wins a collision." with:

  and the author's own value wins a collision — held at the CANONICAL REACT SLOT rather than at the key. Hicasso's codec accepts five spellings of one attribute (keyword, namespaced keyword, symbol, namespaced symbol and string) and folds every one onto a single React prop name, so a merge keyed by `=` would leave a body's `"data-rf-view"` beside the framework's `:data-rf-view` and let the attribute map's iteration order pick the emitted value — the guarantee failing nondeterministically rather than failing. The framework's entry is therefore dropped at any slot the author already claims, in any spelling, and the annotation a body did NOT write is still stamped beside the one it did (rf2-c5w1, audit of PR #9191).

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE BEAD. `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` is a one-toucher hot-zone file and a peer worker (rf2-ss8x, the reagent-adapter teardown fix) held it during the wave PR #9200 landed in, having already committed to it on its branch. The mayor corrected the fence mid-task and asked for the prose rather than the edit. Sequence this after that peer's PR merges, and re-verify the quoted clause against the file at dispatch — the peer's change rewrites parts of 006 and the sentence may have moved.

GATES BY PATH. `spec/` is staged into the docs build by `mkdocs_hooks.py`'s `on_pre_build` on any invocation, so a bare `python -m mkdocs build --strict` covers it (`mkdocs` is not on PATH). `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` validates anchors and repo-relative targets; it exits 0 with an empty log on success, so prove it live with a plant before believing it. The edit adds no link and no heading, so neither gate inspects anything new — say so rather than citing a green that inspected nothing.

title: routing specs still teach retired ui/v route-link surfaces as live prefetch peers
description:
## Finding

Audit of PR #9167 confirmed two current, canonical routing specs still describe retired view-substrate route-link APIs as live prefetch peers. This is separate from rf2-g8pf, which owns the zero-consumer prefetch-on-intent! helper and explicitly fences spec/ out.

## Evidence

- spec/012-Routing.md is explicitly normative. Its linking section still uses [v/route-link ... :prefetch :intent] as the example (line 623) and says rf/route-link, ui/route-link, and v/route-link all reject bad prefetch values identically (lines 640-643).
- spec/009-Instrumentation.md's :rf.error/route-link-bad-prefetch catalogue row still calls link-model “the compiled ui/route-link” and says every link surface declared by Spec 012 shares the behavior (line 2235).
- origin/main tracks no implementation/ui or implementation/freehand tree. The shipped replacement is re-frame.hicasso/route-link; implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/route_link.cljs explicitly declines :prefetch in v0 and fails loud instead of installing the intent handlers.
- Commit 9ae069ac4d0b (“cut the donor testing and route-link surfaces”) removed the explicit ui/route-link and v/route-link rows plus the Freehand descriptor from Spec 012, but these active example/summary claims survived. They are current normative assertions, not retirement history.
- Exact Bead and open-PR searches found no owner for this spec reconciliation. rf2-g8pf mentions the clue only to exclude the hot-zone specs from that symbol-level task.

## Impact

Programmers and AI assistants reading the canonical routing contract are told two nonexistent APIs ship and that the current view substrate supports prefetch when Hicasso deliberately rejects it. That obscures the actual low-friction surface and makes behavior audits reason from imaginary parity.

## Proposed disposition

Reconcile only the live normative claims in Specs 009 and 012 with the shipped surface: teach rf/route-link's current :prefetch :intent behavior and state Hicasso's deliberate v0 decline (or land real Hicasso support first). Replace the retired v/ example with a live spelling. Preserve genuinely historical EP/design donor records; this is not another broad retirement sweep.

## Risks

Do not change routing behavior, weaken fail-loud prefetch validation, or silently promise Hicasso support. The diagnostic table row must retain its column shape and accurate emit/recovery/tag contract.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Specs 009 and 012 contain no current normative claim or example presenting ui/route-link or v/route-link as shipped surfaces.
2. The text accurately distinguishes rf/route-link's supported :prefetch :intent behavior from re-frame.hicasso/route-link's current fail-loud v0 decline, unless tested Hicasso support lands in the same change.
3. Historical EP/design records are left intact unless independently shown to violate their governing status; routing runtime behavior is unchanged.
4. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py passes with the required worktree proof, and edited table rows are manually checked for column count.

title: implementation README: use canonical adapter terminology consistently
description:

- The vocabulary definition and all paths/identifiers remain unchanged.

title: Clarify flow topology dependency and cycle-walk roles
description:
Partition: dependency and topology algorithms.

Evidence and ambiguity cost:
- implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/topo.cljc:33-49 calls the entry count `n` and sorted ids/paths `lo`/`hi`, although ids are heterogeneous values sorted only for stable reporting.

- topo.cljc:140-145 calls the reduce-kv row key `dep-id`; it is actually the dependent node whose dependency set is being peeled, so `dep` is directionally ambiguous in the core Kahn step.

Use `entry-count`, `first/second-flow-id`, matching output-path names, `stuck-node-ids`, `start-node-id`, `node-id`, `next-dependency-id`, `cycle-start-index`, `dependent-id`, and `dependency-ids`/`remaining-dependency-ids`. Compatibility and risk:
Lexical/private-only rename with no ordering, hash sort, graph, path, or exception changes. Tests include heterogeneous ids, deterministic overlap reports, self-cycles, multi-node cycles, and dead-end invariant extraction.

- Topology locals identify node ids, dependency direction, path roles, counts, and cycle indexes without changing algorithms.

title: Drop inert :root-ref from the machines-viz overlay scaffold constructor
description:
Evidence
- make-resizing-overlay-class in chart/overlays/overlay_scaffold.cljs destructures only display-name, remeasure!, and render. It never reads :root-ref.
- after_rings.cljs, spawn_all_join.cljs, and cancellation_cascade.cljs all pass :root-ref to that constructor anyway.
- Each overlay actually consumes its root-ref through its own remeasure! closure and through overlay-root-props; those paths are separate from the constructor argument.
- The scaffold docstring admits the constructor key is unused and retained only so a hypothetical future variant can change teardown without changing the signature. Git history shows this inert argument arrived with the scaffold extraction in b8b7cb99cd.
- The constructor is internal and :root-ref is not part of spec/API.md's public MachineChart contract.

Impact
Every overlay advertises and supplies a parameter that has zero effect. The misleading doc even claims the scaffold gates teardown with it, while unmount simply removes the window listener unconditionally. This adds false coupling and obscures the real ownership of measurement state.

Recommendation
Remove :root-ref from the make-resizing-overlay-class argument documentation and from all three constructor maps. Keep each overlay's local root-ref atom and its overlay-root-props/remeasure! use.

Risks and contracts
Do not remove the local root ref, offsetParent capture, measurement closure, resize listener, or teardown. Preserve the public :overlays descriptors and all DOM positioning behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- make-resizing-overlay-class exposes only the three values it reads: display-name, remeasure!, and render.
- No caller passes :root-ref to that constructor.
- Each overlay still captures offsetParent through overlay-root-props and remeasures on mount, update, and resize.
- Overlay geometry, rendered DOM, lifecycle, and browser tests pass for after rings, spawn-all join, and cancellation cascade.
close_reason: Landed in PR #9094 (branch worker/mvizb-a, commit 2f6dbe2264). Premise HELD and was confirmed at source: make-resizing-overlay-class destructures {:keys [display-name remeasure! render]} and never reads :root-ref, while its docstring claimed the scaffold 'reads it only to gate the resize listener teardown' - :component-will-unmount removes the resize listener unconditionally. :root-ref is gone from the docstring and from all three constructor maps (after_rings.cljs, spawn_all_join.cljs, cancellation_cascade.cljs); the ns docstring's claim that the root-ref atom lives in the scaffold was corrected too (each overlay owns it; the scaffold owns the overlay-root-props :ref that fills it). Every overlay keeps its local root-ref atom, its offsetParent capture, its remeasure! closure, the resize listener and teardown - post-edit grep shows 3 root-ref hits per overlay, unchanged. Two instruments plus a control: git grep -F census of ':root-ref' across the artefact returns nothing after the edit while the control 'root-ref' still fires 3x per overlay; clj-kondo --fail-level error over tools/machines-viz exits 0 with a warning set byte-identical to a git-archive extraction of origin/main (8 warnings, 0 errors, only a viewer.cljs line number shifted). title: Replace the vacuous stale non-delivery event-conformance case
description:
## Finding

`a-stale-completion-is-non-delivering-without-an-explicit-observer` in `implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_reply_envelope_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` builds global and image handlers, then calls only the pure `reply/suppress` function. It never calls `dispatch`, `dispatch-sync`, a delivery helper, or any managed-effect completion path. Therefore its zero call count and unchanged app-db assertions follow from the test performing no delivery operation at all; they cannot detect a runtime that ignores `:deliver?` and dispatches stale app replies.

The row had real teeth before commit `ca7fd0bd93`: it invoked `deliver-through-gate!`, which consumed `:deliver?`. That commit correctly deleted the delivery gate under the new observer-self-dispatch model, but left the negative row's handler/frame apparatus after removing its sole dispatch site. Its remaining pure assertions (`:deliver? false`, valid `:stale`/`:suppressed` envelope, no `:value`) are already owned more strongly by core's `suppress-does-not-deliver-app-target` and `suppress-is-universally-non-delivering`, the cross-family reply-conformance stale matrix, and the production-elision stale suite.

## Recommendation

Delete this row and update the namespace prose from “both stale cases,” unless a real production-path integration gap exists. If app non-delivery needs an event-conformance test, drive an actual managed-effect family completion/lowering path that conditionally could dispatch the target; assert that a superseded completion reaches the suppression branch and leaves both explicit and ambient frames untouched. Do not simulate non-delivery by simply omitting the delivery call.

## Risks and contracts

Retain `an-observer-self-dispatches-a-stale-reply-on-its-own-authority`, which genuinely composes `suppress` + `complete` + frame-targeted dispatch and proves the authorized observation path. Retain the natural success dispatch case. A replacement must depend on production code that consumes the suppression outcome, not a new test-local gate that merely restates it.

## Evidence

The current row's only operational call after setup is `reply/suppress`; `seen-event`, `call-count`, and both app-db values are read before any dispatch. `ca7fd0bd93` removed `deliver-through-gate! outcome ...` from exactly this row. Core and reply-conformance already assert universal suppression and envelope shape in dual-runtime suites.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The no-operation stale case is removed, or replaced by a test that executes a real production completion path with a reachable delivery branch.
2. A replacement demonstrably fails when that production path dispatches despite `:deliver? false`; zero calls cannot be established merely by never invoking delivery code.
3. The observer self-dispatch and natural-success event-pipeline cases remain green on JVM and CLJS.
4. Namespace/deps commentary accurately names the integration boundaries still exercised, and focused JVM plus consolidated Node tests pass.
close_reason: Premise held; vacuity proven by plant. Planting reply/complete's :append leg to stop appending the reply reds reply-completion-is-an-ordinary-reg-event-dispatch (13 failures) and an-observer-self-dispatches-a-stale-reply-on-its-own-authority (6), and leaves a-stale-completion-is-non-delivering-without-an-explicit-observer with ZERO failures -- it is blind to the entire delivery path it names. REMOVED rather than replaced, and the reason is a finding worth keeping: NO production code anywhere reads :deliver?. reply/suppress returns false unconditionally with no branch, and every family (http/registry, http/transport, resources/reply_handlers, routing/nav_token, machines/reply) branches on its OWN staleness decision instead, never on the outcome's :deliver?. So AC1's alternative -- 'a real production completion path with a reachable delivery branch' -- has no target that does not first re-invent the delivery gate ca7fd0bd93 deliberately deleted, which the bead's own risk note forbids. Coverage is not lost: the RETAINED observer row keeps a LIVE non-delivery tooth (zero call-count read BEFORE the observer self-dispatch, exactly-one AFTER, so a runtime that app-delivered a stale reply itself fails the pair), and the pure suppress laws (universal :deliver? false, stale envelope shape, absent :value) are re-frame.reply-cljs-test's across six target shapes including forged stale-authority. AC2 moot under removal; AC3 both retained rows green on JVM and CLJS; AC4 ns prose rewritten to name the narrower ownership. PR #9123.

title: Refresh ssr-node CLI and README after the runtime expansion
description:
## Evidence

Two consumer-facing inventory strings were left behind by the September crossing expansion:

- bin/serve.cjs:53 and README.md:506 describe --max-request-bytes as a ceiling on the request body and on its state. Current protocol.cjs:458-468 instead applies one ceiling to state and runtime together, a contract introduced by rf2-8arzr.3.
- README.md:685 still says the package has 9 suites and 96 rows. The authoritative runner currently executes 9 suites and 104 passing rows; .github/workflows/test.yml:5273 was already updated by rf2-8arzr.4 to record 104 rows across 9 files.
- History explains the split: rf2-8arzr.2 wrote the README at 96 rows; rf2-8arzr.3 then added 8 runtime-partition rows; rf2-8arzr.4 corrected the workflow count but did not own this README section.
- The current JVM adapter sends both state and runtime, so the state-only flag text is operationally misleading rather than hypothetical.
- Closed rf2-1vvx owned earlier pre-crossing README status prose and a classifier suite/fixture comment; its description explicitly excluded test.yml, and it predates this remaining 96-to-104 README drift. No current parent child or ssr-node/runtime-partition search owns these strings.

## Impact

An operator sizing the sidecar can infer that runtime data sits outside the protocol budget, while it actually shares the state ceiling. Contributors also receive contradictory test inventories from the README and CI. Both make the post-crossing surface look partly reverted.

## Disposition

Update the CLI help and matching README flag table to say that the numeric option caps the body and the combined state-plus-runtime EDN text. Reconcile the test inventory with the runner; prefer wording that does not hard-code a volatile row count unless that count is intentionally maintained.

## Risks

Do not imply that the parsed JSON body and partition-text limits are additive or independent: maxRequestBytes is separately used as the body ceiling and as one combined partition ceiling. Do not change runtime behavior or the option name in this documentation repair.
acceptance_criteria:
1. CLI --help and README describe max-request-bytes consistently with protocol.cjs: one body ceiling and one state-plus-runtime combined ceiling.
2. README's suite/row inventory agrees with test/run.cjs output (currently 9 suites, 104 rows), or omits the volatile row count without weakening test instructions.
3. No stale state-only ceiling sentence or 96-row claim remains in implementation/ssr-node.
4. CLI/serve tests, README link checks, and the full ssr-node suite are green.
close_reason: PR #9099. bin/serve.cjs and the README's copy of the same flag table now read 'ceiling on the body, and on state + runtime together' -- matching protocol.cjs:490 (one combined state+runtime ceiling) and http.cjs:133 (the separate body ceiling), and not implying the two are additive. The README's request-too-large refusal-code gloss ('over the state or body ceiling') was the same stale claim and moved with them. PREMISE THAT DID NOT HOLD: the bead says the runner executes 104 rows; it executes 107 on current main (measured foreground, 30+12+7+5+9+16+6+4+18), 108 with rf2-6r9j.74's new row. Took criterion 2's second branch and OMITTED the volatile count rather than restating a third number -- the count has gone stale twice, nothing checks it, and each suite prints its own tally. The nine suites stay named (that number is the length of run.cjs's FILES list). test.yml's comparable count is explicitly dated and self-described as 'a record, not a pin', so it is correct as written and was left alone (fenced besides). Gate nominated BY PATH: a README beside source belongs to scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci, exit 0, control fired (a planted broken relative target reds it naming this file). Neither link gate reads fenced blocks and nothing validates prose or tables, so the usage block's column alignment, the two-column refusal table row and the live --help output were checked by hand and stated in the PR body.

title: Epoch: remove the redundant pre-state argument from the halt hook
description:
Evidence
- implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:353 declares frame-state-before in the single-arity commit-halt-record! hook, but lines 355-372 never read it; clj-kondo reports that exact binding as unused.
- The only production caller is implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:3420-3422, which passes fs-now in both the before and after positions.
- The documented and implemented contract at epoch.cljc:334-370 deliberately derives both halted-depth snapshots from the last retained record :frame-state-after, falling back only to the supplied frame-state-after when no epoch has settled. The pre-state value cannot affect the record.
- Repository-wide hook inventory finds no other executable consumer. The late-bind directory and specifications name :epoch/commit-halt-record! but do not promise its arity.
- History shows frame-state-before became inert when commit 27a4b1d77e9 made last-settled :frame-state-after authoritative; later exact-incarnation work retained the redundant slot.

Impact
The optional epoch artefact and core router maintain a misleading extra protocol argument. The duplicate fs-now call implies two meaningful snapshots even though the halt event never ran and the implementation always commits one durable value into both slots.

Proposed disposition
Remove frame-state-before from the private hook signature and remove one fs-now argument at the sole router call. Keep the hook single-arity, preserve exact-owner-token gating, causal committed-at, residual-buffer harvest, last-settled lookup, first-halt fallback, and equal before/after snapshots.

Risks
This is a late-bound cross-artefact seam, so core and epoch must change atomically. Do not introduce a compatibility multi-arity: the source documents that multi-arity changed Closure advanced reachability and violated production elision (rf2-cprm0q).
acceptance_criteria:
1. commit-halt-record! has no frame-state-before parameter and the router passes one frame-state value.
2. Halted-depth records still use the last settled canonical frame-state, use the router value only for the no-prior-record fallback, and store equal :frame-state-before/:frame-state-after.
3. Exact-incarnation owner loss still cannot harvest or commit a same-id successor store.
4. Focused core/epoch JVM and CLJS tests pass, and the epoch production-elision gate stays green.
5. clj-kondo no longer reports the epoch.cljc unused binding.
close_reason: PR #9098. Premise held: frame-state-before was declared and never read (clj-kondo epoch.cljc:353 before, clean after). Removed from the private hook and one fs-now dropped at the sole caller router.cljc:3421 — core and epoch in ONE commit because the seam is late-bound and an arity mismatch is a runtime fault. Kept single-arity (rf2-cprm0q elision trap). Full caller/implementor sweep: router.cljc:3421 (only executable caller), epoch.cljc:329 (only implementor), epoch.cljc:737 registration, late_bind/directory.cljc:823 (describes the key, promises no arity), spec/002-Frames.md:2023 (illustrative 3-arg pseudocode, carries no frame-state at all), spec/Conventions.md + migration README + conformance fixture (name the key only) — NO spec change needed, no hot-zone file touched. Liveness control: restoring the two-snapshot call reds re-frame.epoch-test/depth-exceeded-commits-halted-record with ArityException (8 args), so the halt seam is exercised end to end. Green: epoch-test (219), core frame-destroy-incarnation-jvm-test (29), scripts/test-epoch-prod-gate.sh (25). NOTED GAP, pre-existing and unaltered: no test covers the first-cascade fallback arm where the router-passed frame-state is the value actually used.

title: Remove evaluate-flow!'s unread dirty-result slot
description:
Evidence
- `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:214-296` documents and returns `[db dirty?]`: `[db false]` on equal inputs and `[new-db true]` after a computation.
- The private function has one call, at lines 330-336. That caller checks the separate `stale-incarnation` marker and then reads only `(first result)`; no source, test, tool, trace, or public API reads the Boolean slot.
