Its commit message explicitly says the tuple's dirty slot is discarded at the call; later exact-owner changes retained that discard.
- Exact repository searches find no destructuring or indexing of the second result element.

Impact and disposition
Every non-stale flow visit constructs a two-element result whose second value has no consumer, and the docstring advertises a dirty contract the cascade intentionally retired. Remove the Boolean slot and simplify the sole caller/result contract while preserving the transformed-db left fold and the distinct stale-incarnation outcome.

Risk
Owner-loss short-circuiting, derive/output-write error attribution, dirty-cache rollback, validation, trace ordering/elision, and the documented three-argument compatibility path of `run-flows-on-db` are deliberate contracts and must remain unchanged. Do not make a legitimate pending db indistinguishable from the stale marker.
acceptance_criteria:
- `evaluate-flow!` no longer returns or documents an unread dirty Boolean.
- Its sole caller consumes the simplified successful result without a second-slot discard.
- Tests cover both equal-input skip and computed-output paths plus owner loss before/after the derive callback, with the same transformed db and stale behavior as today.
- Flow failure attribution and rollback tests, default JVM/CLJS flows suites, and exact-incarnation tests pass.
close_reason: PREMISE HELD — evaluate-flow! now returns the transformed db rather than [db dirty?] (PR #9082). The bead's evidence was truncated at the point where it said what the caller checks, so the caller was read directly: at flows.cljc:330-336 it does (if (= stale-incarnation result) stale-incarnation (recur (rest remaining) (first result))) — it discriminates the stale marker and then takes (first result), and NEVER reads the second element. Census: no source, test, tool, trace, spec or public API destructures or indexes it; every tree-wide mention of evaluate-flow! outside its own file is a comment, a docstring or spec prose, and no test reaches the private var through #'. No new marker ambiguity, which was the bead's stated risk: run-flows-on-db* ALREADY returns either a bare db or stale-incarnation to its own caller (both its (empty? remaining) and empty-flow-map arms return db unwrapped), so evaluate-flow! now returns the same two outcomes its enclosing fold does, discriminated the same way. Owner-loss short-circuiting, derive/output-write phase attribution, dirty-cache rollback, validation, trace ordering/elision and the three-argument run-flows-on-db path are untouched. Gates: flows JVM 250 tests / 6102 assertions / 0 failures; test:cljs 11209 tests / 55849 assertions / 0 failures.

title: Stop retaining the unused streaming root Hiccup tree
description:
## Finding

`render-streaming-shell!` returns the fully resolved root tree in `rendered[:hiccup]`, but the streaming writer no longer reads that field. The detached writer receives a map that can retain an arbitrarily large Hiccup tree for the lifetime of the stream even though every live operation uses `:shell-html`, `:doc-hash`, and (when continuations exist) a fresh post-drain root resolution.

## Evidence

- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj:123-210` documents and returns `:hiccup hiccup`.
- The sole production consumer, `run-streaming-writer!` at lines 270-404, destructures `head-html`, attribute bags, `doc-hash`, `head-hash`, `shell-html`, and `continuations`; it never reads `:hiccup`.
- Final payload hashing at lines 383-399 either re-resolves `root-view` after a continuation drain or reuses `doc-hash`; the carried tree participates in neither arm.
- A repository search finds no read of this result key. The only other ssr-ring occurrences are three hand-built writer-test maps (`streaming_writer_trace_test.clj:83,332` and `streaming_robustness_test.clj:207`), where it is an ignored extra key.
- History proves the disconnect: commit `375fc36ec2` introduced the field for the writer's final-hash computation. Commit `185c149a53` stopped destructuring it when hashing moved to `doc-hash`; later commit `80d28623a4` moved continuation-sensitive final hashing to a fresh `root-view` resolution. Old comments retained it "for diagnostics", but no diagnostic path ever consumes it, and the current docstring still incorrectly says it is "for the final-hash".
- `re-frame.ssr.ring.streaming` is explicitly on the API-manifest generator's internal-namespace roster (`implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj`); the public façade, API docs, specs, examples, and Node crossing expose `stream-handler`, not this intermediate result shape.

Duplicate searches for `render-streaming-shell hiccup final hash`, `streaming hiccup rendered map`, and `ssr-ring hiccup retention` found no owning bead.

## Impact

Every streamed request retains both rendered HTML and the original in-memory tree across the daemon writer, with the worst retention on slow clients or long continuation drains. The stale field and docstring also suggest final-hash logic depends on a pre-drain tree when the correctness fix deliberately made it post-drain-sensitive.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `:hiccup` from the internal rendered map and its result-shape docstring, and remove the three ignored fixture keys. Keep the local `hiccup` binding: it remains required to build `doc-hash` and `shell-html`. Do not change root resolution count or hash timing.

## Risks

The common no-continuation path must still resolve a fn-form root exactly once and reuse `doc-hash`; continuation requests must still re-resolve after draining. This cleanup must not move shell rendering onto the writer thread, alter failure projection, or expose a new public result contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- `render-streaming-shell!` no longer returns or documents a `:hiccup` field, and writer-test fixtures do not carry the ignored key.
- The local resolved tree remains used to compute `doc-hash` and call `streaming/render-shell`; shell bytes are unchanged.
- `run-streaming-writer!` still uses `doc-hash` when no continuation exists and a fresh post-drain `root-view` resolution when continuations exist.
- Streaming tests pass, including exact-once root resolution, post-drain hash/state parity, writer trace/failure, and nested continuation ordering coverage.
- A repo-wide search within ssr-ring finds no stale claim that the carried Hiccup tree drives the final hash.
close_reason:
Confirmed and fixed in PR #9081. NOTE FOR THE EPIC: this bead's subject is implementation/ssr-ring/, not implementation/http/ — it was dispatched clustered with three http beads as one artefact, and only the other three are http.

WHAT HELD THE TREE ALIVE, established before the fix. stream-rendered-response builds the daemon writer as an anonymous fn closing over the WHOLE rendered map and hands that closure to a Thread. The holder is the closure FIELD, not a stack local, so Clojure's locals-clearing never reaches it, and the thread lives until the stream drains — bounded by the client's read rate through a 16 KiB PipedInputStream, so a slow-loris client extends it arbitrarily. Chain: live Thread -> closure field -> rendered -> :hiccup -> the whole resolved root tree, retained alongside the rendered HTML for the request's lifetime. That is the bead's stated impact, confirmed.

THAT THE WRITER NEVER READS IT. run-streaming-writer! destructures exactly seven keys (head-html, html-attrs, body-attrs, doc-hash, head-hash, shell-html, continuations); :hiccup is not among them. The symbol rendered occurs at only three executable sites in streaming.clj — created at the handler, passed to stream-rendered-response, destructured once in the writer — with no (:hiccup rendered), no get, and no other key access (the reduced? check only derefs). Two-instrument census over git-tracked ssr-ring files, line-oriented and whitespace-flattened AGREEING: :hiccup at exactly 5 sites — streaming.clj:128 (docstring row) and :201 (map construction), plus the three ignored writer-test fixture keys the bead named (streaming_robustness_test.clj:207, streaming_writer_trace_test.clj:83 and :332). Every line number in the bead re-derived and correct. CONTROL needle shell-html fired at 22 line-oriented / 23 flattened.

MEASURED. A WeakReference harness reproducing the exact shape — a parked thread holding a closure over the map, the tree scoped out of the constructing frame so the map is the only holder, identical GC pressure both runs — reads tree-retained-by-live-writer? true WITH the field and false WITHOUT it. The field is the only difference between the runs. Two earlier harness shapes were discarded as inconclusive rather than reported: the first held the tree in a live local of the GC frame (both runs read retained), the second let locals-clearing drop the map after its destructure (both read collectable). Sample tree serialises to 106,986 pr-str chars; real magnitude is page size, unbounded.

DISPOSITION AS ORDERED: :hiccup gone from the returned map and from the result-shape docstring row (which still claimed 'for the final-hash'); the three ignored fixture keys gone. The local hiccup binding KEPT — it still builds doc-hash and feeds streaming/render-shell. Root-resolution count and hash timing untouched: the no-continuation path still reuses doc-hash and the continuation path still re-resolves post-drain. AC5: no stale claim that the carried tree drives the final hash survives in ssr-ring.

GATES: ssr-ring clojure -M:test 231 tests / 1163 assertions / 0 failures, captured exit 0 — identical to the pre-change baseline, and re-run green on the rebased final base. clj-kondo --cache false over ssr-ring src+test: 0 errors / 31 warnings, identical to its merge base.

title: Delete orphaned dispatch-fx-handler forward declaration
description:

Reachability proved with two text instruments (line-oriented and whitespace-flattened fixed-string over 4818 tracked files, .beads excluded, plus a hyphen-normalised third pass) AND at the analyser level via clj-kondo :analysis, each against a live control. The macro-generated-name trap the bead flags was checked and cleared: the fragment 'dispatch-fx' returns 28 hits, all of them join-dispatch-fx in machines, test names or local bindings, and every (symbol (str ...)) site in core/src builds a NAMESPACE symbol, none assembles a var name from fragments. Deleted the declaration and its blank line only; the ';; ---- do-fx ----' section banner stays (it heads everything to defn do-fx at :2000). handle-one-fx, dispatch-fx, the reserved-fx table, override resolution and late-bound router dispatch untouched. After the change a repository-wide exact search for dispatch-fx-handler returns ZERO. Core JVM :test exit 0, 2176 tests / 11149 assertions, 0 failures; test:cljs exit 0, 11209 tests / 55849 assertions, 0 failures.

title: Remove the unread :routing/route-sub-fn late-bind hook
description:
## Problem

The routing facade publishes `route-sub-fn` twice: it directly registers the function as the `:rf/route` subscription and also writes it to the optional-artefact hook table as `:routing/route-sub-fn`. Nothing ever reads that hook. The public direct function remains documented, but the late-bind publication and its directory entry are vestigial plumbing.

## Evidence

- Repo-wide fixed-string search for `:routing/route-sub-fn` returns exactly two current locations: `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:489` (`late-bind/set-fn!`) and `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:518` (catalog metadata). There is no `late-bind/get-fn`, `require-fn!`, wrapper, reset-hook roster, or other call site for the key.
- The real subscription registration is direct in the already-loaded routing facade: `(subs/reg-runtime-sub :rf/route ... route-sub-fn)` at `routing.cljc:387-389`. It neither needs nor consults late binding.
- `re-frame.core-routing` contains only the two required optional-artifact wrappers, `reg-route` and `route-link`; it has no route-sub function wrapper.
- `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md` documents `route-sub-fn` as a direct owned-namespace function, so removing the dead hook does not remove that supported function.
- History shows `:routing/route-sub-fn` was added mechanically during the artifact split in `c435165251`. That same change moved the `:rf/route` registration into `re-frame.routing`, leaving no core consumer; no later commit has added a hook read.

## Impact

Every routing load mutates the process-global hook table with an unreachable entry, and the central late-bind directory advertises a cross-artifact seam that does not exist in practice. This enlarges the optional-artifact integration vocabulary and can mislead maintainers into preserving or using a needless indirection.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the `late-bind/set-fn! :routing/route-sub-fn` publication and the matching directory entry. Keep `re-frame.routing/route-sub-fn` and its direct `:rf/route` registration unchanged because those are live/documented surfaces.

## Risks

Late-bind tables can be inspected generically, so rerun the directory drift/coverage checks after removing both sides together. Recheck for computed-key consumers; current code consistently uses literal hook keys and the exhaustive fixed-string search found none. Do not remove the direct public function or subscription registration as part of this cleanup.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `:routing/route-sub-fn` is absent from both the routing publisher and the core late-bind directory, with no remaining lookup or documentation of that hook.
2. `re-frame.routing/route-sub-fn` remains available and `:rf/route` remains directly registered to it after normal load and `:reload` following `registrar/clear-all!`.
3. Routing subscription tests and core late-bind directory drift/coverage tests pass.
4. A repo-wide fixed-string search confirms no computed or literal consumer was orphaned.
close_reason: Removed in PR #9148 (worker/routevest-a). Premise re-verified at branch tip: a fixed-string search for :routing/route-sub-fn returned exactly the two sites the bead named — routing.cljc:489 (late-bind/set-fn!) and late_bind/directory.cljc:518 (catalogue row) — with no get-fn, require-fn!, wrapper, reset-hook roster or computed-key consumer anywhere. Removed both sides together. KEPT, as the bead requires: the public re-frame.routing/route-sub-fn alias (routing.cljc:115) and the direct (subs/reg-runtime-sub :rf/route ... route-sub-fn) registration; docs/api/re-frame.routing.md still documents it and spec/api-manifest.edn's re-frame.routing/route-sub-fn row is unchanged, so the supported function is untouched. core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj:192 resolves that direct var, not the hook, and is unaffected. Gate: implementation/core clojure -M:test -n re-frame.late-bind-drift-test exit 0, 8 tests / 692 assertions / 0 failures — the bidirectional scan the bead's risk section names, which hardcodes no key but walks every set-fn! call site under implementation/**/src against the directory. That gate was proven non-vacuous for exactly this change: restoring the directory row while leaving the publication removed turned it red naming :routing/route-sub-fn as an entry with no publication, which is also why both sides had to move together. The file was restored and verified byte-identical by git blob hash. npm run test:cljs exit 0 (11168 tests / 55728 assertions / 0 failures) covers the core artefact and the routing subscription registration.

title: spec(xray): 007-UX-IA.md $Production posture specifies a dismissable Xray-is-enabled warning banner that tools/xray/src does not implement
description:
Found by the rf2-fguoj worker (PR #9002) while correcting the SKILL, and left unfiled because tools/xray was out of its write surface.

CLAIM (worker's, to be checked at source). tools/xray/spec/007-UX-IA.md $Production posture specifies a dismissable dev-build posture banner near-verbatim. Nothing under tools/xray/src implements it: a fixed-string search for the banner text returned 0 both line-oriented and whitespace-collapsed, with 'dismiss' as the shape-sharing control returning 43 hits.

WHY IT MATTERS. rf2-fguoj was filed as 'the skill teaches a banner that does not ship'. That premise was only half right: the skill was faithfully reproducing the SPEC, and it invented nothing. So a bare deletion in the skill would not have held, and the worker instead marked $Production posture normative-future in the skill. title: ci(pair fixture): three local roots do not arm the shipped-preload test
description:
## Scope

Complete the reverse dependency into the existing `re-frame2-pair-fixture-pure` CI job. Keep the current fixture, workflow, and changed-surface vocabulary; this is classifier reachability only.

## Merged-PR audit finding (#8903)

PR #8903 correctly adds the four local-root reverse edges for the MIG-23 fixture. Because both fixture jobs are gated solely on `skills_structural`, that dispatch incidentally fixes the Pair fixture for the two roots they share, core and the stock Reagent adapter. The Pair fixture has three additional direct `:local/root` inputs that remain unarmed: epoch, schemas, and machines.

`skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/fixture/deps.edn` directly resolves all five in-repo artefacts because the shipped preload requires their public surfaces. At #8903, production classifier probes report `skills_structural=false` for both `src/*` and `deps.edn` under:

- `implementation/epoch`
- `implementation/schemas`
- `implementation/machines`

The `re-frame2-pair-fixture-pure` job is therefore accepted as skipped on a change to three fifths of its in-repo classpath. Epoch happens to arm a different MCP-live gate, but schemas and machines arm neither Pair fixture; none of those substitutions makes this job's shipped-preload compile and pure-function contract run.

## Three lenses

Completeness: the new reverse-edge comment and mirror enumerate only the MIG-23 roots, while the incidental Pair claim stops after the two shared roots and leaves the rest of that fixture's declared local-root roster uncovered.

Correctness: an owned-namespace API or behavior change in schemas/machines/epoch can break `re_frame2_pair.pure` or its runtime preload while the one job that compiles/tests that shipped source is skipped; a skipped required job is an accepted result.

Implementation quality / narrow direction: extend the existing `skills_structural` reverse-edge shape to the remaining Pair local roots at `src/*` plus `deps.edn`, accepting the same small over-fire trade #8903 already chose for ssr/hicasso. Do not add a workflow, fixture, generic dependency engine, or a 29th output.

## Duplicate search

All-status searches covered pair fixture, shipped-preload pure, reverse edge, local root, `skills_structural`, epoch, schemas, and machines. No exact owner exists. `rf2-bbe91` owns the MIG-23 fixture's four roots and is correctly closed; this is its sibling Pair fixture rather than unfinished MIG-23 work.

title: Mayor-side .beads revert vector: checkout of HEAD issues.jsonl + checkpoint re-import silently evaporates recent closes
description:
FILED 2026-07-25 10:55 AUSEST from the in_review cluster dossier (delegated ruling). No existing bead owns this vector (searched); rf2-4l67v (Dolt remote) is adjacent and already ruled - reference it, do not merge into it.

THE VECTOR: CLAUDE.md mandates git checkout HEAD -- .beads before every pull (correctly, to avoid the stale-HEAD pull-abort trap). But if a bd close or bd create happened after the last export-commit, that checkout reverts the JSONL to the pre-close state, and the next checkpoint re-imports the reverted file into the database - the close simply evaporates. Neither the pre-commit hook nor the CI beads-pr-boundary gate can see it, because it is neither a commit delta nor a PR: the doctrine that prevents one fault performs the other. This is the LAST live vector of the .beads time-travel fault family (the PR vector is closed by the unconditional CI gate; the local hook arm is rf2-zt65l).

OBSERVED, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: rf2-5e8zv was reopened exactly this way and had to be re-verified; commit e80786e007 on main (chore(beads): re-close kqxe6.7/.166/1a9au (merged, reverted by re-import)) records three more closes reverted by re-import and manually re-closed. The eight-bead in_review cluster disposed 2026-07-25 is downstream collateral of the same fault family.

FIX IS PROCEDURAL FIRST, MECHANICAL SECOND - options to rule on:
1. Order the mayor loop so a checkout of .beads never follows tracker mutations within a tick: checkpoint (export-commit) FIRST, then checkout+pull. Amend the CLAUDE.md wording (Beads durability + Workflow sections both carry the bare checkout instruction today).
2. Have checkpoints RE-EXPORT from the Dolt database (bd export) rather than trusting the working-tree JSONL, so a reverted file can never be re-imported over newer database state.
3. Optional guard: warn when the checkout would discard a working JSONL newer than the HEAD copy (mtime or row-count delta).
4. Landing rf2-4l67v (durable Dolt remote) demotes the JSONL to a pure downstream artefact and dissolves the risk class - it is the strategic fix; 1-2 are the cheap immediate ones.

ACCEPTANCE: CLAUDE.md sequence updated so close-then-checkout cannot revert within a tick, AND a bd close performed immediately before the standard pre-pull cleanup demonstrably survives the following checkpoint (verify via bd show).
notes: CLOSED via PR #6936 (2026-07-25 15:2x AUSEST). Options 1-3 done; option 4 (rf2-4l67v Dolt remote) untouched, still an operator action for Mike. (1) CLAUDE.md's BOTH copies of the sequence (Beads durability + Workflow) now read checkpoint -> clear -> pull, so a checkout of .beads can never follow a tracker mutation within a tick. (2) scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh + .ps1: a checkpoint runs 'bd export' and commits THAT, never the working file, so a reverted export is unreachable; refuses an empty export or one that drops >10% of rows (2026-06-10 mid-rewrite incident 7aea52459); commits only .beads/issues.jsonl via explicit pathspec (metadata.json is not in the rf2-ydl2p mayor allow-list); refuses to run in a linked worktree, reusing check-beads-boundary.sh's derivation. (3) --pre-pull / -PrePull warns when the working export is ahead of HEAD and is silent otherwise; it compares row SETS not bytes, because bd export does not fix memory-row order and on Windows 'git checkout' writes CRLF while bd export and 'git show' emit LF - a byte comparison warned every single time (caught by test case 8c, which failed until the EOL/order normalisation went in). ACCEPTANCE: 'bd close rf2-51uz1' then measured the danger window live - HEAD said in_progress, 'bd export' said closed, 2625 vs 2626 rows; bd show confirms CLOSED. The commit half runs end to end in test-pre-commit.sh layer 8 case 8a against a stub bd (close in the DB only -> git checkout HEAD -- .beads -> checkpoint -> the COMMITTED file carries status closed), plus the same shape in a .ps1 sandbox; it is sandboxed rather than run in the mayor checkout because a worker may not commit the tracker and the live mayor loop owns those commits. Suite: 56 passed / 0 failed under sh and under dash. Also fixed while verifying the Windows sibling: ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList is null on Windows PowerShell 5.x, and bd/git stdout must be copied as RAW BYTES (a captured string is ANSI-decoded on 5.x, which would corrupt 10MB of bead prose).

title: [MIKE - 1 MIN] xrcorr-st7j0: husk signature matches, content floor fails - remove with --husk, or rule it stays
description:
**[MIKE — OPERATOR DECISION, ~1 MINUTE] A directory at `C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/xrcorr-st7j0`
matches the husk SIGNATURE but fails the removal script's CONTENT floor, so the script refuses it and no
mayor may remove it by any other route.** This bead exists so the disposition stops being re-derived — and
re-derived WRONG — in chat every tick.

## Why it is a bead now

The mayor has reported this in prose across several ticks as "the husk the removal script declines to
touch", and on 2026-09-18 reported it as **positively identified** as this repository's husk on the
strength of one matching blob. **That identification OVERSHOT, and the memory
`husk-classifier-disarmed-a-strangers-junction` says exactly why**: the script's first cut counted MATCHING
FILES, and a throwaway `package.json` containing `{}` genuinely matched a blob of ours — so the rule was
changed to BYTES, because *"the near-miss that defeats you is a file too small to be distinctive."* The
mayor's evidence was a 13-byte `VERSION` reading `0.0.1.alpha`. That is the near-miss, met head-on.

## Measured 2026-09-18 at trunk ed526290e8, every number taken this pass, never inherited

**The script's own verdict, run UNPIPED on the normal classifier path:**

    REFUSED_UNREGISTERED=/c/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/xrcorr-st7j0
      registered as a worktree : no
      .git present             : no
      content from this repo   : 1 of 18 top-level tracked files match a blob this repository
                                 knows, 13 bytes (floor 1024)
    NOTHING HERE WAS TOUCHED.

Exit **1**. The mayor's node_modules canary read `103/2933/2` before and after, `.bin` 27.

**The four-part husk signature, each tested with a live registered worktree as the control:**

| criterion | xrcorr-st7j0 | control (a live worktree) |
|---|---|---|
| appears in `git worktree list` | **0** | 1 |
| `.git` present inside it | **no** | yes |
| `git status` inside it | **exit 128**, 0 bytes stdout, 69 bytes stderr (`fatal: not a git repository`) | exit 0, 0 bytes |
| `git worktree prune --dry-run -v` | **nothing to clear** | — |

**So the signature matches on all four axes** — including the decisive one the method names, that a
clean/dirty test reads it as CLEAN, which here it does for the opposite reason from the control: both
print 0 bytes on stdout, one because the tree is clean and one because there is no repository to ask.

**Contents:** 2 files, 7,271 bytes, **no symlinks, no `node_modules`, no junction** — `VERSION` (12 bytes
of content, hashing to `2f8957a336…`, which IS trunk's tracked `VERSION` blob) and
`__pycache__/mkdocs_hooks.cpython-314.pyc`, build output of the tracked `mkdocs_hooks.py`.

## THE HONEST DISPOSITION, which is narrower than the mayor's earlier one

**Whether this is our husk or an unrelated directory cannot be settled from its content**, and the script
is right to refuse. 13 bytes against a 1024-byte floor is not identification; it is one generic file. What
IS settled is that nothing here is dangerous to leave: no junction to follow, nothing tracked, 7 KB.

## The decision, and it is yours because only you can supply the acknowledgement

The script names its own escape and it needs a human to say so:

    sh scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh --husk C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/xrcorr-st7j0

That path disarms links and then classifies. **A mayor must not invoke it on its own initiative** — the
whole point of the flag is that it encodes a caller's acknowledgement, and the memory above records the
script once unlinking a stranger's junction after misidentifying an ordinary directory. So: either say the
word and it goes, or say leave it and this bead records why it stays.

**Do NOT reach for `rm -rf`.** A husk still holds every file the worktree had, and the method is explicit
that a partial removal kills a running gate exactly as a complete one does. There is no running gate here,
but the rule is the rule and the saving is 7 KB.

## What this bead is NOT

It is not a hygiene backlog item and needs no sweep. It is one directory, measured, with one question
attached. If the answer is "leave it", close this bead with that ruling and the next mayor reads the
ruling instead of re-measuring.
notes:
---

## THE CAUSE IS FOUND, AND IT CHANGES THE DECISION (mayor, 2026-09-18, trunk 242d0b1f93)

**TWO LIVE JVM PROCESSES NAME THIS WORKTREE.** Found while verifying by effect that the shadow-cljs lane
was free — enumerating every `node`/`java` process and READING all ten rows rather than filtering by name:

    PID 80140  java.exe  … clojure.main -i <session-scratchpad>/drive_real_transport_xrcorr_st7j0.clj
    PID 87380  java.exe  … clojure.main -i <session-scratchpad>/drive_real_transport_xrcorr_st7j0.clj

Both carry `-classpath src;…` rooted in that worktree. **Neither carries a shadow-cljs signature**
(`shadow`, `thheller`, `node-test`, `cli/runner` all false on all ten rows, against non-empty command
lines of 51–5061 characters as the control), so they do **not** hold the build lane — but they are two
JVMs alive from a dispatch whose worktree was reaped and whose bead (`rf2-st7j0`) closed and merged as
PR #10010.

**THIS IS THE MISSING PIECE THE CONTENT TEST COULD NOT SUPPLY.** This bead says whether the directory is
our husk "cannot be settled from its content" — 13 bytes against a 1024-byte floor — and that stands. But
it can be settled from something better: **two running processes name it by path.** That is identification
by provenance rather than by bytes, and it is not the kind the removal script can perform, which is
exactly why the script needs a human's acknowledgement.

**AND IT EXPLAINS HOW THE HUSK CAME TO EXIST.** The method's four refusal modes distinguish *held* from
**locked** — "clean and intact with a live process holding a handle", genuinely transient. A
`clojure.main` process holding open files under that tree is precisely what makes `git worktree remove`
gut the metadata and then stop, which is how a partial removal becomes a husk in the first place.

**SO THE DECISION NOW HAS A CHEAPER FIRST STEP, AND IT IS STILL YOURS.** Kill the two PIDs first — they
are driving a script for a dispatch that finished, so nothing is lost — and the directory may then be
removable by an ordinary path with no `--husk` acknowledgement at all. If you would rather not think about
it: `--husk` still works, and the stakes are 7 KB either way.

**I did not kill them.** They are somebody's processes, killing is not reversible, and a mayor acting on
its own initiative against a live process is the shape this project has already been bitten by. Two
JVMs idling is a real if small cost, so this is worth a minute rather than a tick.

---

## STRANDED SWEEP, 2026-09-20 18:48 AUSEST: a SECOND unregistered directory in the worktree parent

Recording this here rather than filing a new item, so the next sweep does not rediscover it cold. It
needs no worker and probably needs no act at all.

`C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/_preserved-provenance/` is the second directory in the
worktree parent that `git worktree list` does not know about — `xrcorr-st7j0`, this bead's subject,
is the first. **It is NOT a husk and NOT a strand, and it should not be treated as either.**

**Measured 2026-09-20 18:48:**

- `git worktree list` does not list it, so a worktree-keyed sweep skips it; a directory-keyed sweep
  over the parent DOES return it, which is how it surfaced.
- It has **no branch, no HEAD and no commits** — the sweep's `rev-parse` returned empty for both
  branch and tip, where every registered worker tree returned both.
- Its mtime is **2026-08-02 09:39**, roughly seven weeks stable.
- It contains four subdirectories and nothing else: `ladder-ymi6j`, `ladder-ymi6j-A`,
  `ladder-ymi6j-confirm`, `ladder-ymi6j-refused`.

**Read the NAME as the disposition.** The directory is called `_preserved-provenance` and its contents
are four variants of one `rf2-ymi6j` ladder experiment, including an arm named `refused`. That is the
shape of a deliberately kept record of an experiment's arms, not of an abandoned checkout — and the
leading underscore sorts it away from the worker trees on purpose.

**So the default is to LEAVE IT**, and this note exists to say so once rather than to open a question.
It costs nothing where it sits, it is not on any reap path (the reap test reads a worker's report and
this has no worker), and `scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh` would refuse it exactly as it refuses

title: skill(re-frame2): patterns leaf size — websocket 29 KB, resources 28 KB, form-action 25 KB, resources-mutations 20 KB, forms 17 KB exceed the 16 KB ceiling and fail the catalogue test; de-dup targets named
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/README.md` §Leaf size discipline: "each leaf file SHOULD be ≤250 lines AND ≤16 KB (target ~150 lines / ~10 KB) — the byte ceiling catches leaves whose long unwrapped prose lines fit under the line count but still bloat the per-session token load … catalogue-shaped leaves … may exceed the ceiling if splitting would multiply file-handle overhead without reducing tokens-per-session. Test: would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session? … leaves that have since outgrown them are refactor targets unless they pass the catalogue test."

## TRUTH AT TIP (`wc -lc skills/re-frame2/patterns/*.md`)

| leaf | lines | bytes | over 16 KB by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `websocket.md` | 242 | 28,932 | +81% |
| `resources.md` | 231 | 27,660 | +73% |
| `form-action.md` | 229 | 25,307 | +58% |
| `resources-mutations.md` | 209 | 20,058 | +25% |
| `forms.md` | 211 | 17,447 | +9% |

All five pass the line ceiling and fail the byte ceiling — exactly the case the byte ceiling was added for. None is catalogue-shaped: each is one pattern with one canonical declaration, and splitting would not reduce tokens-per-session. What inflates them is the same point stated two or three times in different sections:

- `form-action.md` — the redirect-vs-navigate rule at L154-162 (in-code comment), L173 (prose paragraph), and L209 (anti-pattern); the fail-closed CSRF compare at L128-135, L181, L203; the token-not-in-the-field-schema rule at L43, L183, L204; the `:form-params` normalisation seam at L14, L68, L101, L205-206. Each is right; the third copy of each is the bloat.
- `websocket.md` — the settle-in-flight-on-every-door rule at L52-58, L100-102, L137-138, L220; the registration-token rule at L198, L225, L226; the credential-never-in-`:data` rule at L30, L36, L70-72, L127-129, L179, L194, L216. Prose paragraphs of 400-900 bytes (L5, L30, L198, L200) carry most of the excess.
- `resources.md` — §Scope is mandatory (L87-133) is 8 KB on its own: the fail-closed argument at L89-91, L93, L97, L118, L205; the "public is not global" point at L93 and L205.
- `resources-mutations.md` — the workflow-vs-cache axis at L41-50, L82, L192, and the watcher-reaction warning at L82, L191 plus `stale-detection.md:328`.
- `forms.md` — the auth/secret section (L29-74) is a second canonical declaration; the ten-line comment at L41-50 restates the `:sensitive?`-does-not-classify rule that L33 and L72 already state.

## IMPACT

Per-session token load: SKILL.md tells the agent to load at most two leaves; websocket + stale-detection is 43 KB, resources + resources-mutations 48 KB, form-action + forms 43 KB — three of the natural pairs are 2.7-3× the 16 KB target. Hygiene, not correctness (P4): nothing here is wrong, and the correctness beads filed alongside (websocket, resources) will touch two of these files, so this can ride behind them. Sibling bead rf2-udtw3 covers the same discipline for the state-machines leaves (`reg-machine.md`, `spawn.md`); this one is the patterns tree.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR, or one per leaf)

Bring each under 16 KB by de-duplicating, not by splitting: keep each rule's code-adjacent statement, cut the prose restatement and the anti-pattern restatement down to one line that names the section that states it. Do not cut content that exists nowhere else (the token-on-the-wire rule in `websocket.md:226`, the descriptor lattice in `resources-mutations.md:107`). Target ≤16 KB each; ≤12 KB is reachable for `form-action.md` and `websocket.md` by measurement of the duplicated spans above.

## GATE

No script enforces the leaf ceiling (searched `scripts/` for the numbers — only the skills' own `spec/authoring-prompt.md` files defer to `skills/README.md`). Verify by `wc -c skills/re-frame2/patterns/*.md` and say so in the PR body; `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` + `python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py` for links/regressions (`drift` pins the FormAction CSRF compare shape and the WebSocket reply-contract wording — keep those fences intact).

## ACCEPTANCE

`wc -c skills/re-frame2/patterns/*.md` shows every leaf ≤16,384 bytes; no rule listed above is stated fewer than once; both check scripts exit 0.

WHY FOUR STAY OVER, measured rather than asserted. RULED OPTION: B. The memory deletion is DONE at trunk 5741906ee2 (parent 4520025651 is the last checkpoint carrying all 416 receipts). Do NOT run `bd forget`, `bd remember`, or any memory write. Your whole job is ONE SENTENCE in ONE FILE.

WHAT: replace the LAST sentence of the rf2-ornb bullet at CLAUDE.md:94 (the bullet that begins "**Per-PR and per-run bookkeeping goes on the bead and in the commit, never into a memory") so it stops saying 416 memories exist that do not, and names both surviving cursor-shaped keys. Nothing else on that line, and no other line, moves.

THE ONLY FILE YOU MAY EDIT: C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2\CLAUDE.md (in your worktree, the same path under the worktree root), line 94. `git ls-files --eol CLAUDE.md` reads `i/lf w/crlf`.

THE SENTENCE TO REPLACE — it is the tail of line 94, immediately after "...this bullet is the only durable artefact a future harness author reads. " — reads:
It forbids WRITING new per-PR memories and authorises deleting nothing: the standing records stay, and the single rolling `merged-pr-audit-cursor` key is load-bearing for that harness's resume logic — leave it.
(In the file the apostrophe in "harness's" is U+2019 and the dash before "leave it" is U+2014. Read the line with the Read tool and take your old_string from the bytes on screen, never from this note.)

THE REPLACEMENT (copy exactly; it is ONE paragraph with NO line break, because line 94 is a single line and a bullet in this file never wraps):
It forbids WRITING new per-PR memories — and **the class it once protected is CLOSED and DELETED, so do not carry "the standing records stay" forward from an older checkout**: the harness wrote its last per-PR receipt for PR #9874 (merged 2026-09-15T09:18:05Z) and has appended receipts to the source bead's notes since (252 of 252 later PRs carried a bead note and no memory, measured 2026-09-21), and on Mike's instruction the mayor deleted all 416 legacy receipts (`merged-pr-audit-pr-9455` through `-9874`, 947,496 value bytes, 31.8% of memory value bytes) at trunk `5741906ee2` under rf2-lz6dl, committed `--no-verify` past the checkpoint's shrink floor — the guard working as designed, discharged with the escape the floor bullet above names for a genuine mass delete. Every deleted receipt survives byte-for-byte in git history, because `scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh` exports with `--include-memories`: `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 git show 4520025651:.beads/issues.jsonl | jq -r --arg k merged-pr-audit-pr-9664 'select(._type=="memory" and .key==$k)|.value'` recovers one (`4520025651` is the deleting commit's parent and the last checkpoint carrying all 416), and "was PR N audited?" is `git log --oneline --grep='audit merged PR #N'`. Nine `merged-pr-audit-*` keys survive and stay: the rolling `merged-pr-audit-cursor`, which is the key the harness's resume logic recalls (measured 2026-09-21 over 269 harness `.py` files: 320 recall sites name it, 0 name any other cursor-shaped key), and eight method memories — `merged-pr-audit-cursor-correction-pr-7568-timezone-comparison` among them, a correction record that shares the cursor's prefix rather than a second cursor. Leave all nine.

BEFORE YOU EDIT — re-measure the numbers the sentence states, from your worktree root after `git fetch origin main`. If ANY differs, STOP and report instead of editing (the sentence would then be stale on arrival):
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 git show 4520025651:.beads/issues.jsonl | jq -r 'select(._type=="memory")|.key' | tr -d '\r' | grep -cE '^merged-pr-audit-pr-[0-9]+$'      # expect 416
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 git show origin/main:.beads/issues.jsonl | jq -r 'select(._type=="memory")|.key' | tr -d '\r' | grep -cE '^merged-pr-audit-pr-[0-9]+$'    # expect 0
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 git show origin/main:.beads/issues.jsonl | jq -r 'select(._type=="memory")|.key' | tr -d '\r' | grep -cE '^merged-pr-audit'              # expect 9
  git log -1 --format='%H %s' 5741906ee2                                                                                                                       # expect "chore(beads): retire 419 memories - 416 closed per-PR audit class, 3 judged"
  git rev-parse 5741906ee2^                                                                                                                                    # expect 4520025651...
  (`MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` is load-bearing: a ref and a path both carrying a slash are mangled by MSYS otherwise — CLAUDE.md instrument item (d). `tr -d '\r'` is load-bearing: jq writes CRLF here — item (e).)

HOW — every rule here has bitten this file:
- Worktree guard first: `sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh` from your worktree; report the printed WORKTREE_ROOT. Never edit the mayor checkout.
- SERIAL LANE: CLAUDE.md is one-toucher-at-a-time. Before opening your PR run `gh pr list --state open --json number,files --jq '.[] | select(any(.files[]; .path=="CLAUDE.md")) | .number'`; if it names a PR, wait for that PR to merge, then rebase onto origin/main and re-run the BEFORE YOU EDIT probes.
- Edit with the Edit tool (or Python reading and writing BYTES). NEVER `sed -i`: on a w/crlf file it rewrites every line ending to LF while exiting 0 and `git diff` stays silent — instrument item (u).
- The replacement carries backticks and a `$k`. Do not pass it through a double-quoted shell string (backticks are command substitution) or a Bash heredoc (runs of backslashes are halved — item (o)). The Edit tool is the right instrument.
- AFTER the edit, take the three numbers with Python reading the bytes and require cr == crlf AND bare_lf == 0:
  python -c "b=open('CLAUDE.md','rb').read(); cr=b.count(b'\r'); crlf=b.count(b'\r\n'); lf=b.count(b'\n'); print('cr=%d crlf=%d bare_lf=%d'%(cr,crlf,lf-crlf))"
  At trunk 5741906ee2 this reads cr=161 crlf=161 bare_lf=0 before the edit; the line count does not change, so expect 161/161/0 after. Do NOT take these with `grep -c` (item (s): it reads 0 on this very file and passes the check vacuously).
- Verify by EFFECT, not by exit code: `git diff --numstat` reads exactly `1	1	CLAUDE.md`; `git ls-files --eol CLAUDE.md` still reads `i/lf w/crlf`; `grep -c -F 'authorises deleting nothing' CLAUDE.md` reads 0; `grep -c -F 'Leave all nine' CLAUDE.md` reads 1; a nonsense phrase reads 0 (the control that shows the instrument bites).

GATES (name the right one; this is a prose edit to repo-root markdown):
- `python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` — CLAUDE.md is on ITS surface (repo-root markdown), NOT `check_doc_slugs.py`'s. The line carries existing links; the replacement adds none.
- The commit-msg hook / `scripts/check-commit-attribution.sh`: NO AI attribution trailers in the commit message or PR body — CLAUDE.md § Git Conventions wins over the harness reminder; say in your report that you declined them.
- Not needed, do not run: any clojure lane, clj-kondo, shadow-cljs, mkdocs (CLAUDE.md sits outside docs_dir), the browser lane.

PR: title `docs(claude): truth the rf2-ornb bullet to the Tier 0 memory deletion (rf2-lz6dl)`. Body states: the memory-deletion commit it truths against (5741906ee2, parent 4520025651); the five re-measured BEFORE YOU EDIT readings; the CR/LF triple before and after; that it touches one sentence of one file and adds no link. Publish as a DRAFT, push as you go, mark ready as your last act. No `.beads/issues.jsonl` or `.beads/metadata.json` on the branch, ever.

WHAT NOT TO DO: no `bd forget`, `bd remember`, or memory edit of any kind; do not restore any deleted memory; do not touch `.beads/PRIME.md` (its "~950 memories" heading is stale against 1,013 but is deliberately outside this fence — ruled, not forgotten); do not relabel instrument item (e), the "class accumulates either way" sentence, the 1.86 MB latency half, or any other bullet; do not add a gate, a script, a retention policy or an archive; do not rewrap line 94.

DONE WHEN: the PR is merged and `grep -c -F 'authorises deleting nothing' CLAUDE.md` reads 0 on origin/main. Then close this bead with a reason naming the PR number, the merge commit, and the deletion commit 5741906ee2 (docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md permits a worker to close its own item with a cross-referenced reason). The analysis behind the ruling is on this bead's notes (RULING, then DOSSIER parts 1 and 2); you do not need to read it to do the edit.

=== AXIS 3 SUPERSESSION PASS, TIER 1 — WORKED 2026-09-21 06:42 AUSEST (worker, branch worker/memaudit-lz6dl, trunk da60bedaf9). 7 memories retracted in place, 0 deleted, 0 renamed, corpus still 1,432. ===

SCOPE HONOURED: retraction only. `bd forget` not invoked. The 416 `merged-pr-audit-pr-*` memories counted 416 before and 416 after — untouched, pending Mike's ruling. No key renamed. No dangling-path or undated memory acted on. No tracked file edited, no commit, no PR; both this worktree and the mayor checkout read zero porcelain lines throughout, which is the EXPECTED reading for a `bd` write and not evidence the writes did nothing — they were verified by reading the field back.

THE FUNNEL, RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY RATHER THAN TAKEN FROM THE BRIEF. Edge list built from `bd export --include-memories` by matching every memory key as a whole token (key-charset boundaries, longest-match-first) inside every other memory's value: 196 occurrences, 193 distinct src->dst edges, 116 memories named by at least one other, 124 naming at least one other. The bead's description records 206 edges / 128 named; my stricter boundary rule is the likely difference and the discrepancy is not material to the verdicts. Applying the three tightenings the dispatch describes gave 171 -> 85 -> 26 against the mayor's 134 -> 75 -> 27; tier 1 is higher because my correction vocabulary was wider (adding obsolete/outdated/no longer/inaccurate/revoked/rescind).

THE HEADLINE FINDING, AND IT IS THE ONE THE DISPATCH PREDICTED: OF THOSE 26 WINDOWS, 20 ARE CROSS-REFERENCES AND NOT CORRECTIONS. Read individually, 20 of 26 are `RELATED:` / `SEE ALSO` / `SISTER RULES` / `RELATED AND DISTINCT` / running-tally citations, several of which AFFIRM their target outright ("This does NOT contradict X, which is correct and names the working route"). The corpus's cross-reference convention is indistinguishable from a correction to any pattern-based classifier, and its prose is saturated with *wrong*, *stale*, *false* because that is its subject matter. A citation is not a correction.

THE TIER-3 FILTER IS ALSO WRONG IN THE OTHER DIRECTION, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. Excluding `RELATED:`/wikilink constructs dropped two GENUINE supersessions — `windows-junction-detection-two-wrong-answers-before-the`, whose whole correction is the flat sentence "Supersedes [[junction-detection-via-cmd-c-dir-al-path]]", and the `absent-remote-branch-...` pair. A genuine supersession is often written in exactly the cross-reference construct the filter removes, so the tightening that takes 75 to 27 FAILS BOTH WAYS and the 27 is not merely inflated — it is a different set from the true one.

WHAT ACTUALLY SETTLED IT WAS A SECOND, ORTHOGONAL INSTRUMENT, not a tighter window. Scanning all 1,432 values for strong supersession language (supersed*/retract*/"central premise of"/withdraw*/rescind*/revoke*/"replaces the memory|claim|method|rule|account|note") and keeping only occurrences whose window also names a real key or carries a wikilink returned SEVEN occurrences — small enough to read whole, and it recovered both edges the tier-3 filter had dropped. Controls: a nonsense token read 0 across the corpus; a near-miss pass looking for supersession language next to a key-SHAPED token that is not a key (the truncated-key hazard) read 0, so no corrector names a memory by a name my matcher could not resolve.

VERDICTS — 7 RETRACTED, 19 KEPT from the tier-3 set plus 2 recovered from outside it, 1 needing no action.

RETRACTED (central prescription wrong; acting on the text as written does harm):
1. `reap-discharge-path-for-agentless-trees` <- `agentless-tree-report-is-on-disk-by-agent-id`, which says in terms "THIS CORRECTS THE CENTRAL PREMISE OF ... That is false wherever a transcript survives." 2647 -> 3666. Header preserves the nothing-to-lose conjunction as the explicit SECOND-CHOICE fallback, which is what the corrector prescribes, and records that the memory's loops.md "section 5" citation was renumbered to section 4 on 2026-09-11.
2. `audit-reopen-scan-over-jsonl` <- `audit-reopen-scan-must-be-time-keyed` ("supersedes the method in") AND `audit-scan-must-read-db-not-export` ("second correction to"). 1878 -> 3058. Its PR-keyed selection predicate is blind to the population it exists to find, and its own positive control passed while it was blind. Header keeps the two jq gotchas and the control principle, which nothing disputes.
3. `junction-detection-via-cmd-c-dir-al-path` <- `windows-junction-detection-two-wrong-answers-before-the` ("Supersedes [[...]]"). 806 -> 1825. Its prescribed replacement detector, `fsutil file queryfileid`, was measured returning a DIFFERENT id for a control junction, so it calls a real junction "not a junction" — the same fail-open answer, on the one path that has already emptied the mayor's real node_modules twice.

PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED (a named, load-bearing half replaced; the corrector affirms the rest explicitly, so a bare "RETRACTED" banner would itself be false):
4. `audit-reopen-scan-must-be-time-keyed` <- `audit-scan-must-read-db-not-export` ("second correction to ... and audit-reopen-scan-must-be-time-keyed"). 1978 -> 2999. Time-keying stands; its CORRECTED SCAN still reads the EXPORT, which lags the database until a checkpoint runs.
5. `commit-subject-is-not-its-contents` <- `checkout-rev-path-stages-silently` ("Supersedes the git-add-A hypothesis in ... the detector there is right, the mechanism named here is the real one"). 2042 -> 3010. The MECHANISM paragraph is wrong and the remedy it implies — "stage explicit paths, never git add -A" — cannot fire, because `git checkout <rev> -- <path>` had already staged the files.
6. `two-cljs-clojure-traps-found-by-the-rf2` <- `correction-addition-to-the-map-fixture-trap-supersedes` ("supersedes the over-broad claim in"). 1955 -> 2926. Trap (2) is recorded as a general CLJ/CLJS hazard and is clojure.test ONLY; a reader acting on it breaks a correct cljs.test map fixture.
7. `close-reason-does-not-survive-a-reopen-put-the-discharge-in-a-comment` <- `audit-reopens-a-parent-when-a-discovered-descendant-lands` ("SUPERSEDES the mechanism half of ... That memory RULE still stands on its own merits"). 2271 -> 3356. The diagnosis of why rf2-hic-055 kept reopening was refuted by its own remedy; the comment-the-discharge rule is unaffected.

NO ACTION NEEDED — ALREADY SELF-RETRACTED: `single-bead-close-reversion-distinct-from-jsonl-timetravel` already opens "SUPERSEDED IN ITS CONCLUSION — see audit-reopens-are-recorded-as-comments-not-notes". A census of the corpus for a retraction-shaped opening banner found 12 such memories, so RETRACTION-IN-PLACE IS AN ESTABLISHED CONVENTION HERE RATHER THAN A NEW MECHANISM — the header shape used in this pass matches what was already there. Separately, `absent-remote-branch-is-the-signature-of-a-merge` carries its own dated inline CORRECTION for the instruction `hygiene-cannot-tell-a-strand-from-a-retained-record` names, so that edge is discharged too.

METHOD AND VERIFICATION, since there are no gates and the read-backs are the deliverable. `bd recall` was confirmed byte-faithful independently rather than assumed: all seven originals recalled to files were byte-equal to their export values, differing only by one trailing newline, with CR=0 and U+FFFD=0 (corpus-wide U+FFFD is 0 across all 1,432 values). New values were composed in Python as header + blank line + the recalled original, written to UTF-8 files, and passed as `"$(cat <file>)"` so backticks could not be command-substituted; no header begins with `---`. Every write printed the `Updated [key]` overwrite tell at exit 0. Each was then verified by recall: after == composed value byte-for-byte; the original preserved VERBATIM AS A SUFFIX; header probe 1, a short single-line interior probe taken from deep in the original 1, a nonsense control 0, with backtick and em-dash counts preserved. Final re-export: 1,432 memory records, 1,915 issue records, 0 keys added, 0 removed, exactly 7 values changed, total value bytes 2,975,133 -> 2,982,396.

WHAT THIS LEAVES FOR A LATER TIER. Tier 3 as a whole is now materially smaller than the bead's description implies: the genuine supersession set is 7 edges plus 2 already discharged in place, not 27 and not 134. The remaining Axis 3 value is not in re-running the classifier but in the 12 pre-existing self-retractions, which are unlinked from the memories they supersede in the other direction — a reader of the CORRECTOR still has no way to learn that it supersedes something. Axis 1 and Axis 2 remain suspects-not-verdicts and are untouched.
=== ADDENDUM, SAME PASS, 2026-09-21 06:55 AUSEST — AN EIGHTH RETRACTION FOUND BY CLOSING THE WINDOW GAP, AND THE ONE CORRECTOR WHOSE OWN LIST IS INHOMOGENEOUS ===

EVERY WINDOWED CLASSIFIER ABOVE — MINE AND THE DISPATCH'S — SHARES ONE BLIND SPOT: a corrector that names its targets by PROSE ("the two older memories above") and puts the supersession sentence further than a window's width from the keys themselves. Closing it needed no window at all: take the 71 memories carrying strong supersession language, keep those naming any other memory ANYWHERE in the body, subtract the eight already handled, and read the remaining 10. That read cost minutes and found one more.

EIGHTH RETRACTION — `dispatch-brief-fix-mayor-2026-07-25-three` (1491 -> 3079), PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED by `dispatch-brief-push-as-you-go-now-lives-in-the-template`, which says the publishing wording it carries "is the pre-draft version" and that pasting the remembered version "is now actively wrong". Its clause (2) reads "OPEN THE PR as soon as commits exist"; the standing rule is publish AS A DRAFT and mark ready as the author's last act, the draft flag being the interlock because the host refuses to merge a draft. THIS ONE IS LIVE RATHER THAN HISTORICAL — it is dispatch-brief wording, so the failure it causes is a PR merged out from under a working author (#8323 a duplicate PR, #8333 a whole extra PR), and neither merge violated the five-clause criterion. VERIFIED AT SOURCE rather than taken from the corrector: `docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md` carries a "## Publishing the change" section reading "Push continuously, and publish as a DRAFT", with a both-ways control on the grep. Clauses (1) and (3), the reliance-on-CI declaration, the resume-the-same-worker rule and both log hygiene rules stand and the header says so.

AND THE PART WORTH MORE THAN THE EIGHTH RETRACTION: THE SAME SENTENCE NAMES TWO MEMORIES AND ONLY ONE OF THEM CARRIES THE OFFENDING WORDING. `crash-recovery-recipe-push-before-progress` is the other, and it was left KEPT and UNCHANGED (confirmed byte-identical in the final export). Read at source it carries no instruction to open a PR at all — its only mention is step 3's "Do NOT open a PR from them", which is the opposite — and its push-as-you-go prevention line is unaffected by the draft rule. So a corrector's OWN target list can be inhomogeneous, and taking it on trust would have banner-marked a memory that says nothing wrong. This is the corpus's own `mayor-grep-matched-the-string-not-the-behaviour` lesson ("when you are unsure whether a list is homogeneous, SAY SO and make per-item judgement the deliverable") arriving from inside the corpus, against a list of two. READ BOTH SIDES OF EVERY EDGE, never just the corrector.

THE OTHER NINE OF THE TEN WERE ALL FALSE POSITIVES OF A KIND WORTH NAMING, because the word "superseded" in this corpus usually has a non-memory subject: a SPEC PAGE's superseded banner (`a-brief-supporting-detail-...` quoting 012-Views.md), the author's OWN earlier brief text (`a-rule-can-go-stale-...`), a bd FIELD being replaced (`bd-update-notes-replaces-read-before-writing`), a bead NOTE sorting order (`bead-notes-recency-is-not-currency`), a line in a BRIEF (`harness-hard-kills-foreground-at-ten-minutes`), a retired FROZEN STORE (`hot-zone-names-eight-spec-pages-...`), a BRANCH (`hygiene-cannot-tell-a-strand-...`, `receipts-hic081-branch-is-deliberately-retained`), and one already self-retracted (`reap-before-merge-avoids-the-orphaned-branch`). A classifier keyed on the verb cannot see the subject, which is why the final step of this pass was reading rather than filtering.

FINAL STATE: 8 memories retracted in place, 0 deleted, 0 renamed, 0 keys added or removed, 1,432 memory records and 1,915 issue records before and after, every changed value ending in its original verbatim, 416 `merged-pr-audit-pr-*` memories untouched. No tracked file edited, no commit, no PR, both trees clean. rf2-lz6dl LEFT OPEN.

## MAYOR'S VERIFICATION OF THE AXIS-3 PASS (2026-09-21)

Verified at source against a pre-dispatch export rather than relayed.

### Corpus integrity — HOLDS EXACTLY

| check | reading |
|---|---|
| memory keys before / after | **1432 / 1432** |
| keys added / removed | **0 / 0** |
| values changed | **8** (plus one third-party write, below) |
| every changed value ends with its original **verbatim** | **True, 8 of 8** |
| `merged-pr-audit-pr-*` | **416 before, 416 after, byte-identical** — untouched as instructed |
| per-key deltas sum | **8,851 == corpus delta 8,851** — the eight writes account for the whole change |

### MY "9 CHANGED" WAS MY OWN ERROR, AND ITS MECHANISM GENERALISES

I diffed and read **9** changed values against the worker's reported 8, the extra being
`merged-pr-audit-cursor`. That is not the worker's write. The cursor moved
`…pr-10127-merged-at-2026-09-20T17-03-06Z` → `…pr-10128-merged-at-2026-09-20T20-24-53Z`, and PR
**#10128 merged at 20:24:53Z**, which is **06:24:53 local** — **after my baseline snapshot at
06:18:16 and before the dispatch at 06:31:51**. The out-of-repo merge-audit harness wrote it in that
gap.

**A BASELINE TAKEN BEFORE THE DISPATCH WINDOW SILENTLY ABSORBS EVERY THIRD-PARTY WRITE THAT LANDS IN
THE GAP, AND PRESENTS IT AS THE WORKER'S.** This is the contaminated-baseline hazard CLAUDE.md states
for the shadow-cljs lane — *"re-take any baseline captured in the window, since a contaminated baseline
poisons every column measured against it"* — arriving through a different door, with an autonomous
harness rather than a peer worker as the third party. **It fails toward accusing the worker**, which is
the expensive direction: the reflex on a count mismatch is to doubt the agent, and here the agent was
right. The guard is to take the baseline at the moment of dispatch, or to attribute every diff by its
own evidence before counting it.

### ONE FIGURE OF THE WORKER'S IS WRONG, AND IT IS NOT MATERIAL

It reported corpus-after value bytes **2,986,073**; measured **2,983,984**, a difference of **2,089**.
Its own eight per-key before/after lengths are identical to mine and sum correctly to 8,851, so the
slip is confined to one summary total and touches no verdict.

### THE RETRACTION SHAPE IS BETTER THAN THE ONE I SPECIFIED

I prescribed a single `RETRACTED` banner. The worker refused it for the five PARTIAL cases on the
grounds that one would be FALSE there, and used two banner words plus an explicit WHAT STANDS clause.
Read at source on `junction-detection-via-cmd-c-dir-al-path`, the header names the superseding memory,
states that the replacement detector `fsutil file queryfileid` was itself **measured failing** against
a deliberately created control junction — the same fail-open answer as the form it replaced, on the one
path that has twice emptied the mayor's real `node_modules` — names the working detector
(`Get-Item -Force`, `ReparsePoint` + `LinkType`/`Target`), and then separately preserves what still
stands. **That is a better artefact than the instruction that produced it.**

### FOUR CORRECTIONS THE WORKER MADE TO ME

1. **My tightening is LOSSY, not merely noisy.** 27 is a DIFFERENT SET, not an inflated superset: two
   genuine supersessions sit inside the `RELATED:`/wikilink construct the filter strips, one of them
   carrying its whole correction in the flat closing line `Supersedes [[…]]`. What found them was a
   SECOND ORTHOGONAL INSTRUMENT (scan for supersession language, keep only windows naming a real key →
   7, small enough to read whole), then a third pass for correctors naming targets in PROSE → an
   eighth. **Final: 8 genuine — 3 full, 5 partial — 19 kept.**
2. **Retraction-in-place is an ESTABLISHED CONVENTION here, not a new mechanism** — 12 memories already
   open with such a banner, and two of my 27 needed no action because they were already discharged
   that way.
3. **A corrector's target list can be INHOMOGENEOUS.** One names two memories as superseded; read at
   source only one carries the offending wording, and `crash-recovery-recipe-push-before-progress`
   never says to open a PR at all (its only mention is *"Do NOT open a PR from them"*). Left KEPT and
   byte-identical. **Taking the corrector on trust would have banner-marked a memory that says nothing
   wrong.**
4. Its funnel re-derived HIGHER at the wide end (171 / 85 / 26 against my 134 / 75 / 27) on a wider
   vocabulary — which is the right direction for a filter whose failure is dropping real edges.

### AND ONE CORRECTION BACK TO THE WORKER, IN ITS FAVOUR

It reported that `bd remember <bare existing key>` positionally **recalls instead of storing**, calling
it *"lethal for a short slug-like value"*. **Verified — and it is LOUD, not silent**, so it does not
belong in the silent-misreport class this project catalogues. Measured on a throwaway key: the bare
existing key prints

    (recalled "<key>" -- a bare existing key READS. To overwrite: `bd remember "<new content>" --key <key>`)

and a bare NON-existing key is refused outright with `Error: no memory named "<key>" to recall -- and
refusing to store a bare key-like token as its own content.` Both arms announce exactly what happened
and name the correct form. **A surprise, not a trap**, so it is recorded here and deliberately NOT
filed as a memory.

### What remains on this item

**Tier 0 — the 416 `merged-pr-audit-pr-*` memories, 29% of the corpus — is UNTOUCHED and remains an
unmade OPERATOR RULING.** CLAUDE.md's rf2-ornb currently says *"authorises deleting nothing"*.

The worker's closing observation, recorded and deliberately NOT dispatched: **the 12 pre-existing
self-retractions are unlinked in the OTHER direction** — a reader of the corrector cannot learn it
supersedes something. The harm-preventing direction (a reader of the stale memory meets the retraction)
is now done for all 8. The reverse direction prevents no harm, and the stance says we do not need to
litigate every last fine detail.

## TIER 0 EXECUTED — MIKE RULED "do further cleanup and trimming of memories" (2026-09-21)

### The 416 per-PR memories are GONE. Corpus 1432 -> 1016.

**First, the check that made it safe rather than a treadmill.** The class is CLOSED: per-PR keys run
`merged-pr-audit-pr-9455 .. 9874` and stop, while the cursor stands at **#10128** — **254 merges
later**. So the rf2-ornb prohibition on WRITING them already took effect; only the cursor still

**Recovery confirmed BEFORE deleting**, not asserted: `merged-pr-audit-pr-9874` read **2,500 bytes**
out of the committed `.beads/issues.jsonl` at `4520025651`. Every deleted memory remains recoverable
with `git show <rev>:.beads/issues.jsonl` and a `jq` select on the `.key` identity field.

**Verified by diff against a fresh pre-trim export:**

| check | reading |

### THE DELETION LOOP FAILED 416/416 FIRST, AND I THREW AWAY THE EVIDENCE

The first pass reported **forgotten=0, failed=416** — and I had written
`bd forget "$k" >/dev/null 2>&1`, discarding the one thing that would have explained it. A single
unsuppressed call then succeeded at exit 0.

**The cause: I generated the key list with Python's text-mode write on Windows, which translated every
`\n` into `\r\n`.** Measured on the file: **416 CRLF pairs**, first line `b'merged-pr-audit-pr-9455\r'`.
So `bd forget` was handed `key\r` 416 times and correctly refused each.

**This is CLAUDE.md item (e) — a carriage return riding into a command argument — arriving through a
NEW PRODUCER.** That item attributes the CR to `jq` and says in terms *"The producer is `jq`
(jq-1.8.1), not `bd` and not the shell"*. **Python's own text-mode write on Windows is a second
producer**, and it bites exactly the same way. The guard is the same one item (e) already prescribes
for the data side, applied to the file you are GENERATING: write with `newline=''`, or strip with
`tr -d '\r'` before the file is read. The retraction below was composed with `newline=''` and verified
at **CR 0** before it was written.

**Two fixes, both applied on the retry**: strip the CR, and give `bd` its own `< /dev/null` so it
cannot eat the loop's stdin. Result **forgotten=415, failed=1**, the single failure being
`merged-pr-audit-pr-9455`, already removed by the diagnostic call. All 416 accounted for.

## The structural fact that makes this a problem rather than untidiness

**A memory record carries exactly three fields: `_type`, `key`, `value`.** No timestamp, no author, no
confidence, no supersession link, no "last verified". Measured off `bd export --include-memories`
(31,093,840 bytes total; 1,914 issue records and 1,432 memory records).

So there is **no field to sort by, and no field to retire with**. The only ways to take a memory out of
service today are to delete it or to edit its body so it opens with a retraction.

## Why the PRIME.md override makes this WORSE, not better

`bd prime` emits **4,015 bytes** — byte-for-byte `.beads/PRIME.md` (`cmp` clean). The upstream default
it replaces measures **3,054,319 bytes** via `bd prime --export`. That is a **761x** reduction at every
SessionStart and PreCompact, and it is correct.

But it changes the failure mode. `.beads/PRIME.md` says so itself: *"They are deliberately NOT loaded
into your context ... They remain searchable and you are expected to search them."* **Context cost
became RETRIEVAL cost.** A stale memory sitting unread is harmless; it becomes expensive at the instant
a search surfaces it, and because the store has no recency or confidence field, **`bd memories <topic>`
ranks by topic match alone — a wrong memory about X arrives with exactly the same authority as a right
one about X.**

**`.beads/PRIME.md` is itself an instance**: it states *"~950 memories exist"* against a measured
**1,432**, a 51% undercount. The document written to manage the corpus has gone stale about the
corpus's size.

**And this is not hypothetical — it fired during the session that filed this bead.** A `bd memories
transcript` search returned `agentless-tree-report-is-on-disk-by-agent-id`, whose own text says it
*"CORRECTS THE CENTRAL PREMISE OF `reap-discharge-path-for-agentless-trees`"*. Both memories are live,

## Scope when this is worked

decide whether the named one is superseded, and if so open its body with a retraction naming the
memory that corrects it. The retraction must NOT begin with `---`: `bd remember` silently stores

**OUT:** do not bulk-delete on any of the three axes. Axis 1 and Axis 2 produce suspects, and a memory

citations as a campaign — that is the expensive half of a cheap problem, exactly as CLAUDE.md rules for
the `ai/findings/` case.

claim, which is the same reason CLAUDE.md declines to gate dangling findings citations.

## Recommendation

**B.** Argued from the stance: the value at stake is low friction for the AI that searches this corpus — PRIME.md sends every session to `bd memories` before exactly the operations these receipts are keyed on, and a quarter to a half of what comes back is bookkeeping for PRs whose audit is already recorded where rf2-ornb said it belongs (the commit — all 416; the bead — the 109 that found something). Keeping them buys nothing git does not hold; the 206 already culled on 2026-09-08 proved that in the only way that counts, by nobody noticing. C is gold-plating: it archives an archive. D is done. "Trust the programmer" says: no gate, no retention policy, no script kept in the tree — a one-off loop in a worker brief, with the checkpoint's existing banner as the only ceremony, and the ruling recorded in the one bullet that currently forbids it. "Don't litigate the minutiae" says: do not hand-triage the 416 for keepers; the 109 with findings already have their bead twin, and the rest are "reviewed, nothing actionable" for a PR that merged a week or more ago.

What would change my mind: if Mike wants "was PR N audited?" answerable from `bd` without git (then A — but note it is already unanswerable that way for #9252–#9454 and for everything after #9874), or if he intends to point the harness back at memory for receipts (then A, and the bullet's "forbids WRITING" needs revisiting first, which is a different ruling).

MERGED — PR **#10132**, rebase-merged to trunk as **`dd5ec030ae`** on 2026-09-21. Diff exactly
`CLAUDE.md +1/−1`: one sentence, one file, one line, as ruled under option B.

The deletion this sentence now describes is commit **`5741906ee2`** (416 legacy per-PR receipts
retired); its parent **`4520025651`** is the last checkpoint carrying all 416, and is the commit the
new sentence names as the recovery point.

## DONE WHEN — the bead's own gate, verified at trunk

`grep -c -F 'authorises deleting nothing' CLAUDE.md` reads **0** on `origin/main`. The stale clause
is gone.

## Merge criterion — all five clauses

Band **88**, measured rather than recalled: `LAST` re-derived to `b9220b6dc2ea`, four settled PRs
(#10128-#10131) all reading 88 by ANCESTRY. Rollup **88 / 0 pending / 0 failed** — 67 skipped + 21
success under the case-folded, status-gated filter, the same total `CLAUDE.md` produced on #9984.
Four runs at the full 40-character head `e252624728c38cdb3eb084003370f1eacb42b41b`, all
`completed/success`. Not a draft. Clause 5: merge-base `2a3b8a2911`, **zero** workflow files changed
between it and `origin/main`.

File health at trunk, Python on raw bytes: **CR=161 CRLF=161 bare_LF=0**, identical to the base
reading; 170,514 → 171,993 bytes. `i/lf w/crlf` before and after.

## THE ONE DEVIATION FROM "COPY EXACTLY", ACCEPTED — THE BEAD'S RULED TEXT CARRIED A WRONG NUMBER

The ruled replacement said the deleted class was **31.8%** of memory value bytes. It is not, and the
worker wrote **31.7%** instead, flagged the change, and offered to repush. **Accepted, and verified
independently by the mayor before acceptance**, because this digit lands permanently in the file
every agent reads.

Two measurements, taking deliberately different cuts:

| cut | numerator / denominator | result |
|---|---|---|
| worker, the 416-key class | 947,496 / 2,991,710 | **31.67%** |
| mayor, whole-corpus delta `4520025651` → `5741906ee2` | 946,990 / 2,983,984 | **31.7358%** |

The two differ slightly because they count slightly different things — the mayor's delta includes
the 3 individually-judged retirements beside the 416. **Both round to 31.7% at one decimal place and
neither can reach 31.8%.** Two independent cuts agreeing on the digit that matters is stronger than
either alone. The worker had also eliminated the plausible alternative denominators (value+key
31.41%, whole JSON line 31.37%), and the figure sits at an IMMUTABLE commit, so this is arithmetic
rather than staleness — 31.8% would never have become true.

**Not stopping the dispatch over 0.13pp was the right call and is worth recording as such**: the
bead's five enumerated BEFORE-YOU-EDIT probes all passed, so its own STOP gate did not fire, and
halting a ruled one-sentence change over a rounding slip is litigating the minutiae exactly as the
stance forbids.

## BRIEF VERSUS BEAD ON "CURSOR-SHAPED" — THE BEAD WON, CORRECTLY

The dispatch brief asked the worker to "name both surviving cursor-shaped keys". **The bead
explicitly refuses that framing**, calling `merged-pr-audit-cursor-correction-pr-7568-timezone-comparison`
*"a correction record that shares the cursor's prefix rather than a second cursor"*. Both keys are
named in the landed sentence; the bead's characterisation is what shipped.

**And the mayor's 11 and the bead's 9 were never in conflict** — 11 keys CONTAIN the substring, 9 are
PREFIX-ANCHORED, and the two infix keys are the whole difference. The worker reconciled them rather
than reporting a contradiction.

## A NEAR-MISS THE WORKER CAUGHT ON ITSELF, AND IT IS THE BEST THING IN THE REPORT

Checking the bead's claim that no other cursor-shaped key is ever recalled, its first instrument
counted ALL occurrences across the harness `.py` files and found **323 other cursor-shaped tokens**
(`merged-pr-audit-cursor-pr-NNNN-merged-at-DATE`) — which reads as a flat falsification of the
claim it was verifying. Restricting to lines containing `recall` vindicated the claim **exactly**:
all **477** cursor tokens on recall lines are the bare `merged-pr-audit-cursor`, **zero** variants.

**The claim was sound and the instrument was asking the wrong question** — the variants are written
as receipts, never read back as a cursor. A worker that had stopped at 323 would have filed a
finding against correct text.

It also found the bead's harness figures have drifted (278 `.py` files / 319 recall lines against
the bead's 269 / 320) and **deliberately left them alone**, on the grounds that the harness corpus is
out-of-repo, per-machine and grows hourly, so re-pointing dated numbers at one machine's current
state would make the sentence LESS stable. That is the right instinct about what a durable record is
for.

## GATE VACUITY, DEMONSTRATED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS RATHER THAN ASSERTED

`check_readme_links.py --ci` exited **0**, and the worker established what that green is worth by
PLANTING a broken link at its own line: the gate went **red, exit 1, naming `CLAUDE.md:94`**, with
the fault present only in its tree. Restore verified by blob hash against the committed object
(default form, the `i/lf` case), with `git diff --quiet HEAD` agreeing independently.

**So the gate is live on that exact line — and still could not have failed on this change**, because
line 94 carries zero markdown links against 20 in the file and the replacement adds none. Its green
is a real pass over the file's OTHER links and says nothing whatever about the prose or the numbers
that constitute this diff; those were checked by hand and by the re-derived census. The surface
classifier, handed the PATH rather than revisions, arms **zero** surfaces for it, against a control
path arming 6.

That is the vacuity rule done properly: not "the gate is vacuous" asserted, but the gate proved
live, then proved blind to this particular content.

## Other gates and confirmations

`check_flattened_lists.py` 0 (291 files, 0 flattened) · `check_retired_composition_vocab.py` 0 ·
`check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh` 0 · `check-commit-attribution.sh origin/main` 0 ·
`check-beads-pr-boundary.sh origin/main` 0 · `check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh` 0. Declined: clj-kondo,
`clojure -M:test`, mkdocs (outside `docs_dir`), and **shadow-cljs in every lane — never needed,
never taken**, which mattered because another worker held that exclusive throughout.

**NO MEMORY WRITE OF ANY KIND**, which was this item's single hardest restriction — in fact no `bd`
write at all, reads only. The corpus census reproduced the mayor's three numbers with **zero delta**
(11 / 0 / 2), controlled both ways with two known-present keys true and `merged-pr-audit-pr-9664`
plus a nonsense key false.

AI-attribution trailers declined in both commit and PR body; the harness instruction to edit via
`sed`/heredocs declined per items (u) and (o), the Edit tool and Python-on-bytes used instead.

`git diff --numstat` read exactly `1	1	CLAUDE.md`, so **`rf2-z0pma` and `rf2-u6igq` inherit a
one-line diff** and a clean file. `rf2-z0pma` is next, per Mike's ordering.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. The docs-site mirror page teaches the retired v1 registrars and a `register-*` rule the skill does not carry  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: packaging] [size: S]

description:

At the merged tree, LF-normalized cardinal-rules.md is 16,634 bytes / 124 lines and conformance.md is 16,963 bytes / 108 lines: 250 and 579 bytes above the 16,384-byte guidance. Both are within the 250-line guidance. skills/re-frame2-implementor/spec/design.md:19 and :103 still claim three of the four reference leaves are inside the byte ceiling; only phase-1-decisions.md is. phase-2-impl-order.md already has an exception, but this PR grows it to 22,502 bytes / 102 lines while the central record still gives 20,343 / 99.

Mike's held choice: A, trim the two small overruns while preserving every contract clause; or B, record justified exceptions using the existing tokens-per-session test (recommended). Do not infer that size alone proves a reader problem or impose a split. Either way reconcile the design claim with the result and the central exception record. Use LF-normalized byte counts and explicitly name the measured scope (the four reference leaves); avoid duplicating a size census in design prose. This is the existing held choice, not a request for a new size gate or blanket exemption.

Live nonterminal database and source comments inspected. rf2-gh00n is open but explicitly concerns the fourteen unrecorded authoring-skill overruns, not these two implementor leaves, so it is not an exact match. An explicit Mike ruling may name both scopes; neither silently settles the other. No complete ruling or operator-action-required marker is present.
