Preserve contracts and existing direct routing; no new gate is required.
notes:
DOSSIER (preserved verbatim from ai/decisions/rf2-rker6.implementor-leaf-size.md; two independent reviewers; the file is deleted). THIS NOTE IS THE CANONICAL RECORD.

Depends on / feeds: audit follow-on of rf2-ikbgk.10 (closed; PR #10158 merged 2026-09-21T18:42:21Z with finding 3 held for Mike). Sibling rf2-gh00n asks the same question of `skills/re-frame2` (dossier `ai/decisions/rf2-gh00n.leaf-size-policy.md`, written concurrently). Standing policy ruling rf2-wh25 (Mike, 2026-09-03, landed as PR #9065) and worked precedent rf2-ytkt (PR #9051). Gates nothing; blocks nothing.

## The decision in one sentence

`references/cardinal-rules.md` (16,634 B, +250 over 16,384) and `references/conformance.md` (16,963 B, +579) are over the SHOULD byte ceiling with no recorded exemption: either **A** trim ~830 bytes out of them, or **B** record both exempt on the tokens-per-session test the policy already uses — and under either, correct `spec/design.md`'s false "three sit under the ceiling" sentence and refresh the stale recorded figure for the third leaf.

## The problem, carefully

**The policy.** `skills/README.md:258-331` §Leaf size discipline is the single source of truth (per-skill `spec/authoring-prompt.md` files defer to it — `skills/re-frame2-implementor/spec/authoring-prompt.md:39` says "Leaf sizes are `skills/README.md` §Leaf size discipline's to state — don't restate them here"). The operative sentences:

- `:263-264` — "each leaf file SHOULD be ≤250 lines AND ≤16 KB (target ~150 lines / ~10 KB)"; the byte ceiling exists to catch "long unwrapped prose lines" that "bloat the per-session token load".
- `:272-273` — the exemption test: "would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session?" Two recognised shapes pass it: catalogue leaves (scanned whole because unordered) and dense teaching leaves (read whole because one arc, `:278-289`).
- `:290-323` — the list of leaves "Recorded exempt on the token test, so the next author cites this list rather than re-deriving it", with LF-normalised figures measured 2026-09-13. This skill's `phase-2-impl-order.md` is on it at `:304-309` as "99 L / 20,343 B".

title: False HTTP exact-join claim: named and anonymous work IDs collide
description:
Audit PR #10266 (3506675e8a48a05b498f6329e725a9d0cc257870), source rf2-x8oz5; downstream consumer rf2-6ooch.

The claimed exact HTTP issuance/completion key remains ambiguous for a supported mixed case. registry.cljc keeps independent named [frame request-id] and anonymous [frame event-id] counters, while reply.cljc work-id places either identifier into the same untagged logical-id position. Thus a named request-id equal to an anonymous request's originating event-id collides at the same issuance number. This is concurrent live work, not the explicitly accepted sequential named-id reuse or JVM teardown window.

Measured through real HttpClient transport and trace listeners in audit-sep23-monitor: dispatch :audit/go for anonymous /a and hold its response; dispatch :audit/go for /b with :request-id :audit/go, let /b complete, then release /a. Both issued rows were [:rf.work/http :audit/go 1 1], and both delivered replies carried that identical work-id. Both requests completed; two issued rows existed; only the distinct-work-ID assertion failed. A most-recent preceding issuance join by (frame, work-id prefix) therefore attributes the late anonymous completion to the named issuance.

Required correction: make concurrent anonymous and named logical identities distinguishable in the issuance-to-completion contract while preserving valid user request IDs, anonymous non-supersession, and existing named supersession semantics. Do not ask programmers to reserve event IDs or adopt naming conventions. Keep the fix local to identity/correlation and add a mixed named+anonymous overlapping/reverse-completion regression. Update the owning work-id contract wherever the chosen correction changes it; rf2-6ooch must consume the unambiguous key.

Validation: existing new HTTP trace suite passed 11 tests/55 assertions, exit 0. Added temporary probes gave 13 tests/63 assertions, 2 expected assertion failures and 0 errors (one for this collision, one separately filed for retry wording); source restored byte-for-byte and git diff clean. No exact open Bead recorded this collision when the live ledger was checked.
notes:
== WORKER RESULT (PR #10275, cluster rf2-5g0bt + rf2-ojn0y) ==
KEY SETTLED FOR rf2-6ooch: the anonymous HTTP logical-id is now TAGGED, [:rf.http/anonymous event-id]. Named request-ids are untouched. So the work-id is [:rf.work/http <request-id | [:rf.http/anonymous ev]> issuance attempt], and the join key stays the three-element prefix (subvec work-id 0 3) within the frame.
WHY THIS SHAPE: one form in reply.cljc/work-id, the only place a work-id is built. Four slots are kept, so the prefix join is unchanged. The registry, both counters, supersession and abort are untouched. A caller's request-id can take the tagged shape only by using a reserved :rf.* keyword, so no app naming rule is needed. It follows the existing [:rf.mutation instance-id] logical-slot precedent. Rejected: tagging named ids (it rewrites user handles), a shared counter (it changes named numbering and breaks anonymous never-evict), and a fifth slot (it changes the tuple shape and prefix length).
RED on pre-fix code: http-issued-trace-test 13 tests/71 assertions, exit 1, 2 failures. Both issued rows read [:rf.work/http :audit/go 1 1], which reproduces the audit.
CONTROL: tag removed plus G11 set to full equality gave exit 1 with 7 failures. Restored, and the default-form blob hash equals the committed blob for both files.
GATES: implementation/http JVM 523/4123, exit 0 (predicted +2/+16, exact). test-jvm-implementation exit 0 (21 artefacts). Node lane compile exit 0 with 0 warnings, run 12408/62370 exit 0 (predicted delta 0). No changed form sits in a reader conditional. All 47 scripts/check_*.py exit 0.
MOVED PINS (7, all anonymous work-ids now carrying the tag): issued-trace G3 x3 (:anon/go), G4 (:pair/go), reply-lowering JVM work-id-head (:article/load), reply-lowering cljs work-id-head (:article/load) and self-identify (:e). No named pin moved.
rf2-ojn0y prose corrected in the emit-issued-trace! docstring, the spec/009 :rf.http/issued row and the spec/014 issuance-row paragraph: the issued row carries attempt-1, each completion carries its own attempt, and the join is on the issuance prefix. G11 pins that with a 503-then-200 retry.
Merged-PR audit #10275 (4a43e759d2db3a747a0dce415981b0309ef97ac8; merged 2026-09-23T04:45:49Z). Completeness: Both audit corrections are covered: anonymous identities are distinguished from named request IDs; issuance-to-completion joins are documented as the first three work-id elements within the frame, with retry attempt kept in the full head. CLJ and CLJS expectation pins and all three specified contract locations are updated. Correctness: Independently ran the HTTP issuance/transport and reply-lowering JVM namespaces: 38 tests, 214 assertions, zero failures/errors (gate-http-fix-audit-sep23-monitor-2, exit 0). Removing only the anonymous tag in this guarded worktree produced 7 failures, including the concurrent mixed named/anonymous regression (attempt 1, exit 1); original source bytes restored. The real-transport retry test verifies two sends, one issuance, final attempt 2 and matching issuance prefix. Named IDs, counters, cancellation and supersession paths remain unchanged; CLJS was inspected but not rerun in this audit. Implementation quality: One shared portable identity constructor carries the disambiguation to issuance, completion and work heads without an extra public knob. The anonymous tag follows the existing reserved-keyword convention; no additional application naming policy or defensive machinery is introduced. Retry documentation accurately distinguishes attempt identity from issuance identity. No new actionable defect found. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

DONE — merged as PR #10275 (head 0a373ebb94), a two-bead cluster: rf2-5g0bt and rf2-ojn0y. Worker verdicts are appended to both beads.

rf2-5g0bt (named/anonymous work-id collision): anonymous requests now use `[:rf.http/anonymous event-id]` as their logical id; named request-ids are unchanged. The work-id is `[:rf.work/http <request-id | [:rf.http/anonymous ev]> issuance attempt]`. One form in reply.cljc/work-id, the only place a work-id is built; four slots kept; registry, both counters, supersession and abort untouched; no naming rule asked of programmers (a request-id can only take that shape by using a reserved :rf.* keyword). Mutations already do the same with `[:rf.mutation instance-id]`. Rejected: tagging named ids (rewrites handles programmers chose), one shared counter (changes named numbering, breaks never-evict), a fifth slot (changes the tuple).

rf2-ojn0y (retry prose): the emit-issued-trace! docstring, the spec/009 catalogue row and spec/014 now say the issued row carries the attempt-1 id, each completion carries its own attempt id, and THE JOIN IS ON THE THREE-ELEMENT PREFIX (`subvec 0 3`) within the frame. EVIDENCE. Red on old code: 2 failures, both issued rows reading `[:rf.work/http :audit/go 1 1]` (the auditor's collision reproduced). CONTROL: tag removed + retry assertion changed to full equality -> 7 failures; restored, blob-verified. implementation/http JVM 523 tests / 4123 assertions, predicted +2 / +16, actual +2 / +16. All 21 JVM artefacts exit 0 (a :rf.work/http search found no other producer of anonymous work-ids). npm run test:cljs exit 0, 12408 / 62370, predicted delta 0, actual 0; no changed form inside a reader conditional. 7 moved pins, every one an anonymous id now carrying the tag; no named pin moved. `C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/review-sep23`, detached at `034d0c8fc8`. `git status --porcelain` reads 0 lines at the end of the review.

The gitignored `tools/story/.cpcache` in that tree is not from this review. Every probe ran from the scratch directory, whose own `.cpcache` holds the only basis they wrote.

All 25 primary files in the scope file, 19,333 lines, were read in full under `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/`:

Supporting material, read in part:

- the whole of spec 004-Assertions;
- spec 017-Testing-Story: wait-until (~1060-1075), merge rules (1389, 1491), the aggregation rule (2410-2420), the canonicalization set (2644-2668), invariant sentinels (2879-2960), and the determinism strip (3570-3590);
- spec 009-Test-Mode, the Re-run contract;
- `requirements.cljc` (`select-runner`, `aggregate-status`), `verdict.cljc`, and `story.cljc`'s `run-result` / `result-status` facade;
- the UI callers needed for reachability: `ui/play_status.cljs`, `ui/recorder_export_dialog.cljs`, `ui/recorder.cljs:775-821`, `ui/canvas.cljs:415-520`, `ui/shell.cljs:500-600` and `1150-1225`, `ui/sidebar.cljs:690-720`, and `ui/canvas_listeners.cljs`;

### Method

1. Read the whole engine, weighted by the brief's order: verdict, then play settle and ordering, then identity and fingerprint, then golden and diff, then recorder, then frames.
2. Traced each candidate from its public entry point (`story/run`, `run-variant`, `story/is`, `runner-events/re-run!`, the recorder REC and export dialogs, `golden-match?`, `diff-runs`).
3. Confirmed each candidate with bounded, process-local JVM probes. All ran from the scratch directory with `:local/root` deps on `tools/story` and `implementation/epoch`, so nothing was written into the tree. Seven probes, each under 2 minutes.
   - Once a first probe had read a false `dispatched?` failure because `re-frame.epoch` was not loaded, every tape-dependent probe was re-run WITH it loaded (see rejection 3).
4. Tracker: full-text search over a dump of all 2,238 beads, with live controls taken from the same dump.
5. Siblings: rf2-3x7nj.28 and rf2-3x7nj.29 were checked with `check_surface.py` before each filing.

### Findings

| Bead | P | Title |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.30.1 | P2 | The unified run-result folds only `:cannot-run` refusals from the play run-state, so a failed wait-until, a no-match click or a settle error reads `:pass`. EXECUTED: wait-until reads unified `:pass` with 0 assertions against run-state `:fail`; the control reads `:fail`. |
| rf2-3x7nj.30.2 | P2 | The recorder captures fx-cascaded child dispatches as their own steps, so every replay of a chained-event recording runs the child twice. EXECUTED: the session ended at `:audits 1` and both codegen paths replay to `:audits 2`; `:rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id` is the discriminator. |
| rf2-3x7nj.30.3 | P2 | `runner-events` `run!` / `re-run!` / `run-play!` (the toolbar Re-run, the banner Re-run and Run play) set no fresh-run boundary. EXECUTED: Re-run fails a correct counter variant (`:n` 2), and `dispatched?` passes on the previous run's epoch (a false green, the rf2-3okc class through the engine's other door). |
| rf2-3x7nj.30.4 | P3 | `canonicalize` strips `:source` / `:elapsed-ms` / `:runner` at every depth, so golden, diff-runs, determinism, run-hash and plan-hash are blind to app-db and args under those keys; the 017:3576-3579 safety claim is spec-stale. EXECUTED: golden-match true, diff `:same?` true and plan-hash equal on real differences; the `:src` / `:n` controls detect the change. |
| rf2-3x7nj.30.5 | P3 | The recorder's `tag:nth-of-type(N)` fallback replays through document-global DOM queries, so a recorded type or click on an unlabeled canvas element hits Story's sidebar and toolbar; the promised "harden this selector" hint is never emitted. The pure half was EXECUTED; the DOM order was INSPECTED. |

### Considered and rejected

1. One click recording two steps, the click and the dispatch it caused, was RULED "keep both" on rf2-0ae7o.11 and is not refiled. rf2-3x7nj.30.2 is a different mechanism: fx-cascaded children, observable headless.
2. The export dialog's "replay in this story" replaying onto the live frame is already filed by story-ui-evidence as rf2-3x7nj.29.4. rf2-3x7nj.30.3 carries the engine and epoch-baseline half, which a bare app-db reset would leave open.
3. `dispatched?` against an fx-cascaded child: the first probe read `:fail`, but only because the epoch artefact was not loaded. With `re-frame.epoch` loaded, each child commits its own epoch and the assertion passes. Not a defect.
4. A clean second run of the same variant: `reset-state!` runs `run-teardown-walks!` (stub log, run-state and accumulators cleared), and phase 0 re-stamps the epoch baseline (rf2-3okc). Correct on the runtime path.
5. `record!` / `settle-terminal-assertions!` swallowing throws is record-don't-throw by design (spec 004). A throwing assertion handler surfaces through the pending-exception drain as an `:error` record.
6. Check records DO group the schema and causal records minted at the boundary (`result.cljc:899-903`), so check verdicts agree with the run.
7. `check-record` over an empty group returns `:pass`, but plan construction rejects an unregistered check id (rf2-jjhy), so only a hand-built plan reaches it.
8. A zero-assertion clean run returns a vacuous `:pass`, which spec 017:2419 rules on; the related option is held on rf2-0ae7o.13.
9. `with-invariants` around an ASYNC body (a CLJS `story/run` promise) unregisters before the epochs commit and reports vacuous passes. The macro is documented and exemplified for synchronous bodies; a promise-aware form would be a feature.
10. The snapshot-identity `content-hash` is strip-free, so rf2-3x7nj.30.4 does not touch visual baselines.
11. `resolve-strict-conflict` sorts by `pr-str`; that is deterministic and feeds explain only (excluded from plan-hash).
12. A plan `:script` not inheriting through `:extends` is ruled by spec 017:1491 ("Parent scripts never append").
13. `append-dom-buffered` appending regardless of `:recording?` is deliberate (rf2-eztym.3), and start/clear drain the buffer (rf2-x76af2.18).
14. The selector attribute escape (backslash, then quote) is correct CSS string escaping. A newline in an attribute value is not worth a morning.
15. `gen-play-snippet` wrapping inserted assertions as `[:dispatch-sync [:rf.assert/…]]` is fine: they dispatch to the registered canonical handlers and record normally.
16. Document-global DOM queries for hand-authored selectors are author-controlled (trust the programmer). Only the recorder's AUTO-generated positional fallback was filed, as rf2-3x7nj.30.5.
17. `emitted-fx` as the union of the tape and the stub log: the stub log is cleared at teardown and reset, so nothing leaks across runtime runs. The live-frame Re-run leak is part of rf2-3x7nj.30.3.
18. The sidebar Run all reading `:assertions` rather than `:status` is story-ui-workspace's rf2-3x7nj.28.1, not this slice.
19. Plays sequencing on one frame ("Run all plays" / auto-run) is by design: plays share a frame within a run.
20. `select-runner` defaulting to fixed `:headless` while the browser still drives real DOM steps: the capability refusal is reported through requirements-unmet (`:cannot-run`), so the verdict is honest.

### What could not be verified

- No browser and no shadow-cljs lanes were run, per the hard limits. The CLJS-only instances in rf2-3x7nj.30.1 were INSPECTED; they share the executed wait-until shape. Those instances are:
  - a click, type or focus that matches no node;
  - the precondition timeout in the `js/setTimeout` loop;
  - a presence-host `:error`.
- rf2-3x7nj.30.5's chrome collision was read from `shell.cljs`'s render order and the `querySelector` semantics, not observed in a browser.
- rf2-3x7nj.30.3's browser wiring (`play_status.cljs` calling `re-run!` / `run-play!`) was INSPECTED; the engine behaviour was EXECUTED on the JVM.
- The CI script `examples/scripts/serve-and-run-story-play-scripts.cjs` and `play/ci_runner.cljc`, which grade the run-state rather than the unified result, were not executed because they reach shadow-cljs.

description:
## Defect

When one parent macrostep exits a `:spawn`-bearing state and re-enters it (an `:on-error` → `:failed {:always … :loading}` retry, or any `:always`/raise bounce), the transition reducer commits the parent snapshot with `[:data :rf/spawned <invoke-id>]` already naming the NEW child. The fx drain then runs the tracked destroy of the OLD child BEFORE the new child's spawn fx, which is the documented order `destroy-fx` then `spawn-fx` (transition.cljc:3515-3520). `teardown-actor` clears the parent-side mirror `[:data :rf/spawned <invoke-id>]` unconditionally by invoke-id, never checking that it still names the actor being torn down, so it deletes the NEW child's id. The spawn fx then re-populates only the registry slot. The parent ends with a live child in `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawned P invoke-id]` and NO `:rf/spawned` entry. Spec 005:86 says this slot "mirrors the runtime registry slot … Always-written on a declarative spawn". It exists so an action can read its child's id and message or `[:rf.machine/destroy <id>]` it, and that action now reads nil. The `:spawn-all` exit-cascade clear (`destroy.cljc:534-541`, same `teardown-actor` call with nil actor-id) wipes the children-map mirror the same way (inspected, not probed).

## Where

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/teardown.cljc:87-89` and `:110-112`: `clear-parent-data?` tests only that the parent snapshot is present, then `dissoc`s `invoke-id` from `[:data :rf/spawned]` regardless of its value. The step (4c) prune at `:131-136` then removes the emptied map.
- Reached via `lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc:684-726` `destroy-tracked!` → `destroy-resolved!` (`:591-593`, teardown-args carry `:parent-id`/`:invoke-id`), from the `[:rf.machine/destroy {:rf/parent-id … :rf/invoke-id …}]` fx that `transition.cljc:2324-2348` emits for an exited `:spawn` node.
- Public entry: any declarative `:spawn` parent whose single macrostep exits and re-enters the spawning state.

## Failure scenario

Parent `:loading {:spawn {:machine-id :pe/child} :on {:retry :bounce}}`, `:bounce {:always :loading}`. After `[:pe/parent [:start]]`: `:rf/spawned {[:loading] :pe/child#1}`, registry `{[:loading] :pe/child#1}`. Dispatch `[:pe/parent [:retry]]`. The parent is back in `:loading` with registry `{[:loading] :pe/child#2}` (child#2 live, child#1 destroyed), but the parent's `(get-in data [:rf/spawned [:loading]])` is `nil`. With `:fixed-actor-id :pe/kid` the same happens: registry `{[:loading] :pe/kid}` live, mirror `nil`.

## Evidence

Executed with a bounded JVM probe (`probe_e.clj`, frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`). Generated address: before retry, mirror and registry both `{[:loading] :pe/child#1}`; after retry, registry `{[:loading] :pe/child#2}`, `live? true`, mirror `nil`. Fixed address: after retry, registry `{[:loading] :pe/kid}`, `live? true`, mirror `nil`. The control is the before-retry line, where mirror and registry agree. Tracker searched (`rf/spawned … mirror`): no bead.

## Smallest fix

In `teardown-actor`, clear `[:data :rf/spawned invoke-id]` only when its current value is the torn-down `actor-id` (or, for the slot-only forms, the value the registry slot held when the teardown was decided). A mirror already re-pointed at a successor is left alone. Fence: `lifecycle_fx/teardown.cljc` (+ caller args in `destroy.cljc` for the `:spawn-all` form), plus one test. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`.cljc` shared code, no reader conditional: `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh` (`implementation/machines`) and `npm run test:cljs`.

## Decision needed

no

title: Correctness review: examples-patterns — examples/patterns
description:
Surface bead for slice `examples-patterns` of the 2026-09-23 correctness review wave (epic rf2-3x7nj).

Surface: examples/patterns (examples/). Scope: 24 tracked files, 6262 lines; the exact file list is the slice scope file in the mayor's session scratchpad (review-wave/examples-patterns.scope.txt), supporting detail only. Supporting context: prior wave rf2-fn0kx.5.

Frozen review tree: C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/review-sep23 at trunk 034d0c8fc8.

One reviewer reads this slice and files ONE child bead per actionable correctness finding under this bead (labels review-wave:rf2-3x7nj, surface:examples-patterns), appends its report to these notes, and closes this bead with the finding count and ids. The child beads are the fix work; this bead is the review.

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.
notes:
== REVIEW REPORT — slice examples-patterns (rf2-3x7nj.41) ==

## Tree
Frozen review tree `C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/review-sep23`, detached at `034d0c8fc8`. Every path:line in the child beads cites that tree.

## Scope read
I read all 24 tracked files under `examples/patterns/` in full, 6262 lines:
- boot: README 164, boot.cljs 409, core.cljs 221, index.html 21, schema.cljs 156, views.cljs 139.
- long_running_work: README 173, core.cljs 121, index.html 21, schema.cljs 98, views.cljs 201, worker.cljs 419.
- nine_states: README 218, core.cljs 989, index.html 35, stories.cljs 412, stories_host.cljs 124.
- websocket: README 204, connection.cljs 823, core.cljs 132, index.html 21, messages.cljs 626, schema.cljs 320, views.cljs 215.

Supporting evidence I read in part:
- `spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md`: §state machine, the worked example, §Subscription protocol.
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md`: :on-done/:on-error rows 3000 and 3390, §spawn-all child keys at 3808-3812, the child completion protocol at 3860-3890 and the unhandled no-op at 1560.
- `spec/010-Schemas.md` row 7.
- `spec/Pattern-NineStates.md`, grep-targeted.
- `docs/async/http.md` supersession, `docs/machines/examples.md`, `docs/machines/hierarchical-states.md` §Parent lifecycle.
- `implementation/machines/.../lifecycle_fx/{finalize,join,resolver}.cljc`, the parts on completion carriers and per-child :on-done.
- `implementation/http/.../test_support.cljc` :after-ms.
- `implementation/core/.../router.cljc` frame binding around handler and fx.
- `implementation/core/.../frame.cljc`, the :story preset.
- The adapter tests `boot_`, `long_running_work_` and `websocket_cljs_test.cljs`, targeted.

## Method
1. **Prior wave.** I read rf2-fn0kx.5: its close reason, notes and description (7 findings, all fixed by PR #10178), and the child list, which is empty. I also read the earlier examples-patterns reviews rf2-gwye.55/.56, rf2-fzbj.34 and rf2-t9va, with their coverage and no-action sections, so nothing fixed or ruled there is refiled.
2. **Commits since 2026-09-21.** I read the four commits: 59b2178c20 and 144a19fcd3 (the rf2-fn0kx.5 fixes), 38e6913138 (nine-states search and Loading control), and 2e929e7718 (stories.index.html retired).
3. **Probes.** The examples are `.cljs`, so I ran bounded, process-local JVM probes that `load-file` the example sources VERBATIM from the frozen tree. These were `connection.cljs`, `boot.cljs` and boot's real `schema.cljs`. `core.cljs`'s demo-stub forms were read from the file and eval'd verbatim, skipping only ns, mount and run. Only the js-bound socket actor was stubbed. I ran them from my scratch dir on the core, machines and http artefacts, plus schemas for probe 2. Afterwards the frozen tree read `git status --porcelain` 0 lines, and no `.cpcache` there postdates the probes.
4. **Tracker search.** `bd search` matches titles only, so I searched all 2317 beads by exporting them and regex-searching title, description, notes and close_reason. The controls `ws/request` (4 hits) and `websocket` (14) show the search is live.
5. **API names.** I checked the public API names used against `spec/API.md`.

## Findings

| bead | P | title |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.41.1 | P2 bug | boot's failure seam hangs at :loading-deps in the dev build. The :spawn-all per-child :on-done folds the failed /user.json error map into `:user` (`[:maybe User]`), BootData rejects the candidate, and the rollback swallows :on-any-failed. **Executed**, with the real schemas. The root cause is runtime: `join.cljc` runs per-child :on-done for `:error?` finality, contrary to 005:3000/3390/3812. Decision A/B is recorded on the bead. |
| rf2-3x7nj.41.2 | P3 bug | websocket `:ws/subscribe` is dropped in :disconnected/:reconnecting/:failed; in the spec sample it is dropped everywhere but :connected. A topic subscribed while not connected is silently lost, and the README says the opposite. **Executed.** |
| rf2-3x7nj.41.3 | P4 bug | websocket: a clean `:ws/disconnect` from `:active` keeps `:retries`, so the next manual `:ws/connect` inherits the abandoned run's budget. This affects both the example and the spec sample. **Executed**, with a control from :reconnecting. |
| rf2-3x7nj.41.4 | P4 task | the boot demo promises to show :on-any-failed cancelling two siblings, but equal 60 ms delays mean both siblings always finish first. **Executed**, with a discriminating control at a 10 ms failure delay. |

The example also exhibits one runtime bug, not refiled: **rf2-3x7nj.1.2**. The websocket `:register-request` arms its timeout with `:dispatch-later` from a machine action, which front-inserts when it fires.

## Considered and rejected
- **long_running_work, a last `:progress` lost behind `:work/all-done`.** No. The completion carrier is queued (`finalize.cljc` `dispatch-carrier!`) after the action's own `:dispatch`, and the join event is queued after that, so the final tick lands in `:working`.
- **long_running_work, Start disabled outside `:idle` while `:cancelled`/`:error` accept `:start`.** The UI is stricter than the machine; already noted in rf2-fn0kx.5.
- **long_running_work, a hot-reload remount fires the with-let cancel.** Dev-only and not part of the recipe.
- **nine_states, a local append during an in-flight load is replaced by the server reply.** Documented design (core.cljs:422-432), accepted in the #10178 audit.
- **nine_states, Archive while loading.** The reply still folds under the archived view. Pattern-NineStates.md:368 documents this.
- **nine_states, request-id supersession.** docs/async/http.md:313 says a superseded reply is suppressed, not delivered as a failure, so there is no spurious `:error`. The docstring is accurate.
- **nine_states lazy-starts its machine with `[:reset]`, not `:rf.machine/start`.** long_running_work's docstring calls this a smell, but it is style, not correctness.
- **nine_states stories rely on `:preset :story`'s canned-success redirect.** It exists (frame.cljc:2396), and the error variant's own `:fx-overrides` wins.
- **websocket, re-subscribing an already-subscribed topic on `:connected` sends a second subscribe.** Whether that matters depends on the server protocol; trust the programmer.
- **websocket, Connect is enabled during `:connecting`/`:authenticating`.** `:ws/connect` is an unhandled no-op there, so it is harmless.
- **websocket, messages.cljs says a raw dispatch in an action body "would run with no frame".** The router binds `*current-frame*` around handler and fx (router.cljc:3262), so the comment overstates. It still steers readers to the right idiom (effects) and misleads nobody into wrong code.
- **boot, the fx stub calls `rf/dispatch` (core.cljs:149).** It resolves through the router's frame binding. Probed: the seam disarms.
- **boot, re-boot from `:ready` leaves the old top-level app-db slices until hydration.** The main app is unmounted meanwhile and the slices are overwritten on success.
- **`re-frame.registrar/handler` in the demo stubs.** It is an internal namespace, not in API.md, but it exists (registrar.cljc:913) and the canned-stub idiom is corpus-wide. Not a correctness defect.
- **All other public names used** are present in spec/API.md. These include frame-state-value (565), capture-frame, with-frame, frame-root, frame-provider, make-frame, defmachine, reg-machine, reg-view, reg-cofx, `:rf.cofx/requires`, init!, client-root, render!, reg-app-schema and dispatch-sync.

## Could not verify
- **No CLJS compile, browser or Xray run.** The shadow-cljs lane and browsers are forbidden.
- **Finding 1 was measured on the JVM**, with the real `schema.cljs` and the real `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` rollback. The CLJS dev build takes the same `.cljc` join and validation code, which I inspected but did not run.
- **Findings 2-4 ran the example sources on the JVM runtime**, not the CLJS runtime. The logic under test is portable data and pure functions.
- **The stubs.** The websocket socket actor was a stub, and the schemas were stubbed in probe 1 only.

Review of examples/patterns (boot, long_running_work, nine_states, websocket) complete at frozen tree 034d0c8fc8. All 24 files (6262 lines) read. I filed 4 findings, each executed by a bounded JVM probe that load-files the example sources verbatim:

- **rf2-3x7nj.41.1, P2 bug.** Boot's failure seam hangs at :loading-deps in the dev build. The :spawn-all per-child :on-done folds the failed /user.json error map into BootData's `[:maybe User]` slot, and the machine-data schema rollback swallows :on-any-failed. The root cause is runtime (join.cljc runs per-child :on-done on `:error?` finality, contrary to spec 005:3000/3390/3812), so a decision is needed.
- **rf2-3x7nj.41.2, P3 bug.** websocket `:ws/subscribe` is dropped outside :active, and outside :connected in the spec sample. A topic subscribed while not connected is silently lost.
- **rf2-3x7nj.41.3, P4 bug.** websocket: a clean :ws/disconnect from :active keeps :retries, so the next manual :ws/connect inherits the abandoned budget. Affects both the example and the spec sample.
- **rf2-3x7nj.41.4, P4 task.** The boot demo's promised sibling cancellation never happens, because equal 60 ms delays let both siblings finish first.

The examples also exhibit runtime bug rf2-3x7nj.1.2 (a machine :dispatch-later front-inserts); it is not refiled. Nothing already fixed or ruled in rf2-fn0kx.5, rf2-gwye.55/.56, rf2-fzbj.34 or rf2-t9va was refiled.

title: spec/Conventions.md:228 still says inline :reg-sub accepts only the layer-1 db-reader form (stale since rf2-kuky.45; EP-0026 and the implementation accept derived subs)
description:
## Defect

spec/Conventions.md:228 (section "The public rf/image source keys", the :registrations row) still says inline :reg-sub "accepts only the layer-1 db-reader form (fn [db query] ...)". That constraint expired: EP-0026 Inline Registration Grammar (docs/EP/EP-0026-image-api-simplification.md:461-469) records that since rf2-kuky.45 inline :reg-sub accepts derived subscriptions too - a sub declares its dependencies under :inputs in the metadata map, so a :static or :parametric inline sub lowers through the same seam the public registrar uses (subs.cljc lower-inline-sub, via declared-inputs->slots). The implementation agrees with EP-0026, not with Conventions.

This is the governing text for the inline grammar (the same row says each kind lowers "through that kind's own registrar parser"), so a reader who trusts it would refuse or avoid an inline derived sub that works.

rf2-kuky.49 fixed the same stale claim in docs/core/images.md; this row was missed. Verified at trunk 5d74c334bb: grep for "accepts only the layer-1" matches spec/Conventions.md exactly once (and one closed bead record); control: EP-0026's "derived subscriptions as well as the layer-1" sentence is present at :461.

Found while ruling rf2-3x7nj.5.1 (noticed by that item's decision dossier); deliberately kept out of that item's fix because spec/Conventions.md is a hot-zone file and the drift is unrelated to the inline fx/cofx/event metadata defect.

## Fix

Replace the parenthetical with the current rule: inline :reg-sub accepts the layer-1 db-reader form and derived subscriptions declared with :inputs in the metadata map (rf2-kuky.45), lowering through the same seam as reg-sub. One clause.

HOT ZONE: spec/Conventions.md - sequence against any other holder (rf2-3x7nj.5.2's ruling also adds one clause to Conventions' :rf.gen/* row).

## Gates

scripts/check_doc_slugs.py and mkdocs build --strict (no link or anchor changes expected); verify by hand that the table row's column count is unchanged.

## Decision needed

No.

title: story-execution: the recorder captures fx-cascaded child dispatches as their own steps, so every replay of a chained-event recording runs the child twice
description:
## Defect

The recorder captures every `:rf.event/dispatched` trace on the target frame, including CASCADED children: an event dispatched by another event's `:fx [[:dispatch …]]`, and the same for `:dispatch-later`, machine actions and HTTP reply events. Both codegen paths turn every captured event into its own script step. On replay the parent step dispatches the child again through its own `:fx`, and then the recorded child step dispatches it a second time. Every recording of an app that chains events (the ordinary re-frame pattern: submit → validate, request → success) therefore replays with the chained handlers applied twice. The generated test then encodes behaviour the app never exhibited. Worse, the export dialog's default auto-assert (the final app-db captured from the real session) contradicts the replay, so a correct app gets a failing test.

This is NOT the click + dispatch pair that rf2-0ae7o.11 recorded and accepted as minutiae ("one click still records two steps, the click plus the dispatch it caused"). That ruling rests on "headless runs cannot observe a double dispatch". The cascade doubling here is observable HEADLESS, through dispatch-only recordings, on both codegen paths.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/recorder.cljc:988-1013`, `trace-listener`: it filters on op-type, operation, `(:frame tags)`, a vector event and `recordable-event?`. Nothing distinguishes a root dispatch from a cascaded one.
- `recorder.cljc:595-633`, `append`, and `:212-227` / `:229-293`, `event->step` / `gen-play-snippet`: one `[:dispatch-sync ev]` per captured event.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/recorder/play_export.cljc:131-166` / `:176-214` / `:373-440`: `event->step` / `entry->step` / `recording->script-body`, which produce one `[:dispatch ev]` per `:event/dispatch` entry.
- The discriminator already exists on the trace. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:4215-4216` stamps `:rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id` on a dispatch made from inside a handler, while a root dispatch carries none.

Public entry points: `re-frame.story/start-recording!` / `stop-recording!` / `gen-play-snippet` / `recording->script-body`, the recorder toolbar REC, and the save and export dialogs (`play-export/save-dialog-output`, `play-export-events/build-export`).

## Failure scenario

```clojure
(rf/reg-event :p/submit (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (update db :submits (fnil inc 0))
                                               :fx [[:dispatch [:p/audit]]]}))
(rf/reg-event :p/audit  (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (update db :audits (fnil inc 0))}))
;; REC on the variant frame, then ONE user dispatch:
(rf/dispatch-sync [:p/submit] {:frame :story.rec/src})
;; recorded session ends at {:submits 1 :audits 1}
;; recorded :events => [[:p/submit] [:p/audit]]
;; exported script  => [[:dispatch [:p/submit] …] [:dispatch [:p/audit] …]]
;; replay           => {:submits 1 :audits 2}
```

With the export dialog's `:auto-assert?` default (`true`, `ui/recorder_export_dialog.cljs:77`), the generated script ends `[:assert-db [:audits] 1]`, and that step FAILS on replay. Without it, the pasted variant silently documents a double-audit.

## Evidence

- EXECUTED. A process-local JVM probe against the frozen tree (`:local/root` deps, plain-atom adapter, the recorder trace listener installed, the same set-up as `story_recorder_test.clj`) recorded one `[:p/plain]` and one `[:p/submit]` dispatch:
  - recorded session app-db `{:plain 1 :submits 1 :audits 1}`;
  - recorded events `[[:p/plain] [:p/submit] [:p/audit]]`;
  - replay through the rich `:entries` path (`recording->script-body`) read `:status :pass` and app-db `{:plain 1 :submits 1 :audits 2}`;
  - replay through the `gen-play-snippet` `[:dispatch-sync …]` shape gave the same `{:plain 1 :submits 1 :audits 2}`;
  - CONTROL: the non-cascading `:p/plain` replays 1:1.

title: examples-real-apps: realworld_resources :auth/store-session declares :sensitive [[1 :token]] — a silent no-op, so a directly dispatched session ships its JWT raw; the rf2-oxyle fix reached only the http twin
description:
## Defect

`realworld_resources`' `:auth/store-session` declares `:sensitive [[1 :token]]`. That is the vector-relative path, and it redacts nothing. An event's classification paths are rooted at the ARG-MAP (`(second event)`), so `[1 :token]` asks the User map for a numeric key `1`, which no map has. A mark at a missing slot is a silent no-op.

So a directly dispatched `[:auth/store-session user]` ships the JWT RAW into the dispatched-event trace, and on to every off-box sink projected from it. The declaration reads as protection.

This is exactly the defect rf2-oxyle fixed in the managed-HTTP twin (PR #10175, merge `cfe0225795`). That fix never reached this twin: the text of rf2-oxyle's description, notes and close reason contains the word `resources` 0 times. The docstring here still carries the false argument that rf2-oxyle's close reason says "was the reason this survived review": "The incoming `user` arg is itself the positional second element of THIS event's own dispatched-event trace ... so `:sensitive [[1 :token]]` redacts that positional slot too." The handler's `[_ user]` destructuring is a different coordinate system from the classification root.

It is a privacy slip in a flagship example, and a teaching defect in the most-copied spot. A reader who diffs the two twins sees two different spellings of one declaration, each with a confident docstring.

## Where

- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/auth.cljs:211-231`: the registration, where `:sensitive [[1 :token]]` is at `:229` and the false rationale at `:222-228`.
- The fixed twin, for contrast: `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/auth.cljs:174-209`. It uses `:sensitive [[:token]]` at `:207`, and its docstring at `:186-202` explains the arg-map root.
- The mechanism: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc:337` (`redact-with-paths`), and `:377` onward (`redact-event-vec`, which redacts `(second event)` only).
- Direct dispatchers exist today: `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs` dispatches `[:auth/store-session {... :token "jwt..."}]` at `:484`, `:533`, `:566`, `:718`, `:880` and more. The docstring names "test fixtures and any external caller" as the event's audience.

## Failure scenario

EXECUTED, on the JVM with Babashka and the real `re-frame.classification` namespace from the frozen tree on the classpath (`bb -cp <tree>/implementation/core/src probe_token.clj`). The probe projects `[:auth/store-session user]`, where `user` carries `:token "JWT-PROBE-SENTINEL-7c2d"`, through the registration's paths:

```
shipped   [[1 :token]] -> [:auth/store-session {:email a@b.c, :username alice, :bio nil, :image nil, :token JWT-PROBE-SENTINEL-7c2d}]
control   [[:token]]   -> [:auth/store-session {:email a@b.c, :username alice, :bio nil, :image nil, :token :rf/redacted}]
control   [[:nope]]    -> [:auth/store-session {:email a@b.c, :username alice, :bio nil, :image nil, :token JWT-PROBE-SENTINEL-7c2d}]
private rev [[1 :token]] -> [... :token JWT-PROBE-SENTINEL-7c2d}]
private rev [[:token]]   -> [... :token :rf/redacted}]
```

The controls run both ways:
- The arg-map path `[[:token]]` redacts, so the instrument bites.
- The shipped `[[1 :token]]` gives output byte-identical to a deliberately nonsense path `[[:nope]]`.
- The last two lines go through the PRIVATE `redact-event-vec` itself, via its var, not a mirror of it. That rules out a mirroring error in the probe.

The probe exited 0, and the frozen tree's porcelain read 0 lines afterwards.

## Evidence

- Probe source and output are in the reviewer's scratch directory (`probe_token.clj` and `probe_token.out`). The decisive output is quoted above.
- Census over `implementation`, `tools`, `examples`, `docs` and `spec` for `[1 :token]` / `[[:token]]`. The ONLY live `[1 :token]` declaration is `realworld_resources/auth.cljs:229`. Every other hit is `[[:token]]`, or prose recording the rf2-oxyle fix.
- Why no gate caught it: the rf2-oxyle pin (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/example_realworld_password_classification_cljs_test.cljs`, deftest `store-session-event-token-redacts-at-its-arg-map-path`, around `:490-540`) loads ONLY the http twin. Its ns docstring (`:1-20`) says it cannot co-load `realworld-resources.auth`, because both apps register `:auth/store-session` and the image-assembly duplicate-id guard rejects that. Its `:103-105` defers the resources twin to "its own test file". No resources-side pin of this registration exists: the resources observability test's JWT sentinel checks `[1 :auth :token]` inside an error record's `:event`, a different path and event.
- Tracker: a full-text search of a `bd export` (2316 issues) finds no bead naming the resources twin's `store-session` token path.

## Smallest fix

1. `realworld_resources/auth.cljs:229`: change `:sensitive [[1 :token]]` to `:sensitive [[:token]]`.
2. Replace the false rationale at `:222-228` with the http twin's arg-map explanation, or a pointer to it.
3. Add ONE positive pin beside the resources app's existing suite: `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs` already loads `realworld-resources.core`. Mirror the rf2-oxyle deftest: assert `(registration-classification :event :auth/store-session)` is `{:sensitive [[:token]]}`, and that the `:rf.event/v` slot reads `:rf/redacted` at `[1 :token]` with the username visible.

Examples stay test-free (rf2-8cevm). The pin lives in the framework tree, as rf2-oxyle's did. No hot-zone file is touched.

## Gates

- `npm run test:cljs`, the node lane. The app and the pin are `.cljs`, so no JVM artefact compiles either. The `:node-test` build selects `cljs-test$`, and `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:52` puts `adapters/reagent/test` on its classpath.
- CI's `cljs-examples-compile` sweep arms on the `examples/*` surface.

## Decision needed

No. rf2-oxyle already ruled this defect and its fix. This applies the same ruling to the twin it missed.

Merged-PR audit #10316 (423809164fa372d16aa3144a59baf41ba58f615b; merged 2026-09-23T23:33:22Z). title: test-infra: derivation graph-egress leak predicate matches only a leaf EQUAL to the secret, so a projection that embeds it stays green
description:
## Defect

Section (g) of the derivation-algebra conformance suite is the gate that the graph egress boundary (`re-frame.derivation.egress/project-graph`) ships no raw secret. Its leak predicate `contains-secret?` returns true only for a leaf that is EQUAL to the secret token. It never looks inside a string, keyword or symbol. So a projection that EMBEDS the secret inside a larger value passes every "no raw secret survives anywhere" assertion. That is exactly the regression `egress.cljc`'s own `opaque-handle` docstring names as the danger: shipping the CEDN-1 canonical token instead of its hash ("the token PRESERVES the raw value, which would defeat redaction"). The token for the fixture scope is `v[k::rf.scope/tenant s:"tenant-jwt-9f3a-SECRET"]`. It is a string that contains the secret, not one equal to it. The reply-egress conformance suite already closed this gap for its own slots (rf2-3fc89f.7 Finding 2, `embeds-raw-token?` uses `str/includes?`). This suite never got the same fix.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:
- `implementation/derivation-conformance/test/re_frame/derivation_algebra_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:1200-1209`: `contains-secret?`, with `(= v secret-token)` as its only leaf test.
- It is the sole leak assertion at `:1234`, `:1301`, `:1343`, `:1354`, `:1362`, `:1400`, `:1417` and `:1512`. These are the tests `g-live-resource-identity-redacted-at-graph-egress`, `g-graph-egress-for-unknown-frame-fails-closed`, `g-graph-egress-nil-frame-is-unregistrable-and-fails-closed`, `g-graph-egress-is-idempotent` and `gplus-resource-cache-graph-egress-via-the-tooling-path`.
- The boundary under test is `implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc:147-171` (`opaque-handle`, whose docstring names the token-vs-hash hazard), reached from `project-graph`.
- The same predicate is copied at `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/derivation_graph_redaction_cljs_test.cljc:354-362`. That file is outside this slice. These two files are the ONLY tests that name `derivation.egress` or `:rf.resource/opaque` (repo-wide search of `**/test/**`: 2 files).

## Failure scenario

Someone "simplifies" `opaque-handle` to `[:rf.resource/opaque (rf.identity/canonical-bytes v)]` and drops the `hash` step. Every tenant-scoped resource identity then crosses the graph egress boundary with the raw scope and params token inside a string: in the node key, `:id`, `:output`, the work-ledger `:work/id` and `:resource/key`, and the host-transient address. The section-(g) tests all stay green. So does the Xray copy.

## Evidence

EXECUTED as a bounded JVM probe from `implementation/derivation-conformance` on its own `:test` classpath (CLJ_CACHE redirected to scratch, frozen tree left clean). The probe used `with-redefs` on `re-frame.derivation.egress/opaque-handle` to return `[:rf.resource/opaque (canonical-bytes v)]`, keeping the real `already-projected?` idempotence guard so only the leak differs.
- Direct check: `(contains-secret? [:rf.resource/opaque token])` is `false`. A substring check on the same value is `true`.
- Baseline, running the four (g) tests through `clojure.test/test-vars` with their own fixtures: `{:test 4, :pass 58, :fail 0, :error 0}`.
- Regressed: again `{:test 4, :pass 58, :fail 0, :error 0}`. On the graph built exactly as the (g) test builds it, `contains-secret?` is `false` while `(str/includes? (pr-str graph) secret)` is `true`.
- Controls: the predicate's positive half works. The existing `(is (contains-secret? raw))` sanity rows pass on the raw graph, so the instrument sees a secret that is present as a whole leaf. The blind spot is embedding only.

## Smallest fix

Make the leaf test match by substring, and add a `pr-str` fallback so keyword and symbol forms are also caught, as `re-frame.security.gen/contains-string?` and reply-conformance's `embeds-raw-token?` already do. For example: `(or (and (string? v) (str/includes? v secret-token)) ...)` plus `(str/includes? (pr-str v) secret-token)` at the top. Fence: `implementation/derivation-conformance/test/re_frame/derivation_algebra_conformance_cljs_test.cljc`, and optionally the Xray copy `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/derivation_graph_redaction_cljs_test.cljc`. Neither is a hot-zone file. Consider one adversarial control row that mirrors reply-conformance's `sentinel-predicate-catches-a-marker-that-embeds-the-raw-value`: an embedded-token handle must trip the predicate.

## Gates

The file is `.cljc` with no reader conditional around the predicate. Both lanes grade it: the JVM lane `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/derivation-conformance` (in `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh`) and the CLJS node lane `npm run test:cljs`. The Xray copy is graded by the Xray artefact's own lanes.

## Decision needed

No.

title: story: the canvas run-status marker vanishes after a re-run started from the play chip (follows rf2-3x7nj.30.3's rerun!)
description:
Discovered while closing rf2-3x7nj.30.3 (PR #10310, merged at 2b16d6683e). Since #10310 every author-triggered run goes through runtime/rerun!. After a re-run started from the PLAY CHIP, the canvas's run-status marker disappears instead of following the new run. The fix belongs in tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/canvas.cljs, which was outside that worker's fence: the canvas marker should follow the run owner's current run, however it was started.

Fence: canvas.cljs and a Story CLJS test beside the run-owner tests (run_owner_cljs_test.cljc). No implementation/ change; no hot-zone file.

Regression: start a run, re-run from the play chip, and assert the canvas marker reflects the new run. Show it red with the fix removed.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## FIX — PR #10317 (worker/story-ws-3x7nj), 2026-09-24

Premise verified at trunk 51fe95a7fb. The canvas wrote `run-settled` only from the promise of its own `run-if-needed!` resume. `runtime/rerun!` re-prepares under the owner's stored opts, which carry the canvas's own run-key, so the canvas never runs again itself. Only the play chip holds the Re-run's promise, and play_status discards it. After a chip Re-run the section therefore compared a stale generation and dropped the stamp. Because the outer canvas render does not re-render on a generation change, the old verdict could also stand while the Re-run was in flight.

**This fix is NOT canvas-only, and `runtime.cljc` changed.** The item's fence named canvas.cljs alone, but no canvas-only fix exists: only a run's starter holds its promise, and nothing in the runtime announced a settlement.

runtime.cljc:
- Adds the public `listen-runs!` with a private `announce-run!`.
- `prepare-run!` announces each fresh generation as `{:run-key :generation}`.
- `resume-run!` routes every settle path through a `resolve` that first announces `{:run-key :generation :result}`. Superseded settles are announced too, so listeners compare generation against `current-generation`.

canvas.cljs:
- The new `follow-run!` listener, registered at ns load under `enabled?`, is now the writer of `run-settled`. A fresh generation drops the verdict, so the section is unstamped in flight. A settlement records the verdict while its generation is still current.
- `run-if-needed!` just prepares and resumes.

The Tutorial-Playwright `data-run-status` row now says the stamp follows a run however it was started.

Regression: `canvas_run_status_cljs_test` `a-rerun-from-the-play-chip-is-stamped-when-it-settles`. The canvas's own run passes; `rerun-n` then flips so setup seeds a failing value; `rf.story.runtime/rerun! vid {:play nil}` runs, as the chip does. The test asserts the verdict is dropped as the Re-run starts, and that the stamp reads "fail" once it settles. The existing mc87a/oovoq tests stay green under the listener.

Control: CI node-test job 107416574113 ran on control commit a6c4ee5669 (sources back at base 51fe95a7fb, tests kept). The test went RED at the "dropped as the Re-run starts" assertion and at the settled "fail" stamp. With the fix (50973da622, job 107409346262) it is green. The fix sources were checked restored by blob hash, and the control commit was dropped.
Merged-PR audit #10317 (63e118215cb01387943edb775501b714367f58e3; merged 2026-09-23T23:38:52Z). Completeness: All four workspace findings are covered across canvas, grid, workspace, switchers and Run all. The run-owner listener also addresses open audit finding rf2-iftxj, annotated without status change. Correctness: Read every production diff and the actual rerun regression. Compiled plan drives component/substrates/args/decorators, override scope covers both missing render paths, status is preserved, and run generation guards reject stale settlement. Accepted Story JVM 2064/7740 and CI red control (20 failures)/green delta (+12 tests, +34 assertions). Implementation quality: Consolidates previously duplicated plan reads and uses the existing run owner as the notification source. No additional public authoring knobs, no new actionable finding. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: rf2-iftxj.

title: story-authoring-data: run-artifact replay drops every non-dispatch step, so check-property!/sweep-faults!/replay-run-artifact read :pass on a false [:assert ...] and on a headless [:click ...]
description:
## Defect

Run-artifact replay executes only the `[:dispatch …]` / `[:dispatch-sync …]` steps of an `:event-program`. Every other step in the tagged grammar is dropped without trace: `[:assert …]`, `[:wait-until …]`, `[:click …]`, `[:type …]`, `[:focus …]` and `[:flush-presence]`. The replay status is then computed only from dispatch settle outcomes and the tape floor.

The generated-run surface judges each program by that replay status:
- `check-property!`;
- `shrink-program!`;
- `sweep-faults!`.

The spec says a generated program is made of tagged steps (spec 017 §Generated runs), so the natural way to state a property is an `[:assert …]` checkpoint. Such an assertion can never falsify. A property whose assertion is false reports `{:status :pass}` over every seed.

Steps that need a richer runner are affected the same way. A `[:click …]` step, which the play runner refuses under the headless runner, reads `:pass` rather than `:cannot-run`.

This contradicts spec 017 §Script step runner. That section says the play runner "is the single executor across the live canvas auto-run, the interactive step-debugger, and the headless run / replay paths; it does not branch on caller." It also contradicts the rule that a step needing a richer boundary "refuses rather than under-flushing".

## Where

All cites are at `034d0c8fc8`.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/artifact.cljc:300-351` is `replay-into-frame!`. The `(keep … (when-let [evec (rf.story.play.runner/step-event step)] …))` at `:336` keeps dispatch steps only. The docstring at `:323-326` states the skip ("Non-dispatch steps (`:wait` / `:assert-*`) are skipped here").
- `artifact.cljc:384-391` is `replay-result`. `:status` is `refusal → :cannot-run`, `errored → :error`, `tape-red? → :fail`, else `:pass`. No step other than a dispatch can contribute.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/generate.cljc:156-162` is `failing?`. The drivers are `run-seed!` `:192`, `shrink-program!` `:227`, `check-property!` `:300` and `sweep-faults!` `:403`, and all of them judge by replay `:status`.
- Public entry points:
  - `re-frame.story/check-property!` (`story.cljc:1267`);
  - `re-frame.story/sweep-faults!` (`:1279`);
  - `re-frame.story/replay-run-artifact` (`:1194`).
- Contract:
  - `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md:1036-1040` (single executor, including replay);
  - `:3288-3290` (`:event-program` is "the same grammar the play runner executes");
  - `:3428` (a `gen-fn` returns "tagged steps").

## Failure scenario

Register `(rf/reg-event :probe/inc (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (update db :count (fnil inc 0))}))`, then run each of the following.

1. `(story/check-property! (fn [_] [[:dispatch [:probe/inc]] [:assert [:rf.assert/path-equals [:count] 99]]]) {:seed 1 :num-tests 3 :shrink? false})` returns `{:status :pass :num-tests 3}`. The count is 1, so the property is false.
2. The same program as a variant `:script` through `run-variant` reads `:fail`, with one `[:rf.assert/path-equals false]` record.
3. `[[:dispatch [:probe/inc]] [:click ".nope"]]` through `check-property!` reads `:pass`. The same script through `run-variant` reads `:cannot-run`.
4. `(story/replay-run-artifact (story/make-run-artifact {:event-program <program 1>}))` returns `:status :pass`, app-db `{:count 1}`, and one replay step. The assert step was never run.
5. `sweep-faults!` over program 1 reports `:failing []`.

## Evidence

All of this was EXECUTED: a one-shot JVM script run through `clojure.main`, on the `tools/story` `:test` classpath, in the frozen tree. The script and its output are in the reviewer scratch dir (`probe1.clj` / `probe1.out`).
- A0, controls with the same step vectors as variant scripts through `run-variant`:
  - false-assert gives `[:fail [[:rf.assert/path-equals false]]]`;
  - true-assert gives `[:pass [[:rf.assert/path-equals true]]]`;
  - click gives `:cannot-run`.
- Replay and property paths on the same programs:
  - A1, `check-property!` on false-assert, gives `{:status :pass, :num-tests 3}`;
  - A3, `check-property!` on click, gives `{:status :pass, :num-tests 3}`;
  - A4, `replay-run-artifact`, gives `[:pass {:count 1} 1]`;
  - A5, `sweep-faults!`, gives `:failing []`.
- Probe-teeth control A6: a program whose fx throws DOES falsify through `check-property!` (`:fail`). The instrument can see a failure; it cannot see an assertion.

Also observed, and deliberately NOT part of this bead because it sits in the story-execution slice: an unmet `[:wait-until [:db [:count] 99]]` reads `:pass` even through `run-variant`. The executor's `step-fail` does not reach the run `:status`. That is already filed as rf2-3x7nj.30.1 (the unified run-result folds only `:cannot-run` refusals). This bead is the replay path, which never runs such a step at all.

No tracker duplicate. `bd search` on replay, check-property, sweep-faults and "Non-dispatch steps" finds no bead on this.

## Smallest fix

Route replay through the play runner's step executor, as spec 017 already says it does: `rf.story.play.runner-events/exec-step!`, or at minimum its assertion and refusal arms. Then:
- an `[:assert …]` evaluates against the replay frame and records into the result's `:assertions`;
- a step the replay runner cannot prove refuses with `:cannot-run`;
- `replay-result` folds those outcomes into `:status`.

Fence:
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/artifact.cljc` (`replay-into-frame!`, `replay-result`);
- the tests `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/artifact_test.cljc` and `generate_test.cljc`;
- correct the `replay-into-frame!` docstring.

`determinism.cljc` and `golden.cljc` consume the same replay and would then compare assertion verdicts too. That is already in the run-slice (`:assertions` is in `run-hash-input-keys`).

No hot-zone file is touched.

## Gates

- JVM: `clojure -M:test` in `tools/story`. `artifact.cljc` and `generate.cljc` are `.cljc` with no `#?(:cljs …)` change needed.
- `npm run test:cljs`: `generate_test.cljc` and `artifact_test.cljc` also run in the node lane.

## Decision needed

No. Spec 017 §Script step runner already names the play runner as replay's executor, so the fix brings replay in line with it. If Mike prefers replay to stay dispatch-only, the alternative is for `check-property!` and `sweep-faults!` to refuse (`:cannot-run`) a program carrying non-dispatch steps, with spec 017 saying so.
notes:
== WORKER VERDICT (2026-09-24 10:00 AUSEST): FIXED in PR #10321 (branch worker/story-art-3x7nj), awaiting review/merge. Not closed.

Reproduced at trunk 423809164f: a plan with a false :rf.assert/path-equals checkpoint replayed :pass; check-property! reported :pass over 3 trials; sweep-faults! reported no failing fault; a :click step (the headless runner cannot prove it) also read :pass.

Fix (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/artifact.cljc): replay-into-frame! now runs every non-dispatch step through the play runner's own step executor (rf.story.play.runner-events/exec-step!, exceptions via step-exception) and records each step result; replay-result folds them through the play runner's run-state-refusals / run-state-failures and rf.story.result/assertion-records. Status precedence: refusal -> :cannot-run, error -> :error, tape red or a :fail record -> :fail, else :pass. The result now carries :assertions. Docstrings of replay-into-frame! / replay-result / replay-run-artifact corrected; 017 §Run artifact and replay gains a "run every step" rule and the status rule.

Control: step execution removed from replay (one-line anchored plant) -> tools/story JVM suite exit 1, 10 failures across the four new tests; restored with git checkout, restore verified by git hash-object == committed blob.

Note: the item's claim that these .cljc tests also run in the node lane is false (:node-test selects cljs-test$; these namespaces end -test), so they are JVM-graded only.
Chronological audit of PR #10321: remaining tape-evaluated assertion gap is separately tracked OPEN in rf2-0viz4. Artifact replay delegates to exec-step!, whose schema/causal branch intentionally skips; replay-result does not run the boundary matchers. Existing status unchanged.

title: INCOMPLETE: machine spawn-error ensure-set omits destination entry coeffects
description:
PR #10296 at merge 779281870b7b8fbe5d5d7a83999d1815994287e7 repairs the :spawn :on-error guard/action diet but leaves the target entry action without its declared coeffects. This is residual completeness, not a claim that the PR introduced the whole defect.

Executed through the real router, with a registered :audit/child and parent initially :working. The parent has :spawn {:machine-id :audit/child :on-error :errored}; :errored has :entry :capture. The named :capture action declares :rf.cofx/requires [:audit/token], whose recordable generator returns 42.
CONTROL: add ordinary :on {:go :errored} to :working and dispatch [:go]. ensure-set contains :audit/token; state becomes :errored; entry reads 42.
CASE: dispatch [:rf.machine.spawn/error [:working] {:boom true}]. ensure-set is empty; state becomes :errored; the same entry action runs and reads nil. Thus real error-recovery work can write wrong data despite explicitly declaring its input.

Cause: implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/cofx_attach.cljc:575-600 spawn-error-diet-for-event adds candidate guards/actions and calls add-always! for the target. add-always! at line 686 only walks always guard/action diets. It never adds the target's lifecycle entry diet, unlike the ordinary :on path at 718-730. The related on-done/after helpers have the same target-only closure shape; audit them as part of the same small correction, without creating new API.

Correction: include the destination and initial-descent entry actions' requirements for a selected synthetic transition, using the existing lifecycle/target walkers; preserve deduplication and region scoping. Pin a public-dispatch CASE/CONTROL pair with a declared entry coeffect. Check other synthetic target paths for the same omission.

Evidence: ai/gate-entry-cofx-10296-audit-sep23-monitor-3.log/.exit: exit 0 confirms both observed outcomes (it pins the defect, not corrected behavior). Gate root names this worktree's actual loaded cofx source. Baseline touched suites: 40 tests / 83 assertions, zero failures/errors, exit 0. title: adapters: reagent-slim render-to-static-markup writes :xlink-href / :xml-lang / :transform-origin as xlinkhref / xmllang / transformorigin where react-dom 19.3.0 writes xlink:href / xml:lang / transform-origin (and ui_tree's panose1 alias row is the one off)
description:
## Defect

reagent-slim's pure static serialiser `reagent2.dom.server/render-to-static-markup` writes three SVG/XML attribute names differently from react-dom 19.3.0. Its README contract is byte-parity with `react-dom/server.renderToStaticMarkup` (IMPL-SPEC §8.4).

| hiccup | slim writes | react-dom 19.3.0 writes |
|---|---|---|
| `:xlink-href` | `xlinkhref` | `xlink:href` |
| `:xml-lang` | `xmllang` | `xml:lang` |
| `:transform-origin` | `transformorigin` | `transform-origin` |

The practical casualty is `[:use {:xlink-href "#icon"}]`. `xlinkhref` is an unknown attribute, so the sprite reference does not resolve in the static markup.

**Mechanism.** `attribute-name` (`implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs`, about :468-492) camelCases through `template/cached-prop-name`, looks the camel token up in `react-attribute-name-overrides` (about :295-466), and otherwise lower-cases. The override table has no `xlinkHref`, `xmlLang` or `transformOrigin` row. At trunk f6bb999d6e, `grep -c -E '"(xlinkHref|xmlLang|transformOrigin|panose1)"' server.cljs` read 0 (exit 1). The control `grep -c -E '"(strokeWidth|viewBox)"'` read 4 (exit 0).

**react-dom evidence** (installed `implementation/node_modules/react-dom` 19.3.0, `cjs/react-dom-server.node.development.js`):

- `xlinkHref` is a dedicated `pushAttribute` case writing `"xlink:href"` (about :1462-1476).
- `xmlLang` is a case writing `pushStringAttribute(target, "xml:lang", value)` (about :1598).
- `transformOrigin` is in the `aliases` Map as `["transformOrigin", "transform-origin"]` (about :9551).

**One row in the OTHER direction, in a different table.** `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/ui_tree.cljc` `dom-attr-aliases` maps `panose1 → panose-1`, inverted from `standard-names`' `"panose-1" "panose1"`. But react-dom 19.3.0's `aliases` Map keys that row on the hyphenated name, `["panose-1", "panose-1"]` (about :9533), and has no `panose1` key. So react-dom writes the prop `panose1` verbatim as `panose1`. Here slim is RIGHT (it writes `panose1`) and ui_tree is the one off. `panose-1` is an obsolete SVG 1.1 font attribute, so this row is minutiae. Correct it only if it is free: it moves `emit-ui-tree`'s output for `:panose-1`, and `dom-attr-aliases`' own docstring says the table "has not been re-derived" as a whole.

## Smallest fix

Add the three rows to `react-attribute-name-overrides`, with `parity_cljs_test.cljs` rows pinning each against react-dom. Optionally re-derive the ui_tree `panose1` row against the installed react-dom.

description:

The new authoritative populate/patch transitions clear :current-work and suppress/abort the read, but preserve its :refetch-sweep. A later ordinary load-more completion consumes that obsolete cursor and starts unsolicited replacement fetches of previously populated pages.

Reproduction through public events, executed on the exact merged JVM resources sources with plain-atom and a capturing managed-HTTP effect:
1. Register an infinite feed with :refetch {:refetch-all-pages? true}; accumulate pages 0,1,2 with cursor parameters nil,c1,c2 and next cursor c3.

title: examples-patterns: websocket :ws/subscribe is dropped in :disconnected/:reconnecting/:failed (spec sample: everywhere but :connected), so a topic subscribed while not connected is silently lost
description:
## Defect

In the websocket connection machine, `:ws/subscribe` is handled only inside `:active`. The `:connected` leaf records the topic and sends; the `:active` parent only records. `:disconnected`, `:reconnecting` and `:failed` have no `:ws/subscribe` clause, so a subscribe issued there is an unhandled no-op. The topic never enters `:data :subscriptions`, so it is never re-issued on the next `:connected` entry, and the subscription is lost silently.

This contradicts the example's own README: in its offline-queue bullet, "A `:ws/subscribe` records its topic in `:data :subscriptions` ... so subscriptions ride straight through a reconnect". It also contradicts the pattern's rule that subscription state "must survive reconnects" (Pattern-WebSocket.md:23).

`spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md` §Subscription protocol goes further and wires `:ws/subscribe` into `:connected` alone, so there a subscribe during `:connecting` / `:authenticating` is dropped too. The spec already fixed this exact hole for `:ws/send` / `:ws/request` (Pattern-WebSocket.md:58: "or the offline queue would have a hole in exactly the two states a user is most likely to be sitting in"). Subscriptions were left out of that repair.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:
- `examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs`:
  - The `:disconnected` `:on` at `:578-582`, `:reconnecting` at `:717-723` and `:failed` at `:727-743` have no `:ws/subscribe`.
  - `:active` records at `:628-632`, with the comment "Subscribe before we're fully connected? Just note the topic down".
  - `:connected` has `:register-subscription` at `:695`, and the resubscribe on entry is at `:366-378`.
- `examples/patterns/websocket/README.md:161-168`.
- `spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md:23`, `:58`, `:609-623`. Its `:disconnected` (`:397-401`), `:reconnecting` (`:559-571`) and `:failed` (`:583-589`) have no `:ws/subscribe`, and `:active` (`:438-459`) has none either.
- Public entry: `[:ws/connection [:ws/subscribe topic]]`. For example, a room view dispatches it on mount while the socket is reconnecting, or boot dispatches it before `:ws/connect`.

## Failure scenario

A chat app subscribes to `:room/42` when the room view mounts. The wifi blips, so the machine is in `:reconnecting` when the user opens room 42. The subscribe is dropped. The reconnect succeeds, and `:connected` entry re-subscribes only the old set. Room 42 never receives a push, with no error anywhere; an unhandled event is a benign `:rf.machine.event/unhandled-no-op` trace (005:1560).

In the spec's version the same happens to a subscribe dispatched right after `:ws/connect`, while the connection is still `:connecting`.

## Evidence

**Executed.** The probe loaded `connection.cljs` VERBATIM with `load-file` on the JVM. The socket actor was replaced by a stub that records every `[:send body]`, and a stub `websocket.schema` stood in because schemas are inert for this path. Output is in the review scratch dir at `probe/ws.out`.
- A subscribe while `:disconnected` left subs `#{}`.
- **Control:** a subscribe while `[:active :connecting]` gave subs `#{:t/while-connecting}`.
- Drop, then a subscribe while `:reconnecting`, left subs unchanged.
- After the reconnect, the new socket received exactly one subscribe frame: `[{:type :subscribe, :topic :t/while-connecting}]`.

The demo UI hides this: its Subscribe button is enabled only when connected (`views.cljs:158-161`). The recipe does not, and the README states the opposite.

**Tracker.** An all-status search over title, description, notes and close_reason found 0 hits for `ws/subscribe` and for subscribe near reconnect / disconnect / offline. rf2-fzbj.34 inspected "subscription replay" and retained no defect; it made no ruling on this path.

title: examples-capabilities: ssr_streaming's comment on the flaky card teaches the retired missing-state mechanism (card-view renders the skeleton) that the same file, the README and the code say the failed-boundary set replaced
description:
## Defect

The streaming example's comment on its failure-path card describes the RETIRED client mechanism. It says "Client-side that missing delta is the whole story — no `:flaky` entry ever reaches app-db, so `card-view` renders its skeleton, matching the fallback the failed chunk left in the DOM." Both halves are false at trunk: the `:flaky` slot's body is `[throwing-card]`, not `card-view`, so `card-view` is never rendered for it; and `card-view` has had no nil branch since 2026-07-19 — the client shows the skeleton because the boundary finds `:card.flaky` in the final payload's failed set and re-renders its DECLARED `:fallback`. The same file says so twice (the ns docstring: "the client re-renders that boundary's DECLARED fallback rather than every view having to guess from absent state"; `card-view`'s own comment: "No nil branch … A card whose boundary failed never reaches this view on the client"), as does the README. The stale comment teaches exactly the "infer failure from absent state" design the example says it replaced, and "It differs only in its deferred body, and only on the wire" is false too: on the client the failed boundary deliberately does not render its body, which is what keeps `throwing-card` from throwing in the browser.

## Where

- `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/core.cljc:167-173` — the stale comment above `(card-slot :card.flaky :flaky [throwing-card])` at `:174`.
- Contradicted in the same file by `:18-22` (ns docstring) and `:95-98` (`card-view`), and by `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/README.md:133-138`.
- git blame: the comment lines carry `0c0f171013` (2026-07-18); `card-view`'s "No nil branch" lines carry `5da98db260` (2026-07-19) — the comment predates the redesign and was never updated.

## Failure scenario

A reader building a streamed dashboard follows the comment: they expect a failed boundary to "just work" because its data never reached app-db, so they give their card views nil branches that render a skeleton and wrap bodies that can throw on the client, instead of relying on the boundary's declared `:fallback` and the payload's failed set. The comment tells them the wrong layer owns the failure rendering.

## Evidence

INSPECTED; the comment is prose, but its claims were checked against running code. EXECUTED at the frozen tree: `ssr-streaming.core/handle-request` produces a final payload carrying `{:rf.runtime/ssr {:streaming {:failed-boundaries #{:card.flaky}}}}` and a `:card.flaky` chunk with `failed? true` and no delta — the failed set, not absent state, is the signal (the same probe found the static `index.html` byte-identical to the live shell, all four chunks and the payload bar the placeholder hash, so the page itself is not stale). Control that the comment is the outlier: the three other passages above say the opposite and agree with each other. Tracker: no bead names this comment; prior-wave rf2-fn0kx.6 (finding 2) touched this file's footer and README but not this passage.

## Smallest fix

Rewrite `core.cljc:167-173` to say what happens: the flaky boundary's body throws on the server, so its chunk carries the declared fallback marked `data-rf2-suspense-failed` and no delta; the final payload names `:card.flaky` in its failed set; on the client the boundary sees that and renders its declared `[card-skeleton :flaky]` — `throwing-card` is never called in the browser and `card-view` is not involved. Fence: `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/core.cljc`. Comment-only, no hot-zone file; the baked `index.html` source coords are unaffected as long as the line count above the `reg-view` forms at `:83`, `:88` and `:158` does not change (this comment sits below all three).

## Gates

No gate reads this prose. It sits outside any reader conditional, so if the line count changes above a `reg-view` the stand-in page must be re-baked (it does not: the passage is below `:158`). JVM `clojure -M:test -n re-frame.examples-test` from `implementation/core` confirms the file still loads; verify the wording by hand.

## Decision needed

No.

title: xstate-parity dim B: execution semantics (SCXML algorithm: microsteps, selection, conflicts, exit/entry order, raise queue, final/history)
description:
Dimension B of the XState 6.0.0-alpha.59 parity campaign (epic rf2-2n6uv): execution semantics — the SCXML algorithm as both systems run it. Fourteen rows, every one dynamic: macrostep/microstep composition and the eventless depth limit; transition selection (deepest-wins, document order, guard-blocked parent fallthrough, exact-before-wildcard with guard fallback); conflict resolution across parallel regions and the root ancestor fallback; exit-set / entry-set / LCCA geometry for self, ancestor, descendant and disjoint targets with and without reenter; action order and data threading across exit / transition / entry; the raised-event queue (FIFO, entry-vs-transition raise order, always-before-raise, depth limit, external events during a macrostep); done-state and final semantics (compound onDone in the same macrostep, parallel all-regions-final, output evaluation, root final); history (shallow, deep, never-entered default, per-region, reenter); self / targetless / internal transitions and whether timers, children and entry actions restart; guard evaluation and a throwing guard; a throwing action mid-macrostep; wildcard + guard fallthrough; after-timer semantics (cancel on exit, restart on re-entry, root after, two timers, guard-false, after + always); and initial-state entry order.

Method: for each row the SAME chart is written in both systems and driven with the same event sequence. XState side: node scripts under the campaign scratch `xs/B-<n>.mjs` against the installed xstate@6.0.0-alpha.59, using the pure API (initialTransition / transition / getMicrosteps / getInitialMicrosteps) and createActor where the actor loop is the subject; the v6 docs pages and the next-branch test fixtures (microstep.v6, transient, parallelConformance, predictableExec, history, final, internalTransitions, guards, eventDescriptors) and stateUtils.ts are the documentary ground truth. re-frame2 side: JVM scripts under `jvm/B/B-<n>.clj` driven through reg-machine + dispatch-sync with a trace listener, and the pure machine-transition on the registered definition; spec/005-StateMachines.md and transition.cljc / parallel.cljc at trunk fe8de195bd are cited by line. title: schemas: bulk reg-app-schemas has no per-path :doc, so every bulk path now warns missing-doc with no remedy but the singular form
description:

2. Otherwise, treat bulk registrations like the programmatic carve-out: no missing-doc warning. Do NOT invent a new entry shape or API just to carry a doc string.

State which case applied and why. Update spec/001's obligation text (the missing-doc obligations that #10377 edited) so it states the bulk behaviour in one sentence.
