Evidence and scope
Original claim and required correction, preserved verbatim:
## What

Discovered from the ruling on rf2-2n6uv.2.1 (2026-09-24 20:55 AUSEST). That ruling WIDENS `:spawn :on-done`:
- A fn stays the data fold.
- An `:on`-shaped value (keyword / vector-path / `{:target :guard :action}` / guarded candidate vector) becomes a TRANSITION, resolved at the spawning state's own level. This is the `:spawn :on-error` symmetry.

tools/machines-viz enumerates `[:spawn :on-error]` by hand at every projection site and knows nothing of a transition-shaped `[:spawn :on-done]`. So once rf2-2n6uv.2.1 lands, the chart draws a spawning state whose success exit is a FALSE DEAD END.

Measured by the rf2-2n6uv.2.1 Codex review at trunk f798840db7: the current chart projector returns ZERO edges for a transition-shaped spawn `:on-done`, against ONE edge for the matching `:on-error` control.

## Sites (all under tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/, line numbers at trunk 16523099d2)

- `chart/layout.cljc:420-434` — the `:spawn :on-error` edge block in `collect-state-edges`. Add the twin for a NON-fn `[:spawn :on-done]`: event `:rf.machine.spawn/done`, resolved with the same `resolve-tgt` (keyword target = sibling of the spawning state).
- `chart/projection.cljc:217-230` `event-variant` — decide the chip.
  - The compound `:on-done` already buckets as `:on-done` (the ✓ done chip).

- `mermaid.cljc:284-290` (internal action-only notes) and `:524-530` (edges): add twins of the `:spawn :on-error` blocks.
- `grammar.cljc:789` — the static defect mirror of the runtime target validation. Add `[:spawn :on-done]` (NON-fn only) beside `:spawn/on-error`.

- `scxml.cljc:91-95` — the docstring records that `:spawn` is omitted from SCXML export "INCLUDING its `:on-error` parent transition". Say the same of a transition-shaped `:on-done`; the export itself does not change.

## Rule

- ONLY a non-fn `:spawn :on-done` is an edge. A fn `:on-done` is a data fold and must NOT draw anything.
- A `:spawn-all` child's `:on-done` is always a fold, and draws nothing.

## Tests

- Extend `tools/machines-viz/test/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart/projection_cljs_test.cljc` and `cross_emitter_agreement_cljs_test.cljc`: the chart and Mermaid must agree on the new edge.

- CONTROLS:

  - the `:on-error` edge is unchanged;
  - the compound `:on-done` edge is unchanged.
- Red-with-fix-removed: revert the layout twin and the edge test goes red.

- It does not touch implementation/ at all.

title: INCOMPLETE audit handoff: history transition domains (resolution reported)
description:
Recovery of prior merged-PR audit work, explicitly requested by Mike on 2026-09-25.

Source: rf2-2zk0h; status at recovery: closed. No original Bead has been reopened or claimed. This is a new, independently trackable record.

Audited PRs: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/10372

Historical handoff — resolution already reported. This record does not assert that the original defect still exists.

Evidence and scope
Original claim and required correction, preserved verbatim:
Split out of rf2-2n6uv.4.1 (the LCCA ancestor-target fix). Worker lcca-41 reproduced this and correctly stopped on it, because it needs a change to history-resolution code that .4.1's brief excluded. First noticed by worker xseng-2n6uv on rf2-2n6uv.4.2 (closed, PR #10363).

## Defect, executed

Chart: `:p` has children `:b` (with children `:b1`, `:b2`) and a shallow history `:hist`. The machine is at `[:p :b :b2]`, and the recorded history is `{[:p] :b}`. A transition declared on `:b2` targets `[:p :hist]`.
- re-frame2, before AND after the .4.1 LCCA fix: `[:exit/b2 :act :enter/b1]`. `:b` stays standing.
- xstate 5.32.6 and 6.0.0-alpha.59 both give: exit b2, exit b, act, enter b, enter b1. `:b` is exited and re-entered.

## Cause

For the transition domain (the LCCA), XState treats a history target as the history pseudo-state. That node is a CHILD of `:p`, so the domain is `:p`, and everything active under `:p` exits. re-frame2 resolves the history target to its RESOLVED LEAF (`[:p :b :b1]`) before computing the domain. The LCCA of `:b2` and `:b1` is `:b`, so `:b` stays. A resolved leaf can never be a proper ancestor of the source, so the .4.1 LCCA fix cannot reach this case.

## Options

1. ALIGN (recommended). For the LCCA and exit set, a history target counts as the history node's own position (a child of its parent state), as SCXML and XState do. The resolved configuration is still what gets ENTERED. This makes a history transition's exit set the same as a literal transition to the history's parent's child, which is the reading SCXML specifies.
2. KEEP and document. re-frame2's spec already says a restore "behaves like a literal :target" (to the resolved configuration). Record the divergence in spec/005's parity text, so nobody re-opens it.

## Recommendation

Option 1, under the stance and the parity campaign's direction. It is the same geometry principle rf2-2n6uv.4.1 ruled for ancestor targets (align with the ordinary LCCA rule), and it removes a divergence rather than documenting one. It is pre-alpha, so no compatibility shim.
- Sequencing interplay: rf2-2n6uv.4.2 (closed) made history exits use the macrostep-start recording. Keep that ordering; this bead changes only which node the domain is computed against.
- Operator may reverse: this narrows the spec/005 sentence "a restore behaves like a literal :target". If Mike prefers Option 2, it becomes a prose-only change.

## Fence

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc`: where a history target is resolved before `compute-transition-geometry`. Keep the change local to which path feeds the domain computation.
- The machines tests beside the history and geometry tests, e.g. `machine_history_smoke_test.clj`, `machine_active_path_geometry_test.clj` and the scxml conformance tests.
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md` (HOT): the history and geometry passages, including qualifying "a restore behaves like a literal :target" to say the domain is taken at the history node.

## Sequencing

Dispatch AFTER rf2-2n6uv.4.1's PR (#10372, worker lcca-41) has MERGED, because it owns transition.cljc's geometry and spec/005 until then. Re-derive line numbers at that trunk.

## Gates

- `python -m mkdocs build --strict` and `check_doc_slugs.py`, with a planted anchor shown red first.

FIXED under Option 1, as the mayor ruled. A history target's exit domain is now taken at the pseudo-state's own position. What gets entered is unchanged.
- The executed case now gives [:exit/b2 :exit/b :act :enter/b :enter/b1]. xstate 5.32.6 and 6.0.0-alpha.59, taken from the parity campaign's installed copies, give the same.

PREMISE PARTLY DOES NOT HOLD (worker finding): XState computes the domain from the RECORDED nodes, not the pseudo-state.

- For a DEEP restore, XState runs :b's entry WITHOUT its exit. Before the fix, re-frame2 left :b untouched. Option 1 now exits and re-enters it. So neither matches XState in that one case. spec/005 records the comparison.

MAYOR (2026-09-25): Option 1 stands. XState's deep-restore behaviour enters a state without exiting it, which breaks the entry/exit pairing every other path keeps. Copying that asymmetry is not what parity is for, and Option 1 is the coherent rule.

title: Spec truth follow-ups: :sensitive? as HTTP interceptor metadata (spec/014, middleware docstrings), schema-walker hooks 'consumed by re-frame.elision', MachineActionRanTags missing :frame/:transition-slot
description:
## What

Worker apitruth-6blat settled these from the code while fixing rf2-6blat (PR #10429, merged at trunk 2d45737584), and left them because they were outside its fence. Each is the same defect the PR fixed elsewhere. Re-verify each at your trunk.

1. **`:sensitive?` as interceptor metadata.** PR #10429 established that `reg-http-interceptor` stores extra keys on the interceptor's slot but nothing reads `:sensitive?` from it. Request sensitivity comes from the per-call top-level `:sensitive?` or `[:request :sensitive?]`. Yet two places still list `:sensitive?` as interceptor metadata:
   - `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` §Middleware;
   - the docstrings in `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/middleware.cljc`.

   Correct both to match `spec/API.md`'s corrected `reg-http-interceptor` row. Check spec/014 line 191's "whose handler is marked `:sensitive?`" against the same code.
2. **Schema-walker hooks.** PR #10429 established that `re-frame.elision` reads neither schema-walker hook: only the resources `:params-schema` failure trace and the managed-HTTP `:decode` body use them. Yet the `:schemas/extract-*` entries in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc` (about lines 352 and 355) say "Consumed by re-frame.elision". Name the actual consumers.
3. **`MachineActionRanTags`.** In `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` it leaves out the `:frame` and `:transition-slot` keys the `:rf.machine/action-ran` trace also carries. Add them, with the optionality the emit site actually has.

## Ruling (mayor, 2026-09-25, under the stance)

Truth fixes only. Settle each from the code, add no mechanism, and change no behaviour.

## Your fence

- `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md`
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/middleware.cljc` (docstrings only)
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc` (the two `:description` strings only)
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` (HOT; the one schema only)

**Sequencing:** `late_bind/directory.cljc` is held by the worker for rf2-24bwn (PR #10426). Dispatch this bead only after that PR merges.

## Gates

- `python -m mkdocs build --strict` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`.
- `cd implementation/core && clojure -M:test` and `cd implementation/http && clojure -M:test`, with counts unchanged. `late_bind_drift_test.clj` reads the directory, so run it.
- clj-kondo, WITHOUT `--fail-level error`.

All three items were fixed, and each was settled from the code. The four fenced files were the only ones touched, and only in their docs, docstrings and description strings.

1. FIXED. spec/014 §Middleware §Shape and the re-frame.http.middleware docstrings (the interceptors atom doc and reg-http-interceptor) now list the registration metadata as :doc / :tags / :schema, which matches spec/API.md. Each also says that request sensitivity is the per-call :sensitive? or [:request :sensitive?] (re-frame.http.privacy/request-sensitive?).
   - The spec/014 JVM-degradation sentence (old line 191, "whose handler is marked :sensitive?") was false. What check-cljs-only-keys! -> prepare-emit-tags actually does: denylisted query values are always redacted, all query values are redacted when the request is sensitive, and :sensitive? is an event stamp (hoisted out of :tags).
   - Probe on the JVM: an interceptor slot carrying :sensitive? true is stored but inert. The :rf.error/http-interceptor-failed event had no stamp and the URL ?user_id=42 was unredacted. Per-call :sensitive? true gave a stamp and ?user_id=:rf/redacted.
2. FIXED. The :schemas/extract-large-paths-from-schema and :schemas/extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema descriptions now name re-frame.http.privacy-body (the :decode body classification) and re-frame.resources.classification (the :params-schema validation-failure trace).

3. FIXED. MachineActionRanTags gains [:frame :keyword], which is always present in run-action's base-tags, and [:transition-slot {:optional true} <discriminator map>], which appears only on a selected transition's :action.

title: docs/async review in four serial steps: completeness, correctness, quality, holistic structure
description:
Mike asked (2026-09-26) for a review of docs/async/ (8 pages), in FOUR SERIAL steps. Each step reviews the tree the previous step left. It produces a read-only report, which is triaged, and then its accepted findings are applied as one commit. Step N+1 starts only on the tree step N produced.

1. COMPLETENESS: compare what is taught with the full API.
   - Are the happy path AND the unhappy paths discussed?
   - Are errors explained: which error ids a reader can meet, what each means, and how to recover?

2. CORRECTNESS: check every factual claim and every code sample against the implementation (then the spec). Evaluate samples where the code is portable. A spec or implementation defect found along the way is filed as its own bead, not fixed here.
3. QUALITY: review for a human senior developer, against docs/AUTHORING.md.
   - Do the docs make a good tutorial, with progressive disclosure?
   - Are they cohesive and consistent?
   - Are they human-friendly?
   - Do they use good, simple examples that build progressively?

   - Is the current set of pages the right way to teach this?

title: Test-suite pruning: other surfaces with significant unit tests (bench, skills, migration, scripts)
description:
MIKE'S INSTRUCTIONS (2026-09-26, verbatim; for other read "the named surfaces below" where the text says /implementation):

for each distinct surface under /implementation, carefully review the unit test suite and reduce unnecessary testing. The aim is a smaller, clearer suite that preserves confidence in important behaviour, not simply fewer tests or a higher coverage percentage.
Work one artefact at a time (propose an order, largest suites first), each in its own worktree and PR, babysat to green. Use background workers as needed. Within an artefact, work in these stages, in order:
1. UNDERSTAND THE SUITE. Map its structure, the behaviours and contracts it protects, and any tests failing today. Read the implementation wherever you need it to judge what a test actually proves. Record the baseline: tests, assertions, runtime.
2. REMOVE DUPLICATION. Find exact and near duplicates: tests exercising the same behaviour, under the same conditions, with the same failure mode. Keep the clearest one and delete or fold the rest. Similar-looking tests may protect different boundaries or regressions; keep those distinctions. A .cljc test that runs on both JVM and ClojureScript is not a duplicate, and neither is a pair covering genuinely platform-specific code.
3. REMOVE LOW-VALUE TESTS. For each candidate, ask: "What plausible bug would this catch that the retained tests would miss?" Candidates are tests that:
- repeat implementation details;
- verify trivial setup;
- assert little of consequence;
- test mock or library behaviour rather than ours.
Give a concrete reason for each removal, and name the retained test that covers its behaviour. Where it is unclear, plant a fault in the code under test and see what goes red: a test that is the only red for a plausible fault stays. Do not delete a test merely because it is small, awkward, flaky or currently failing.
4. IMPROVE ORGANISATION. Group what remains around behaviours or contracts, and fix unclear names. Fold repetitive cases into a table (`are` or a data table) where failures stay readable. Simplify fixtures and helpers where that makes the tests easier to understand. Do not add elaborate abstractions just to cut lines. Always keep:
- tests that pin documentation or spec wording (the *_guide_truth_* and terminology
tests). They guard prose, not code, so they look weak and aren't;
- self-tests of gates and ratchets;
- tests of documented error ids;
- regression tests for real past bugs, unless a retained test demonstrably catches the same failure.
VERIFY as you go:
- Change in small batches. Before each batch, predict the change in test and assertion counts. After it, run the artefact's suite and confirm the counts moved by exactly that much, with everything still green.
- Then run the repository checks CLAUDE.md requires.
- Treat coverage as supporting evidence, never as proof that a removal is safe.
- Before any shadow-cljs run, ask the mayor for the lane.
Proceed wherever the evidence is clear. Keep uncertain cases and say what makes them uncertain. Do not change production behaviour, weaken a retained assertion, or add replacement tests to hold the count up.

== HOW THIS EPIC RUNS (mayor, 2026-09-26)
- ONE CHILD BEAD PER ARTEFACT, created at dispatch time (a child of this epic), each with one worktree and one PR. A very large suite (core, xray, story) may be split into several children by sub-area, each still one PR.
- ORDER: the census below, largest first. Re-derive the counts at the child's own tip; they are the mayor's regex census, not a runner count, and the runner's own baseline (stage 1) is the authority.
- ONE ARTEFACT AT A TIME within this epic. The three sibling epics (implementation / tools / other surfaces) are disjoint trees, so the mayor may run one child from each concurrently.
- SEQUENCING against live work: never dispatch a child onto an artefact whose test directory a live worker is editing, or whose open PR adds tests there. Pruning and adding in one directory collide at merge and can delete a test that was just written. Record the fence on the child.
- THE SHADOW-CLJS LANE is machine-wide exclusive, and most artefacts have a CLJS lane, so every count-verification run on that lane goes through the mayor's grant and queue. Prefer batching CLJS verification; use the JVM lane freely.
- HOT ZONES: implementation/deps.edn and implementation/shadow-cljs.edn. If a child's test-build wiring must change (e.g. a namespace regex or build id), STOP and report; do not edit them in a pruning PR.
- REPORT per child: baseline (tests / assertions / runtime) -> final; per batch the predicted and measured deltas; each removal with its reason and its covering retained test; uncertain cases kept, with why. The removal ledger goes in the PR body, and a summary on the child bead.
- This is behaviour-preserving work: production code is untouched, and CI must be green on the same check count.

CENSUS (mayor, 2026-09-26, trunk 3dd4182af7; test files and test forms outside implementation/ and tools/, regex count; the proposed order):
bench/fresco 853 (78 files), skills/re-frame2-pair 153 (22), scripts/git-hooks 91 (1 file: test-pre-commit.sh), migration/from-re-frame-v1 88 (2), migration/reagent-to-fresco 64 (35), skills/re-frame2-setup 46 (4).
Below the threshold, SKIPPED unless a child finds a reason: skills/re-frame2-improver 16, docs/design 14, scripts (python gate tests) 9, skills/re-frame2-pair-retro 9, skills/reagent-migration 3, skills/re-frame2 2. examples/ is test-free by rule (CLAUDE.md § Build & Test).
NOTES: scripts/git-hooks/test-pre-commit.sh is almost entirely GATE SELF-TESTS (keep-by-rule), so expect organisation-only changes there. Sequence it after the attribution-guard work (rf2-jp9on / rf2-w1kma), which is editing that file now. bench/fresco is a benchmark harness: separate its measurement fixtures from its unit tests before judging value.

== MAYOR NOTE (2026-09-27), after rf2-by74t.1 (bench/fresco, PR #10578): the census that set this epic's order counts test FORMS, not tests that RUN. bench/fresco's 571 CLJS deftests are compiled and never executed, so only its JS harness self-tests could be pruned (684 -> 661). Wiring a runner for the CLJS tests is filed separately; they get pruned here only after that lands.

title: docs(resources): optimistic tag patch leaves matching list articles unchanged
description:
The optimistic-writes example in docs/resources/how-to/invalidate-after-a-mutation.md:345-348 says :optimistic-tags patches the detail, every list and the feed consistently. Its patch is (fn [old] (update-in old [:article :favorited] not)). Earlier on that same page the tagged list resource stores {:articles [...]} and tags each row by [:article slug]. On a matched list, the shown patch adds a stray top-level {:article {:favorited true}} and leaves every visible :articles row unchanged. Readers copying the recipe therefore get no optimistic list update.

This example was present before PR #10513 and remains verbatim on current origin/main fc45d9978c2d23bad1bc69e3a109c8299dfc1f17 despite the subsequent complete guide review tracked by rf2-e4zsm. It is a concrete missed documentation defect, not a runtime regression introduced by #10513.

Verified the exact patch on the JVM with data {:articles [{:slug "a" :favorited false} {:slug "b" :favorited false}]}; assertions pass that the :articles vector is unchanged and the stray [:article :favorited] is true. implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc:495-520 assigns the same patch to each entire matched entry. Lines 1500-1504 merge exact and tag targets with exact winning, so overlapping forms do NOT double-apply; that is not the defect.

Use a small slug-aware helper that updates the matching article in each supported response shape (the shipped example already has favorite-patch), or separate the examples and scope the claim to the shapes they actually update. Do not change the runtime or add a new API. Evidence: ai/probe-10513-audit-sep23-monitor-1.log in audit-sep23-monitor.
acceptance_criteria: The documented tag-addressed favorite updates both a detail response and matching rows of the documented list/feed response shape; nonmatching rows remain unchanged. Evaluate the shown helper against representative detail and list values. Preserve ordinary runtime rollback and exact-target precedence; no API changes.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #10608, commit "docs(resources): the optimistic favorite flips the article in list entries too".

Defect: the :optimistic-tags example in docs/resources/how-to/invalidate-after-a-mutation.md claimed to patch "the detail, every list, the feed". Its patch was (update-in old [:article :favorited] not), and a list entry stores {:articles [...]}. The feed on that page lives in a session scope, which a :rf.scope/global descriptor never reaches.

Fix: the example carries a slug-aware toggle-favorited helper that flips the matching article under :article or inside :articles, leaving other rows alone; the shipped example's equivalent is apply-fav, not favorite-patch as this bead named it. The comment now says the descriptor reaches the detail and every list in its scope, and that a read in another scope needs its own descriptor. The exact-target :optimistic form is unchanged. No runtime change and no new API.

Decisive measurement: the page's two reg-resource forms and its reg-mutation, copied verbatim, were run through the real resources runtime on the JVM. A detail {:article {:slug "a" :favorited false}} and a list {:articles [a b]}, both unfavorited, were own-loaded; :realworld/favorite was executed for "a"; the cache was read before any reply.
- OLD sample: 2 of 6 assertions fail. The list :favorited values read [false false], and the list's keys read #{:articles :article}, i.e. a stray top-level :article.
- NEW sample: 3 tests / 8 assertions, 0 failures. The detail is flipped. The list reads [true false] with keys #{:articles}. The helper was also evaluated directly on a detail value and a list value.
- PLANTED (= changed to not= in the helper's slug test): 2 failures, the list reads [false true].
The runs were repeated after the final rebase with identical results.

title: machines-viz follow-ups from rf2-qwtkk (PR #10622): nested containers sort child-first, and two comments that misdescribe the code
description:

PR #10634, commit "fix(machines-viz): order nested containers parent-first on any input (rf2-mmfgq)". All three claims were real at tip.

1. NESTED CONTAINERS SORT CHILD-FIRST: REAL, FIXED. xyflow-graph's defensive sort in chart/projection.cljc ranked every container (machine-root, region, compound) equally, so a container listed before its own parent container kept that order and reached xyflow child-first. The parse (layout/collect-nodes) emits pre-order, so only input not in parse order was affected. Containers now rank [1 depth], with depth read off the parent-of chain the projection already builds. The root frame stays [0 0] and non-containers stay [2 0], so leaf order is unchanged. The change is outside any reader conditional, so both dialects change. Regression: xyflow-graph-nested-containers-parent-first-on-reversed-input in projection_cljs_test.cljc. It reverses nested-compound-machine's nodes, asserts the inner container precedes the outer one in that input (non-vacuity), then requires every parentId to precede its child. With the old equal rank planted ([1 0], anchor match count 1), exit 1 with exactly one failure, "parent outer must precede child outer__mid", actual (not (< 2 1)). Restored, and the default-form blob hash equals the committed blob.

2. chart.cljs "re-fits": REAL, CORRECTED. The measured relayout settles under the same this-key. :fit-key already holds that key, set either by the first settle or by onInit, so the relayout does not re-fit. auto-fit-gate-keys-on-layout-key pins this: "a same-key settle does NOT re-fit". The comment now says the relayout fits only if no earlier settle has fit that key, and leaves the viewport and any manual zoom/pan where it was.

3. share.cljs (fn? v) rationale: REAL, TRIMMED. Ids named :fn are keys of identifier-indexed-slots (:states :regions :on :after :guards :actions), so the identifiers? clause keeps them before the (= :fn k) clause runs. The comment now states only what the gate still decides: a :fn slot holding data is kept (pinned by data-valued-fn-slot-survives-sanitisation).

title: Claim incomplete: resource timer rearm tests do not verify cancellation of the prior host handle
description:
Merged-PR audit #10628 (652bcff757f09b7f2e42dbe8ffe2ecbc596e38ca), run 05cbee6c-4f38-4714-b3be-11f5ee0837ff.

The pruning correctly removes timer-reschedule-cancels-prior because it cannot detect the cancellation failure it names. The underlying host-resource contract is still unprotected and needs a focused regression, separately from the behavior-preserving pruning.

Evidence accepted from PR #10628's P1b: skipping schedule!'s cancel only for a positive-delay rearm leaves the entire suite green (869 tests / 7998 assertions at that batch), including the removed test loaded from its base. P1a makes a sibling disarm test red, establishing that the planted code and test copy are live. No repeat run was needed.

Exact-merge source confirms why: timers.cljc:283-310 promises cancel-then-arm and invokes cancel! at :298 before replacing the token-owned table slot. The removed test checks only a changed slot and one keyed table entry. The retained resources_timer_rearm_cljs_test.cljc:118-138 likewise observes replacement of the poll slot and survival of sibling slots, but never observes cancellation of the former host handle. Token replacement suppresses stale callbacks without releasing an uncancelled host timer, so these observations cannot pin the no-zombie-timer promise.

title: Canned HTTP replies omit :correlation that the resources tutorial's reply guards read
description:
Canned managed-HTTP replies carry no :correlation, while the resources tutorial teaches reply handlers that read it.

At 954e86a4fe, docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md guards `:auth.login-form/submit-success`, `:auth.login-form/submit-failed`, `:auth/session-restored` and `:auth/session-expired` with `(second (:request-id correlation))` against `:auth-generation`. The live transport's reply does carry `:correlation {:request-id ...}` (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/reply.cljc). The framework's canned stubs do not: `emit-canned-success!` in implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc builds `{:status :ok :value v}` (plus optional `:meta`), and its comment says the omitted identity facts are ones "no handler reads". So a handler written exactly as the tutorial teaches reads `(second nil)` = nil under `:rf.http/managed-canned-success`, `with-request-stubs` or a canned demo backend, and drops every reply. The result is a login or restore that silently does nothing in tests and in canned-backend demos.

Measured consequence: the RealWorld examples' demo backend (realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs) answers through these canned fxs, so rf2-nahcr (PR #10680) could not use the tutorial's correlation guard for the restore reply and checks the restore window instead.

Two fixes are possible. One: have the canned stubs echo `:correlation {:request-id (:request-id args)}` when the args carry one, which is the real transport's reply contract for that fact. Two: have the tutorial carry the generation another way. The first keeps the tutorial's code testable as written.
notes:
== MAYOR RULING (2026-10-02 00:12 AUSEST): option one ==
Have the canned managed-HTTP stubs echo :correlation {:request-id (:request-id args)} whenever the request args carry a :request-id, matching the live transport's reply contract for that fact (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/reply.cljc). Not an operator call: the tutorial's guard is the documented reply contract, and a test double that drops a contract fact a handler is taught to read is a defect in the double. Omit :correlation when the args carry no :request-id, as the live reply does. Apply it to both canned success and canned failure, and correct the test_support.cljc comment claiming no handler reads the omitted facts. The tutorial stays as written.
== RESULT (worker httpcanned-nhz44, 2026-10-02 AUSEST) ==
PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/10685 (one commit, rebased onto 9c36507278).

Shipped, per the mayor ruling (option one):
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc: a private helper, `with-request-correlation`, attaches `:correlation {:request-id <id>}` when the args carry a `:request-id` and attaches nothing otherwise, as `re-frame.http.reply/base-reply` does on the live reply. `emit-canned-success!` and `emit-canned-failure!` both build their reply through it, and the failure path covers `:error` and `:cancelled` alike. The "no handler reads" comment is corrected.
- Spec 014 §Testing and docs/api/re-frame.http.md state the echo. Neither is a hot-zone file, and neither was in any worker's surface.
- The tutorial is unchanged.

Canned delivery paths, re-derived at tip. Every canned reply is built by `emit-canned-success!` or `emit-canned-failure!`, which are reached from:
- `:rf.http/managed-canned-success` and `:rf.http/managed-canned-failure`, both immediate and `:after-ms`-deferred; the deferral goes through `:rf.http/deliver-canned-reply`, which keeps `:request-id` on the args.
- The route-map `stub-handler`, behind `with-request-stubs` (`:rf.test/managed-http-scope-stub`) and `install-managed-request-stubs!` (`:rf.http/managed-test-stub`). Story's network stubs reuse the same handler.

Key-set pin census: no test pinned the canned reply's exact key set for a request carrying a `:request-id`, so no test flips. The only exact-map pin is in fx_redirect_classification_cljs_test.cljc, and it issues no `:request-id`, so it holds.

title: schemas: :rf.warning/schema-walker-opaque labels a real compiled m/schema root :unknown, not :compiled-schema-object
description:
Found while pruning implementation/schemas/test (rf2-98kzs.15, PR #10699). Production labelling defect (diagnostic only).

`:rf.warning/schema-walker-opaque` stamps `:schema-kind :compiled-schema-object` when `(map? schema)` (storage.cljc, `maybe-warn-walker-opaque!`). A real compiled Malli schema is NOT a map, so registering one at the root reports `:schema-kind :unknown`; the `:compiled-schema-object` kind is only ever produced by a plain map. Spec 009's catalogue row lists `:compiled-schema-object` as a root-shape kind and names "a compiled `m/schema` object" as the first opaque root.

Decisive measurement (JVM, base 5cbce8a842): `(map? (m/schema [:map [:a :int]]))` returned false. The only test of the kind, `schemas_walker_opaque_warning_test.clj::warning-fires-when-schema-is-compiled-map-object`, registers a plain map as a stand-in, so it passes while a genuine compiled root is mislabelled.

Fix idea: classify with `malli.core/schema?` (or the walker's existing opacity predicate) before the `map?` arm, and drive the test with a real `m/schema` value.
notes:
== FENCE (mayor, 2026-10-02 02:02 AUSEST): dispatch only after PR #10699 (rf2-98kzs.15, schemas pruning) MERGES == That open PR edits implementation/schemas/test/**, the directory this bead's witness or fix lands in. Clears when #10699 is merged into main.
== FENCE LIFTED (mayor, 2026-10-02 02:21 AUSEST): PR #10699 MERGED (2026-10-01T16:20:58Z, trunk 09ba2631ac). Dispatchable. ==
== WORKER RESULT (schemasreg-gaps, 2026-10-02 02:37:08 AUSEST): DONE in PR #10704, head 1c62577d7f ==
In maybe-warn-walker-opaque! (storage.cljc), `:schema-kind` now classifies the root with the walker's own `rf.schemas.walker/schema-opaque?` (non-vector, non-keyword) before the local-registry arm, instead of `map?`. A compiled `m/schema` root now reports `:compiled-schema-object`, and a plain-map root still does. I chose this over `malli.core/schema?` because storage and the walker are deliberately Malli-free (Spec 010 §The `:schema` value is opaque to re-frame), and Spec 009's row already defines the root-opaque class as "a compiled m/schema object, a map, or any other non-vector, non-keyword value". Spec 009 is unchanged.
The test is renamed `warning-fires-when-schema-is-a-compiled-schema-object` and now registers `(m/schema [:map [:a :int]])`.
Control: the arm was planted back to `(map? schema)` in a classpath-overlay copy of the HEAD blob. `schemas-walker-opaque-warning-test` then went exit 1 with 1 failure, the `:compiled-schema-object` assertion. Without the plant the namespace alone is exit 0, 10 tests / 22 assertions.

title: resources tests: four tests whose names or prose overclaim (settle-time from-db populate, SSR drain gate prose, hydrate roundtrip, global-scope walk)
description:
## Four resources tests claim more than they check (found by the second-pass prune, PR #10801, and not actioned there)

Each was read at source by the prune worker, not run against a plant. Check each one first, and drop any whose premise does not hold.

1. **No test pins settle-time resolution of a `{:from-db}` target in `:populates` / `:patches`.** Only `:invalidates` has one. `map-form-populate-from-db-scope-seeds-the-resolved-session-key` logs in BEFORE execute, so execute-time resolution passes it equally. Add the missing row, using the `:invalidates` settle-time test as the pattern: the scope changes between execute and settle, and the target resolves at settle.
2. **The SSR drain tests say the drain is gated on work-ledger rows**, but `drain-blocking-resources!` reads entry `:status` only. Read Spec 016 (resources) on what the drain waits for. If the code is right, fix the test prose to describe it. If the spec says ledger rows, file what you find as a bug and fix only the prose that is wrong today.
3. **`resources_ssr` `project-then-hydrate-roundtrip-sensitive-installs-no-row` never hydrates.** Either make it hydrate, or rename it to what it checks.
4. **`wire_key` `a-global-scope-is-never-walked` uses an undeclared owner**, so the declaration gate alone passes it. Use a declared owner, so the test reaches the walk it names. Plant a fault in the walk to show it now goes red.

## Fences

implementation/resources/test/** only, unless item 2 turns out to be a code bug. Prose follows CLAUDE.md's present-tense comment rule.

Read rf2-zbnoc first. Its description has Mike's instructions verbatim (stages 1-4 in order, the always-keep list, VERIFY as you go), HOW THIS PASS RUNS, and the RULING on production-gate floors. Its newest note is the parallel ruling. Work to all of it.

SURFACE, from the mayor's census at trunk 6eadbc59d1. These are CLAIMS; your stage-1 runner baseline is the authority. 37 test files: 23 .clj, 4 .cljc and 10 .cljs (no `*_dom_cljs_test`). That is about 369 deftest forms by raw grep.

RUNNERS:
- JVM `clojure -M:test` in implementation/schemas (CI "JVM schemas (clojure -M:test)").
- The shared :node-test build.
- The schemas boundary production build (:browser-test-schemas-boundary-prod) and the schemas bundle-cost gate also read this artefact. Stage 1 says which test files each one executes. A file that only a gate-shaped build executes is out of scope.

No production-gate script with an RF2_MIN_TESTS floor covers this artefact: the mayor's census found core, routing, ssr and epoch only. Confirm that in stage 1.

PRIOR ART: the first pass was rf2-98kzs.15, PR #10699 (470 -> 368 deftests). Read its close reason and PR body for the removal ledger, the kept-uncertain list and the retained covers. A keep recorded there stands unless a plant settles it. Read its notes for any defects bead it spawned. Do not remove a test a defects fix strengthened unless a plant shows a retained test catches the same fault.

LANE PLAN: Do all reading and every JVM measurement first, with no lane. The .cljs namespaces and any `#?(:cljs ...)` edit go in one scoped :node-test head/base window at the end. If a file you change is also compiled by the schemas boundary production build, run that build in the same window and say so in your LANE REQUEST.

KEEP BY RULE:
- tests pinning docs, spec wording or conformance;
- gate and ratchet self-tests;
- tests of documented error ids;
- tests cited by name or file name outside their file;
- regression tests for real past bugs, unless a retained test demonstrably catches the same failure;
- security and privacy tests: redaction, elision, egress.
Gate-shaped harnesses (e2e, acceptance, integration, crossing, stdio-roundtrip, live) are out of scope.

LESSONS FROM rf2-zbnoc.23 AND .24:
- Five read-only reviewers by contract group, each writing an anchored patch script, plus a per-deftest counter run in both postures (`-Dre-frame.debug` on and off), made every per-batch prediction exact. In .24, every one of 8 JVM batches landed on its prediction.
- JVM plants take 5-15 seconds each, so plant generously.
- The ns docstrings and a gate script's triage note can PRESCRIBE witness reads by design. Read them before calling a repeat redundant.
- Search departed names three ways across the whole repo: fixed-string, whitespace-collapsed and comment-stripped.
- A count-only change, such as per-sample loops folded into single reads, goes in its own commit, apart from test removals. In .24 that one commit was -1898 of the -2017 assertions.

EARLIER LESSONS (rf2-zbnoc.9-.22):
- PR CI merges onto a newer trunk than the branch base, so take shared-lane bases from main's run at the merged commit's base.
- Presence guards (`some?`, `seq`, `(is ex)`) are named-failure reads; keep them.
- Rows that re-run a helper's own self-test fixtures are prime candidates.
- `with-redefs` on `debug-enabled?` cannot reach a gate read at load time.
- Lint at base and head with the CI-pinned clj-kondo 2026.04.15, and fix any unused refer a removal leaves.
- Run git diff --check after every batch.
- The Bash tool halves runs of backslashes, so write scripts with the Write tool.
- Run bd from the worktree root.
- Pass origin/main to scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh and scripts/check-commit-attribution.sh.

Every other documented error/warning id a departing test asserted stays asserted on the same input.

title: mcp-conformance: replace-app-db host-object guard misses the spaced #object [ print form
description:

After #10931 (rf2-azypu), an unknown tag decodes to (tagged-literal tag form), and that prints with a space (`#object [Window ...]`), which the regex no longer matches. title: reagent-slim: prose describes the reg-view form-tag fast path as live, but nothing on the re-frame path reaches it
description:
Follow-up to rf2-hlkv9 (PR #10973). At that PR's head the reg-view expansion records the :reagent2/form tag ONLY in the registry slot's metadata; the render fn carries none. On the re-frame path reagent-slim's wrap-render never sees a tag anyway: it reads (meta render-fn), and the fn it is handed is the head (rf/view id) returns, the frame-aware wrapper, whose metadata is {:contextType frame-context} alone. So reagent-slim's compile-time fast path (the two tagged branches of wrap-render) is unreachable from reg-view and reg-view*.

STALE PROSE, outside rf2-hlkv9's fence (adapter src and spec were never-edit there). Each describes the reg-view expansion as feeding wrap-render's tagged branches:
- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs: ns docstring "Compile-time fold" paragraph (about L22-31), the block comment above argv-args (about L240-244), form-tag's docstring (about L254-258), wrap-render's "Compile-time fold" paragraph (about L305-311).
- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.clj: ns docstring (about L5-12, "stamps the wrapper with ^{:reagent2/form ...} meta so the runtime path can skip the cond").
- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md: the wrap-render bullet (about L332) and section 5.2 (about L638, "on the registry slot's metadata and on the emitted wrapper fn").

- spec/Spec-Schemas.md ViewMeta: the :reagent2/form row's "(an additive perf hint ...)" parenthetical (about L471). The stamping half stays true.

DECISION FIRST. Either (1) correct the prose to say the tagged branches serve only a caller that hands reagent-slim a tagged fn directly, or (2) retire the tagged branches, the classifier and the slot key together. Reading for (2): the tagged Form-1 branch returns a seq result WITHOUT the doall the untagged cond applies, so it would realize a lazy-seq root outside the render Reaction, and a :reagent2/form key on a head's metadata would also be threaded into stock Reagent's create-class spec by its fn-to-class (spec = (meta f)) when both substrates share a classpath. == WORKER REPORT (PR #11034, draft until the worker marks it ready) ==

DEFECT, reproduced and fixed. A flow :area = (* w h) on [[:w] [:h]]: seed {:w 2 :h 2} (area 4), set w 3 (area 6), restore the seed epoch, then set w back to 3. The flows dirty-check cache still held the pre-restore inputs [3 2], so the flow was skipped and app-db read {:w 3 :h 2 :area 4} where :area is 6. replace-frame-state! has the same defect. Two pins in implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_test.clj (restore-resets-the-flows-dirty-check-cache, replace-frame-state-resets-the-flows-dirty-check-cache): red on trunk (exit 1, both :area 4); green with the fix (exit 0, 2 tests / 8 assertions); red again with the fix reverted (exit 1); restore verified by blob hash.

OWNERSHIP RULING (implementation-governing). The reset lives in EPOCH. Flows decides "changed" purely by = against the cached inputs (Spec 013 §Dirty-check semantics), and a drain keeps that cache true because the flow pass runs over every db the drain installs. Epoch's two tool writes (restore-epoch!, replace-frame-state!) install frame-state outside any drain, through core's replace-frame-state!, so nothing re-syncs the cache. They are the only out-of-drain installs where this can arise today: SSR render-state restore! seeds a fresh frame with no cache, and client hydration runs as an event inside a drain. A generic fix at core's install chokepoint needs a new late-bind hook and directory row in core. Re-keying the flows cache on the output slot changes Spec 013's dirty-check contract and the row shape core tests and conformance fixtures read. Both are larger and outside this bead's files. The fix is re-frame.epoch.tool-pair/reset-flows-dirty-check!, which calls the existing :flows/restore-last-inputs! hook with an empty snapshot after a successful install. The hook itself fences the reset to the write's incarnation token, and it runs before the first callback boundary. The next drain evaluates every flow afresh. Follow-up for the core owner: the late-bind directory's description of :flows/restore-last-inputs! names only the router as its caller.

STALE TEXT, all done: the spec/009 silencing-law pinning paragraph (the atomicity file is a decision table, and the single critical section is promised but exercised by no test); test-epoch-prod-gate.sh (replay refusal is pinned in epoch-jvm-prod-gate-test only, and the class-B note drops the 68-of-3608 count because lineage-285 now fails 5 of 13 under the gate); the test.yml comment (comment only, no longer counts the with-redefs deftests, which number four); the reagent runtime_cljs_test restore comment. title: A resource request factory may return :reply-to; managed HTTP then refuses mixed addressing and the entry stays :loading
description:
## Bug

A resource or mutation request factory that returns `:reply-to` passes the resource layer's reserved-key guard. The runtime then adds its own `:on-success` / `:on-failure`, and managed HTTP refuses the mixture at fx time. The developer gets an HTTP "mixed addressing" error naming keys they never wrote, and the entry is left `:loading` with `:current-work` set. Nothing settles it afterwards, because the request was never issued.

## Evidence

Code at 475bdcaacf:
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/transport/http.cljc:54-62`: `reserved-reply-keys` is `#{:request-id :on-success :on-failure}`. It omits `:reply-to`, Spec 014's unified addressing key.
- `transport/http.cljc:93-138`: `build-managed-args` runs `reject-reserved-reply-keys!` and then assocs `:on-success` / `:on-failure` onto the app's args. Resource reads (`events.cljc:818, 1073, 1235`) and mutation execute (`mutation_events.cljc:1440`) all lower through it.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/encoding.cljc:255-279`: `validate-reply-addressing!` throws `:rf.error/http-bad-reply-target` (`:reason :mixed-addressing`) when `:reply-to` sits beside either split key. It runs from the `:rf.http/managed` fx handler (`http/handlers.cljc:385`), after the resource event has committed.

Repro (*probed*: JVM, plain-atom substrate, the real `re-frame.http.managed` fx, run at 989a1c6d53, whose core, resources and http trees are identical to 475bdcaacf):

```clojure
(rf/reg-resource :probe/article
  {:scope :rf.scope/global :params-schema [:map [:slug :string]]}
  (fn [{:keys [slug]} _] {:request  {:method :get :url (str "http://127.0.0.1:9/a/" slug)}
                          :reply-to [:app/article-loaded]}))
(rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.resource/ensure {:resource :probe/article :scope :rf.scope/global
                                        :params {:slug "w"} :owner [:app :p 1]}])
```

Observed:

```
dispatch-sync returned
entry status: :loading  current-work set?: true
error traces: 1
   [:rf.error/fx-handler-exception nil "`:reply-to` and `:on-success` / `:on-failure` are EXCLUSIVE reply-addressing styles per Spec 014 §Reply addressing …"]
```

Contract:
- Spec 016 §Transport (`spec/016-Resources.md:1141`) and §Mutations (`:871`) say the runtime owns reply addressing, and that an app `:request` supplying it is rejected.
- The rejection list there and in the code predates the unified key, so a factory `:reply-to` is not rejected at the resource boundary.
- A caller's call-site `:reply-to` on `:rf.resource/ensure` or `:rf.mutation/execute` is a different, valid continuation. It is not affected.

## Expected

A factory-returned `:reply-to` is refused with `:rf.error/resource-reserved-request-key` inside the resource or mutation event, before anything commits. No entry or instance is left in flight.

## Fix direction

- Add `:reply-to` to `reserved-reply-keys`. The guard already runs inside the event handler, so the event fails before its commit.
- Update the guard's message, the spec 016 sentences at `:871` and `:1141`, and the `:rf.error/resource-reserved-request-key` row in spec 009 to name all four keys.

## Acceptance

- Extend `reserved-reply-keys-rejected` and `reserved-reply-keys-rejected-end-to-end` (`implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_managed_http_cljs_test.cljc:101-124`) to `:reply-to`. Both fail before the fix.
- In the end-to-end case, also assert that no request reaches the transport and that no entry is left `:loading` for the key.
- The same assertion holds for a mutation factory under `:rf.mutation/execute`, with no instance row left `:pending`.
- A call-site `:reply-to` on `ensure` still receives its continuation.

## Notes

- Origin: Opus review (HTTP surface), carried into the resources review. Sol 15 §9 agreed after reading it.
- Read, not probed: other args the HTTP fx refuses at fx time, such as a bad `:retry :on`, leave the entry `:loading` the same way. This bead covers only the reserved key.
- Hot zones: `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (error catalogue row at `:2054`). Sequence this against other beads editing spec 009.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/resources.md` action 3; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/15-resources.md` §9.
notes:
== WORKER RESULT (spec009-cluster, PR #11092, 2026-10-10 AUSEST) ==
FIXED in "fix(resources): a resource or mutation request factory cannot claim :reply-to".

:reply-to joins reserved-reply-keys (resources transport/http.cljc). The guard runs inside the ensure / refetch / execute event, so a factory :reply-to is refused with :rf.error/resource-reserved-request-key before anything commits; the guard message points at the call-site :reply-to. Spec 016's reserved-key sentences at :787, :871 and :1142 (the bead named two; :787 says the same thing, so it moved with them) and the Spec 009 row name all four keys.

Tests (resources_managed_http_cljs_test): reserved-reply-keys-rejected covers :reply-to; the end-to-end case now asserts no request reaches the transport AND no entry is left behind, for :on-success and :reply-to; new reserved-reply-keys-rejected-on-execute asserts the same for :rf.mutation/execute with no instance left.
- RED (test only): ns run exit 1, 15 tests / 35 assertions, 5 failures, all :reply-to (unit not rejected; entry left :loading with :current-work; mutation reached the transport and left the instance :pending).
- GREEN: managed-http + reply-to-reads + mutation namespaces exit 0, 82 tests / 250 assertions. Call-site :reply-to on ensure still receives its continuation (resources-reply-to-reads).
- RED AGAIN with transport/http.cljc reverted alone: exit 1, 5 failures.
- Full resources JVM suite exit 0, 627 tests / 1687 assertions.

FINDING (not in fence, for the mayor): user docs still list three reserved keys: docs/api/re-frame.resources.md (:110, :192, :319, :754), docs/resources/tutorial/02-server-data.md:101, docs/resources/errors-and-warnings.md:33, skills/re-frame2/patterns/resources.md:52, skills/re-frame2/patterns/resources-mutations.md:37, migration/from-re-frame-v1/re-frame-query-to-resources.md:51. Each wants :reply-to added.

The guard message, the spec/009 row and spec/016's sentences (:871, :1141, plus :787, which said the same) name all four keys. title: Reagent and UIx: an adopting root topped by rf/frame-root may duplicate the page silently, as Fresco's did (probe first)
description:
Found by the rf2-mn2ht.43 worker (PR #11092), by READING, not probed: Reagent and UIx have the same root-level shape that .43 fixed for Fresco. No HTML element sits between the container and frame-root-fc, whose first pass renders nothing. So an adopting (hydrating) root topped by rf/frame-root should duplicate the page silently, as Fresco's did: React keeps the server DOM and appends the client tree beside it.

It cannot be fixed in core views/frame_boundary.cljs alone. frame-root-fc cannot know it is hydrating, because the spine keeps that flag private to each root. A core fix needs spine plumbing (spine.cljs), and would throw during hydration rather than before it.

FIRST, PROBE: hydrate a Reagent root and a UIx root topped by rf/frame-root over server markup, and count the copies. If the page is not duplicated, close with the evidence. If it is, take the smallest fix: expose the adopting flag from the spine to frame-root-fc, and refuse with the same :rf.error/fresco-frame-root-adopting (or a shared id) before React commits. Then a DOM test that is red at base, green after, and red again with the src reverted alone.

Fence: core spine.cljs and views/frame_boundary.cljs. The substrate worker holds spine.cljs (PR #11096), and rf2-mn2ht.68's UIx code half also edits spine.cljs, so sequence after #11096 and cluster with .68. Gates: the CLJS browser lane via CI; the core JVM lane.
notes:
== WORKER (spine-hydrate, 2026-10-11 01:35 AUSEST): PROBE SAYS DUPLICATED; FIXED in PR #11107, commit 7984157cec. Do not close until the PR merges. ==
PROBE: the page IS duplicated on both adapters, silently.
- Model (React 19.3.0, headless Chromium): the wrappers as plain components over a frame-root-like component (empty first render, ready flip in a layout effect), hydrated over server markup. The bare tree gave 1 copy. The Reagent shape, the UIx shape at base and the UIx shape after rf2-mn2ht.68 each gave 2 copies and 0 recoverable errors.
- Real adapters, through the new DOM rows at base (run 38057622822, browser job 114229996105): rf.adapter.reagent/render! and rf.adapter.uix/render! with {:hydrate? true} over a tree topped by frame-root left 2 copies of <main>, reported nothing and made the frame.
FIX, the smallest that refuses before React commits:
- re-frame.adapter.context/adoption-context: a new React context, default nil. It lives there because the spine and views/frame_boundary both already require that ns and neither requires the other. Putting it in spine.cljs would add a views->spine edge that re-frame.core's CLJS require chain would carry into every bundle.
- spine adoption-window-closer renders a Provider of that context, valued with the root's #js {:adopting true} flag. Both spines now mount the closer on EVERY hydrating root, not only when a reporter is installed, so production refuses too. The ratom spine's wrap changed from (if reporter ...) to (if hydrate? ...).
- frame-root-fc reads the context. While .-adopting is true it throws :rf.error/fresco-frame-root-adopting (:where re-frame.views.frame-boundary/frame-root-fc, :frame = the frame-root's :id) in its first render. No new error id.
- The flag closes on the hydration commit, so a frame-root mounted later under the same root renders normally (modelled).
WHAT THE USER SEES (model only, not asserted in the rows): React retries the root as a client render, the retry throws again, and the error reaches onUncaughtError (window reportError) with 0 recoverable errors, so no false :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch. The root then renders nothing, which leaves the container EMPTY rather than holding the server's markup. That differs from Fresco's door, which refuses before hydrateRoot and keeps the markup.
SCOPE: any frame-root rendered during the hydration render is refused, not only one directly under the root. A frame-root nested inside a host element during hydration was never duplicated (React reports that case as a mismatch), but it is refused now too.
FRESCO: unaffected. It has its own closer and its own adoption context in fresco/impl/roots.cljs, and the core adoption-context is never provided in Fresco trees.

close_reason:
ALREADY FIXED — delivered by `rf2-zryk5` in PR #10162, merged 2026-09-22 at trunk `fa4d69fa76`. No work dispatched against this bead, deliberately.

## THIS IS A DUPLICATE, AND THE BEAD ITSELF SAYS SO

The audit harness filed this while `rf2-zryk5` was `in_progress`. Its own description names that constraint and the correct response: *"Its literal status is now in_progress, so it cannot be reused under the audit's open-only rule and its status must not be changed. This separate open audit finding records the same required correction and links that active implementation; **coordinate with it rather than dispatching a second competing prose edit.**"*

Coordinated: the implementation had already merged by the time this bead reached the top of a dispatch queue. **Dispatching it would have produced exactly the competing prose edit its own text warns against**, against a file that had already been corrected — the expensive failure here, because a second worker would have found the defect absent and had to work out whether its brief was wrong or the tree had moved.

## THE REQUESTED CORRECTION, VERIFIED LIVE AT TRUNK

This bead asked for three things. All three hold, measured at trunk rather than inferred from the sibling bead:

| asked | measured |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md:54` no longer claims a publication gap | `pre-publication` occurs **0** times on that line |
| the real reason (template supports only `:reagent` / `:uix`) replaces it | the line now carries the `:substrate` selector reason (**2** occurrences of `substrate`) |
| the migration sibling left alone | `reagent-migration/SKILL.md` still carries "invent a publication gap" **1** time |

The recommendation to start greenfield projects on an adapter and the migration hand-off are both preserved, which this bead also required — the routing sentence was explicitly kept.

**The candidate-site warning this bead carries was also honoured** by the implementing worker: the true statement that all artefacts are unpublished, and the migration phrase about delivery "rather than a pre-publication detour", were both read in context and left alone as different-sense matches. `docs/skills/index.md` was confirmed already corrected by #10155.

## WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS NOT THIS BEAD

`skills/README.md:94` still carries the same asymmetry — verified present at trunk. It was fenced OUT of `rf2-zryk5` on purpose, because that page also carries the leaf-size exemption roster under an OPEN operator ruling, and a one-sentence prose fix should not be entangled with a pending decision. That is recorded in `rf2-zryk5`'s close reason as a known follow-up and is **not** what this bead describes: this bead is scoped to `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:54`, which is done.

## WHY CLOSED RATHER THAN LEFT OPEN

Leaving a duplicate open costs more than it looks. It re-enters `bd ready` every tick, reads as an unaddressed P2 against a shipped correction, and is precisely the kind of item a later dispatch picks up on priority order without reading to the end of its description. The finding was real, the correction is live, and the record of how it was made lives in `rf2-zryk5`.

**The audit harness did the right thing** — it could not reuse an `in_progress` bead, it recorded the finding rather than dropping it, and it left explicit instructions for the coordinator. Those instructions were followed.

title: fix(story): explain returns :args {} and :effective-args {} for a variant whose STORY carries :args, contradicting 017:603-604; the UI Explain panel shows "ARGS not available" while Docs and Xray show the heading
description:
From the rf2-rln91 Story-parity research (ai/findings/Story/fable/report.md, R6; contradiction 3). Reproduced by the reviewer on the JVM and on the shell at :8043 at trunk 98e8ffe9cb.

WHAT: tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md:603-604 says "[:explain :effective-args] — the same [args that feed the view], surfaced in explain". For `(reg-story* :story.probe {:args {:heading "Sign in"}})` plus a variant with no args of its own, `explain` returns `:args {}` and `:effective-args {}`, while `resolve-args` returns `{:heading "Sign in"}` and the rendered view shows the heading. The UI Explain panel on :8043 shows "ARGS not available / EFFECTIVE ARGS not available" for the same case while the Docs pane and the embedded Xray show the heading.

FIX (S): in tools/story/src/re_frame/story/plan.cljc (the :1599 region, whose comment says ":effective-args at plan time IS the resolved arg-map") fold story-level :args through resolve-args; the Explain panel then shows them without change or with a one-line change. ACCEPTANCE: the JVM probe prints `{:heading "Sign in"}` for both :args and :effective-args; :8043 Explain shows ARGS. GATES: the plan tests plus one new explain test with story-level args; UI cljs tests. Not a hot zone. notes:
== SCOPE CORRECTION (mayor re-frame2-fe, 2026-09-14 11:00 AUSEST) — SUPERSEDES the dispatch brief's fix shape ==
The brief the worker (storyargs-a) was dispatched with said: fold story-level :args through resolve-args in the plan.cljc :1599 region. DO NOT DO THAT. The reconciled research (astra pass, ai/findings/Story/astra/report.md; mayor re-read the panel docstring) traced the mechanism: `re-frame.story.plan/explain` (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/plan.cljc:2005) is the PURE plan compiler and omits the ambient story-level and global arg layers unless it is passed run-arg layers; the UI Explain panel (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/explain_panel.cljc, docstring lines 9-10 and 30-33) renders only the `:explain` map the compiler attaches and "never invents data the compiler didn't emit" — so it faithfully shows the empty maps. `re-frame.story/resolve-args` (story.cljc:1815) already returns the effective `{:heading "Sign in"}`.

CORRECTED FIX SHAPE: route the SCENARIO-FACING explain — the panel's call, and the public `story/explain` when asked about a selected variant — through the existing arg resolution (pass the run-arg layers, or fold resolve-args' answer into `:args`/`:effective-args` at the CALL SITE), and keep the pure compilation API explicit and documented as pure. Do NOT change the pure compiler's own resolution and do NOT build a second resolver. rf2-gwye.7 repaired canvas/save args only; this bead is specifically Explain.

COUPLING (already briefed by the peer mayor): if `:effective-args` feeds the plan hash, the hash value moves under whichever of rf2-noxox / rf2-7vz97 lands second — assert presence and determinism, never a literal hex.
== WORKER VERDICT (storyargs-a, 2026-09-14 AUSEST) — scope correction followed; PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9799 ==

REPRODUCED before the fix (JVM, trunk f17ba993f9): bare explain returned `:args {}` and `:effective-args {}`, while `resolve-args` and `plan/effective-args` returned `{:heading "Sign in"}`. Global-args were dropped the same way.

THE SCOPE CORRECTION HOLDS AT SOURCE:
- The pure compiler folds the ambient layers only when handed `:run-args`, and `variant-plan`'s docstring says so.
- The panel's `explain-for` called that compiler bare.
- Spec 017 does not require the bare compile to fold these layers (017 §Args puts them into compilation through the `:run-args` input).

So the brief's plan.cljc fold was NOT done, and plan.cljc is untouched.

One claim in the correction is narrower than the record, but the conclusion still stands. The correction says rf2-gwye.7 fixed only canvas and save. Its close reason actually routes the facade, canvas, controls, docs, multi-substrate, workspace, schema validation, snapshot identity, save and Copy EDN through `plan/effective-args`. Explain is not in that list either way.

THE FIX (three commits on worker/storyargs-a):
- `story/explain`, for a KEYWORD target: passes `(rf.story.args/run-arg-layers target opts)` as `:run-args`. A caller-supplied `:run-args` wins.
- `story/explain`, for a MAP target: stays bare, matching `run-inline-plan`, which compiles inline plans without the ambient layers.
- The panel's `explain-for`: uses the same keyword-only rule. It calls the compiler directly, because the facade loads the shell that mounts the panel, which would be a CLJS require cycle.
- `plan/explain` and `variant-plan` are unchanged.

PLAN-HASH COUPLING WITH rf2-7vz97:
- `:effective-args` IS a plan-hash input, through `:world` in `fingerprint/plan-hash-input-keys`.
- Yet no hashed plan changes value:
  - the pure compiler is untouched;
  - the run path already compiled with `:run-args`;
  - the render prep is untouched;
  - explain's plan is discarded, and `:explain` is not a hash input.
- So the two PRs can merge in either order.

CONTROL:
- Planted: removed both guards (`(when (keyword? variant-id)` became `(when false`; the facade's `(if (and (keyword? target) …))` became `(if false`).
- Red: the same 138-test / 558-assertion selector failed 12 at exit 1, every failure in the new or extended tests.

- Story CLJS: compile exit 0; the explain-panel-cljs, plan-cljs and plan-network-cljs namespaces ran 95 tests / 272 assertions, 0 failures.
- require-alias and JVM lane-roster ratchets: exit 0.
- clj-kondo: 0 errors.

FOLLOW-UP FILED — rf2-851t0: the same defect class at two sites outside this fence, both reproduced.
- The View-State panel's `compile-model` reports missing-arg for a story-only `[:arg]` placeholder.

## Evidence (tip 6445d0611b)

- `impl.mount/root!` `:152-162`: `(ensure-frame! frame-kw (:initial-events opts))`, then `createRoot` with `(root-options (:identifier-prefix opts) nil)`; `opts` is the whole config (`hicasso.cljc:604-608`), so unknown keys reach `root!` and are dropped there.
- `impl.mount/tree` `:54-82`: the ROOT is the frame provider — `(provider (:frame handle) (codec/root-element (:frame handle) hiccup))`; `codec/root-element` (`impl/codec.cljs:1712-1722`) is "the one creator that has to NAME the frame" by binding `intent/*frame*`. So today frame identity enters at the root handle, not in the tree. `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` builds its element through the same `tree` so client and server agree on `useId` tree position (`:68-72`, HS-11).
- Core's shared two-pass core: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/frame_boundary.cljs` — `frame-root-fc` `:300`, `frame-root-react-element` `:370` (the per-adapter shells are thin: UIx's `frame-root` is `(boundary/frame-root-react-element props (:children props) 're-frame.adapter.uix/frame-root)`, `uix.cljs:134-138`). The first render of `frame-root` emits NO subtree (`frame_boundary.cljs:41-51`), so under hydration the tree must use `frame-provider` (SCOPE) after `rf.ssr/hydrate!` made the frame — exactly what the Reagent SSR examples do (`examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc:460`).
- Consumers of `h/mount!`'s ENSURE keys: example `login/core.cljs:293-298`, testbeds `hicasso_testbed/core.cljs:884-890` (explicit `make-frame` then `{:frame …}` join), `hicasso_hmr_testbed/core.cljs:451-458`, Story test `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/hicasso_substrate_dom_cljs_test.cljs:363`, skill `skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-mechanical.md:294-333`, 10 guide pages (`docs/core/hicasso/`: 00-installation ×15 incl. §"What `h/mount!` creates" :281 and §"A frame that needs more than a seed" :318, 07 ×3, 09, 13, 17, 18-ssr ×11, 20-migration ×5, api-reference ×21 incl. :126-141 and §"not symmetric" :143-181, cookbook ×10, glossary ×5), `docs/api/re-frame.hicasso.md:125-160`, `docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md:20-30` ("a Hicasso tree has no frame component in it"). The test kit (`implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test/mounted.cljs`) reaches the root through `impl.mount/root!` (`catching-root!`, `:696-697`), not the facade — its `hm/mount!` config is its own and is not this bead's target.

## Target API

```clojure
;; ENSURE — a hicasso-owned head, like h/portal / h/error-boundary; takes THE make-frame map, not a curated subset
[h/frame-root {:id :rf/default :initial-events [[:app/init]] :fx-overrides {…} :url-bound? true :images […]}
 [root-view]]
;; SCOPE — an existing frame (SSR after rf.ssr/hydrate!, Story hosts, a second root on a page)
[h/frame-provider {:frame :app/main} [root-view]]

;; the root door carries ROOT options only, and a key it does not own fails loud
(h/mount!   el {:identifier-prefix "main"} [h/frame-root {:id :rf/default …} [root-view]])
(h/hydrate! el {:identifier-prefix "main"} [h/frame-provider {:frame :app/main} [root-view]])
(h/mount!   el {:frame :x} …)            ;=> throws — did-you-mean naming h/frame-root / h/frame-provider
(h/mount!   el {:initial-events […]} …)  ;=> throws — same diagnostic
(h/mount!   el {:foo 1} …)               ;=> throws — unknown root option (No-silent-swallow)
```

Contract the two heads MUST satisfy: `h/frame-root` realises 002 §`frame-root`'s shared contract (`:1697-1703`: commit-owned ensure, discard-safe, reuse-without-reseed, StrictMode-safe, no destroy-on-unmount, fail-loud on a mounted `:id`/opts change and on a `:frame` key) on the shared `frame-root-fc` core, exactly as UIx's shell does — do not fork the two-pass. `h/frame-provider` is the SCOPE-only component (`:1646`): requires a live frame, refuses `:id` with the did-you-mean. Both are Hicasso-recognised heads: the codec must lower a boundary's children under the frame the head resolved (codex: "Hicasso must recognise its head and lower children under the right frame") — `codec/root-element` no longer receives the frame from the handle; the frame boundary in the tree becomes the creator that names it. Whatever the client `tree` becomes, `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` builds the same element shape (mount.cljs:68-72, HS-11 obstruction 2) — the server side scopes with the same `h/frame-provider`.

Before / after for the one app example (`examples/substrates/hicasso/login/core.cljs:285-299`), keeping today's verbs (views.4 changes the verbs):

```clojure
;; before
(rf/make-frame (merge {:id frame-id …} model/frame-config))           ; because :fx-overrides can't ride mount!
(let [config {:frame frame-id :identifier-prefix identifier-prefix}]
  (if (some? payload)
    (do (rf.ssr/hydrate! {:frame frame-id :payload payload})
        (reset! !root (rf.hicasso/hydrate! el config [root-view])))
    (reset! !root (rf.hicasso/mount! el config [root-view]))))

;; after
(let [opts {:identifier-prefix identifier-prefix}]
  (if (some? payload)
    (do (rf.ssr/hydrate! {:frame frame-id :payload payload})
        (reset! !root (rf.hicasso/hydrate! el opts [h/frame-provider {:frame frame-id} [root-view]])))
    (reset! !root (rf.hicasso/mount! el opts
                    [h/frame-root (merge {:id frame-id} model/frame-config) [root-view]]))))
```

## Corroboration

Two-reviewer on the shape (ENSURE/SCOPE in the tree with full frame options; root options on the root call). Codex: "Keep frame creation/scoping in the corresponding `frame-root` / `frame-provider` boundary, with normal frame options; React root options belong to the root call. Do not conflate DOM unmount with permission to destroy durable frame state." Codex Thoughts: "A public in-tree boundary cannot simply expose the existing raw React provider, because Hicasso must recognise its head and lower children under the right frame. Keep ENSURE versus SCOPE explicit, especially after SSR payload installation; adoption must never silently seed replacement state." Grok: "ENSURE spelled once. Hicasso gets public `h/frame-root` (full `make-frame` opts) and `h/frame-provider`. That is more important than collapsing `hydrate!`/`render!`." Fable: the closed three-key config, the "ignored without complaint" keys, the `make-frame`-then-join dance and the migration guide's silent-failure paragraph all go.
