title: api(machines): child completion is :final?/:output-key under :spawn and :spawn-all; delete :on-child-done/-error
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from machines.md (ref machines.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

A machine child has two ways to say "I am done", and which one it must use depends on how its PARENT spawned it:

- Under `:spawn`, the child enters a `:final?` leaf; the runtime (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc`, `finalize-machine` :187) reads `:output-key`, folds the parent's `:spawn :on-done` / routes `:spawn :on-error`, emits the `:rf.machine/done` trace, and auto-destroys the child (005 §Final states, D4).
- Under `:spawn-all`, the child must hand-dispatch `[parent-id [<the parent's :on-child-done keyword> child-id & extra]]` from its terminal state's `:entry`. `join.cljc` intercepts that at the PARENT's handler boundary (`intercept-spawn-all-event` :912), after `stamp-join-completion-fx` (:377, called from `lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:787`) rewrote the carrier into the reserved `:rf.machine/join-dispatch` transport fx (:164; registered `machines.cljc:378-380`) so the exact-attempt coordinate can ride the recordable `:rf.machine/join-attempt` cofx fact.

So the child has to know its parent's join vocabulary, and a child meant to be reusable under both parents implements BOTH protocols: `testbeds/deep_machine/core.cljs:96-99` is `:final? true` AND `:entry :dispatch-child-done`. There is no bridge from finality to the join: `join.cljc:860-871` says a completed child's terminal "is NOT necessarily `:final?`", and `lifecycle_fx/traces.cljc:64` says a joined child's terminal state "was NOT `:final?`, so it stays a LIVE actor that the join tears down at resolution or parent exit". A `:final?` join child that does NOT hand-dispatch auto-destroys without folding the join, and the join hangs. `skills/re-frame2/patterns/long-running-work.md:136` nevertheless tells authors that `:spawn-all` "recognises completion natively" via `:final?` — false at tip; this bead makes it true.

## Evidence (tip `6445d0611b`)

- `:on-child-done` / `:on-child-error` authors: examples 2 — `examples/patterns/long_running_work/worker.cljs:313-314` (child action `:dispatch-done` :145-152, `:done` `:entry :dispatch-done` :195-200), `examples/patterns/boot/boot.cljs:310-311` (child actions `:dispatch-done` :138-153 / `:dispatch-error` :155-161, `:done`/`:failed` :192-193 — NOT `:final?`, `:meta {:terminal? true}` only); testbeds 1 — `testbeds/deep_machine/core.cljs:254-255` (action :76-87, leaf :96-99). Tools 0 (machines-viz `grammar.cljc` does not validate the `:spawn-all` shape, :533-534). 336 occurrences across 73 files repo-wide, 44 of them under `implementation/machines/test`.
- App-author `:final?` sites outside tools: 1 (`deep_machine:97`, the double-protocol child). The working single-`:spawn` consumer is `tools/xray/testbeds/machine_epochs/machines.cljs:223-245` (`:final?` + `:output-key :token` + parent `:on-done`) — unchanged by this bead, a regression surface.
- The resolution event today is `[parent-id (concat <on-all-complete ev> [decisive-child-id] child-extra)]` (`join.cljc:908`), `child-extra` being whatever the child hand-forwarded (:680, :986-993).
- `:on-done` is applied by a direct write to the parent's snapshot `:data` (`finalize.cljc:594`), NOT through a parent macrostep — the parent's `:always` cascade never sees the fold. `:on-error` by contrast is delivered as a dispatched `[:rf.machine.spawn/error …]` event into the parent (`finalize.cljc:398-405`). Boot's `:configuring` phase today ADVANCES on the child's hand-dispatched event (`boot.cljs:143-145`, action `:promote-staged`); after this bead the child dispatches nothing, so the parent must be able to advance on `:on-done`.
- `known-spawn-spec-keys` (`lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:1478-1495`) is one set for `:spawn` AND `:spawn-all` children and already admits `:on-done` / `:on-error` on a child spec; nothing honours them on a `:spawn-all` child and 005:3684 omits them from the child-spec key list.
- Codex's three corrections, all verified in source: `:rf.machine/done` is emitted (`finalize.cljc:452-480`) and consumed nowhere as control; `join.cljc:19-27,97,412-413` and 005:3876 say the exact-attempt coordinate is "a replayable correlation record, NOT authentication"; a joined child today lives on after reporting done (`traces.cljc:55-70`; `:rf.machine/join-reaped` exists for exactly that) while `:final?` tears down synchronously (D4).

## Target API

```clojure
;; CHILD — one completion convention, whatever the parent used.
:done   {:final? true :output-key :result}                ;; success: result = (:result data)
:failed {:final? true :error? true :output-key :reason}   ;; failure: the existing error-terminal grammar (005 §Final states)

;; PARENT, single child — grammar unchanged
:spawn {:machine-id :work/processor :data (fn [{snap :snapshot}] …)
        :on-done  (fn [{:keys [data result]}] (assoc data :answer result))   ;; fold
        :on-error {:target :failed}}                                          ;; transition

;; PARENT, fan-out + join — the child-vocabulary keys are gone
:spawn-all {:children [{:id :s1 :machine-id :work/processor :data …
                        :on-done (fn [{:keys [data result]}] (assoc-in data [:results :s1] result))}  ;; optional per-child fold
                       {:id :s2 …} {:id :s3 …}]
            :join            :all                 ;; or :any
            :on-all-complete [:work/all-done]     ;; :on-some-complete for :any
            :on-any-failed   [:work/any-failed]}
```

Before / after for the worker example (`worker.cljs`):

```clojure
;; before
:spawn-all {:children […] :join :all
            :on-child-done :work/child-done :on-child-error :work/child-error
            :on-all-complete [:work/all-done] :on-any-failed [:work/any-failed]}
;; child
:dispatch-done (fn [{:keys [data]}] {:fx [[:dispatch [parent-id [:work/child-done (:shard data)]]]]})
:done {:meta {:terminal? true} :tags #{:work/done} :entry :dispatch-done}

;; after
:spawn-all {:children […] :join :all
            :on-all-complete [:work/all-done] :on-any-failed [:work/any-failed]}
;; child
:done {:final? true :output-key :shard :tags #{:work/done}}
```

Rules of the target:

1. **Completion is finality.** A child under either parent form completes by entering `:final?`; `:output-key` selects the result; `:error? true` marks failure. The child carries no parent vocabulary. Progress and other milestones remain ordinary `[:dispatch [parent-id …]]` messages and are never reinterpreted as completion (codex correction 3).
2. **The parent decides how results combine.** `:spawn-all` keeps `:join`, `:on-all-complete` / `:on-some-complete`, `:on-any-failed`. The resolution event keeps its shape `[parent-id [<resolution-ev…> <decisive-child-id> <result>]]` where `<result>` is now the decisive child's `:output-key` value (its error payload on `:on-any-failed`) — one value, not a vector of extras. A `:spawn-all` child invoke-spec additionally honours `:on-done` (the same `(fn [{:keys [data result]}] new-data)` fold as `:spawn :on-done`, run against the parent's `:data` at that child's finality, before the join fold). This is not a new envelope: the validator already admits the key on a child spec; honouring it is what lets the boot example delete its app-db staging slot (`boot.cljs:83,150` `:boot/stage-payload`). `:on-error` on a `:spawn-all` child is NOT honoured — failure control flow under a join is `:on-any-failed` — so remove it from the child-spec key set (split `known-spawn-spec-keys`) and let the existing `:rf.error/machine-unknown-spawn-key` fire; no new error category.
3. **Runtime-owned path (codex correction 1).** `finalize-machine` already computes `result` / `error-leaf?` and reads `:rf/join-child` (:340) for the reply facts. When the finishing actor carries `:rf/join-child`, finalize hands `{parent-id invoke-id child-id spawned-id attempt work-generation kind result}` straight to a join fold entry point in `join.cljc` (the runtime calls it; keep `intercept-fold` :1166, `compute-resolution` :621, `build-resolution-fx` :790, the `emit-*` trace fns, `suppress-stale-completion!` :451). No event is dispatched by the child, no trace is subscribed to; `:rf.machine/done` is EMITTED from the result exactly as today (:480).
4. **Correlation preserved, not ceremonised (codex correction 2).** The exact-attempt gate (`join-attempt-current?` :422, `join-work-generation` :438) keeps working from the coordinate the runtime stamped into `:rf/join-child` at spawn (`spawn.cljc:296-330`, incl. the `:work-generation` discriminator :313 for `:fixed-actor-id` children that reuse ids across attempts, :1184). Duplicate suppression (`:rf.machine.spawn-all/duplicate-completion`), `attempt-superseded` / `attempt-unverified`, post-resolution `late-completion`, the non-decisive `child-completed` terminal (one per child — `join_child_terminal_cljs_test`), sibling cancellation with `cancelled-on-join-resolution`, and the parent-exit cascade all keep their outcomes. Describe the gate in spec and docstrings as causal correlation; do not add a capability/secret.
5. **Recorded / replayed completion.** The coordinate rode the recordable `:rf.machine/join-attempt` cofx fact only because the carrier was a PUBLIC app event that had to survive EDN recording and `:dispatch-later` (005:3882). With the fold inside the child's own finalize step, replaying the child's terminal event replays the fold; there is no separate carrier. Rewrite `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/join_strict_mint_epoch_replay_test.clj` and `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/join_strict_mint_cljs_test.cljc` to drive children to `:final?` and still prove: strict-mint replay folds exactly once per child, no host generation, identical resolution.
6. **Parent advancement on a single child's completion — the measured gap you must close.** Pick ONE delivery mechanism and use it for both forms: (a) keep the synchronous fold (API.md:951 "fires synchronously", 005 D4) and run the parent's `:always` cascade after it, inside finalize, as one macrostep; or (b) deliver completion as ONE reserved internal parent event, the way `:on-error` already does, routed at the parent boundary to the `:on-done` fold / `:on-error` transition / join fold — which moves `:on-done` from same-tick to next-macrostep and must carry 005 §Final states step 3 and API.md:951 with it. Do NOT add an event-vector `:on-done` spelling or any completion-policy grammar (codex: "do not add a general completion-policy language"). The boot example's `:configuring` phase (single `:spawn`, must advance to `:loading-deps` on the loader's finality) is the acceptance case that forces the answer.
7. **Finality means teardown (codex correction 3) — make it explicit and check cleanup.** Under `:final?` a joined child is destroyed synchronously at completion with `:reason :rf.machine/finished`; it no longer "reports done and lives on". Consequences: (i) `:rf.machine/join-reaped` (post-terminal cleanup of a LIVE completed child) has no producer left, and neither has the verified-reap destroy form `{:rf/reap true :rf/parent-id :rf/invoke-id :rf/child-id}` that `build-resolution-fx` emits for completed children (`join.cljc:885-900`; `destroy.cljc:34-45,618,714,830-870`) nor the `:unverified-reap` / `:unresolved-join` causes of `:rf.error/machine-destroy-bad-arg` (`traces.cljc:111`; 009:2217) — delete them (list below); if you find a live producer, keep it and say so in the PR. Survivors still go `:explicit` + `cancelled-on-join-resolution`. (ii) `worker.cljs` and `boot.cljs` already treat done as terminal (`:meta {:terminal? true}`; `worker.cljs:196-197` "the exit cascade then sweeps the child away"); verify by test that nothing dispatches to a completed child afterwards (a dispatch to the destroyed address is `:rf.error/no-such-handler`, D5). (iii) `:meta {:terminal? true}` on those leaves is redundant with `:final?` — drop it in the migrated sites.

## Corroboration

Two-reviewer. Fable proposed the collapse (`fable/machine-child-lifecycle-and-addressing.md` §Completion); codex checked it against `finalize.cljc` / `join.cljc` and calls it "the strongest compositional improvement in either corpus" (`codex/machine-child-completion.md`), adopting it with three corrections that this bead honours verbatim: the join must not be implemented by listening to the `:rf.machine/done` trace; the exact-attempt coordinates are causal correlation, not authentication, and are preserved inside the unified path; finality tears the child down immediately, so "done means terminal" is made explicit and worker/boot cleanup is checked. `fable/README.md` §Relationship lists "child completion unified under `:final?` for `:spawn` and `:spawn-all`" as two-reviewer. acceptance_criteria:
- One child machine registered once (e.g. `:work/processor`) is used under a `:spawn` parent and under a `:spawn-all` parent with no parent vocabulary in the child. Under `:spawn`: the parent's `:on-done` receives the `:output-key` value and the parent transitions to its next state with no dispatch from the child. Under `:spawn-all :join :all`: three children reaching `:final?` fire `:on-all-complete` exactly once with the decisive child's id and result. Under `:join :any`: the first `:final?` fires `:on-some-complete`; survivors are destroyed with `:rf.machine.spawn/cancelled-on-join-resolution`.
- Error: `{:final? true :error? true :output-key :reason}` under `:spawn` fires the parent's `:on-error` transition with the payload; under `:spawn-all` fires `:on-any-failed` (when declared) and cancels survivors; without `:on-any-failed` the existing unsatisfiable-join diagnostic (`join.cljc:589-593`) still fires.
- Per-child `:on-done` on a `:spawn-all` child folds the parent's `:data` before the join fold; `:on-error` on a `:spawn-all` child is rejected at registration with `:rf.error/machine-unknown-spawn-key`.
- Progress: an ordinary `[:dispatch [parent-id [:progress …]]]` from a live child leaves the join's `:done` set unchanged.
- Cancel / restart: parent exits the `:spawn-all` state mid-flight → every child destroyed `:explicit`; re-entry mints a new attempt; a completion carrying the prior attempt's coordinate (a `:fixed-actor-id` child) is suppressed `:rf.machine.spawn-all/attempt-superseded`; a replayed record for an already-folded child is suppressed `duplicate-completion`.
- Cleanup: after resolution no child snapshot, no `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawned <parent> <invoke-id> :children]` entry and no registrar handler remains; a dispatch to a completed child's address yields `:rf.error/no-such-handler`; no `:rf.machine/join-reaped` destroy is emitted anywhere in the suite (or the PR names the surviving producer).

- `:rf.machine/done` is emitted for every finality with `:parent-id` and the reply facts; `grep -rn 'rf.machine/done' implementation/*/src` shows only emit sites and docstrings — nothing subscribes to it as control.
- `rg -n 'on-child-done|on-child-error|join-dispatch|join-attempt|rf/reap' examples testbeds tools implementation spec docs skills migration` returns 0 hits outside dated history (CHANGELOG / EP records).
- `long_running_work`, `boot`, `deep_machine` compile under `node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cljs`; `implementation/adapters/reagent` `long_running_work_cljs_test` passes; machines JVM + `npm run test:cljs` green; `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check` green; `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` and `mkdocs build --strict` green for the spec/docs edits; `python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` green for the two example READMEs; table column counts and anchors in the edited 005 sections verified by hand and stated in the PR body.

title: [method-drift] CLAUDE.md names the wrong link gate for root and implementation READMEs, and omits the CI classifier from the hot-zone list
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-08-18, after the same defect cost two dispatches in one evening. Both items are in CLAUDE.md, which every agent in this repo reads before it does anything, so a wrong line here is repeated by every worker that trusts it. Filed rather than committed: the mayor checkout does not commit worker-tracked surfaces.

ITEM 1 — CLAUDE.md:114 STATES A LINK-GATE COVERAGE CLAIM THAT IS INCOMPLETE IN THE FAIL-OPEN DIRECTION.

The sentence today: "`scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` *does* validate the tree's markdown link targets and heading anchors (it runs in the fast-PR spine and — since rf2-v7fui — unconditionally in `test.yml`'s `verify-readme-links` job, so on every PR rather than only a docs-classified one)".

What is missing is which markdown it reads. `check_doc_slugs.py`'s own docstring says it: its roots are `docs`, `spec`, `skills`, `migration` plus `tools/*/spec`, and "`TESTING.md`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `SKILL-REDIRECT.md` are never opened here — this gate exits 0 on a broken link in any of them." `implementation/**/README.md` is likewise outside its roots.

MEASURED, not inferred, by the rf2-0yp7w.9 README-slice worker on 2026-08-18: a broken link target planted in `implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md` returned check_doc_slugs.py GREEN, exit 0. The same plant under `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` returned RED, exit 1, naming the file.

THE SURFACE IS NOT UNGATED — the fix is prose, not a new gate. `.github/workflows/test.yml:855-858` runs BOTH `check_readme_links.py --self-test --verbose` and `check_readme_links.py --ci` inside the very job CLAUDE.md names, `verify-readme-links`. So CI covers it; only the sentence in CLAUDE.md is wrong, and it is wrong in the direction that makes a mayor nominate a gate that verifies nothing.

NOTE THE IRONY, because it is the reason to fix the sentence rather than to add another: the same paragraph already warns that "a prose list drifts" and tells the reader to consult `exclude_docs` in `mkdocs.yml` rather than a list in prose — and then states this coverage claim in prose, incompletely. The paragraph's own remedy applies to itself.

THE REPAIR. Name both gates and their split, in one clause:
  * `docs/**`, `spec/**`, `skills/**`, `migration/**`, `tools/*/spec`  -> `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`
  * repo-root markdown and `implementation/**/README.md`               -> `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci`
Both run in `test.yml`'s `verify-readme-links` job on every PR. And say the thing that generalises: the job's NAME reads as though it checks READMEs, and the gate that actually does is the other one.

ITEM 2 — THE HOT-ZONE LIST OMITS THE CI CLASSIFIER.

CLAUDE.md:91 enumerates the hot-zone files as spec pages, top-level `implementation/deps.edn`, `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` and `.github/workflows/*`. It does not name `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh`, which is one-toucher by construction rather than by convention: `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs` mirrors it and the two pin each other, so a change to either alone lands a tree where the suite contradicts the script. Two workers in that pair conflict every time.

That omission is live right now — rf2-7b1ti's routing half is in flight and had to be fenced by hand because the list does not carry it.

THE REPAIR: add `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` and its mirror `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs` to the hot-zone enumeration, noting that they move in ONE commit.

BOTH ITEMS ARE ONE SMALL PROSE PR ON A HOT-ZONE FILE. CLAUDE.md is not in the enumerated hot-zone list itself, but it is a single-toucher in practice — sequence it against anything else editing it.

comments.text:
CORRECTION FROM THE MEASURING WORKER, 2026-08-18 — MY OWN BRIEF GOT THE MKDOCS REASON WRONG, AND THE RIGHT REASON IS DIFFERENT IN KIND.

I told the README-slice worker to 'read mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs block and say whether it covers these paths'. It read further and reported that exclude_docs is not the mechanism at all: mkdocs cannot see implementation/**/README.md because docs_dir is 'docs', and mkdocs_hooks.py:30 records implementation/ as 'CLJS source; not docs'. A path outside docs_dir is not excluded — it was never a candidate.

WHY THAT MATTERS FOR THIS BEAD RATHER THAN BEING A QUIBBLE. CLAUDE.md's paragraph on mkdocs teaches ONE mechanism — 'read exclude_docs, it is the authority on what the build cannot see' — and that sentence is true for the design trees it was written about and MISLEADING everywhere else. A worker applying it to implementation/ finds the path absent from exclude_docs and can reasonably conclude the build does cover it. Two mechanisms keep a path out of the site: being outside docs_dir, and being excluded from within it. The repair should name both, or the same class of wrong-gate nomination this bead already records will recur through a different door.

ALSO WORTH CARRYING INTO THE SAME EDIT: no gate validates the PROSE of these README files at all. check_readme_links.py --ci validates their link targets and anchors; nothing checks whether a sentence describes a live surface. That is the honest state and CLAUDE.md's 'the worker verifies by hand and says so in the PR body' wording already covers it — it just needs to reach this surface too.

comments.text:
ADDENDUM AFTER CLOSE — a THIRD surface was added to the landed sentence, and the mayor was right to ask.

My first landed draft named only two gates and their split. check_readme_links.py carries a third arm I had not stated: COMMAND_FILE_PATHSPEC = '.claude/commands/*.md' (scripts/check_readme_links.py:390). Verified at source in this worktree before adding, not taken on report.

What it does is DIFFERENT IN KIND from the other two, which is why it needed its own clause rather than a name in a list: it resolves path-shaped REFERENCES, not anchors. The five tracked command files contain zero markdown links and zero headings, so there is no fragment id to resolve and the _N-versus--N duplicate-suffix disagreement between the two gates does not arise at all. It matches bare AND backticked paths, deliberately NOT masking inline code, because in text the CLI feeds a model verbatim a backticked path is exactly as load-bearing as a bare one — which is precisely what makes the two ordinary link gates blind there.

WHY IT BELONGS IN CLAUDE.md RATHER THAN BEING GATE TRIVIA: the command files are what the mayor loop EXECUTES, while docs/the-mayor-method/** only DESCRIBES the same practice. CLOSE REASON DAMAGED BY BACKTICK COMMAND SUBSTITUTION — the evidence quotation is missing from it, and this note restores it. Recorded by the mayor 2026-09-22, minutes after the close.

WHAT HAPPENED. The close reason was built by a script whose content travelled inside a DOUBLE-QUOTED shell argument. Backticks inside a double-quoted shell string are command substitution, so every backticked span in the quotation was EXECUTED and its output spliced in where the words stood. The shell said so on stderr — "command not found" for two spans and "Is a directory" for a third — while bd printed its ordinary success line and exited 0. The damaged close reason carries ZERO backticks where the source had several.

This is the exact trap CLAUDE.md records under Beads durability, including its remedy, which I had already applied correctly several times this session and then dropped when the content happened to be built by a Python one-liner rather than written to a file first. The rule is not about heredocs: what protects the text is that it reaches bd from a FILE, and building that file through a double-quoted shell argument re-opens the hole from the other side.

THE MISSING EVIDENCE, restored here. Measured at trunk a5d3a1fa26 before the close, skills/re-frame2/examples-map.md line 66 reads, in part:

    It does **not** demonstrate the route :can-leave guard - for that read
    examples/real-apps/realworld_http/, whose editor routes declare
    :can-leave [:editor/can-leave?].

(Written without code spans deliberately, so this note cannot suffer the same damage if it is ever re-processed by a careless caller.)

So the claim rf2-9bjih reports as false is no longer made: that line now states the opposite and points at the example which does demonstrate the guard. The duplicate close stands, and its reasoning is unchanged — only its quoted evidence was lost and is now restored.

THE CLOSE REASON WAS NOT REOPENED TO FIX IT, and that is deliberate: reopening a bead ERASES close_reason and closed_at outright, and the text is not copied anywhere first. Appending the correction as a note is the non-destructive repair, and this note is the newest text on the item so a newest-first reader lands on it.

## Make it tangible

**What a user does today in the App-DB tab.** Each section is one `[ei/edn-inspector-view {:opts {:panel-id :rf.xray/app-db … :card? true :zoomable? true :header title}}]` (`app_db_diff_state.cljs:401-417`). A key like `:items` is rendered by `key-segment` (`edn_inspector.cljs:1459-1470`) — a coloured `[:span …]` with **no handler at all**; single-clicking it does nothing. Every non-root container carries `zoom-trigger-attrs` (:3469-3539): tooltip "Double-click or press Enter to zoom into this node", double-click / Enter dispatches `[:rf.xray.edn-inspector/zoom-to panel-id mount-id path]`, a breadcrumb `app-db › :cart › :items` appears and each crumb zooms back (:3595-3597), Esc zooms up. That IS "inspect app-db at a prefix", in place, with the diff annotations re-rooted (:3844-3855). The ▸/▾ triangle expands. That is the whole gesture set.

**What a host gets from the embedding contract.**
```clojure
(xray/focus! :checkout {:panel :app-db :path [:checkout :state]})
;; => {:ok? true
;;     :applied [[:rf.xray/select-frame :checkout]
;;               [:rf.xray/select-tab :app-db]
;;               [:rf.xray/focus-slice-path [:checkout :state]]]
;;     :source nil}
```
The App-DB tab is selected; `[:checkout :state]` lands in Xray's frame db; nothing on screen changes. `focus_cljs_test.cljs:198` pins exactly this and calls it "App-db slice highlighted".

**Under A** (wire the click to the popup): single-click `:items` in `[:cart :items 0 :price]` → a 560 px dialog "app-db at `[:cart :items]`" (`app_db_segment_inspector.cljs:192-212`) over a dimmed backdrop, showing that subtree as an expandable tree, Esc / ✕ / backdrop to close; `:path` in `focus!` would open the same dialog. If show-me-when is also restored, the dialog gains a pivot listing `epoch 14 :cart/add-item added {…}` rows (the list spec 004 :771-777 sketches, which was never rendered even before 27 May — the only pre-excision consumer was a `:<-` input in a sub, hunk line 1778). Note the gesture collision that has to be designed around: a double-click fires `click, click, dblclick`, so "click = popup, double-click = zoom" opens the popup twice and then zooms behind it unless the click is deferred or moved to a modifier/crumb.

**Under B** (delete + rewrite): nothing on screen changes for anyone. ## Recommendation

**B.** Argued from the stance: the three mechanisms are ~670 lines of source and ~1,430 of tests that a user cannot reach and that have already cost one repair on dead code (rf2-jmucu) and one false finding (rf2-y8doi.9 #4 read the popup as live). The value on the other side — a prefix inspector — is already delivered in place by zoom, which Mike asked for AFTER the popup and on the same day ruled the App-DB panel roomy enough not to want a popup at all (rf2-7sdja); "show me when this changed" was dropped by Mike's own rf2-okvit item 4; and the embedding `:path` field, the one thing that reads as a value a host can rely on, has no host relying on it. The spec lock is the strongest reason to rule rather than let it lie: 021 tells an implementer that propagation is "the only path-click semantic" while its own §10.0.11 says Enter zooms, and the B.9 text says only the mayor can reopen it. A rewrite to "zoom is the gesture; propagation not built" is one honest sentence where A is a rebuilt feature. ## Codex Recommendation

Reviewed 2026-09-17 21:04:50 +1000 (Australia/Sydney), bead `rf2-y8doi.29`, source revision `23cbf7f1f9eb0248698c96153ffff22dd49d87b6`. Relevant Xray source/spec/tests and the Story caller remained unchanged when HEAD advanced to `327b74ac6b54d6f6693951da6bf680f157171d5d` during review.

**Recommend B, as a bounded removal of unused mechanisms and misleading promises.** Keep the current container zoom and breadcrumb navigation. Retire the segment popup, dormant history query and unused flash, and withdraw the advertised `focus! :path` highlight. This gives SPA programmers and their AI a smaller, truthful tool surface without inventing another interaction. The four behaviours are separable product choices; none needs rebuilding merely because another once referenced it.

**Independent findings.** Source paths below are repository-relative.

- The popup is callable programmatically but has no shipped UI opener. Source search finds its registration at `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_segment_inspector.cljs:108` and a documentation mention, while actual close handlers exist at lines 188, 264 and 281. Its exported `mount-segment-inspector!` still exists at `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels.cljs:572`. Thus “no built-in click reaches it” is supported; “nothing changes for anyone” is too strong for an exported API. I found no in-repository runtime consumer of that mount function, but cannot establish external usage.
- Path focus terminates in unused state: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/focus.cljc:219` emits `focus-slice-path`; `panels/app_db_diff_events.cljs:30` stores it; `panels/app_db_diff_subs.cljs:138` feeds it only into the history-result subscription, which has no view consumer. The assertion at `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/focus_cljs_test.cljs:198` checks the stored vector, despite calling it a highlight. Story's real caller uses the pathless arity at `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/evidence_spine.cljc:500`; its four-argument builder and test still promise paths at lines 305 and `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/evidence_spine_test.cljc:195` respectively.
- Zoom has an actual interaction path: App-DB opts in at `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs:408`; `views/edn_inspector.cljs:3515` dispatches zoom from double-click/Enter, and line 3609 builds breadcrumb click handlers. Existing tests exercise those handlers in `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector_cljs_test.cljs:3672`, 3685 and 3898. These were read, not run. This supports precise documentation of container zoom and breadcrumb clicks, rather than the blanket claim that clicking a path does nothing.
- The flash has a declaration at `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/global_styles.cljs:446`, with no source application. The normative conflict is real: [021](../../tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md) lines 5061 and 5172 promise cross-panel propagation, while line 4869 specifies Enter-to-zoom. [008](../../tools/xray/spec/008-Embedding-Contract.md) line 211 promises the absent highlight. Retiring those promises is necessary whichever code option wins.

The archived bead records at `965dee34e0:.beads/issues.jsonl`, selected by identity, confirm rf2-okvit's explicit removal of the history affordance and rf2-h71e0's subtree-zoom purpose. However, rf2-7sdja removes the generic popup-affordance button from App-DB; treating that as an explicit ruling against every possible segment popup overstates it. **Options and tradeoffs.** Wiring the popup is feasible, but adds another way to inspect the same subtree. Restoring history search offers something genuinely different from manually scrubbing epochs, yet requires more than the dossier's new list renderer: an executed Babashka probe loaded the current helper namespace and changed `{:cart {:items [{:price 10}]}}` to price 11. `epochs-touching-path` returned one hit for `[:cart :items]` and zero for `[:cart :items 0 :price]`. Add the omitted flash tests at `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/global_styles_cljs_test.cljs:85` and 94 to the implementation scope. Keep `focus!` permissive rather than adding unknown-field rejection. Describe the public mount/field retirement explicitly as a pre-alpha API simplification. No compatibility layer or replacement feature is justified by the callers found.

title: Incomplete: sibling skill eval instructions still omit trigger-format conversion
description:
Merged-PR audit #9770 (c09c413ad67c9a115e13c3c48f990261cc22d31c). The eval-format repair is incomplete across the skill surfaces named in this PR: pair-retro is corrected, but the implementor, improver and setup eval metadata still advertises Anthropic skill-creator compatibility without the trigger-format conversion. The PR explicitly records this remainder under Findings not fixed and defers it to the sibling surface owners; those owners are now closed and no exact open finding records this correction. This new Bead makes that remainder actionable without reopening them.

Owned correction locations:
- skills/re-frame2-implementor/evals/evals.json:4: says anthropics/skills/skill-creator evals.json per references/schemas.md, and that should_trigger lets the description-optimisation loop score the corpus.
- skills/re-frame2-improver/evals/evals.json:4 and evals/README.md:39-45: the same upstream-schema attribution for a local mixed-kind wrapper; the trigger half needs conversion and the behavioural half must not be fed into the trigger loop.
- skills/re-frame2-setup/evals/evals.json:4: the same native-schema/description-optimisation claim for a wrapped prompt-based corpus.

Primary reference: https://github.com/anthropics/skills/blob/3d59511518591fa82e6cfcf0438d68dd5dad3e76/skills/skill-creator/scripts/run_eval.py (run_eval iterates the loaded value and reads item[query], then item[should_trigger]); references/schemas.md defines the separate prompt/expected_output task schema. The corrected pair-retro README in this PR already explains this distinction and gives the narrow adapter.

Bounded actual-corpus witness: both passing the raw wrapper and passing just its trigger entries fail the upstream shape accesses, respectively TypeError and KeyError query. On the audited files there are 20 implementor triggers, 16 improver triggers among 33 mixed-kind fixtures, and 18 setup triggers. Running jq with a boolean-should_trigger selector and mapping prompt to query yields exactly 20/16/18 valid rows, preserving every prompt and boolean. The 17 improver behavioural rows remain separate. As a positive control, executing the actual jq filter extracted from the newly corrected pair-retro README yields its 22 rows unchanged. No models, upstream executors or external sessions were started. Evidence: C:/Users/miket/.codex/tmp/audit-re-frame2-pr9770-format-witness-1.json; Python witness and every jq subprocess exit 0.

Required correction: describe these wrappers as repository-owned, distinguish task/behavioural evaluation from description-trigger evaluation, and document the small explicit conversion in each relevant maintainer entry point (metadata may point to a shared local explanation). For the improver corpus select the trigger kind/boolean labels so behavioural rows never become null trigger labels. Keep all source fixtures, labels and behavioural expectations intact; do not replace the local corpus or add a model runner, scorer, runtime dependency or new shipped API. Limit this Bead to these three sibling surfaces rather than a speculative repository-wide expansion.

Impact: maintainers following the advertised native trigger-loop format hit a data-shape failure before scoring. This is P3 maintenance workflow correctness, not a failure of normal skill invocation. The landed HTTP lifecycle, pin cleanliness and setup classpath corrections remain valid. Literal-open duplicate search (31 Beads) found no existing explicit owner of this same defect and correction. Closed source work is preserved; source forward pointers and discovered-from links do not mean the mayor was notified or acknowledged it.

Existing behavioural expectations, manual grading, packaging exclusions and corrected pair-retro conversion remain unchanged. title: The meaning pass: new rationale, supersede HD-001, prose a sed cannot fix
description:
CONTEXT IS ON THE PARENT EPIC rf2-d1nr. Read it first — it is the durable record.

AFTER child .2. This is the pass a `sed` cannot do: the places where the OLD NAME'S MEANING is
load-bearing, and a mechanical substitution leaves prose that is grammatical and false.

THE CENTRAL EXAMPLE. docs/design/hicasso/charter.md:24 currently reads, in substance: "The
wordplay is the product claim: Picasso's single-line freehand drawings — a complete figure in
one unbroken pass — are one-pass interpreted rendering; Cubism's decomposition into primitive
forms is hiccup's decomposition of UI into vectors and maps. Verified unclaimed on Clojars,
GitHub, and npm; single-c spelling is canonical." After a sed, every word of that still stands
and none of it is about Fresco.

== WHAT TO WRITE INSTEAD ==

The new rationale, which is BETTER than the one it replaces and should be written as such
rather than apologised for:

  A fresco is painted onto wet plaster and MUST be completed in one continuous pass, before
  the plaster sets. There is no going back over it and no second layer. That is one-pass
  interpreted rendering stated by the medium itself — the claim the old name made by way of a
  person's name, now made directly. The art lineage the charter wanted is kept; the celebrity
  is dropped.

Also drop, because they are artefacts of the old name and are now false or meaningless:
  * "single-c spelling is canonical" — there is no double-c hazard in Fresco.
  * "one letter apart" and every Picasso/Cubism reference.
  * The old availability sentence. Replace it with what child .1 actually verified, citing
    child .1 by bead id.

== THE PLACES ==

1. docs/design/fresco/charter.md (post-rename path) — the name table and the rationale
   paragraph. The one-liner becomes "Fresco — Hiccup views for re-frame2."
2. docs/design/fresco/decisions.md — HD-001. SUPERSEDE IT, DO NOT DELETE IT OR REWRITE ITS
   HISTORY. HD-001 currently ends "Reopens never — names are permanent after first publish",
   and that clause was correct: it simply had not bound yet, because the product was
   pre-publication. Add a superseding block in the house style already used by HD-002 (a
   dated "Superseded by operator ruling" note above the original text), naming this epic,
   the date, and the reason — the trademark-adjacency finding — and stating that the "never"
   clause now attaches to FRESCO from its first publish. The original ruling stays readable
   underneath. A decisions log that quietly rewrites a ruling is worth nothing.
3. Sweep for surviving name-rationale prose anywhere else: docs/EP/EP-0038, the product
   pilots pages, skills, READMEs, any "why it is called that" sentence. Search for the
   CONCEPTS (Picasso, Cubism, wordplay, "one letter", "single-c") rather than the name, since
   child .2 has already removed the name — this is the one search in the epic where the old
   spelling is NOT the needle.
4. `h` ALIAS: wherever prose explains the alias, it should now say `h` is for HICCUP, which is
   what it always meant and is why it survives the rename unchanged. That is a small
   clarification worth making explicitly, because a reader who sees `re-frame.fresco :as h`
   with no explanation will file it as an inconsistency.

== POSITIVE CONTROL ==
Take one on every zero. `grep -iF` ABORTS on this box (exit 134, silent stdout) — do not use
that flag pair. And note that a search for "Picasso" will legitimately still hit the
decisions.md supersession block, which QUOTES the old rationale on purpose. That is a correct
hit, not a miss — do not remove it.

== GATES ==
docs/design/** is EXCLUDED from `mkdocs build --strict` by mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs block, so
that is not the gate here. The gates that do reach this tree are scripts/check_doc_slugs.py
(anchors and repo-relative targets, docs/ is in its roots) and scripts/check_provenance_pins.py,
which runs as its own docs.yml job over CHANGED pages under this design tree — note the path it
matches moved in child .2. Neither gate looks inside a fenced code block, and nothing validates
prose, tables or nav, so verify anchors and table column counts by hand and say so in the PR.

title: api(registry): RULING — defreg generator; kind-keyed (rf/clear kind id) vs nine clear-* names; http fx pair
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from registration-and-testing.md (ref spellings.3); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

Three design questions from the registration-spellings review, one ruling bead. All one-reviewer (fable); codex reviewed the doc and cautions on each. @spellings.1 (aliases + concordance + table drift) and @spellings.2 (the written fx-form rule) are ruling-independent and already filed; nothing here blocks them.

## Q1 — generate both faces of a registrar from one `defreg`

**Today.** `defreg-macro` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_macros.cljc:250`, under `#?(:clj …)`) emits the JVM `defmacro` that captures `(meta &form)` / `*file*` / `*ns*` and splices to the owning fn. The CLJS same-name value alias is a separate hand-written `#?(:cljs (do (def reg-x …)))` block (`core.cljc:262-352`) — the list that drifted (10 of 15; @spellings.1 fills it and pins concordance).

**Options.** (a) One `defreg` row per registrar emits the macro on JVM and `(def reg-x delegate)` on CLJS — the expansion is host-aware (`(:ns &env)` discriminates a CLJS expansion), carries the docstring once, and applies the same `:doc` DCE gating (rf2-9wwkcm) the macros already have. Removes ~90 lines and makes a missing alias impossible by construction. (b) Keep two lists, pinned by @spellings.1's concordance check.

**Codex.** "The generator sketch is not an implementation: the existing macro generator is JVM-reader-gated and emits JVM macros. Simply teaching it to emit another reader branch does not ensure the CLJS compilation gets its value definition. Prefer the smallest repair — missing aliases plus a concordance check — unless one shared declaration can serve both host compilation paths without new build machinery. … The rule must exclude macros that walk syntax, not just macros that define a Var."

**Recommendation.** (b) now — it is @spellings.1 — and (a) only as a follow-up if the concordance check proves noisy or the block keeps growing. Fable prefers (a); the difference is ~90 lines against one more compile-time mechanism in the facade.

## Q2 — one kind-keyed inverse vs the nine `clear-*` names

**Today.** Nine public `clear-*` names in THREE shapes, and six registrar kinds with no inverse at all:

| shape | names | where |
|---|---|---|
| nilary clear-all + `(id)` | `clear-event`, `clear-sub`, `clear-fx` | `core.cljc:1069/1075/1080` → `events.cljc:1509`, `subs.cljc:367`, `fx.cljc:162` |
| `(id)` / `(id {:frame f})`, TOLERANT opts (`{:keys [frame]}`) | `re-frame.flows/clear-flow` | `flows/registry.cljc:833` — off the facade (`core.cljc:1036-1048`, rf2-wad2fl) |
| `(id)` / `(id {:frame f})`, EXACT fail-closed opts | `clear-http-interceptor` | `core.cljc:2545` → `http/middleware.cljc:245` (rf2-s32bf) |
| `(id)` only | `re-frame.routing/clear-route` (off facade), `clear-resource`, `clear-mutation`, `clear-resource-scope` | `routing/registry.cljc:594`; `core.cljc:1501/1545/1573` |

No inverse: `:cofx`, `:interceptor`, `:view`, `:head`, `:error-projector`, `:app-schema` (per-path). The substrate is uniform — `re-frame.registrar/unregister!` (`registrar.cljc:713`) takes `(kind id)` for every registrar kind (and forgets every provenance slot for the id, :724). The read side already speaks kinds: `(handler-meta kind id)` (`API.md` §Introspection), `(registrations kind)`; the kind table is `spec/001-Registration.md:87-117`.

**Consumers.** Non-test: THREE calls in ONE file — `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/registry.cljs:352` (`run! rf/clear-sub`), `:411-412` (`run! rf/clear-sub`, `run! rf/clear-event`). Every other `clear-*` (route, http-interceptor, the resource trio, `flows/clear-flow`): 0 non-test. Test calls (impl + tools): clear-event 7, clear-sub 19, clear-fx 4, clear-flow 4, clear-route 3, clear-http-interceptor 30, clear-resource 6, clear-mutation 10, clear-resource-scope 0 → 83. Fixtures reach `registrar/clear-all!` / `clear-kind!`, not the public names.

**rf2-uhk4** (open, P4) records the facade asymmetry — `clear-flow` off the facade, the other eight on — and asks which direction to make consistent. This ruling SUBSUMES that question; do not act on rf2-uhk4 separately, close or re-point it with this bead's ruling.

**Options.**
- **(E) one verb.** `(rf/clear kind id)` / `(rf/clear kind id {:frame f})`: opts EXACTLY `{:frame f}`, fail-closed (rf2-s32bf applied to every frame-scoped kind at once), rejected for non-frame-scoped kinds; unknown kind fails closed. Registrar kinds route to `registrar/unregister!`; side-table / lifecycle kinds (`:flow`, `:http-interceptor`, `:route`, `:resource`, `:mutation`, `:resource-scope`, `:app-schema`) route by late-bind to the OWNING lifecycle fn — the same hooks the fx forms already call. Delete the nine names and the nilary clear-all arities (tests use `registrar/clear-kind!`). Completeness for `:cofx` / `:interceptor` / `:view` / `:head` / `:error-projector` / `:app-schema` falls out with zero new names. `:rf.fx/clear-flow` stays (its arg is the same id). Mirrors `handler-meta`.
- **(F) complete the family.** Six new names, ONE shape `(id)` / `(id {:frame f})` exact, nilary dropped; reunite `clear-flow` on the facade (rf2-uhk4's first reading). Same rule, more names.
- **(G) leave it.** Close rf2-uhk4 as won't-fix.

**Codex (carry into the ruling).** "The universal `clear` proposal is underdiagnosed. Resource clearing removes the registration AND disposes live cache entries, timers and in-flight work across frames (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc`). Route clearing emits its dedicated lifecycle trace. Flow clearing vacates an output leaf and settles dependents (`flows/registry.cljc:833` docstring; see rf2-g1zb for a live bug in exactly that settle). Therefore routing every registrar kind through `registrar/unregister!` is not behaviour-preserving; the nine names are not nine spellings of `dissoc-in`. A generic inverse remains possible as a thin dispatcher to owning lifecycle operations, but then its kind-specific semantics, scope rules and return values still exist. With three observed non-test clear call sites, there is no strong ergonomic case to build a universal teardown abstraction or invent six missing inverses merely for symmetry." Fable's honest costs: `rf/clear :sub` is less greppable than `rf/clear-sub`; `clear-event` / `clear-sub` / `clear-fx` are v1-preserved (`API.md:162-164`) so a migration README row is owed; the generic verb cannot carry per-kind docstrings — the 001 kind table becomes the doc.

**Recommendation.** (E), with codex's parity condition as the acceptance bar: the dispatcher routes each kind to its OWNING lifecycle fn and never short-cuts a kind that owns runtime state to `unregister!`; the PR shows resource disposal, route trace and flow settle preserved by the EXISTING tests for those three. If that parity cannot be shown cheaply, (F) is the fallback — but (F) is how the family reached nine names in three shapes. Not (G): three shapes with six holes is option soup wearing a uniform, and pre-alpha is the cheap moment.

## Q3 — the http interceptor fx pair

**Today.** `:rf.fx/reg-http-interceptor` / `:rf.fx/clear-http-interceptor` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/managed.cljc:226-260`, ns docstring :12-19, rationale comment :212-225). Zero consumers in `examples/`, `testbeds/`, `tools/` after ~200 registration opportunities; both shipped http examples register at boot with the macro. Args are a re-spelled map (`{:id …}`), which @spellings.2's rule would forbid.

**Consumers the fable census did not class.** The conformance corpus drives BOTH fxs as pure data (rf2-yhfgf): `spec/conformance/fixtures/http-interceptor-before-transforms.edn` (6 mentions), `spec/conformance/fixtures/http-interceptor-clear.edn` (8), the DSL realisation arm `implementation/core/src/re_frame/conformance.cljc:267-380` (the interceptor's `:before` body is a DSL body realised into a fn), `spec/conformance/README.md:539-540`. `spec/conformance/` is port-facing, so deleting the pair is a conformance-corpus change, not only an fx removal. Plus `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_interceptors_test.clj:880-1030` (rf2-oyd1b tests), `spec/API.md:403-404`, `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` (2 mentions), `docs/api/re-frame.http.md:255-283`, `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:2528`, `skills/re-frame-migration/references/pre-rename-upgrades.md:23`, `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:86`, `middleware.cljc:214,273` (comments).

**Codex.** "HTTP interceptors are frame-scoped, and their effects deliberately carry the dispatching frame. They satisfy that half of the proposed rule; what is absent is a shipped handler-time consumer. Removing or demoting those effects is a reasonable low-priority pruning decision, not proof that effects and boot-time function calls are equivalent. Do not manufacture an application-specific wrapper just to improve the public-name count."

**Options.** (H) delete the pair and its fixtures, park with the un-park trigger "a shipped example installs an interceptor from a handler (post-login bearer token)" and the pre-settled POSITIONAL shape `[:rf.fx/reg-http-interceptor [id interceptor-map]]` per @spellings.2's rule. (I) keep, re-shape args to positional per the rule (breaking to zero app consumers; fixtures and tests update). (J) keep as is, recorded as the rule's exception.

**Recommendation.** (H). The demand bar has ruled; the two conformance fixtures exercise the fx TRANSPORT, not the middleware chain (which `http_interceptors_test.clj` covers through the fn form), so no port obligation is lost except the fx itself. **Coordination:** `http-request-surface.md` proposes the same deletion; if the http area's spec file carries it, the coordinator keeps one bead and re-points the other.

## Implementation beads to file when ruled

- **Q1 (a)** → `api(registry): emit the CLJS same-name alias from defreg-macro; delete the hand-written alias block (core.cljc:262-352)`. After @spellings.1 (its concordance check is the regression net). Non-hot except Conventions' one sentence.
- **Q2 (E)** → `api(registry): add (rf/clear kind id ?{:frame f}) and delete the nine clear-* names`. Code: `core.cljc` new `clear` dispatching on kind → `registrar/unregister!` or late-bind hooks (`:flows/clear-flow`, `:http/clear-http-interceptor`, routing's, resources' three, a new `:schemas/clear-app-schema`); `flows/registry.cljc:833` opts hardened to the exact shape; delete `core.cljc:1069-1080, 1501, 1545, 1573, 2545` and the public re-exports in `flows.cljc:48` / `routing.cljc:78` (owning fns stay as hook targets). Consumers: Xray `registry.cljs:352,411,412`; ~83 test calls. Spec (HOT): `API.md` §Clearing registrations :156-166 → one row, rows :402 / :460 / :462 / :464, :839-852; `Conventions.md` :1370-1378 tear-down roster, :1586. Non-hot: `001-Registration.md:87-117` (clear column), `013` / `014` / `016` (`clear-*` mentions: 2 / 2 / 5). Docs: `docs/api/re-frame.core.md` (8), `re-frame.http.md` (1), `re-frame.resources.md` (3), `docs/core/flows.md` (1), `docs/async/http-going-further.md` (1), `docs/EP/EP-0003-resource-queries.md` (2). Skills: `api-cheatsheet.md:86,95,187`. Migration README: new row `clear-event` / `clear-sub` / `clear-fx` → `(rf/clear :event id)` etc. Manifest: `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen` (nine rows out, one in; `docs/api` projection check). Close rf2-uhk4 citing the ruling.
- **Q2 (F)** → `api(registry): complete the clear-* family — six names, one exact-opts shape, clear-flow back on the facade`. Closes rf2-uhk4.
- **Q3 (H)** → `api(http): delete :rf.fx/reg-http-interceptor / :rf.fx/clear-http-interceptor, their conformance fixtures and DSL arm` (or the http area's equivalent). Deletion list as enumerated above; `spec/conformance/README.md` rows; then @spellings.2's open-disposition sentence is removed. mcp-conformance: `git grep` finds no tool reference to the two fixtures, but the worker re-checks the conformance runner's fixture roster.

## Priority

P3: medium, one-reviewer, codex cautions on all three. Q2's v1-preserved names and Q3's fx ids ARE surface at the first alpha tag, so a ruling before the tag avoids a post-tag break.

## The problem

All 15 macro rows are generated by one form, `defreg-macro` (core_reg_macros.cljc:250; `reg-event` by `defreg-event-macro`, :311): bind `re-frame.source-coords/*pending-coords*` (source_coords.cljc:54) from `(meta &form)` / `*file*` / `*ns*` around a call to the owning fn, which merges the coords into the stored metadata (`merge-coords`, :90). The alias rows are a **second, hand-written list** (F:262-352).

### The rule as written

1. **`*` twins** — Conventions.md:1462-1479: a `*` fn exists only where the macro does something the same-name alias cannot (defs a Var / injects locals — `reg-view`; walks a literal — `reg-machine`); "a separate `*`-suffixed Var would be a pure redundant twin". Cross-Spec-Interactions.md:231 §21 says the same and calls it Locked.
2. **Convention A** — Conventions.md:1481-1483: for `reg-event, reg-sub, reg-fx, reg-cofx, reg-flow, reg-route, reg-app-schema, reg-app-schemas, reg-interceptor, dispatch, dispatch-sync, subscribe` the macro's own name is also the fn value on CLJS; "adding a `reg-event*` synonym would be a pure alias".
3. **Why macros at all** — 001-Registration.md:164-206: coords come from `(meta &form)`; the macro is the capture path, the fn the merge path; production strips coords from public meta and keeps them only in the error-coord registry. API.md:22: registration macros stay on the facade "because they capture call-site source-coords and have no owned-namespace macro form — registration stays central" (rf2-wad2fl).
4. **fx forms** — 013-Flows.md:425-447 gives the mechanism: a handler cannot call a registrar (it is an effect), and the fx threads the dispatching frame in as `:frame`. No rule anywhere says *which* registrars get an fx form; 014 has no fx-form rationale at all — the only one is a comment in managed.cljc:222-225 ("a clean alternative to the fn-call shape for codebases that prefer to drive bootstrap through the dispatch surface"). Conventions.md:478-482 places the flows pair under `:rf.fx/*` as a "single principled exception".
5. **Inverse** — Conventions.md:1370-1378: `clear-*` is the "symmetric inverse of `reg-*`"; roster `clear-event, clear-sub, clear-fx, clear-flow, clear-route, clear-http-interceptor`.

### The rule as applied

**A. One form per registrar, both faces generated.** Fold the CLJS alias block (F:262-352) into `defreg-macro`: on the CLJS reader branch the same form emits `(def reg-x owning/reg-x)` with the macro's docstring; on the JVM it emits the macro as today. Every one of the 15 non-Var-defining registrars then has Convention A by construction — the five missing aliases appear, and the list in Conventions.md:1483 is replaced by "every `reg-*` that does not def a Var". **The written rule (one paragraph, for Conventions.md).** A registrar is a macro in call position and a fn in value position, under one name, on every host that has macros; the macro's only job is provenance capture and it is generated, never hand-written. A `*`-suffixed fn exists only where the macro also does syntactic work a value cannot (defs a Var, walks a literal) — today `reg-view*` on the facade and `reg-machine*` in its owning namespace. An fx form exists only for a frame-scoped registrar with a named handler-time consumer and takes the registrar's positional args verbatim. The inverse of every registration is `(clear kind id ?opts)`; there are no per-kind clear names.

## Why this is better (ethos)

- **The macro is the right axis, and it is Clojure's own.** `defn` stamps `:line` / `:file` on the Var; definition forms carry provenance, and Clojure spells them as macros. `reg-*` are re-frame2's definition forms — the same reason `assert` and `is` are macros. Runtime stack capture (001:181 lists it for TypeScript ports) costs a `js/Error` per registration, depends on source maps, has no JVM parity, and cannot be DCE'd; the macro path is compile-time and strips to nothing in production (001:193-206). What was wrong was never the macro, it was naming the fn twice — `let` / `let*` cuts both ways: `let*` earns its star because it is a *different* form (no destructuring), while a `*` that only forgets the line number is a name for nothing. rf2-m90brg said this; A makes it structurally impossible to need one again.
- **Regularity over cleverness (Principles:18).** Two hand lists that must agree will not; the tree proves it (five aliases missing, two unlisted, four wrong M/Fn rows). One generator, one table, one sentence of convention.
- **Many definers, one un-definer.** Clojure has `def`, `defn`, `defmacro`, `defmulti` — and `ns-unmap`. The registrar is one map; nine `clear-*` names for `dissoc-in` on it is the "one fact, many names" hazard Principles §The demand bar (:124) exists to prevent, and the missing six show the per-kind naming cannot even stay complete. `clear` mirrors `handler-meta`: kinds are data (Principles §Data is code, :103), and the tear-down axis collapses to one verb with one opts contract — so the rf2-s32bf hardening applies to every frame-scoped kind at once instead of one.
- **Data is code, literally.** An fx form is the fn form written as data; the http pair re-spelled the args, so the two spellings of one registration disagreed on shape. Rule C fixes the shape by construction: `(apply reg-x args)`.
- **The demand bar has already ruled** on the http fx pair (0 takers, ~200 opportunities), on `reg-app-schemas` (3 takers for a `run!`), and *for* the flows pair (two boot-time and two handler-time consumers — a designed dual with a mechanism discriminator).
- **Honest costs.** `rf/clear :sub` is less greppable than `rf/clear-sub` (mitigated: the kind keyword is greppable, and only three non-test call sites exist). `clear-event` / `clear-sub` / `clear-fx` are v1-preserved names (API.md:162-164) — a migration row is owed. The generic `clear` cannot carry per-kind docstrings; the kind table in 001:87 becomes the doc. A/E touch the two hottest spec files.

## Codex Thoughts

**Verdict: repair the alias/documentation drift; do not adopt this entire package as one simplification.** The macro/value distinction is useful Clojure machinery, and the remaining `reg-view*` and machine construction seams perform additional syntactic or programmatic jobs. The original star-twin cleanup is already landed. Correct teaching material and fill genuine Convention-A omissions without reopening that work.

[The current facade](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc) still maintains a separate CLJS alias block. A common descriptor can prevent drift, but the generator sketch is not an implementation: [the existing macro generator](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_macros.cljc) is JVM-reader-gated and emits JVM macros. Simply teaching it to emit another reader branch does not ensure the CLJS compilation gets its value definition. Prefer the smallest repair—missing aliases plus a concordance check—unless one shared declaration can serve both host compilation paths without new build machinery. Check value-position calls as well as literal macro calls, and preserve coordinate capture and production elision. The rule must exclude macros that walk syntax, not just macros that define a Var.

**The universal `clear` proposal is underdiagnosed.** [Resource clearing](../../../../implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc) removes the registration **and** disposes live cache entries, timers and in-flight work across frames. [Route clearing](../../../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc) emits its dedicated lifecycle trace. [Flow clearing](../../../../implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc) vacates an output leaf and settles dependents. Therefore, routing every registrar kind through `registrar/unregister!` is not behavior-preserving; the nine names are not nine spellings of `dissoc-in`. A generic inverse remains possible as a thin dispatcher to owning lifecycle operations, but then its kind-specific semantics, scope rules and return values still exist. With three observed non-test clear call sites, there is no strong ergonomic case to build a universal teardown abstraction or invent six missing inverses merely for symmetry. Keep the existing lifecycle doors for now; remove demonstrably unnecessary public exposure separately.

The HTTP effect-pair argument also needs correction: [HTTP interceptors are frame-scoped](../../../../implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/middleware.cljc), and [their effects](../../../../implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/managed.cljc) deliberately carry the dispatching frame. They satisfy that half of the proposed rule; what is absent is a shipped handler-time consumer. Removing or demoting those effects is a reasonable low-priority pruning decision, not proof that effects and boot-time function calls are equivalent. Do not manufacture an application-specific wrapper just to improve the public-name count.

Keep `reg-app-schemas`, as the cross-check already concludes. Its up-front path validation protects feature registration from partial application caused by a bad path. Precisely, this is **prevalidation**, not a general transaction rolling back every possible later failure. No new transactional machinery is required.

Implementation should therefore be small and separable: alias conformance and stale documentation first; optional HTTP-effect pruning second. If generic clearing is reconsidered, first demonstrate parity for resource disposal, flow settling and route evidence, rather than treating lifecycle correctness as a follow-up. Elegance is fewer concepts, not merely fewer exported names.

import re, subprocess, sys, collections, os
os.chdir(r"C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2")
files = subprocess.check_output(["git","ls-files"], text=True, encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
exts = (".clj",".cljc",".cljs",".edn",".md")
def cls(p):
    if p.startswith("examples/"): return "examples"
    if p.startswith("tools/"):
        return "tools-test" if "/test/" in p else "tools"
    if p.startswith("testbeds/"): return "testbeds"
    if p.startswith("docs/"): return "docs"
    if p.startswith("skills/"): return "skills"
    if p.startswith("migration/"): return "migration"
    if p.startswith("spec/"): return "spec"
    if p.startswith("implementation/"):
        return "impl-test" if "/test/" in p else "impl-src"
    return None
names = ["reg-event","reg-sub","reg-fx","reg-cofx","reg-interceptor","reg-view","reg-view*",
         "reg-machine","reg-machine*","defmachine","make-machine-handler",
         "reg-app-schema","reg-app-schemas","reg-flow","clear-flow","reg-route","clear-route",
         "reg-head","reg-error-projector","reg-http-interceptor","clear-http-interceptor",
         "reg-resource","reg-mutation","reg-resource-scope","clear-resource","clear-mutation","clear-resource-scope",
         "with-managed-request-stubs","with-managed-request-stubs*",
         "register-listener!","unregister-listener!","register-observability-sink!","unregister-observability-sink!",
         "clear-event","clear-sub","clear-fx","clear-cofx","clear-interceptor","clear-view","clear-machine",
         "clear-app-schema","clear-head","clear-error-projector"]
fxs = [":rf.fx/reg-flow",":rf.fx/clear-flow",":rf.fx/reg-http-interceptor",":rf.fx/clear-http-interceptor"]
# counts[name][cls][spelling] -> n ; spelling in {call:<alias>, value:<alias>, bare-call}
counts = collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter))
examples = collections.defaultdict(list)
fxcounts = collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter)
fxex = collections.defaultdict(list)
name_re = {n: re.compile(r"(?<![\w.*!?/-])(?:([\w.*!?-]+)/)?" + re.escape(n) + r"(?![\w*!?-])") for n in names}
for p in files:
    if not p.endswith(exts): continue
    c = cls(p)
    if c is None: continue
    try:
        txt = open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except Exception: continue
    for n in names:
        if n not in txt: continue
        for m in name_re[n].finditer(txt):
            alias = m.group(1)
            start = m.start()
            prev = txt[start-1] if start>0 else ""
            # skip definitions
            line_start = txt.rfind("\n",0,start)+1
            line = txt[line_start: txt.find("\n",start) if txt.find("\n",start)!=-1 else len(txt)]
            if re.match(r"\s*\((defn-?|defmacro|def)\s+" + re.escape(n) + r"(?![\w*!?-])", line): continue
            if re.match(r"\s*" + re.escape(n) + r"\s+[\w.-]+/" , line) and alias is None: continue  # def alias line
            if alias is None and prev != "(":
                continue  # bare symbol not in call position: ambiguous (refer lists, prose) — skip
            kind = ("call" if prev == "(" else "value")
            if alias is None: sp = "bare-call"
            else: sp = f"{kind}:{alias}"
            counts[n][c][sp] += 1
            lineno = txt.count("\n",0,start)+1
            if len(examples[(n,c,sp)]) < 4:
                examples[(n,c,sp)].append(f"{p}:{lineno}: {line.strip()[:110]}")
    for fx in fxs:
        if fx not in txt: continue
        for m in re.finditer(re.escape(fx)+r"(?![\w-])", txt):
            fxcounts[fx][c]+=1
            lineno = txt.count("\n",0,m.start())+1
            line_start = txt.rfind("\n",0,m.start())+1
            line = txt[line_start: txt.find("\n",m.start())]
            if len(fxex[(fx,c)])<4: fxex[(fx,c)].append(f"{p}:{lineno}: {line.strip()[:110]}")
order = ["examples","testbeds","tools","tools-test","docs","skills","migration","spec","impl-src","impl-test"]
for n in names:
    print(f"\n=== {n}")
    for c in order:
        if counts[n][c]:
            print(f"  {c:10s} " + ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k,v in sorted(counts[n][c].items(), key=lambda kv:-kv[1])))
print("\n=== fx forms")
for fx in fxs:
    print(f"  {fx}: " + ", ".join(f"{c}={fxcounts[fx][c]}" for c in order if fxcounts[fx][c]))
if "--examples" in sys.argv:
    print("\n=== example lines")
    for k,v in examples.items():
        if k[1] in ("examples","testbeds","tools","docs","skills"):
            print(k); [print("   ",x) for x in v]
    for k,v in fxex.items():
        if k[1] in ("examples","testbeds","tools","docs","skills"):
            print(k); [print("   ",x) for x in v]

## The problem

The registrar is one map, `(kind, id) → metadata` (`spec/001-Registration.md:89`; the closed kind set is `implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc:144-145`). The **read** side already speaks that grammar: `(handler-meta kind id)`, `(registrations kind)` (`spec/API.md:520-521`). The **write** side is per-kind by design — `reg-event`, `reg-sub`, `reg-flow` … — because each registrar's argument grammar differs, and that is not in question here. What is in question is the third verb, the **inverse**, which is neither uniform like the read side nor principled like the write side. Three questions came out of the wave-3 registration-spellings review; two sibling beads from the same review (rf2-kuky.23, rf2-kuky.24) have already merged and changed the ground under Q1 and Q3, so each question is stated as it stands at tip, not as filed.

### Q1 — the macro table and the alias table

`re-frame.core` emits its fifteen `reg-*` macros from one generator, `defreg-macro` / `defreg-event-macro` (`core_reg_macros.cljc:250` / `:311`, both under `#?(:clj …)`), with the fifteen rows at `core.cljc:499-689`. Each macro captures `(meta &form)` / `*file*` / `*ns*` and splices to the owning fn. The CLJS same-name value alias — `(def reg-flow rf.core-flows/reg-flow)` for HoF / programmatic callers — is a **second, hand-written list** at `core.cljc:277-408`.

When the review ran, that second list had drifted: aliases for 10 of 15, and the spec's roster named a different 12. **That is fixed.** PR #9291 (rf2-kuky.23, merged 2026-09-05) added the five missing aliases and landed `implementation/core/test/re_frame/registrar_alias_concordance_cljs_test.cljc`, which reads `core.cljc` itself once under `:features #{:clj}` and once under `#{:cljs}` and fails the suite when the two halves differ — no third list to drift. `Conventions.md:1491` now states Convention A as a rule, not a roster, and cites the pin. The comment at `core.cljc:265-275` records the same.

So Q1 today is not "how do we stop the drift" — it is "having stopped it with a derived test, do we also want the generator to make a gap impossible by construction, at the cost of host-dispatch machinery inside the facade's one compile-time mechanism". The .23 worker considered exactly that and declined: *one declaration serving both hosts would need host dispatch plus lifting the 15-row table out of its reader conditional — new machinery, and the generator is itself the open ruling on rf2-kuky.25*.

Honest reading of that diff: the one-verb form is a keystroke *worse* in HoF position, and `rg clear-sub` becomes `rg 'clear :sub'`. Those are the real ergonomic costs; they are small, and they are the whole of them.

**The strongest counter-evidence is codex's, and it is correct as far as it goes.** The nine are not nine spellings of `dissoc-in`. `clear-resource` removes the registration **and** disposes every frame's cache entries, timers and in-flight work (`registry.cljc:647-671`); `clear-route` emits `:rf.route/cleared` (`routing/registry.cljc:594-606`); `clear-flow` vacates the output leaf and, outside a drain, settles dependents — and rf2-g1zb was a live P2 bug in exactly that settle (a dependent flow kept publishing a value derived from a producer that no longer existed), fixed by PRs #9204 and #9257. So a `clear` that short-cuts every kind to `unregister!` would be a behaviour change, and codex's conclusion is that with three call sites there is *no strong ergonomic case to build a universal teardown abstraction*. Read carefully, though, rf2-g1zb cuts both ways: it proves that clear is **lifecycle, not dissoc** — which is an argument for a dispatcher rather than against a single door, and it means today's nine names were *hiding* that the operations differ. Under one verb the difference sits in one docstring's kind table instead of nine files.

## The decision

- **Q1.** Build a host-aware `defreg` that emits the CLJS alias from the same row (**A**), or keep the two hand-written lists pinned by the landed concordance test (**B**)?
- **Q2.** One kind-keyed `(rf/clear kind id ?{:frame f})` replacing the nine names (**E**); complete the per-kind family — six new names, one exact-opts shape, `clear-flow` back on the facade (**F**); or leave the family as it is (**G**)?
- **Q3.** Delete the fx pair, fixtures and DSL arm (**H**); keep it and re-shape its args to positional per the rule (**I**); or keep it as-is as the rule's recorded exception (**J**)?

## Options

### Q1

#### A. Fold the CLJS alias into `defreg-macro`

*What changes.* `defreg-macro` dispatches on `(:ns &env)`: JVM expansion emits today's `defmacro`; CLJS expansion emits `(def reg-x delegate)` with the same docstring and the rf2-9wwkcm `:doc` DCE gating. The 15-row table leaves its `#?(:clj …)` conditional; the alias block (`core.cljc:277-408`, ~130 lines) is deleted; the concordance test becomes a tautology and is deleted too. *Cost.* New host-dispatch inside the facade's one macro-defining macro; `core.cljc` is a hot-zone-adjacent single-toucher file that ~20 rf2-kuky children queue behind; the two docstrings (macro-flavoured, alias-flavoured) become one. Feasibility is unprototyped — codex: *"simply teaching it to emit another reader branch does not ensure the CLJS compilation gets its value definition"*. *Buys.* A missing alias becomes impossible rather than test-caught; ~130 lines gone. *Weighed in.* Fable for; codex against ("prefer the smallest repair"); the .23 worker declined it on the same grounds.

#### B. Keep the pin; do nothing

*What changes.* Nothing. The derived test already turned the drift from latent into red-on-PR, and `Conventions.md:1491-1493` states the rule. *Cost.* Two declarations per registrar remain, side by side in table order. *Buys.* No new mechanism; the cheap moment for a generator is *after* the alias block next grows, if it ever does.

### Q2

#### E. One verb: `(rf/clear kind id)` / `(rf/clear kind id {:frame f})`

*What changes.* One facade fn. Registrar kinds (`:event :sub :fx :cofx :interceptor :view :head :error-projector`) route to `registrar/unregister!`; `:route` to `routing/clear-route` (trace preserved); `:flow` / `:http-interceptor` / `:resource` / `:mutation` / `:resource-scope` late-bind to the owning lifecycle fns through the `defwrapper`s that already exist (`core_flows.cljc:15`, `core_http.cljc:86`, `core_resources.cljc:43/:101/:166`) — so artefact-absent still raises the documented `:rf.error/<artefact>-artefact-missing`. The whole implementation is the dispatch table; this is the shape Mike is ruling on, not a sketch of new machinery:

(defn clear

   owning lifecycle fn (see 001 §Registry model, clear column); the rest to

description:
GATED ACT, MIKE'S HANDS ONLY. Three tag pushes, in a fixed order, with a mandatory read
between each. No worker pushes a tag. RULED 2026-09-09 (see notes for the full runbook,
the dependency proof, the recovery cascade and the local rehearsal).

THE SEQUENCE (V=$(cat VERSION); re-read it, never type a version from memory):

  1. machines-viz-v$V   -> release-machines-viz.yml -> 1 jar
     READ: registry 200, published pom by eye, cold -Stree with a fresh :mvn/local-repo
  2. xray-v$V           -> release-xray.yml         -> 1 jar
     READ: same three. Then settle rf2-qvyr before going on.
  3. story-v$V          -> release-story.yml        -> 3 jars (mcp-base, story, story-mcp)
     READ: same three, ONCE PER JAR.

Push the ONE tag by name each time. NEVER git push --tags -- this checkout carries
local-only safety/* tags that must not reach origin.

THE ORDER IS STRUCTURAL, not editorial. tools/xray/deps.edn:75 declares machines-viz as a
top-level runtime coordinate; tools/story/deps.edn:67 declares xray. Each workflow rewrites
those :local/root coords to :mvn/version and resolves the graph FROM CLOJARS before
deploying (release-machines-viz.yml:278; preflight-xray-package.sh:135 for xray, which has
no explicit clojure -P; release-story.yml:373 and :512). An out-of-order tag fails at
classpath resolution rather than publishing something broken.

BUT A RED RUN DOES NOT MEAN NOTHING PUBLISHED. release-story.yml gives deploy-story
(needs [verify-version, test-story], :307) and deploy-mcp-base (needs [verify-version,
test-mcp-base], :409) INDEPENDENT prerequisites -- they run in parallel, and only
deploy-story-mcp waits on both (:468). A story-v* tag whose story branch dies can still
have permanently published mcp-base. After any red run, inspect EVERY publishing job and
EACH exact GAV. Never push a premature tag as an ordering probe.

run, inspect EVERY publishing job and EACH exact GAV before concluding nothing shipped.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Codex found this; the dossier missed it; verified at source. The PUBLISHED Story graph
pulls TWO providers of one canonical namespace:

re-frame.adapter.reagent-slim. A complete pom and a green clojure -P are both consistent
with the collision -- neither gate looks at it.

Source-derived, not reproduced at runtime. Settle it at the dependency boundary and prove
the packaged consumer graph before story-v* is cut; do not let classpath order pick an
adapter. Do not turn it into an adapter re-architecture, and do not assume an untested
exclusion preserves both tools' contracts.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. THE RECOVERY CASCADE -- see rf2-yskb (open, P3)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

rewrite-local-root-coord.sh:91 pins EVERY sibling at the single repo-root VERSION. There is
no per-sibling override anywhere in the three workflows. So a tools-tier recovery bump
CANNOT ship alone: xray-v0.0.1.alpha-1 would pin nine framework artefacts at 0.0.1.alpha-1,
which do not exist, and the tag dies at classpath resolution. Restoring the full set is:

  v0.0.1.alpha-1 (14 framework) -> machines-viz-v0.0.1.alpha-1 -> xray-v...-1 -> story-v...-1 (3 jars)

All 19, in order. docs/release-process.md:174-177 says only that the framework goes "out of
lockstep", which is incomplete; rf2-yskb owns correcting it. BOUND IT CORRECTLY (Codex):
19 is the cost of RESTORING THE COMPLETE SET at a bumped version -- it is NOT the blast
radius of every single failure. A bad machines-viz caught at tag 1 does not force xray and
story to be published if they stay deferred, and it does not make mcp-base bad. What
reading between tags shrinks is the number of WRONG jars in public (1 vs 5) and how early
you learn, not the cost of a full restore.

Recovery posture is unchanged: bump-and-supersede. Never re-run the same tag (Clojars 409s
the duplicate and the re-run looks stuck), never ask for a yank. Clojars' FAQ does allow
exceptional deletion requests, so "impossible" is strictly too strong -- that changes
nothing here and is not licence to plan around it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. THE LOCAL REHEARSAL -- free, and it is how you de-risk the irreversible step
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Every step of a tool release except clein deploy runs locally. Toolchain confirmed present
(Clojure CLI 1.12.4.1618, JDK 21, python3 3.14; the rewrite script is POSIX sh + python3
and runs from Git Bash). Run it AFTER the framework tier publishes (the rewrite resolves
