title: A with-frame taken inside a Reagent render no longer decides the frame: listeners that dispatch there reach the provider's frame
description:
## Problem

Since 3c2550942e (#11535, Reagent views resolve their frame from the component tree first), re-frame.views/current-frame asks the tree before the dynamic var whenever a Reagent component is rendering. So code that runs during a render, but is not itself the view, loses an explicit (with-frame :x ...) taken inside it: an ambient dispatch or subscribe there resolves to the enclosing frame-provider's frame, not :x.

Such code does run during renders. Epoch capture notifies :epoch listeners as it records a view render (re-frame.epoch.listeners/record-render! via re-frame.epoch.capture/capture-event!, which re-frame.views/emit-view-render-trace! reaches from render-in-scope). Trace callbacks run there too.

Measured case (rf2-qrxxc, PR #11555): the Xray testbed runner's :epoch listener called day8.re-frame2-xray.focus/focus!, which dispatched inside (with-frame :rf/xray ...). Every :rf.xray/* event ran in the host frame :rf/default instead. The listener re-fired on each of those epochs, and the host app-db grew until the page's main thread wedged. #11555 fixes that one site by passing {:frame :rf/xray} on every dispatch.

## Question

Is "the tree wins over a with-frame" meant to hold for a with-frame taken INSIDE the render (in a listener or callback the render reaches), or only for one wrapped AROUND a synchronous render (the case #11535's tests pin)? If only the latter, the resolver needs a way to tell the two apart; core could, for instance, deliver epoch listeners outside the render. If both, the other with-frame + ambient-op sites reachable from render-time listeners need explicit {:frame ...}. tools/xray/src has about a dozen with-frame sites; none was audited for render-time reachability.

## Acceptance

A ruling on the rule. Then either core keeps an inner with-frame in charge during a render, or each listener-reachable with-frame site in tools/ and implementation/ names its frame explicitly.
notes:
== RULING (mayor, under the project stance), 2026-10-20 05:40:56 AUSEST: an inner with-frame DECIDES. A with-frame taken inside a render's own extent (in a listener, trace callback or any code the render reaches) is the nearest, most explicit statement of the frame, and it wins over the component tree. The tree keeps winning over a with-frame bound AROUND a synchronous render, the case Spec 002 §Reading the frame from React context item 3 and #11535's tests pin. That rule exists because a binding around a render belongs to a different extent from the render; the reasoning does not reach a binding the render's own code takes. Why: 'trust the programmer' and 'low friction' both reject silently overriding an explicit with-frame. The alternative (every render-reachable callback in tools/ and in user code names {:frame ...}) puts the footgun on every author. Mike may overrule; the change is small and reversible.
Shape: core tells the two apart, e.g. by recording the dynamic binding in effect when a render begins and letting a binding that differs from it at resolution time win. The worker picks the least machinery. The rule covers every render-time ambient op, so delivering only epoch listeners outside the render would be too narrow. #11555's explicit {:frame :rf/xray} sites stay; they become redundant but harmless.
== DISPATCH (mayor), 2026-10-20 05:40:56 AUSEST: worker frame-inner-with-frame (branch worker/frame-inner-with-frame). Spec 002 item 3 is released to it.
== WORKER (frame-inner-with-frame), 2026-10-20 06:29:26 AUSEST: DONE in PR #11556 (draft until marked ready). Disposition: done.
Mechanism: every framework binder of *current-frame* (the with-frame and with-new-frame expansions, bind-fn, and the router's per-handler binding in process-event!) now binds re-frame.frame/*current-frame-bound-in* beside it, set to the component rendering at that moment. re-frame.frame/bound-inside-render? compares it with the rendering component by identity, and re-frame.views/current-frame skips the tree tier when it holds. So a binding the render's own code takes (view body, :epoch listener, trace callback, a handler the render runs synchronously) decides, while one taken around the render (component nil at bind time) still loses to the tree. The binding records the render because a plain Reagent fn offers no render-start seam. Comparing by identity also covers an inner with-frame that names the same frame as an outer one.
The handler-in-render case (rf2-o9ti0) is now an instance of the same rule. event-run-inside-render? and the :render-host entry on the event-owner binding are deleted; a census at HEAD finds 0 hits, against 3 at trunk 4262a17899.
Tests: plain_fn_frame_from_tree_dom_cljs_test gains three server-render cases (plain fn, reg-view, and an :epoch listener the render notifies). In each, with-frame :tenant/inner resolves current-frame-id, subscribe and dispatch-sync to :tenant/inner, while the bare read beside it resolves the provider. A further case pins a with-frame around a server render losing to the tree. Red at trunk: 11 tests, 19 assertions, 9 failures. Green after the fix: 0 failures.

== MERGED CODE (mayor), 2026-10-20 06:31:11 AUSEST: PR #11556 rebase-merged at 33187bb78e. Every framework binder of *current-frame* (the with-frame and with-new-frame expansions, bind-fn, and the router's per-handler binding) also binds the no-doc var re-frame.frame/*current-frame-bound-in* to the component rendering at that moment. re-frame.frame/bound-inside-render? compares it by identity with the rendering component, and re-frame.views/current-frame skips the tree when it holds. CI: 84 checks (76 passed, 8 skipped).

title: Disposal runs every on-dispose callback even when one throws, then rethrows the first failure
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 that a disposal runs every registered on-dispose callback, in registration order, even when one throws, and then rethrows the first failure.

No new error classes, no policy switches, no universal disposable scope. One focused throw-and-re-entry test settles it.

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e. Paths are under `implementation/core/src/re_frame/`.

- **The promise.** `IDisposable/-dispose` (`disposable.cljs:48-53`) promises to "fire every registered on-dispose callback", and Spec 006 §On-dispose hooks says the same (`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:949`). Neither says what a throw does.
- **The spine.** Its derived value's `-dispose` (`substrate/spine.cljs:972-999`) works in this order:
  1. flips its disposed guard;
  2. releases its source wires;
  3. snapshots and clears its callbacks;
  4. runs them with a bare `doseq` (`:997-999`).
- **Plain-atom's derived value.** Its shared `dispose!` (`substrate/plain_atom.cljc:116-123`) does the same. It is reached from the CLJS `-dispose` (`:152-157`) and the JVM `-dispose` (`:141`).
- **So one throw strands every later callback.** They are already cleared and the guard is already flipped, so no later dispose can run them. Those callbacks include:
  - the sub-cache's slot eviction and input releases (`subs.cljc:1357`, `:1384`);
  - the React hook's release of its committed reference (`substrate/spine.cljs:3367`);
  - the disposal callback `acquire-watched-reaction!` arms for Fresco's collector (`subs.cljc:2542`).
- **The spine already drains this way elsewhere.** `drain-after-render-queue!` (`spine.cljs:1503-1526`) and the adapter-teardown capture (`:1660-1730`) both:
  - run every step;
  - keep the first throw by presence against `capture-none` (`:101`), so a thrown `nil` still counts;
  - surface that throw once the walk ends.

## Change

- **The walk.** At both sites, run the whole snapshot in order, each callback under its own catch. After the walk, rethrow the first failure unchanged; drop later ones. Keep the first by presence, as the spine does, so a `nil` or `false` throw still surfaces.
- **The order stays:** guard flip, source release, snapshot-and-clear, then the walk. Re-entry from a callback stays a no-op.
- **Shape.** Use one small helper both sites call, or the same loop at each; the worker's call. Both files already require `re-frame.error`.
- **Docstring.** The `-dispose` docstring (`disposable.cljs:48-53`) adds that a throwing callback does not stop the walk, and that the first failure is rethrown after it.
- **Out of scope:**
  - Reagent reactions dispose through stock `reagent.ratom`, which this bead does not change.
  - The JVM `re-frame.interop` `Reaction` (`interop.clj:98-111`) walks the same way, and its protocol docstring states that rule (`:93-96`). Its only constructor is the JVM `make-reaction` (`:120-124`), which no production code calls. Leave it.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:949`, §On-dispose hooks, gains one sentence. On the re-frame-owned derived values (the spine and plain-atom), a throwing callback does not stop the walk: every callback runs, then the first failure is rethrown. Reagent's stock dispose is outside that sentence. **Hot zone.**

## Acceptance

title: Move with-fx-overrides from re-frame.core to re-frame.test-support, no alias left behind
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 that `with-fx-overrides` moves from `re-frame.core` to `re-frame.test-support`, with no alias left behind.

It is test tooling, and `re-frame.test-support` is where the other test macros live.

Its ns has no self `:require-macros`, so CLJS callers name each macro in their own `:require-macros` (`:1171`).
- **Call sites: four.**

title: skill(re-frame-migration): O-16 companion lets a boot machine skip the run token and keep :final? terminals, but v1 async-flow restarts on a re-issued :async-flow and orchestrating §3 allows no exception
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626. Priority 2: two pages disagree, and the companion's exception leads a migration into a machine that cannot be restarted.

## Skill file and section

- migration/from-re-frame-v1/async-flow-fx-to-reg-machine.md (the O-16 companion), §Retarget the producers, the paragraph after the worked example (line 196).
- skills/re-frame-migration/references/orchestrating-a-large-migration.md §3, first bullet (line 79).

## What it says

- Companion :196: "A consumer that runs once and is never restarted — a boot machine — can skip the token and its guard; its terminal states may be `:final?`, since a singleton rests in either kind."
- orchestrating :79: "A adds the tag, the run token and the terminal states without `:final?` that make the forward safe." There is no boot exception.

## What happened (generic)

The companion's exception assumes a boot flow runs once. v1's add-on restarts a flow whenever the event that returns `:async-flow` fires again with the same `:id`. The fx re-registers the flow's event handler under that id and queues `[id :setup]`. `:setup` then resets the seen-events and rules-fired sets to empty and re-registers the event forwarder. Real apps restart boot that way: re-running boot after logout and login, a "retry" button on a failed boot, or a re-init on hot reload.

The companion has no check for this. A migration that takes the boot exception therefore ships a machine with `:final?` terminals and no run token. A second start then needs a transition out of a terminal state that the design never gave it. And without the token, a completion still queued from the previous run cannot be told apart from one for the new run. The two pages also give a partitioned migration different answers: §3 (the unit brief) says no `:final?`, while the companion says a boot machine may use it.

## Evidence

- v1 `day8.re-frame/async-flow-fx` 0.4.0, `day8/re_frame/async_flow_fx.cljs`:
  - :215-220 `flow->handler`: `(re-frame/reg-event-fx id (make-flow-event-handler flow'))`, then `(re-frame/dispatch [id :setup])`.
  - :147-156 `:setup`: `(set-state db #{} #{})` and `:forward-events {:register id …}`.
- Observed on a ~170-file app whose boot event can be dispatched more than once.
- Related, closed: rf2-u0clc, which introduced the lifecycle rule and this exception.

## Suggested change

Make the companion's exception conditional on a check. Grep every dispatch of each event whose handler returns `:async-flow`, including `:dispatch` / `:fx` entries that name it. If any of them can fire more than once in a page's life, the machine is restartable and needs:

- the run token and its guard;
- terminal states without `:final?`;
- a restart transition.

Only a flow whose starting event provably fires once may take `:final?` terminals. Add one sentence to orchestrating §3 so the two pages agree: ":final? only where the companion's run-once check passed".

TWO FENCES, TWO DIFFERENT RELEASE EVENTS. Read both before acting on either.

  1. RE-DISPATCH FENCE. Do not dispatch a second worker onto this bead or that branch.
     RELEASES ON: a completion report, or a recorded death.
     This is the condition the reaping rule uses. The test is: can you quote the
     sentence where this agent says it is done?

  2. SURFACE FENCE. The worker holds migration/from-re-frame-v1/async-flow-fx-to-reg-machine.md, orchestrating-a-large-migration.md §3, async-flow-to-machines.md
     RELEASES ON: THE PR MERGING. Not on the report.
     A reported worker still has an open PR editing those files; a second worker
     branched off trunk would not carry them, and the two diffs collide at merge.
     The test is: has the PR that edits this surface MERGED?

A YES TO THE FIRST AND A NO TO THE SECOND means: reap the worktree if you like,
but DO NOT dispatch onto that surface.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #11660 (commit "O-16's token-free consumer depends on a run-once check, not on being boot"). The restart premise held at source. In v1 async-flow-fx 0.4.0, async_flow_fx.cljs:215-220, every run of the :async-flow fx calls reg-event-fx under the flow id (replacing the handler) and dispatches [id :setup]. At :147-156, :setup runs (set-state db #{} #{}) and :forward-events {:register id ...}; re-frame 1.4.3 router add-post-event-callback replaces a same-id callback. So a re-issued flow restarts from scratch, mid-run or after a halt. Companion :196 now allows a consumer to skip the token only when its run starts at most once per page load, checked by grepping every dispatch of each event whose handler returns :async-flow (:dispatch and :fx entries included). If any of those can fire more than once, the machine is restartable: it is started from that event's handler under the condition the handler tested, with a fresh token; the awaiting transitions are guarded on the token; and the start event is handled in every state (a root-level :on). PREMISE NOT ADOPTED: the bead's call for "terminal states without :final?" on a restartable machine. Spec 005 §Final states D7 says a singleton rests at :final? and "a declared way out (a root :on transition) leaves the final state like any transition", so :final? terminals stay allowed either way. Orchestrating §3's "terminal states without :final?" was stale: it predates singletons resting at :final?, and companion :148 already says terminal states, :final? or not. That phrase is gone, and §3 now names the run-once check, so the two pages agree. NOT DONE, OUT OF SCOPE: the pass-4 comment's SKILL.md fact 4 (:108 starts every boot machine from :initial-events, which run once). SKILL.md §Boot and init is held by worker/migration-boot-unwrap; that one needs its own bead. Control: a broken link on the new §3 sentence made check_doc_slugs exit 1. comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
Pass-4 evidence from the same downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626. The companion :196 and orchestrating §3 :79 findings above stand as filed; this adds two things.

## 1. SKILL.md §Boot and init makes the same run-once assumption

skills/re-frame-migration/SKILL.md:108 (fact 4): "A singleton boot machine needs an explicit start and address. If O-16 turned boot orchestration into a machine, start it from the frame's `:initial-events` (the reserved `:rf.machine/start` marker) and address it by its registered id".

`:initial-events` fire once, when the frame is constructed. They do not re-fire when the frame is re-registered (spec/002-Frames.md:722 and :959; spec/001-Registration.md:358). So the routing page sends every boot machine to a start that can happen only once, and the start carries no run token. That is the restartable-run gap this item describes, now in the page a migration reads first.

## 2. A conditional start lands in the wrong place

A v1 flow starts when, and only when, an event handler returns `:async-flow`. Real boot handlers return it on one branch only. On a ~170-file app the boot handler returns `:async-flow` only when its own pre-flow init did not fail and the boot is not a partial boot (a test mode). Moving that start into `:initial-events` makes it unconditional.

The companion already says where a conditional start belongs, but only for `:first-dispatch`. At :214 it says: "hoist the condition into the parent event that calls `rf/dispatch` to spawn / start the machine". Its own worked example also starts the machine from the app's entry point, not from `:initial-events` (:121-122: `(rf/dispatch [:app/boot [:rf.machine/start]])`). So the three passages give two answers to where a boot machine starts.

## Suggested addition to this item's change

Make SKILL.md fact 4 depend on the same run-once check:

- Use `:initial-events` only when the v1 starting event was dispatched exactly once, unconditionally, at boot.
- Otherwise keep the start in the v1 starting event's `:fx`, under the same condition the v1 handler tested, e.g. `[:dispatch [<machine-id> [<start-event> {:run <fresh token>}]]]`.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): no rule for an ambient subscribe inside a reg-sub computation fn; v2 resolves it only while the body runs inside a render, so it yields nil from the first recompute, and "What stays the same" reads as preserving it
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626. Priority 2: "What stays the same" reads as keeping the pattern, and the kept pattern passes the first render and the boot smoke, then yields nil on the first state change.

## Skill file and section

- migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md §M-75 (lines 2991-3072), §M-71 (lines 801-880), §M-18 (lines 738-797), and "What stays the same" (lines 3418-3423).
- skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-views-m11.md §M-11 Identify (lines 13-16).

## What it says

- M-71 :807: "A v2 `input-fn` must **not** call `subscribe`". That covers the input fn only, not the computation fn.
- M-75 covers only where `:inputs` is declared and the one-input bracket.
- "What stays the same" :3422: "**`@(subscribe [...])`.** The deref-to-read pattern is the documented contract and stays valid." :3423: "The layer-1 `reg-sub` fn-tail is preserved".
- guided-views-m11.md never mentions `reg-sub` (0 hits; the control grep for "sub" hits).

## What happened (generic)

Some v1 apps deref another sub inside a `reg-sub` computation fn, as a dynamic dependency:

```clojure
(rf/reg-sub :cart/lines
  (fn [db _] (mapv #(deref (rf/subscribe [:product/by-id %])) (:cart/ids db))))
```

v1's `subscribe` read the global app-db, so this worked anywhere. No migration rule says whether it survives, and "the fn-tail is preserved" reads as yes.

In v2 an ambient `subscribe` needs a frame: a `with-frame` or router binding, or the tree's boundary while a Reagent component renders. A sub's computation fn gets neither. The body runs under no frame binding, and the tree tier is gated on Reagent's in-flight component. So the in-body subscribe resolves only when the body happens to run inside a render (its first deref from a view).

When an input changes, Reagent re-runs the watched reaction from its ratom flush, outside any render. The in-body subscribe then raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context`, and the sub machinery recovers the throw to nil with `:rf.error/sub-exception`. The view shows nil from the first state change on.

This is the same mechanism as rf2-ula8a (reaction bodies created in views), at a different site with a different remedy: a sub body has no render at which to capture a frame.

## Evidence (source read at 0783705626; not executed)

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:1223-1345: the body fn is wrapped by `rf.subs.memo/make-layer-*-memoised-body` and handed to `make-derived-value`. Neither subs.cljc nor subs/memo.cljc binds a frame around the body (subs/memo.cljc: 0 hits for `with-frame` / `current-frame`).
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs:254-276 (`current-frame`: the tree tier "is gated on Reagent's in-flight component because the context slot means something only during a render").

title: Rewrite Spec 009's pair-server sensitive rule to redact-but-record, matching Security.md:118
description:
Spec 009 says the pair server's default is to DROP `:sensitive? true` events. `spec/Security.md:118` says pair recorders REDACT the payload but keep the record. Rewrite 009 to match Security.md and the shipped pair-MCP behaviour, and delete 009's line mandating an "Xray-MCP server" that does not exist.

## Ruling

**Decision.** The re-frame2-pair server's contract becomes "project, then forward". Every record the pair server forwards to the AI surface has first been projected by `project-egress` under `:rf.egress/off-box-tool`. `:sensitive?` and `:rf.epoch/sensitive?` ride on that record as annotations; whole records are not dropped by default. The two-key opt-in widens only the app-db sensitive axis.

This resolves the spec's self-contradiction in favour of `spec/Security.md:118` ("Recorder redact-but-record … The slot survives so the dev can correlate the run; the payload is scrubbed"), which stays as written.

This is the fourth of four beads from one ruling. It records the contract that rf2-42gpe ships.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned. Mike's instruction, verbatim:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original
> recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then
> remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

**Decisive facts (read in source at trunk 89517e8f54):**

1. `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2822`: "The re-frame2-pair server … MUST drop or redact `:sensitive? true` events before forwarding to the AI surface. The default policy is **drop**". This contradicts two Security.md lines:
   - `spec/Security.md:118`, quoted above;
   - its rationale row at `spec/Security.md:338`: "devs lose useful correlation otherwise".

   Since 009 already says "drop or redact", flipping the default is a change of default, not a contract break.
2. `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2823` mandates that "The Xray-MCP server … MUST default-drop `:sensitive? true` events". No Xray-MCP server exists in the tree.
3. `spec/Tool-Pair.md:111` calls the rollup "a trustworthy off-box-branch signal". The rollup fires on ANY non-nil declared-sensitive leaf in `:db-before` / `:db-after` (`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/assembly.cljc:147-178`), so it means "this record contained classified material", not "this run touched a secret". The spec text should say that.

**Rejected options:**
- **Keep 009's drop default, and make the code match it.** That leaves the AI pair blind in any app with authentication. The ruling chose the projected record, option B.
- **Rewrite Security.md:118 toward drop.** Same reason; Security.md already states the chosen rule.
- **Keep the Xray-MCP line.** It mandates behaviour for a server that does not exist. Xray's on-box Epoch panel drop is a separate, unruled question and is not described by that line.

**Supersedes:** no ruling bead or EP. It replaces the default stated at `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2822`.

## Work

**`spec/009-Instrumentation.md`** (`:2819-2825`):
- Keep the framework-published-listener default for external error monitors (the Sentry / Honeybadger bullet at `:2821`).
- Rewrite the pair-server bullet (`:2822`) as follows:
  - the pair server forwards only `project-egress`-projected records under `:rf.egress/off-box-tool`;
  - `:sensitive?` and `:rf.epoch/sensitive?` are annotations on those records;
  - it does not drop whole records by default;
  - `:include-sensitive` (with the `--allow-sensitive-reads` boot gate) widens only the app-db sensitive axis.
- Delete the Xray-MCP bullet (`:2823`).
- Check that the config-knob paragraph (`:2825`) still reads true for the pair: its `include-sensitive?` still defaults to suppressing values.

**`spec/Tool-Pair.md`:**
- `:111`: describe the rollup as "record contained classified material", which consumers may annotate or drop. The pair annotates; external forwarders drop.
- Census Tool-Pair for any other sentence implying the pair drops flagged epochs, and align it.

**`spec/Privacy.md`:**
- `:120`, the `:rf.epoch/sensitive?` row: add that the pair MCP surfaces it as an annotation.
- `:131`, the `strip-sensitive` row: it stays, since Story-MCP still uses it. Remove any wording that names the pair's epoch tools as callers.

**`spec/Security.md`:**
- `:109`: "Listener fan-out, off-box egress, and recorder consumers branch on the rollup the same way…". Make it read consistently with `:118`: recorders and the pair annotate, and external forwarders may drop.
- `:118` stays as is.

**`spec/Conventions.md`:**
- `:794`, the `:dropped-sensitive` slot: it stays, because Story-MCP and `get-app-db` still report it.
- Edit only if its text names the pair's epoch tools as reporters.

**Deliberately stays:**
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:4417`, the flag's definition, which already matches the code.
- The listener guidance at `009:688-697`.
- Spec 015.

## Sequencing

- **Hot zones touched:**
  - `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`;
  - `spec/Tool-Pair.md`;
  - `spec/Conventions.md`, only if `:794` needs it.
- **Depends on:**
  - rf2-ot1aa (delete the db-focus redaction heuristic), which also edits 009;
  - rf2-42gpe (flip the pair MCP epoch tools to the projected record), whose shipped behaviour this records.
- **Cross-dossier:**
  - Sequence, never parallel, with every Spec 009 bead from `observability-listener-scheduler-and-fan-outs.md`.
  - Precede `durable-app-db-classification-static-or-runtime.md`'s work.
  - `resource-identity-privacy-and-correlation.md` edits Spec 016, not these lines.
- `spec/011-SSR.md` is not touched.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): guided-views-m11 has no case for a callback built inside a reg-sub body; capture at render does not apply there and the sub body has no frame scope of its own
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626.

## Skill file and section

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-views-m11.md §M-11, Identify (lines 13-16) and Decision shape (lines 20-25).
- The corpus rule it operationalises, migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md §M-11 (line 491 on), offers the same three fixes.

## What it says

- Identify 1 (:15): "Every bare fully-qualified `rf/dispatch` / `rf/subscribe` … inside an `:on-*` handler or any other callback that runs after the render … in a `reg-view` and a plain fn alike."
- Decision shape 1 (:22): "Capture at render time. Call the ops a `reg-view` injects …, or take `(rf/capture-frame)` during the render — in a plain fn too — and call its ops from the callback".
- Decision shape 2 (:23): "Carry the frame explicitly. … Use this where the frame is a fixed, known one."
- The leaf never mentions `reg-sub`.

## What happened (generic)

v1 code sometimes builds a callback inside a subscription's computation. For example, a `reg-sub` body returns a notification or menu-item map whose `:on-close` / `:on-click` fn bare-dispatches. Identify 1 catches the dispatch, because it is a callback that runs after the render. But neither fix in the decision shape fits it:

- Option 1 assumes a view owns the callback, and here the owner is a sub body, which is not a render. Applied literally, it means moving the callback out of the sub and into every view that reads it. That changes the sub's value shape; it is a refactor, not a frame repair.
- A `(rf/capture-frame)` taken inside the sub body is not a documented capture site. The runtime gives a sub body no frame binding of its own, so what a capture there resolves depends on where that recompute happens to run. The value is also cached per (frame, query) and shared by every view that reads it.
- Option 2 is the fix that holds, but the leaf limits it to "a fixed, known one" frame and does not name this case.

A census that assigns each site to the view that owns it classes these sites as option 1, and the unit then has to overrule the census.

## Evidence

- guided-views-m11.md :15, :22 and :23 are quoted above. `grep "reg-sub"` over the leaf exits 1, so the string does not occur. Control: `reg-view*` occurs 10 times in the same file.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/memo.cljc:280-292: the sub body is called as `(body-fn body-arg query-v)` inside `rf.trace/with-handler-scope` only. `frame-id` is threaded through for traces and validation, and no frame binding is established.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs:254-297 (`current-frame`): the tree answers only while a Reagent component is in flight. Otherwise `rf.frame/*current-frame*` answers, or nothing does.
- Observed on a ~170-file app: a `reg-sub` body built a default `:on-close` callback that bare-dispatched. The parsed M-11 census classed it as option 1, capture at render in the owning view. The unit used option 2, `{:frame <app frame id>}`, because option 1 meant moving the callback out of the sub.

## Suggested change

Add a row to the Decision shape, and name the case in Identify 1 ("including a callback built inside a `reg-sub` body"):

"A callback built inside a `reg-sub` body (the sub's value carries an `:on-*` fn). The body is not a render and has no frame scope of its own, so it is not a capture site. Either:
(a) carry the frame explicitly, with `{:frame <id>}` on the call or `(rf/capture-frame <id>)`, where the app has one known frame; or
(b) have the sub return data (the event vector), and build the callback in the view with its render-captured `dispatch`.
(b) changes the sub's value shape, so a behaviour-preserving migration takes (a) and leaves (b) to the author."

close_reason: Done in PR #11661 (commit 07a9ecd35f). Premise verified at runtime with a throwaway node-lane probe. title: ssr-node: the JVM owns the sidecar - ship its .cjs as resources in ssr-ring's jar and add a :module mode to re-frame.ssr.ring.node/renderer that spawns, ready-checks and restarts it (Mike ruled option (c) on rf2-8arzr.8)
description:
## Why

Running a Fresco app's SSR today takes three manual chores:

- copying the ssr-node sidecar out of a checkout (`implementation/ssr-node/package.json` is `private: true`, and nothing publishes it);
- supervising a second process yourself: start it, scan its stdout for the ready line, read off the port, restart it when it dies;
- keeping the JVM's `:admission-ms` in step with the sidecar's `--admission-ms` by hand.

Our own tests pay for this too: `node_crossing_test.clj` (`pump-lines!` / `spawn-sidecar!` / `stop-sidecar!`, about lines 61-125) and `login_host_crossing_test.clj` (about lines 102-170) each carry a copy of the roughly 35-line spawn helper that every user has to write.

Mike ruled on 2026-10-28 (recorded on rf2-8arzr.8): the sidecar ships as OPTION (c), as classpath resources INSIDE `day8/re-frame2-ssr-ring`'s own jar. No new artefact, no npm, and `package.json` stays private. The publishing chain (rf2-uelji -> rf2-fo4ng -> rf2-kmqx3) does not block this work: the resources go out with whichever ssr-ring jar the first tag publishes. The GraalJS spike (rf2-x6yr2) rendered Fresco in-process byte-identical to the sidecar, but nowhere near as fast on a stock JDK, and it recommends this route instead.

## The change

`re-frame.ssr.ring.node/renderer` gains a `:module "<server-bundle path>"` mode in which the JVM owns the sidecar process:

1. **Package.** The sidecar's runtime files (`bin/serve.cjs`, `src/*.cjs`, zero npm dependencies, about 100 KB) go on ssr-ring's classpath under a namespaced prefix such as `re_frame/ssr_node/`. This has to work for a `:local/root` consumer (deps.edn `:paths`) and in the built jar (`:clein/build :src-dirs`). One constraint we measured: clein (pinned sha 2b83503246) copies each `:src-dirs` entry to the jar ROOT through `tools.build` `copy-dir`, with no prefix mapping (`noahtheduke/clein.cljc:116`), so adding `../ssr-node` as a root would dump `bin/`, `src/`, `test/` and `README.md` at the root of the jar. Keep `implementation/ssr-node/` as the one tracked source: no committed second copy, unless a gate pins the two together. tools.deps `:deps/prep-lib` is one candidate mechanism. Pick the smallest one that works, and avoid a `release.yml` change if you can (it's a hot-zone file).
2. **Spawn at construction.** Extract the resources to a temp dir (Node can't run code out of a jar) and run `node <dir>/bin/serve.cjs --module <bundle> --port 0 --host 127.0.0.1 --timeout-ms <:timeout-ms> --admission-ms <:admission-ms>`. Scan stdout for the line whose `"rf.ssr-node"` key is `"ready"` (a bundle that logs at boot shares stdout). Check `protocol` is 1 and `buildId` equals `:build-id`, and take `url` as the endpoint. So a misconfigured deployment, a skewed bundle included, fails at BOOT rather than on the first request. In this mode the JVM passes `--admission-ms` itself, so the pair can't drift; the condition rf2-mn2ht.35 parked goes away.
3. **Supervise, minimally.** If the child exits, restart it with capped backoff. While it's down, requests fail through the existing `:rf.error/ssr-node-unreachable` (a 5xx). The JVM needs a way to stop the child (SIGTERM via `.destroy`, then `.destroyForcibly`), and a forgotten stop must never leak a node process: a JVM shutdown hook as the backstop. Choose the smallest shape for the stop handle and say why in the PR.
4. **Keep `:endpoint`** for operators who run the sidecar themselves. `:module` and `:endpoint` are mutually exclusive, and naming both is `:rf.error/ssr-node-renderer-opt-invalid`. Small optional knobs only: the node executable (default `"node"`) and `:isolates`. Nothing more speculative than that.

Reuse the existing error ids (`ssr-node-renderer-opt-invalid`, `ssr-node-unreachable`, `ssr-node-build-skew`) so `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (hot zone) stays put. If a new id turns out to be genuinely necessary, that's a Spec 009 edit and has to be sequenced.

## Moves with it

- Tests: both crossing tests drop their spawn helpers and use `:module` (the stub sidecars that test the failure paths keep `:endpoint`). New `:crossing` tests cover: boot and render; a `buildId` mismatch refused at construction; a killed child restarted, with the next request succeeding; stop leaves no node process behind. These run under ssr-ring's `:crossing-test` alias (CI job `jvm-node-crossing`, needs Node 24).
- The login example: `examples/substrates/fresco/login/host.clj` and its README's "Build it and run it" lose the start-the-sidecar and read-the-url steps, and the `LOGIN_FRESCO_SSR_NODE` env var stays only if `:endpoint` is still taught there.
- Prose that currently says "not published / none planned", which becomes false: `implementation/ssr-node/README.md` §Running it and §Deployment; `docs/ssr/concepts.md` §Render on Node step 5 ("Start the sidecar, and mind the skew"); `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.ring.node.md`; `spec/011-SSR.md` §the ssr-node crossing paragraph (about line 458, the construction-opts list); the comment on ssr-ring's `deps.edn`.
- Hot zone: if this adds a public var to `re-frame.ssr.ring.node` (a stop fn, say), `spec/api-manifest.edn` regenerates, which moves the `spec/API.md` + manifest holding as one. Sequence it against any other bead touching those. If rf2-fo4ng (the coordinate rename) is in flight, sequence against it too, since both edit `implementation/ssr-ring/deps.edn`.

## Acceptance

Sol's condition from the review: for the login example, BOTH the operator steps AND the lifecycle code fall. Quote the before and after counts in the PR, meaning the steps in the login README's run recipe and the lines of spawn/supervise code across the two crossing tests. List the built ssr-ring jar and show `re_frame/ssr_node/bin/serve.cjs` present, with no `test/` files and no `README.md` at the jar root. Report `:crossing-test` and the default ssr-ring `:test` with their runner exit codes.

Source: the adversarial review of `implementation/` (Opus report "SSR hosts", Sol report 30 "Node SSR service and worker isolation"). This bead carries everything they said; the local copy at `C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2\ai\findings\advisarial-review\` no longer lists the item.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair): no guidance for several browser tabs on one build: evals go to the first-connected runtime, and nothing says how to tell or pin one (:runtime-count is undocumented)
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 2a6fd908a6.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md "Connect once — the resolved build sticks" (line 105) and "Read the `:freshness` token" (line 109), plus references/errors.md. The behaviour lives in tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl.cljs `cljs-eval` (lines 742-765) and tools/freshness.cljs (`:runtime-count`, lines 46 and 176).

## What it says

SKILL.md:105 covers several BUILDS ("With several, `discover-app` errors with the running-builds list rather than guess: pass `build`, or the open tab's URL port as `port`"). Nothing in the skill covers several browser tabs, that is several JS runtimes, connected to ONE build: which one receives an eval, how to tell, or how to pin one.

## What happened (generic)

Opening a second tab on the same dev build (a browser-automation tab next to the developer's own, or a reload that leaves a stale tab connected) is routine. Every Pair read and write then goes to whichever runtime shadow-cljs picks, and the skill gives no way to know which. An agent can dispatch into or read from a tab other than the one it is looking at, and everything still reports `:ok? true`. Hit while preparing Phase-4 readiness on a ~170-file app, where the boot-smoke drives the app in its own tab.

## Evidence

* The server sends `(shadow.cljs.devtools.api/cljs-eval <build> <code> {})` (nrepl.cljs:754-755). The opts map is empty, so there is no `:runtime-id`.
* shadow-cljs 3.4.10 (the pin re-frame2 builds with), shadow/cljs/devtools/api.clj:639-669: `cljs-eval` passes `:runtime-id (:runtime-id opts)` into the REPL state. With none, server/repl_impl.clj:140-153 uses the worker's `:default-runtime-id`. server/worker/impl.clj:775-789 sets that default to the FIRST runtime that connects, unless `:repl {:runtime-select :latest}` is configured (or the host is react-native). When the default disconnects, :413-430 re-picks the oldest remaining runtime by `:connected-since`. So by default, evals go to the OLDEST connected tab, not the newest or the focused one.
* The freshness token already reports `:runtime-count` ("connected REPL runtimes for this build", freshness.cljs:46). The discover-app tool description lists it too, without saying what a value above 1 means (descriptors_data.cljs:186). But `git grep -n "runtime-count"` over skills/re-frame2-pair finds 0 hits (exit 1). The control: the same grep over tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src finds freshness.cljs:46, :176 and :193, and probe.cljs.
* `git grep -n -i -E "several (browser )?tabs|multiple (browser )?tabs|more than one (browser )?(tab|runtime)|two tabs|one-tab|runtime-id|which runtime|multiple runtimes|select.*runtime|pin.*runtime"` over skills/re-frame2-pair finds only frame-selection hits (ops.md:59/:64 operating-frame pin, recipes.md:46), and nothing on runtimes.

## Suggested change

Add a short paragraph after SKILL.md:105 (or an errors.md entry): "One build, several tabs: shadow-cljs sends every eval to its default runtime, which is the first tab that connected (or the newest, if the app sets `:repl {:runtime-select :latest}`), and on disconnect falls back to the oldest one left. `:freshness :runtime-count` > 1 means this is in play. Keep one tab open on the build while pairing, or close the others and re-run `discover-app`." Optionally, have `discover-app` warn when `:runtime-count` > 1, and accept a `runtime-id` that the server passes through to `cljs-eval`'s opts.

title: re-frame2-pair-mcp: no way to pick or identify the runtime when several browser tabs share one build (cljs-eval sends no :runtime-id; discover-app does not flag :runtime-count > 1)
description:
## Gap

With several browser tabs (several JS runtimes) connected to ONE shadow-cljs build, every Pair op reaches whichever runtime shadow-cljs treats as the build's default, and Pair offers no way to choose a different one or to be told which one answered.

## Evidence (verified at source)

- tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl.cljs `cljs-eval` is the single CLJS eval site, and it sends `(shadow.cljs.devtools.api/cljs-eval <build> <code> {})`: the opts map is empty, so it never carries `:runtime-id`.
- shadow-cljs 3.4.10: `api/cljs-eval` puts `(:runtime-id opts)` into the REPL state; `server/repl_impl.clj` falls back to the worker's `:default-runtime-id` when it is nil. `server/worker/impl.clj` `add-runtime` sets that default to the FIRST runtime to connect (or the newest under `:repl {:runtime-select :latest}`, or always for react-native), and `maybe-pick-different-default-runtime` re-picks the oldest remaining runtime by `:connected-since` when the default disconnects. shadow also exposes `api/repl-runtimes <build>` (lists connected runtimes) and `api/repl-runtime-select <build> <runtime-id>` (sets the default), which Pair does not use.
- The freshness token's `:runtime-count` (tools/freshness.cljs `summarise-build-state`) counts every runtime on the build, but `discover-app` neither warns when it is above 1 nor reports which runtime answered beyond the preload's `:runtime-instance-id`.

## What the skill says today

skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md "One build, several tabs" tells the agent that `:runtime-count` above 1 means only one tab is reached, and to pair against a single tab (close extras, re-run `discover-app`, check `:runtime-count` reads 1). That is the whole workaround: no tool argument picks a tab.

## Possible directions (not decided)

1. `discover-app` adds a `:hint` (or a liveness note) when `:runtime-count` > 1.
2. A `runtime-id` argument, or a session pin like the operating-frame pin, that the server passes through as `cljs-eval`'s `:runtime-id`, with `discover-app` listing the runtimes from `repl-runtimes` (URL / user-agent / connected-since) so the agent can choose.

Either changes the tool contract fingerprint and the descriptor manifest, so it is a server change with a skill follow-up, not a prose fix.

It can be lost through the wipe above, through a fold into the wrong frame, or through a frame declaration made in a namespace that never loads. An audit, validation or undo interceptor lost this way fails only in its effect.

Yet the fact is cheap to read. `(rf/frame-meta <frame-id>)` returns the frame's config, `:interceptors` included.

## Evidence

- The quotes above.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1416-1434: `frame-meta` merges `(:config f)` into its result, and :2992 lists `:interceptors` among the frame config keys.
- Raised on a ~170-file app whose v1 global interceptors were folded into frame `:interceptors`.

## Suggested change

Add a step to the loop, after step 2: "For each frame, read `(rf/frame-meta <frame-id>)` and compare its `:interceptors` with the plan's chain for that frame (the M-17 fold): the same ids, in the same order." Then add the wipe to silent-runtime-failures.md's checklist as the failure this step catches.

title: migration corpus: the O-16/O-17 companions have no verification section comparing the converted subsystem with v1
description:
## Gap

The O-16 and O-17 corpus companions, migration/from-re-frame-v1/async-flow-fx-to-reg-machine.md and migration/from-re-frame-v1/http-fx-to-managed-http.md, have no verification section. Their headings run Summary, Acting is forced, Detection, concept mapping, Before / after, Mapping notes, Explicit escalation cases, Out of scope, Reporting. The corpus README's own "### Verification steps" (around line 3461) checks only that the app boots and that events and subs behave "as expected". Nowhere in the corpus does a reader compare the converted subsystem with what v1 did.

## Why it matters

The person who rewrote the subsystem also writes the expectation, so the expectation shares the rewrite's blind spots. A converted boot flow or HTTP layer can compile, boot and match that expectation while still differing from v1: a request fires twice or not at all, or out of order, or a slot is written at a different moment.

## What the skill already has

The skill's runtime smoke-test leaf (skills/re-frame-migration/references/runtime-smoke-test.md, loop step 9, "Compare with v1 wherever v2 replaced a subsystem or loads what v1 saved") covers this for a skill-driven migration. It drives the same scenario on the v1 and v2 builds, diffs the request sequence (method, URL, order, count) and the app-db slots the subsystem writes, and records each comparison as its own result. A reader working from the corpus companion alone never meets that step.

## Suggested change

Give each companion a short "Verification" section ahead of "Reporting", one or two sentences long. It should say to drive the same scenario on both builds and diff the request sequence and the slots the converted subsystem writes, and name the skill leaf's step 9 as the fuller procedure. Keep it to that: the step lives in the skill leaf, and the companion only points at it.

## Fence

Before starting, check that no open PR holds async-flow-fx-to-reg-machine.md. At filing, two open PRs held it.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): M-8's fold into an existing :fx shows only a literal :fx vector; no worked form for a computed :fx value (vec (for ...)), (when ...) or a nil-able folded value
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main d53a3faf09.

## Skill file and section

- migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md §M-8, transformation step 4 (line 384) and step 3 (lines 381-382).
- skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md §Effect-map consolidation (M-8), step 4 (line 410), which defers to the corpus ("fold in v1's run order as the corpus describes").

## What it says

- :384: "If the effect map already has a `:fx`, fold around it in v1's run order. … `{:db db :demo/log log :fx [[:demo/send a]] :demo/ping p}` becomes `{:db db :fx [[:demo/log log] [:demo/send a] [:demo/ping p]]}`". The one worked example's existing `:fx` is a literal vector.
- :384 flags a site only where the order cannot be read: "a map built at run time (`assoc`, `merge`, `cond->`, a helper's return value) or a literal of more than 8 entries".
- :381: "Single value … wrap as `[[:key value]]` inside `:fx`."
- The nil-skipped `(when …)` row appears only in the `:dispatch-later` row pass (:391: "A `(when …)` entry becomes a `(when …)` row, which `:fx` skips when nil"), not in the top-level fold.

## What happened (generic)

v1 handlers often return a literal map whose existing `:fx` VALUE is computed:

    {:db db :fx (vec (for [x xs] [:dispatch [:load x]])) :dispatch [:done]}
    {:db db :fx (when ok? [[:dispatch [:a]]]) :http req}

The map is a literal of 8 entries or fewer, so step 4's order rule applies and the site is not flagged. But the step shows only splicing rows into a literal vector, and a row cannot be spliced into an expression. Each unit re-derived the shapes by hand: `(into [row] <expr>)` for a key before `:fx`, and `(conj (vec <expr>) row)` for a key after it. Each also had to re-check that `(vec nil)` is `[]`, and that a nil-able folded value wants the whole row wrapped in `(when …)`, as :391 shows only for `:dispatch-later`.

## Evidence

- The quotes above.
- Observed on a ~170-file app: one unit's handlers had several literal maps with a `(vec (for …))` or `(when …)` `:fx` value beside top-level keys, and the corpus gave no form to follow.

## Suggested change

In corpus M-8 step 4, after the literal example, add a computed-`:fx` case:

- A key before `:fx`: `{:db db :k v :fx <expr>}` becomes `{:db db :fx (into [[:k v]] <expr>)}`.
- A key after `:fx`: `{:db db :fx <expr> :k v}` becomes `{:db db :fx (conj (vec <expr>) [:k v])}`. `(vec nil)` is `[]`, so a `(when …)` expression that returns nil still works.
- A folded value that can be nil: wrap the whole row, `(when ok? [:k v])`, which `:fx` skips when nil (as :391 already shows for `:dispatch-later` rows).

Also say that a literal map whose `:fx` value is an expression still follows step 4's order rule: it is not "a map built at run time".

title: skill(re-frame2-pair) + pair-mcp: read-mounted-boundaries on a non-Fresco app returns Xray's own tool-frame boundaries (about 7K tokens, overflow, no data), with no argument to exclude them; screen-reads.md:83 predicts an empty roster
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (a suggestion, not a work order). Verified at re-frame2 origin/main fd1d1565f1. Observed on a ~170-file Reagent app with no Fresco code of its own, running Xray.

## Skill file and section

- skills/re-frame2-pair/references/screen-reads.md §Fresco evidence (line 83).
- skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md, the loading-map row for `read-mounted-boundaries` (line 183).
- The tool: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/tool-descriptors.edn line 23, and src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/fresco_tool.cljs (line 221).

## What it says

- screen-reads.md:83: on a Reagent or UIx app that has loaded the door through Xray, "with no Fresco boundary mounted their rosters are empty: `:boundaries []` there means no **Fresco** boundary holds a live read edge".
- SKILL.md:183: such an app "gets valid envelopes about its Fresco boundaries only".
- The descriptor: "No arg, deliberately: the question is what is mounted." Its `:input-keys` are `["build" "max-tokens"]`. fresco_tool.cljs:221: "Every read on this door is NULLARY".
- Elsewhere the skill keeps reserved tool frames out of app reads. SKILL.md:137 says `orient` returns "the app frames (reserved `:rf/*` tool frames excluded)", and recipes.md:56 says those frames are excluded "so the summary never overflows on a tool frame's working set".

## What happened (generic)

The docs lead the agent to expect an empty roster on a Reagent app. In practice the Xray panel, which is what loaded the door, renders through Fresco itself, so whenever the panel is mounted its own boundaries fill the roster. On this app `read-mounted-boundaries {}` returned about 7K tokens and overflowed the 5000 default, so it gave no data at all. title: core(classification): a classified frame's trace walk realises an endless lazy seq in a view's render args, so the render never returns — now that most frames are classified
description:
A classified frame's trace walks a view's whole render args to project them, so an endless lazy seq in a view's args (`(range)`, an `iterate`, a lazy stream) is fully realised and the render never returns. Reported by the static-classification stage-2 worker (rf2-plhgw, PR #11705): it was already true of classified frames, but with classification now registered by `reg-classification` and process-wide, most frames are classified, so the hazard now reaches ordinary dev apps. The worker isolated the affected Xray test and did not change the walker.

## What to establish first (claims, not findings)

- Which walker it is (the render-args projection for trace/egress under Spec 015) and whether it runs in production builds or only where tracing is enabled — read the elision guard around it.
- Whether it realises an unrealised lazy seq, or only walks what is already realised. Reproduce with a view taking `(range)` in a classified frame on the node test bundle.

## Suggested direction

The walker should not force what the app has not forced: an unrealised lazy seq (`realized?` false, or a `LazySeq`/`Iterate`/`Range` that is not counted) projects as an opaque marker rather than being walked — or the walk is bounded the way other large values are elided (Spec 015's `:large` handling). Pick whichever matches how the projection already treats large values; one rule, not a new knob. Cite the Spec 015 section that holds the projection contract and add a sentence there only if the contract is silent on unrealised seqs.

## Acceptance

A view taking `(range)` in a classified frame renders and its trace records a marker; a test pins it (red against the current walker). Existing classification/redaction tests unchanged.

title: senior review: adapters: Reagent and UIx
description:
SENIOR-DEVELOPER REVIEW of one slice of the tree. Part of the review sweep rf2-r5cc2, which partitions implementation/, tools/, examples/ and skills/ into slices; this bead owns exactly the slice below, and its siblings own the rest.

SLICE:
- implementation/adapters/**

FOCUS: The two shipped adapters, their late-bind hook sets and testbeds (Spec 006, spec/Conventions.md adapter rows).

PERSONA. A senior Clojure/ClojureScript developer who did not write this code, reading it as its next maintainer and as a programmer who has to use it. Judge it against the project stance (CLAUDE.md), quoted verbatim:

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

So record material, actionable insights only: a defect, a simplification that removes real weight, an ergonomic sharp edge a programmer (or the AI they use) will hit, a test that cannot go red, a doc or docstring that misleads. Not style preferences, not nagging diagnostics, not defensive belt-and-braces, not renames for taste.

LENSES, in priority order:
1. Correctness — error paths, concurrency, cleanup, and fail-closed behaviour on any security or privacy boundary.
2. Simplicity and clarity — dead code, duplication (within the slice or with another slice), accidental complexity, an abstraction that earns nothing.
3. Ergonomics — the API or tool as a programmer, or the AI they use, actually meets it.
4. Performance — hot spots on real paths, never at the expense of clarity.
5. Test rigour — a test that cannot fail, a gap on a branch that matters.
6. Comments and docstrings — per CLAUDE.md § Conventions & Patterns: present tense, the reason plus a spec pointer, no provenance, no restated spec.

METHOD. Read the slice's source first, then its tests, against the owning spec sections (spec/Ownership.md maps each surface to its spec). A finding is a CLAIM until checked: confirm each one at source, and confirm a behaviour claim with a quick REPL or test run where that is cheap. This is a read-only review: edit no file, and run only read-only commands and the slice's existing test lanes.

OUTPUT, recorded on THIS bead and never in a separate file: write the section to a file and append it with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes "$(cat <file>)"` (never `--notes`, which replaces). Head it `== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (<datetime with zone>, trunk <short sha>)` and include:
- 0 to 15 numbered findings, most important first. Each gives: `path:line` (plus a short quote so it can be re-found by text), what is wrong, why it matters (the concrete failure or cost), the fix (a sketch is fine), size (S/M/L), confidence (verified / probable), and its lens.
- A short "looked at and sound" list, so the review's coverage is visible.
- Cross-slice findings, whose defect lives in another slice's files, in a separate list naming the owning slice. Do not act on them.

Then add the label `findings-recorded` and leave the bead OPEN: its findings become this slice's fix work, which the coordinator dispatches in clusters. If the slice needs nothing, record zero findings with the coverage list and close the bead with that as the reason.
notes:
== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (2026-10-29 13:56:14 AUSEST, trunk dde786b07a)

Slice: implementation/adapters/** (101 tracked files: 2 adapter namespaces of about 320 lines each, 82 test namespaces, 2 testbeds, 3 smoke-harness scripts, READMEs, deps). Read at trunk 0383b5ce75; the commits up to dde786b07a touch no slice file and no file cited below (empty diff stat over those paths). Upstream sources were read from the pinned jars (reagent 2.0.1, uix.core 1.4.4) and from implementation/node_modules/react 19.3.0.

Verdict: the adapter SOURCE is sound. Its two load-bearing tricks, the exactly-once disposal guard and the hydrate-root rebuild, match stock Reagent 2.0.1 line for line and are pinned by rigorous tests. Every finding is in documentation, testbeds, test scaffolding or the smoke harness. None is a correctness defect in shipped code.

--- FINDINGS (most important first)

1. Reagent `render!`: every call after the first remounts the whole tree, and the docstring that sells it as the hot-reload hook does not say so.
   Where: implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:188 (`render!` docstring: "Every later call updates that same Root with the new tree ... That is what makes the one call both the boot path and the `^:dev/after-load` hook"); reagent/README.md has no mention.
   What: updates go through stock `reagent.dom.client/render`, which makes a fresh `comp` closure on every call (client.cljs:59-63) and renders it as `(react/createElement (.-comp js-props))` inside `reagent-root` (client.cljs:48). React sees a new element type every time and unmounts and remounts everything below it. The only place this is stated is a test ns docstring (reagent/test/re_frame/adapter_client_root_dom_cljs_test.cljs:10-14: "React remounts the subtree ... what survives a hot reload is the Root and the frame, not the DOM nodes").
   Cost: every save in a shadow-cljs dev loop throws away all component-local state: Form-2 `r/atom`s, `r/with-let` state, uncontrolled input contents, focus and scroll. A v1 migrant expects that state to survive and gets no warning that it won't. Frames survive, so app-db is fine.
   Fix: minimum, one sentence in the `render!` docstring and a short paragraph in reagent/README.md ("each later render! remounts the tree below the Root; component-local state does not survive a hot reload — keep it in a frame"). Optional, M: render updates through an adapter-owned component whose type stays stable, so React reconciles instead of remounting. That ties the adapter to reagent.impl internals (`*always-update*`, `flush-after-render`), so do it only if hot-reload state matters to the project.
   Size: S (doc) / M (code). Confidence: verified at source (stock client.cljs:40-67) and by the test ns statement; no test asserts it either way. Lens: 3 ergonomics.

2. The Reagent testbed teaches a rule that is false at tip, and it does not mount the way its own comment says.
   Where: implementation/adapters/reagent/testbed/adapter_testbed_reagent/core.cljs:28-35 ("ONLY a `reg-view`-registered component carries the `:contextType` ... a plain Reagent fn's `(.-context cmp)` is the no-provider sentinel, so its subscribe would resolve nil → `:rf.error/no-frame-context` and the render crashes") and :57-60 ("the same shape the boot guide and the generated template teach, so this smoke mounts the way an app does").
   What: (a) a plain Reagent fn under `frame-provider` resolves its frame from the tree. reagent/test/re_frame/plain_fn_frame_from_tree_dom_cljs_test.cljs pins exactly this: `a-server-render-resolves-the-provider` runs on the node lane, `a-plain-fn-resolves-the-nearest-provider` on the browser lane, and its ns docstring reads "for a plain Reagent fn that never registered". (b) `init` boots with `rf/make-frame` + `with-frame` `dispatch-sync` + `rf/frame-provider`. docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md teaches `[rf/frame-root {:id … :initial-events […]} …]`, and so does the adapter's own `client-root` docstring (reagent.cljs:175-182). The UIx smoke's header (uix/testbed/spec.cjs:9-11) says this same shape "would leave frame-root's browser path uncovered".
   Cost: this testbed is the adapter's minimal "how an app does it" file. A reader, or an AI, takes away a false constraint (wrap every subscribing component in `reg-view`) and a boot shape the guide does not teach. Real-DOM `rf/frame-root` coverage does exist elsewhere (frame_provider_context_dom_cljs_test Scenario 6), so the coverage gap is small. The doc cost is the real one.
   Fix: boot as the guide does, with `(rf.adapter.reagent/render! app-root [rf/frame-root {:id :rf/default :initial-events [[:counter/init]]} [root]] el)`. That deletes the `make-frame` / `with-frame` / `dispatch-sync` lines. Delete the false comment (or keep `root` as a `reg-view` without a reason that isn't true).
   Size: S. Confidence: verified (existing tests and the boot guide, read at source). Lens: 6 docs (and 5).

3. UIx `set-hiccup-emitter!` docs tell SSR consumers to install the emitter by hand. Requiring `re-frame.ssr` already does it.
   Where: implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:58-62 ("Idempotent. ... SSR consumers install the hiccup emitter explicitly (mirroring the Reagent adapter)"); uix/README.md:30 ("SSR consumers call this to wire the hiccup emitter explicitly").
   What: `make-react-adapter` chains this setter into `:reagent/set-hiccup-emitter!` at load (core spine.cljs:3720), `re-frame.ssr.emit` invokes that hook at ns-load (ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:1182), and install re-arms it through `:arm-hiccup-emitter-if-unarmed!`. The core shared suite pins it (core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:642-648, run for UIx by uix_react_shared_cljs_test). So the Reagent adapter is not being "mirrored": its docstring (reagent.cljs:154-158) correctly says the hook exists so `re-frame.ssr` can install the emitter. "Idempotent" also undersells the semantics, which are "last call wins" (spine `set-hiccup-emitter!` is a bare `reset!`).
   Cost: a programmer or AI adds redundant boot wiring and reads SSR on UIx as needing a manual step that Reagent does not. One spine function is described two different ways.
   Fix: reuse the Reagent wording: "Install the hiccup → HTML fn used by render-to-string. Last call wins. Requiring `re-frame.ssr` installs it through the chained late-bind hook; call this only to install a different emitter." Make the same edit in uix/README.md:30.
   Size: S. Confidence: verified (source plus an existing test). Lens: 6 docs.

4. The smoke runner logs console errors but never fails on them. The Reagent smoke is blind to them, and the UIx smoke carries its own workaround.
   Where: implementation/adapters/scripts/run-adapter-smokes.cjs:201-222 (the console listener only `log`s; only `pageerror` fails a spec); uix/testbed/spec.cjs:18-43 and :55-62 (its own listeners, a re-navigation, a NAV_TIMEOUT_MS knob mirrored from the runner, and its own throw); reagent/testbed/spec.cjs (no console check at all).
   What: the runner attaches its console and pageerror listeners BEFORE `page.goto` (lines 201-218), so it already sees boot-time console output. It just doesn't count it. The UIx spec re-navigates so its own listeners are armed for the boot, which is about 30 lines plus a second timeout budget. The Reagent smoke gets no clean-boot check: a React dev-build `console.error` at mount (missing keys, a hydration-attribute warning, "Cannot update a component while rendering") passes it green.
   Cost: one of two smokes has a weaker contract than the other for no reason, and the stronger one pays for its strength with a workaround that duplicates a runner budget.
   Fix: in the runner, collect `msg.type() === 'error'` messages from the pre-goto listener and fail the spec when any were seen, the same way it treats `pageErrored` (line 220). Then delete the UIx spec's listeners, re-navigation, NAV_TIMEOUT_MS and throw.
   Size: S. Confidence: verified for the asymmetry and the listener order. Probable: that the Reagent boot is console-clean today. One `npm run test:adapter-smokes` after the change settles it, and a red there would itself be a finding. Lens: 5 test rigour.

5. Sixteen test rows "skip" with `(is true …)` when `React.act` is missing. The branch is dead today and would fail open if it ever ran.
   Where: 9 files. reagent/test/re_frame/frame_provider_context_dom_cljs_test.cljs:526, :625, :742, :806 and sub_dispose_real_unmount_dom_cljs_test.cljs:232; uix/test/re_frame/adapter/ uix_boot_order_source_coord_dom:45, uix_effect_frame_deps_dom:27, uix_evicted_shared_child_dom:56, uix_frame_context_read_dom:54/:91, uix_frame_root_ensure_dom:44/:75, uix_reg_view_direct_mount_dom:26, uix_use_sub_dom:432/:471/:536 (each: `(is true "act() not reachable from this runner; skipping")`). Beside them, the slice defines its own private `browser?` in 30 files and a private `get-act`-style helper in 12.
   What: React 19's development build exports `act`, and its production build exports none (node_modules/react/cjs/react.production.js has 0 `exports.act`; react.development.js has 1). The rows guarded this way are `-dom-cljs-test` namespaces, which only `:browser-test` runs, and that compiles dev React. So the branch never fires. If the lane ever resolved prod React, all sixteen rows would pass with no assertion run.
   Cost: defensive scaffolding that fails open, plus about 40 copies of two helpers to keep in step.
   Fix: one shared test helper (e.g. in core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_test_support.cljs, beside `react-element-attr`) that returns `React.act` or fails the row (`(is (some? act) "React.act must be reachable in the browser lane")`), plus one shared `browser?`. Then delete the per-file copies and the skip branches.
