title: senior review: MCP base, MCP conformance and Story-MCP
description:
SENIOR-DEVELOPER REVIEW of one slice of the tree. Part of the review sweep rf2-r5cc2, which partitions implementation/, tools/, examples/ and skills/ into slices; this bead owns exactly the slice below, and its siblings own the rest.

SLICE:
- tools/mcp-base/**
- tools/mcp-conformance/**
- tools/story-mcp/**

FOCUS: The shared MCP base, the conformance harness and wire vocabulary, and the Story MCP server.

PERSONA. A senior Clojure/ClojureScript developer who did not write this code, reading it as its next maintainer and as a programmer who has to use it. Judge it against the project stance (CLAUDE.md), quoted verbatim:

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

So record material, actionable insights only: a defect, a simplification that removes real weight, an ergonomic sharp edge a programmer (or the AI they use) will hit, a test that cannot go red, a doc or docstring that misleads. Not style preferences, not nagging diagnostics, not defensive belt-and-braces, not renames for taste.

LENSES, in priority order:
1. Correctness — error paths, concurrency, cleanup, and fail-closed behaviour on any security or privacy boundary.
2. Simplicity and clarity — dead code, duplication (within the slice or with another slice), accidental complexity, an abstraction that earns nothing.
3. Ergonomics — the API or tool as a programmer, or the AI they use, actually meets it.
4. Performance — hot spots on real paths, never at the expense of clarity.
5. Test rigour — a test that cannot fail, a gap on a branch that matters.
6. Comments and docstrings — per CLAUDE.md § Conventions & Patterns: present tense, the reason plus a spec pointer, no provenance, no restated spec.

METHOD. Read the slice's source first, then its tests, against the owning spec sections (spec/Ownership.md maps each surface to its spec). A finding is a CLAIM until checked: confirm each one at source, and confirm a behaviour claim with a quick REPL or test run where that is cheap. This is a read-only review: edit no file, and run only read-only commands and the slice's existing test lanes.

OUTPUT, recorded on THIS bead and never in a separate file: write the section to a file and append it with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes "$(cat <file>)"` (never `--notes`, which replaces). Head it `== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (<datetime with zone>, trunk <short sha>)` and include:
- 0 to 15 numbered findings, most important first. Each gives: `path:line` (plus a short quote so it can be re-found by text), what is wrong, why it matters (the concrete failure or cost), the fix (a sketch is fine), size (S/M/L), confidence (verified / probable), and its lens.
- A short "looked at and sound" list, so the review's coverage is visible.
- Cross-slice findings, whose defect lives in another slice's files, in a separate list naming the owning slice. Do not act on them.

Then add the label `findings-recorded` and leave the bead OPEN: its findings become this slice's fix work, which the coordinator dispatches in clusters. If the slice needs nothing, record zero findings with the coverage list and close the bead with that as the reason.
notes:
== ROUTED FROM rf2-r5cc2.22 (pair-mcp review, trunk 9657b27a5d) — an item this slice owns

tools/mcp-base overflow.cljc:40 `overflow-hint-fallback`: the shared overflow fallback text "Re-call with narrower args" is unsafe advice for any tool that is not safe to repeat (an action tool whose overflowing reply followed a side effect). It is shared with story-mcp. Confirm, and record it as a finding with a fix (e.g. wording that does not invite a blind repeat, or a per-tool hint) or under "looked at and sound".
== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (2026-10-29 15:05:50 AUSEST, trunk 2a2dbdff22)

Slice: tools/mcp-base/**, tools/mcp-conformance/**, tools/story-mcp/**. Read against the per-ns docs in tools/mcp-base/spec, tools/story-mcp/spec and spec/Cross-Cutting-Designs.md. Review began at 2fab1acb29. `git diff 2fab1acb29 2a2dbdff22` touches no file in the slice, so every line cited below holds at 2a2dbdff22.

Overall: the code is careful and well tested. The story-mcp JVM suite is green (146 tests, 332 assertions) and so is the mcp-base suite (114 tests, 344 assertions). The real problems:
- two correctness defects in story-mcp, a false green and a run that is never actually cancelled;
- what the AI client receives: a 14k-token tools/list, a dedup wrapper that hides `:status`, and two tools that cannot succeed on the shipped server;
- a handful of gates that cannot go red on the thing they claim to check.

1. tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/testing.cljc:370, `:status (rf.story/aggregate-verdict records nil)`, where `records` are the SCRUBBED records.
   WHAT: `read-failures` works out its verdict after dropping `:sensitive? true` records. So a run whose only failures are sensitive reports `:status :pass`. The docstring (:355-357) says the reverse: "a dropped sensitive failure doesn't quietly flip the verdict to `:pass`". The test pins the flip but its message says it doesn't happen: tools_test.clj:1223-1234 seeds two failing sensitive records and asserts `:status :pass`, with the message "does not flip the verdict".
   WHY: this is a false green at the privacy boundary, and the slice already rejects it twice:
   - `run-variant` keeps the raw `(:status outcome)` for the same accumulator.
   - `egress/scrub-checks` refuses to recompute a check status after hiding records, because "a failed check into a vacuous pass ... is the worse lie".
   So an agent gets `:fail` from one tool and `:pass` from the other for the same run.
   FIX: work out `:status` over `(rf.story/assertion-records raw)`, and keep `:total` / `:failures` / `:assertions` over the scrubbed records. The `:dropped-sensitive` count already explains the gap. Flip the test to expect `:fail` and fix its message.
   SIZE S. CONFIDENCE verified. A JVM probe with `read-assertions` redefined to one passing record plus one failing sensitive record gave `{:status :pass :total 1 :failures [] :dropped-sensitive 1}`; `aggregate-verdict` over the raw records gives `:fail`. LENS 1.

2. tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/lifecycle.cljc:160-166 ("the worker is CANCELLED (interrupting its `Thread/sleep`, so the scheduled post-wait continuation never runs ...") and :187 `(future-cancel worker)`.
   WHAT: a deadline only interrupts. A run that is busy rather than blocked keeps running after the tool has replied, and it goes on writing into the variant frame. That frame's id is the variant id, so the next `read-failures` / `preview-variant` / `run-variant` of the same variant reads or races it.
   WHY: the reply says the run "was abandoned". After it, later reads return the zombie's state, and a re-run of that variant runs at the same time as the zombie on the same frame. The single-threaded stdio loop is freed, so the next request does run concurrently.
   FIX:
   - On deadline, fence the run: destroy or reset the variant frame after `future-cancel`, so late writes cannot reach a frame a later call reads.
   - Better: a run token that Story checks between steps. That part is cross-slice (tools/story, `run-variant`).
   - Make the docstring true: interruption stops blocking waits, not computation.
   SIZE M. CONFIDENCE verified. A probe variant whose `:setup` event spins for 1.5 s, run with `:timeout-ms 200`, replied `:status :error` ("Story lifecycle deadline exceeded ... abandoned") after 212 ms. At reply its handler had not finished. 2.5 s later it had, and the frame's app-db was `{:rf.story/lifecycle :ready, :spun? true}`, which looks like a completed run. LENS 1.

3. tools/story-mcp tools/list costs about 14,000 tokens. Sources: the `:description` strings in tools/dev.cljc, docs.cljc, testing.cljc and write.cljc (e.g. testing.cljc:387, dev.cljc:239, testing.cljc:442), and server.cljc:163 "The bounded registry is small enough to return in one response".
   WHAT: `(json/generate-string {:tools (registry/tool-descriptors)})` is 56,168 characters for 19 tools, about 14,042 tokens by the server's own chars/4 rule. The largest descriptions are `run-variant` 4,597 chars, `read-a11y-violations` 3,038 and `preview-variant` 3,014. Much of the text is server internals a model cannot act on: "EP-0025 FAIL-OPEN", how `project-egress` resolves profiles, "the named `scrub-re-keyed-runtime` egress exception", "zero leak-delta".
   WHY: an MCP host puts tools/list into the model's context every session. That is nearly three times the 5,000-token budget the server enforces on any single reply, and it is paid before the first call.
   FIX: cut each description to purpose, key arguments, the one or two behaviours an agent acts on (the refusals and `:status` values), and one or two examples. The egress architecture already lives in spec/API.md and tools/story/spec/006. Add a tools/list size ratchet to tools/mcp-conformance so it cannot regrow. Regenerate tool-descriptors.edn.
   SIZE M. CONFIDENCE verified (JVM probe). LENS 3 (and 4).

4. The default structural dedup on `run-variant` / `preview-variant` makes small replies bigger and hides the verdict.
   - Policy: tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc:674-686 `dedup-value`.
   - Default: story-mcp wire_pipeline.cljc:425-427 (`:dedup` defaults true).
   - Advice: tools/schemas.cljc:32 and :46 tell "the agent host" to call `(re-frame.mcp-base.dedup/expand cache-map)`.
   WHAT:
   - `dedup-value` wraps whenever any subtree repeats, even when the result is larger. Empty vectors count: `(dedup-value {:a [] :b [] :c []} true)` turns each two-character `[]` into the 21-character `de-dupe.cache/cache-1`.
   - The wrapped reply's structuredContent has exactly one top-level key, `:rf.mcp/dedup-table`. The headline `:status` sits inside `de-dupe.cache/cache-0`, so a JSON-reading host cannot see it without implementing the codec. An AI client cannot call a Clojure function.
   - Encoding cost: escape-literals rebuilds every node even when nothing needs escaping, which defeats `=` short-circuiting. The count pass is a `prewalk` whose rebuilt tree is thrown away (dedup.cljc:496-505 and :548). A non-rebuilding visitor gives the same counts in 20.8 ms against 45.9 ms; the whole `de-dupe-eq` is 54-63 ms.
   - The story-mcp corpus mostly reads the non-default shape: tools_test.clj:86-91 `invoke` defaults `:dedup false`.
   WHY: the default reply of the two headline tools is larger on ordinary runs, harder to read, and slower to build.
   FIX:
   - In `dedup-value`: return the raw value unless the wrapped rendering is actually smaller, and do not substitute empty collections.
   - Make escape-literals identity-preserving, and replace the counting `prewalk` with a visitor.
   - In story-mcp: keep `:status` readable without decoding (default `:dedup false`, or hoist the verdict beside the table), and drop the "call expand" advice from the schema text.
   SIZE M. CONFIDENCE verified. Probe on a trivial variant: dedup on gave 1,250 text plus 1,335 JSON chars, against 924 plus 944 off (+38%). On a variant with a 6-item app-db: 2,002 plus 2,243 on, against 2,473 plus 2,546 off (-15%). LENS 3/4.

5. tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/cljs_resolve.cljc:84 `(def ^:dynamic *substrate-provider*` / :134 `*a11y-provider*` / :169 `*a11y-incomplete-provider*`, all `nil`.
   WHAT: nothing outside tools_test.clj binds these seams. `git grep` finds only the tests and a README tree line; the control is the seams' own definitions. So on the only shipped host:
   - `list-substrates` and `read-a11y-violations` always return capability-unavailable;
   - an explicit `:substrate` on `run-variant` / `preview-variant` / `snapshot-identity` always errors.
   The descriptors also teach calls that cannot succeed (dev.cljc:242 and testing.cljc:425 use `:substrate ":uix"`).
   WHY: tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md:685-694 retired `record-as-variant` under "every advertised success path must be exercisable through the published transport". These two tools fail that same test. They cost tools/list space (about 4,200 description chars) and an agent round-trip each. They also carry real weight: cljs_resolve.cljc (184 lines), egress `scrub-re-keyed-runtime` and its carve-out prose, the `:substrate` validation and their tests.
   FIX: retire both tools and the `:substrate` argument until a browser bridge binds the seams; they land with the bridge. Alternatively, register them only when a provider is bound, so tools/list never advertises a dead tool. Update the tool-names fixture, spec/API.md and tools/story/spec/006 together.
   SIZE M. CONFIDENCE verified (census plus reading). LENS 2/3.

6. tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/run-re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite.cjs: three faults in the boot path of the hermetic runner.
   a) :1099-1108: every `safeReadFileInside` error inside the 100 ms port-file poll is rethrown as "refusing to read nREPL port candidate ... must not be trusted". That includes EBUSY, EPERM, EACCES and EISDIR while shadow-cljs is writing the file. The module already has `isContainmentEscape` (:1014) and the wipe path uses it. A transient Windows file lock therefore kills the run with exit 2 and a misleading symlink diagnosis. FIX: rethrow only when `isContainmentEscape(e)`; otherwise `continue`. Verified: a directory placed as the candidate threw that message for EISDIR.
   b) :68 `const FIXTURE_HTTP_PORT = 8030;`: nothing checks the port is free. When 8030 is already bound, shadow-cljs 3.4.12 logs a warning and runs with no dev-http (`dev_http.clj`: `(catch Exception e (log/warn-ex e ::http-start-ex ...) nil)`), and `probeHttp` (:1122) / `probeBundleReady` (:1145) accept whatever process holds 8030. With concurrent worktrees, or a fixture JVM leaked by a dirty teardown, Chromium attaches to the other build and the run fails after 60 s with the wrong diagnosis. FIX: `if (await probeTcp(FIXTURE_HTTP_PORT)) throw ...` before spawning. Optionally also fail on `http-start-ex` in shadow's output.
   c) :1239 `txt.includes('"status"')`: the probe speaks bencode, where the key is `6:status`, so the done branch is dead and every not-ready poll waits out the 2 s idle timeout (:1203). FIX: match `4:done`.
   SIZE S. CONFIDENCE (a) and (c) verified; (b) mechanism verified, frequency probable. LENS 1 (c: 4).

7. tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/sensitive.cljc:240 `scrub-snapshot`.
   WHAT:
   - It has no production caller. Its only callers are mcp-base tests and implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/mcp_egress_security_cljs_test.cljc. story-mcp uses `strip-sensitive`, and pair-mcp does not filter (sensitive.md:100).
   - Its 3-arity, the "public for pair-mcp's `:rf.epoch/sensitive?`" rationale (:155-162) and the fixture comment "pair-mcp's union strip-fn" (sensitive_test.clj:83) describe a consumer that does not exist.
   - It fails open on two shapes: a set-shaped slice, and an un-keyed single-frame map. A probe gave `[{:traces [{:id 1, :sensitive? true, :secret "LEAK"}]} 0]`.
   WHY: a privacy primitive that is published, documented as a boundary and guarded by a security test, yet guards no real egress and leaks on plausible input, invites the next caller to trust it.
   FIX: delete it, with its spec/API.md and api-manifest rows (hot zone, one holding), the spec/Privacy.md row and the security test. If it is kept, make non-batch slices fail closed.
   SIZE M. CONFIDENCE verified (call census plus JVM probe). LENS 2/1.

8. tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/cursor.cljc:245-249 (`::cursor-eof-sentinel`, "Qualified + unguessable") and :294-297. envelope.cljc:195-227 is a copy of the technique.
   WHAT: two defects.
   - The wrap-and-sentinel reader's sentinel can be spelled. A decoded cursor `{...} :re-frame.mcp-base.cursor/cursor-eof-sentinel] {:junk 1}` is accepted, as is the same with `] #foo/bar 1 ]]]`, and the trailing forms are silently dropped. `marker-text?` likewise returns true for `{:rf.mcp/overflow {:limit :reached}} :re-frame.mcp-base.envelope/marker-eof-sentinel] 42`.
   - On CLJS, `cljs.reader/read-string` merges its built-in tag table (`inst uuid queue js`) under the caller's `:readers`. So `#js` and `#queue` get past the `:default` reject, on pair-mcp, the host that runs this. spec/cursor.md:98 wrongly lists `#js` as unregistered.
   WHY: the one-form and no-tag guarantees both docstrings advertise are false. Practical harm is low because the result is still a valid map, but the marker case can skip pair-mcp's cap/cache step for a crafted reply.
   FIX: one shared reader for both namespaces: a pushback reader with `:eof` set to a fresh `(Object.)`, read one form, then require the next read to return that object. Use `clojure.edn/read` on the JVM and `cljs.tools.reader.edn/read` on CLJS, whose default readers are `{}`. This deletes the wrap and sentinel code and its prose. Add `#js` / `#queue` cases to the CLJS test.
   SIZE S. CONFIDENCE verified (JVM probe for the sentinel; CLJS by reading cljs/reader.cljs 1.12.145 :134-140, :189-190). LENS 1.

9. tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc:201-203 `(rf.story-mcp.protocol/method-not-found id (str "tools/call name=" tool-name))`.
   WHAT: a mistyped tool name gets JSON-RPC `-32601 "Method not found: tools/call name=list-storys"`, a protocol error naming the wrong thing, since `tools/call` exists. pair-mcp answers the same mistake with an `isError` `:unknown-tool` result carrying `:hint`, `:available-tools` and `:did-you-mean` (re-frame2-pair-mcp tools.cljs `unknown-tool-envelope` / `refuse-unknown-tool`). story-mcp's own spec gives the reason that is the right shape (003-Write-Surface-Gating.md:66-70: `-32601` "would make the agent think the server is broken rather than configured").
   WHY: in the same pair, the same typo is recoverable on one server and a dead end on the other. Many hosts surface protocol errors as a failed call rather than handing them to the model.
   FIX: return the pair's recovery envelope as an `isError` result: `:rf.error :rf.story-mcp/unknown-tool`, `:available-tools` from the registry, and a near match. Update 001-Wire-Protocol.md, the retired-tool note in 002-Tool-Registry.md:697, and end-to-end-story.cjs:690-712, which pins -32601.
   SIZE S. CONFIDENCE verified (dispatch probe). LENS 3.
10. tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/write.cljc:29 "Write surface disabled. Set `:rf.story-mcp/allow-writes?` (or `--allow-writes` CLI flag, or `-Drf.story-mcp.allow-writes=true` JVM property)". The same key appears in the descriptors at :373, :377, :398, in spec 003-Write-Surface-Gating.md:3 and :48, spec/API.md:622, spec/README.md:8, and twice in tool-descriptors.edn.
   WHAT: no `:rf.story-mcp/allow-writes?` key exists. `git grep` finds only prose; the gate is the `config/allow-writes?` atom. The message gives the phantom key as the first option and omits the env var `RF_STORY_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES`, which config.cljc:219-224 does read.
   WHY: this is the one message an operator reads when writes are off, and its first instruction cannot be followed.
   FIX: name the real routes: `--allow-writes`, `-Drf.story-mcp.allow-writes=true`, `RF_STORY_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES=true`. Correct the descriptor and spec prose, and regenerate tool-descriptors.edn.
   SIZE S. CONFIDENCE verified (probe printed the text; census). LENS 6/3.

11. tools/mcp-conformance: four checks that cannot go red on what they claim, plus a stale alias list.
   a) wire-vocab/test/re_frame/mcp_conformance/trace_catalogue_lint_test.clj:47 `emitter-source-files` is a hand-written list of 10 files. Its docstring says "Any file that emits a reply-envelope trace row belongs here" (:40), yet it omits the builders that write `:rf.reply/work-id` into map literals: implementation/http reply.cljc:157 and handlers.cljc:347, resources reply.cljc:94, routing reply.cljc:160 and :213. FIX: derive the list from disk (every implementation/*/src .clj/.cljc containing `:rf.reply/`), and assert it is non-empty and contains a known member.
   b) wire_vocab_test.clj:211-239 `re-frame2-pair-overflow-js-required-grep-markers` compares hand-copied, column-aligned JS lines and never reads `ReFrame2PairOverflowBody` (wire_vocab/schemas.clj:17). A new required schema field passes; re-aligned whitespace fails. lib/overflow-marker.cjs:60-64 claims "a drift in either direction trips the JVM-side test". FIX: iterate the schema's children, match a `['<field>',` row by regex, compare counts, and correct the comment.
   c) test/end-to-end-project-stories.cjs:84-86, phase 0: it builds its own `clojure -M -e ... -m re-frame.story-mcp.server` command line, so it tests `clojure.main`'s `-e`-before-`-m` ordering, not story-mcp or the fixture alias. Nothing can turn it red that the main phase misses, and it costs a JVM boot (240 s cap). README.md:41-44 presents it as a project guarantee. FIX: delete it, or use `clojure -P -M:story-mcp` if only a warm-up is wanted.
   d) package.json:8-31: 19 per-file `test:*` aliases with no caller in tracked code, docs or workflows. Three unit tests have none (hermetic-grading, live-list-completeness, overflow-marker), contrary to README.md:207-221's one-owner rule. FIX: keep only the documented entry points.
   SIZE S. CONFIDENCE verified (reading plus `git grep`). (a)'s detector was not run; no current duplicate was found in the unswept files. LENS 5/2.

12. tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/section_grouping.cljc:296 (`patches-all-direct-child?` plus `(not container-existed?)`) and :371 `(sort-by #(pr-str (patch-path %)) patches)`, also :392.
   WHAT:
   - `:section-kind :added` is never emitted. The encoder only emits a patch whose parent exists in `:db-before`, so a new subtree reads `:modified` (`{} -> {:user {...}}` gives `[[:user] :modified]`). A 5,000-epoch fuzz produced `{:modified 5482 :removed 1500}` and zero `:added`. The `absent` sentinel, `path-present?`, the direct-child rule, the `:db-before` plumbing (diff_encode.cljc:764-770) and a CLJS test all serve a label the wire never carries.
   - `sort-by` recomputes `pr-str` on every comparison. For an 8,000-patch update, grouping takes 110.6 ms against 10.8 ms to collect the patches; the sort is 99.8 ms of it, and 15.9 ms with precomputed keys. That contradicts the "negligible vs the walk" claim (:141-147 and section-grouping.md §Cost).
   FIX: mark a section `:added` when every patch is `:assoc` at a path absent in db-before, and drop the direct-child and container rules. Decorate-sort-undecorate both sorts. Update section-grouping.md §5.
   SIZE S. CONFIDENCE verified (JVM fuzz and timing). LENS 2/3/4.

13. tools/mcp-base: dead public surface and docstrings that mislead.
   - cap.cljc:264 `sum-payload-chars` has no caller anywhere, tests included. Its docstring (:268) says "Used by the secondary character ceiling", but `apply-cap` folds its own sums (:385-392). The private `sum-payload-by` exists only to serve it and `sum-payload-tokens` (which pair-mcp does call, cap.cljs:165, the census control).
   - overflow.cljc:11-15 says "the cap-enforcement glue (counting tokens, replacing the payload) lives consumer-side". That is false: cap.cljc is the shared algorithm, as its own ns docstring says.
   - args.cljc:269 `fresh-keyword` has one call form, in args_test.clj:37. Its own docstring names `register-variant` as a user, but that calls `fresh-keyword-checked` (story-mcp write.cljc:338). The `fresh-keyword-checked` docstring (:322-325) describes it as the intern-before-validate hazard.
   - vocab.cljc:32-39 says "the seven per-call policy keys ... the keys the `-opt` defs below carry"; there are four `-opt` defs.
   - vocab.cljc:217-219 points to an `include-sensitive?` in `re-frame.mcp-base.sensitive` that does not exist (it is story-mcp tools/args.cljc:69).
   - args.cljc:165, :225, :282 and args.md:41 say "pinned Clojure (1.12.4)"; deps.edn:23 pins 1.12.0.
   - story-mcp wire_pipeline.cljc:63-66 says the cap counts "every `:text` slot"; it also counts `:structuredContent`.
   FIX: delete `sum-payload-chars` (inline the fold into `sum-payload-tokens`) and `fresh-keyword` (fold its intern into `fresh-keyword-checked`, then update args.md and the consumer docstrings in the cross-slice list), and correct the rest.
   SIZE S. CONFIDENCE verified (call-form census with controls). LENS 2/6.

14. Routed item (from rf2-r5cc2.22): tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/overflow.cljc:37-40 `overflow-hint-fallback` "Response over budget. Re-call with narrower args, or raise `max-tokens` (0 disables the cap)."
   VERDICT: confirmed as a latent hazard, with small exposure today.
   - Overflow replaces the reply after the side effect has run. Probe: `register-variant` with `:max-tokens 3` returned `{:rf.mcp/overflow {... :hint "Largest slots: :variant-id 77%, :registered? 22%. Response over budget. Re-call with narrower args, or raise `max-tokens` ..."}}`, and the variant was registered.
   - pair-mcp already gives each of its action tools its own "do NOT ... again" hint (cap.cljs:93-96).
   - story-mcp's two write tools reach the fallback only under a cap below about 25 tokens, and their effects are near-idempotent (a re-register replaces; a second unregister is a not-found error).
   So the risk is any future action tool on either server that is missing from its hint table.
   FIX: make the shared fallback safe to repeat: "Response over budget. If this call changes state it has already run: do not repeat it, read the state back instead. Otherwise narrow the arguments, or raise `max-tokens` (0 disables the cap)." Optionally give `register-variant` / `unregister-variant` their own entries in story-mcp's `overflow-hints`.
   SIZE S. CONFIDENCE verified (probe). LENS 3.

15. Bead-id and review-wave provenance in prose that CLAUDE.md § Conventions requires to be present-tense.
   - tools/story-mcp/spec has 101 matching lines (108 ids): API.md 37, 002-Tool-Registry.md 42, 001-Wire-Protocol.md 18, others 4. Examples: heading "## Run options (rf2-sw1d)", "(rf2-ovmc5e)".
   - tools/mcp-base/spec has 21 lines (22 ids): dedup.md's §Provenance narrative, section-grouping.md's "since excised", README.md's "vendored ... under rf2-2ii52" and egress row "since rf2-kuky.88".
   - tools/mcp-conformance has about 40, mostly in test titles. Examples: runner-cleanup.test.cjs:81 "(rf2-7ckmwx finding 1)", classification-ratchet.test.cjs "RED: rf2-6i2yi4 finding 4", NAMING.md:31.
   - The src trees are clean: 0 in tools/story-mcp/src and tools/mcp-base/src. The control is the same `git grep -o -E "rf2-[a-z0-9]{3,}"`, which finds the spec hits.
   - rf2-tv5ac is closed, so nothing else will sweep these.
   FIX: a mechanical pass under rf2-tv5ac's calibration (R1-R6): drop the ids and narration, keep the present-tense rule, and leave temp-dir identifiers and asserted strings alone. Rename end-to-end-story.cjs step 9's retired-tool probe to a neutral `no-such-tool` name; it stays the unknown-tool check of finding 9.
   SIZE S (mechanical, 3 dirs). CONFIDENCE verified (census). LENS 6.

LOOKED AT AND SOUND
- story-mcp server.cljc and protocol.cljc. The parts checked:
  - lifecycle gate, notifications, params-container -32602 guard;
  - stdout bound to stderr for the length of dispatch;
  - UTF-8 byte-bounded frame reader with drain and surrogate pairs;
  - no-intern ingress (`normalize-frame`, unknown-arg metadata);
  - `shutdown-agents` placed in `-main`, not `run-loop!`.
- story-mcp config.cljc: precedence CLI > sysprop > env; an explicit `false` sysprop wins.
- story-mcp wire_pipeline.cljc: dedup-before-cap order, `cap-error` capping the pre-dispatch errors, per-tool unknown-argument backstop, `isError` carried across overflow.
- story-mcp result.cljc: total `wire-safe-ex-data`; type-preserving `wire-safe-success`, including the record respelling case.
- story-mcp egress.cljc: `elide-app-db` / `scrub-rendered` fail closed on a non-live frame; empty-tree short-circuit; `project-narrative` / `project-epoch-rows` route through the epoch projector; `scrub-checks` keeps check status.
- story-mcp args.cljc and write.cljc:
  - run-option shape, semantic and substrate guards (refuse rather than drop), and nested override key alignment;
  - EDN body hardening: UTF-8 byte cap, depth cap, width cap before interning, and tags rejected.
- story-mcp cursor.cljc paging and stale-cursor handling.
- The descriptors' load-time asserts, and the descriptor-manifest generator.
- story-mcp tests: rigorous overall. wire_encodability_test drives the real run-loop and reads the raw bytes.
- mcp-base:
  - cap.cljc: two-stage gate, resolver domain checks;
  - envelope `with-indicators`;
  - elision walker;
  - egress profile mapping;
  - args parsers;
  - `safe-keyword` no-intern;
  - cursor base64 and size cap;
  - sensitive fail-closed classifier, plus `strip-sensitive`;
  - dedup grammar and escaping;
  - diff-encode round-trip: a 5,000-epoch fuzz was exact;
  - descriptor-manifest.
- mcp-conformance:
  - `_runner.cjs`: client lifecycle, watchdog exit ordering, classification and call-coverage ratchets;
  - hermetic runner: inner-test grading on `close`, `runTrusted` timeouts, idempotent cleanup, stale-port wipe;
  - lib: dedup-envelope (cycles, orphans, `__proto__`), overflow-marker, exec-safety;

  - wire-vocab: fixtures, comment/string stripper, verb-vocab, source pins.

CROSS-SLICE (do not act here)
- tools/story (rf2-r5cc2 tools/story slice): finding 2's complete fix is a run token / cancellation check between run-variant steps.
- spec/Privacy.md:133 says `scrub-snapshot` descends "into nested registration handles". It is shallow and leaves `:app-db` alone. OWNER: spec/ (coordinator routes), together with finding 7.
- implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/mcp_egress_security_cljs_test.cljc:105 guards only `scrub-snapshot`, which no production path calls. OWNER: implementation/security slice, together with finding 7.
- tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp: about 9 docstrings cite "the shared `fresh-keyword` path", which nothing calls:
  - args.cljs:226, :323, :593
  - trace_window.cljs:68
  - watch_epochs.cljs:93
  - dispatch.cljs:325
  - read_ui.cljs:177
  - probe.cljs:150
  - discover_app.cljs:314
  The same citation appears in spec/API.md:69 and spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md:1150. OWNER: pair-mcp slice (rf2-r5cc2.22), together with finding 13.
- skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/fixture/shadow-cljs.edn `:dev-http {8030 ...}` and tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/live-e2e-fixture.cjs probably share finding 6b's port-8030 exposure (not read). OWNERS: the skills/re-frame2-pair and pair-mcp slices.

NOT SETTLED
- Finding 2: only the "abandoned run keeps writing" half was measured. A concurrent re-run racing the zombie on one frame was reasoned, not reproduced.

The hermetic runner's Windows teardown order (SIGTERM to the launcher before `reapShadowTree`, so the reaper always takes its vacated-root branch, :887-929) may be better reaped first. title: senior review: flows, integration tests and the conformance runners
description:
SENIOR-DEVELOPER REVIEW of one slice of the tree. Part of the review sweep rf2-r5cc2, which partitions implementation/, tools/, examples/ and skills/ into slices; this bead owns exactly the slice below, and its siblings own the rest.

SLICE:
- implementation/flows/**
- implementation/integration/**
- implementation/derivation-conformance/**, implementation/event-conformance/**, implementation/reply-conformance/**

FOCUS: Flows (Spec 013), the cross-artefact integration suite, and the conformance runners against spec/conformance.

PERSONA. A senior Clojure/ClojureScript developer who did not write this code, reading it as its next maintainer and as a programmer who has to use it. Judge it against the project stance (CLAUDE.md), quoted verbatim:

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

So record material, actionable insights only: a defect, a simplification that removes real weight, an ergonomic sharp edge a programmer (or the AI they use) will hit, a test that cannot go red, a doc or docstring that misleads. Not style preferences, not nagging diagnostics, not defensive belt-and-braces, not renames for taste.

LENSES, in priority order:
1. Correctness — error paths, concurrency, cleanup, and fail-closed behaviour on any security or privacy boundary.
2. Simplicity and clarity — dead code, duplication (within the slice or with another slice), accidental complexity, an abstraction that earns nothing.
3. Ergonomics — the API or tool as a programmer, or the AI they use, actually meets it.
4. Performance — hot spots on real paths, never at the expense of clarity.
5. Test rigour — a test that cannot fail, a gap on a branch that matters.
6. Comments and docstrings — per CLAUDE.md § Conventions & Patterns: present tense, the reason plus a spec pointer, no provenance, no restated spec.

METHOD. Read the slice's source first, then its tests, against the owning spec sections (spec/Ownership.md maps each surface to its spec). A finding is a CLAIM until checked: confirm each one at source, and confirm a behaviour claim with a quick REPL or test run where that is cheap. This is a read-only review: edit no file, and run only read-only commands and the slice's existing test lanes.

OUTPUT, recorded on THIS bead and never in a separate file: write the section to a file and append it with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes "$(cat <file>)"` (never `--notes`, which replaces). Head it `== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (<datetime with zone>, trunk <short sha>)` and include:
- 0 to 15 numbered findings, most important first. Each gives: `path:line` (plus a short quote so it can be re-found by text), what is wrong, why it matters (the concrete failure or cost), the fix (a sketch is fine), size (S/M/L), confidence (verified / probable), and its lens.
- A short "looked at and sound" list, so the review's coverage is visible.
- Cross-slice findings, whose defect lives in another slice's files, in a separate list naming the owning slice. Do not act on them.

Then add the label `findings-recorded` and leave the bead OPEN: its findings become this slice's fix work, which the coordinator dispatches in clusters. If the slice needs nothing, record zero findings with the coverage list and close the bead with that as the reason.
notes:
== ROUTED FROM rf2-r5cc2.12 (schemas review), cross-slice, for this slice
implementation/schemas/test/.../schemas_conformance_test.clj is a hand-copied version of core's conformance runner, and the same copied-runner pattern exists in flows, machines and ssr. Core's full-corpus runner already claims every :schemas/* capability, so the five schema fixtures run twice. The schemas reviewer marked this PROBABLE: it did not check which CI jobs run on a schemas-only change, so a per-artefact runner may be the only lane that grades a schemas-only PR. Settle that before recommending deletion. The schemas-fix worker (worktree schemas-fix) is fenced to implementation/schemas/** and will not touch this file.
== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (2026-10-29 15:54:03 AUSEST, trunk 9778206785)

Slice: implementation/flows/** (1.1k source lines, 2.4k test lines), implementation/integration/** (5.3k test lines), implementation/{derivation,event,reply}-conformance/** (1.1k test lines). Read against Spec 013, with the router's flow interceptor and settle (core router.cljc) and elision's policy build read where the flows hooks are called. Line numbers are at 9778206785; none of the slice's files changed by 57f02960f0. "Verified" behaviour claims were reproduced on the JVM by a throwaway probe script run on the flows :test classpath, each beside a control (the same scenario without the trigger, or with the hook in its shipped state). The flows JVM lane (clojure -M:test in implementation/flows) is green at this trunk: exit 0, 83 tests / 198 assertions. So no existing test catches finding 1. The integration suite and the CLJS arms were read, not run: they need a shadow-cljs build that writes into the tree.

1. An ambiguous flow id makes the frame's whole classification policy throw, so the event error is never reported.
   Where: flows.cljc:245 "(let [defs (concat (vals (active-flows (:flows (rf.frame/frame-config frame-id))))" — output-classification goes through active-flows (flows.cljc:230 "(rf.registrar/lookup rf.flows.registry/kind id)"), which throws :rf.error/ambiguous-registration under a live frame's view.
   What: a frame made without :images that names a flow id a second namespace later registers (a namespace rename during hot reload, before the sweep) raises from inside re-frame.elision/frame-policy. That policy build runs outside the :rf/flows interceptor's try, so the throw escapes the event.
   Cost: dispatch-sync throws a raw :rf.error/ambiguous-registration to the caller. The always-on error channel gets nothing, and every elided egress for that frame (traces, tool reads) throws too. That is exactly the situation where the actionable message ("registered by more than one namespace … Recover with (rf/clear :flow id)") matters most. Elision already tolerates this case for its own registrations (elision.cljc:140 resolved-classifications keeps every namespace's declaration of an ambiguous id), and flows' own tooling.cljc:77 frame-flows catches it. output-classification is the one caller that does neither.
   Verified: register :amb/out from ns probe.a, make a live frame, dispatch (control: elide-wire-value for the frame returns normally), then register :amb/out from probe.b and dispatch again. Result: dispatch threw :rf.error/ambiguous-registration, with a stack through flows$output_classification (flows.cljc:245) → active_flows → registrar/lookup → live_frame/live_view. Zero error-emit records, and elide-wire-value for the frame threw. With only the hook wrapped in a catch, the same dispatch returned normally and app-db was unchanged. One always-on record [:rf.error/flow-eval-exception :flow-eval :rf.error/ambiguous-registration] was delivered, which is the Spec 013 §Re-registration abort.
   Fix: make output-classification total. For an id the bound view finds ambiguous, union every namespace's definition's output-declaration (the fail-closed reading, matching resolved-classifications). Let the flow pass, not the policy build, report the ambiguity. Add a JVM test of this shape.
   Size S. Confidence verified. Lens 1 (correctness, fail-closed error path).

2. flows_conformance_test.clj is a hand copy of core's corpus runner, and the copy grades less.
   Where: flows/test/re_frame/flows_conformance_test.clj (350 lines). Core's runner claims every :flow/* capability (core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc:177-185) and realises flows itself (:449 realise-flows!, :1549 the {:reg-flow …} step). It has matchers for every flow channel (:749-783), and the flow-eval-exception error-emit record is graded in core/test/conformance-reference/overlays.edn:80. So all nine flow-*.edn fixtures run twice.
   What: the copy is also weaker. Its run-fixture silently skips any :fixture/expect key it has no channel for (":when (and observe (some? expected))", so a key with no channel never reaches the mismatch map), while core fails such a fixture (conformance_test.clj:282 unknown-expect-key-fails-the-fixture). Its own docstring says a skip would leave a fixture's contract unchecked while the gate stayed green. Today every flow fixture uses only keys it knows (checked: the expect keys of all nine fixtures are inside its channel map), so the hole is latent.
   CI coverage, settled per the coordinator's question: .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh handed a flows-only path (implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc, and separately a flows test path) reports implementation_jvm=true, and its jvm_legs include {"dir":"implementation/core","alias":"test"}. Core's :test alias carries the flows artefact (core/deps.edn :114), and run-conformance-corpus is tagged only ^:requires-debug, which the default lane's -e :slow -e :stress -e :prod-gate does not exclude. Control: docs/index.md arms implementation_jvm=false, with no core leg. So deleting the copy loses no PR grading. The only loss is that a local clojure -M:test in implementation/flows stops running the corpus.
   Fix: delete flows_conformance_test.clj. Repoint Spec 013 §Conformance coverage (it names this file as "the flows artefact's own conformance gate") and the flows_test.clj ns docstring at core's runner.
   Size S. Confidence verified. Lens 2 (duplication) / 5 (test rigour).

3. The memo-distrust hook is redundant now that equal-input visits re-assert the remembered output.
